ANAT-001.citation: Chari ST, Leibson CL, Rabe KG, Timmons LJ, Ransom J, de Andrade M, Petersen GM. Pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes mellitus: prevalence and temporal association with diagnosis of cancer. Gastroenterology. 2008;134(1):95-101.
ANAT-001.design: Retrospective matched case-control with abstraction of all outpatient fasting blood glucose (FBG) values for 60 months before index date
ANAT-001.population: Mayo Clinic pancreatic cancer cases (1981-2004, living within 120 miles of Rochester MN) with age/sex-matched Olmsted County controls
ANAT-001.n: 736 cases and 1875 controls with >=1 outpatient FBG (from 1172 cases/2344 controls)
ANAT-001.time_frame: Cases diagnosed 1981-2004; FBG window 60 months before diagnosis
ANAT-001.finding: Diabetes at any time in 60 months before index: 296/736 (40.2%) cases vs 360/1875 (19.2%) controls, p<0.0001. Proportions similar at -60 to -48 (p=0.76) and -48 to -36 months (p=0.06); higher in cases at -36 to -24 (p=0.04), -24 to -12 (p<0.001) and -12 to 0 (p<0.001) (Fig 1). New-onset among diabetics: 52.3% vs 23.6% (p<0.0001) (Fig 2). Undiagnosed diabetes (FBG criteria without clinical mention): 9.1% vs 6.4% (p=0.003). Diabetic cases vs diabetic controls: weight loss 6.4+/-8.3 vs 1.1+/-6.7 kg (p<0.0001); BMI at index 27.0 vs 29.5 (p=0.002) (Table 2). Median duration of symptoms before diagnosis: weight loss 2.75 mo, abdominal pain 2 mo, back pain 2 mo, anorexia 1.75 mo, jaundice 0.5 mo; median first symptom to diagnosis 2 months (range 0.5-36); 23 patients asymptomatic (incidental).
ANAT-001.effect: Prevalence difference 40.2% vs 19.2%; new-onset fraction 52.3% vs 23.6%; diabetes prevalence diverges from controls starting 24-36 months pre-diagnosis
ANAT-001.limitations: Only 63% of cases had any FBG; many cases seen once near diagnosis; single tertiary centre; retrospective
ANAT-001.interpretation: Temporal precedence (diabetes rises before cancer is clinically evident) supports cancer-induced diabetes but cannot exclude reverse causation for long-standing diabetes

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A Mayo Clinic study found diabetes prevalence diverged from controls starting two to three years before pancreatic cancer diagnosis.

ANAT-002.citation: Demir IE, Schorn S, Schremmer-Danninger E, Wang K, Kehl T, Giese NA, Algul H, Friess H, Ceyhan GO. Perineural mast cells are specifically enriched in pancreatic neuritis and neuropathic pain in pancreatic cancer and chronic pancreatitis. PLoS One. 2013;8(3):e60529.
ANAT-002.design: Cross-sectional quantitative immunohistochemistry (ImageJ colorimetry of 3-5 nerves with neuritis per patient, blinded) correlated with prospectively registered preoperative pain score (intensity 0-3 x frequency 1-3)
ANAT-002.population: Human pancreatic head resection specimens: PDAC n=20 (all UICC stage IIb), alcoholic chronic pancreatitis n=20, normal donor pancreas n=10
ANAT-002.finding: Pancreatic neuritis cells in PDAC: CD68+ macrophages 39.9% (10.2-64.9), CD8+ T cells 33.2%, mast cells 14.5%; B cells, CD4, plasma cells, eosinophils each <2% (Fig 1). PDAC with pain vs without: perineural mast cells 31.0% (10.8-52.1) and 3081 um2 vs 13.4% (6.6-26.3) and 778 um2, p<0.05 (Fig 3); total perineural leukocyte area not different (7574 vs 7320 um2); no other subset differed. Mast cell infiltration did not track neural invasion grade (0: 15.7%, I: 14.8%, II: 37.7%, p=0.08; Fig 5). Chymase+ mast cells 8.73% in painful vs 0.75% in painless PDAC (p<0.05; Fig 7B). PAR-1/PAR-2 mRNA and neural immunoreactivity not pain-related (Fig 6). Normal pancreas nerves had virtually no perineural mast cells.
ANAT-002.effect: ~2.3-fold higher perineural mast-cell fraction (31% vs 13%) in painful PDAC
ANAT-002.limitations: n=20 PDAC; cross-sectional; no functional test; only head tumours; pain score semi-quantitative
ANAT-002.interpretation: Correlational human tissue evidence; identifies a candidate effector cell (mast cell) for neuropathic pain independent of cancer-cell nerve invasion

glosses.pain: A study of 20 resected human tumors found more mast cells around nerves in painful than in painless cancers.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Study of 20 resected pancreatic head cancers showing mast cells around nerves were enriched in painful tumors independent of the grade of nerve invasion.

ANAT-003.citation: van Erning FN, Mackay TM, van der Geest LGM, Groot Koerkamp B, van Laarhoven HWM, Bonsing BA, et al. Association of the location of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (head, body, tail) with tumor stage, treatment, and survival: a population-based analysis. Acta Oncol. 2018;57(12):1655-1662.
ANAT-003.design: Population-based retrospective cohort; multivariable logistic and Cox regression
ANAT-003.population: All (suspected) PDAC in the Netherlands Cancer Registry 2005-2015
ANAT-003.finding: Metastatic at diagnosis: head 42%, body 69%, tail 84% (p<.001); tumour >4 cm (2015 only): 21%, 40%, 51%; resection 17%, 4%, 7%. Adjusted OR for resection: body vs head 0.29 (0.24-0.37), tail vs head 1.46 (1.19-1.78). Median OS all stages 4.5/3.3/2.2 months; after resection 16.8/15.0/17.3 months (5-yr 14.1%/6.9%/20.4%, no adjusted difference); non-resected non-metastatic 5.2/6.1/4.6; metastatic 2.6/2.4/1.9 months (adjusted HR body 1.17 [1.10-1.23], tail 1.35 [1.29-1.41]). Interaction location x stage p<.0001 (Table 1, Fig 2, Table 4).
ANAT-003.effect: Doubling of metastatic fraction from head to tail (42% to 84%); resection 4-fold lower for body/tail
ANAT-003.limitations: No comorbidity or cause-of-death data; suspected (non-verified) cases included; registry under-ascertainment of elderly
ANAT-003.interpretation: Population-level association; supports location -> late presentation -> stage, with residual survival difference in metastatic disease suggesting biology or detection effects

glosses.what-is-pdac: A Dutch national registry of 19,023 patients showing body and tail tumors were far more often metastatic at diagnosis than head tumors.
glosses.jaundice: A Dutch national registry of 19,023 patients showed head tumors were metastatic at diagnosis far less often than body or tail tumors.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Dutch national registry of 19,023 pancreatic cancers relating head, body or tail location to stage at diagnosis, resection and survival.
glosses.pancreas-head: Dutch national registry of 19,023 pancreatic cancers relating head, body or tail location to stage at diagnosis, resection and survival.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Dutch national registry of 19,023 pancreatic cancers relating head, body or tail location to stage at diagnosis, resection and survival.
glosses.splenic-vessels: Dutch national registry of 19,023 pancreatic cancers relating head, body or tail location to stage at diagnosis, resection and survival.

ANAT-004.citation: Walter FM, Mills K, Mendonca SC, Abel GA, Basu B, Carroll N, Ballard S, Lancaster J, Hamilton W, Rubin GP, Emery JD. Symptoms and patient factors associated with diagnostic intervals for pancreatic cancer (SYMPTOM pancreatic study): a prospective cohort study. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2016;1(4):298-306.
ANAT-004.design: Prospective cohort (patient questionnaire + GP and hospital records); Cox models for diagnostic intervals
ANAT-004.population: Adults >=40 referred to 7 English hospitals for suspected pancreatic cancer, 2011-2014
ANAT-004.n: 391 participants (24% response): 119 pancreatic cancer (98 adenocarcinoma; 34% metastatic), 47 other cancers, 225 no cancer
ANAT-004.time_frame: Recruitment 2011-2014; symptoms up to 2 years before diagnosis
ANAT-004.finding: No initial symptom was more frequent in pancreatic cancer than no-cancer (jaundice initial 12% vs 6%, p=0.074). Subsequent symptoms predictive: jaundice 51/105 (49%) vs 25/211 (12%) p<0.0001; weight loss 55% vs 22%; fatigue 51% vs 26%; change in bowel habit 41% vs 16%; decreased appetite 48% vs 26%; back pain 17% vs 14% (NS) (Tables 3-4). Intervals: total diagnostic interval median 117 d (IQR 57-234) cancer vs 131 d no cancer (p=0.32); patient interval 18 vs 15 d; health-system interval 76 vs 79 d. Jaundice shortened total interval (HR 1.38, 1.07-1.78), decreased appetite 1.42; back pain lengthened it (HR 0.77, 0.59-0.99), diabetes 0.71 (0.52-0.97), indigestion 0.71; median total interval 85 d with jaundice vs 183 d with back pain (Tables 5-6). Diabetes comorbidity 21% vs 11% (p=0.014).
ANAT-004.effect: Jaundice as a subsequent symptom: 49% vs 12%; back pain roughly doubles median time to diagnosis
ANAT-004.limitations: Low response rate; underpowered for symptom clusters; includes 9 PNET and 8 ampullary cancers in the cancer group
ANAT-004.interpretation: Prospective; shows which anatomical consequences (biliary obstruction) trigger rapid diagnosis versus which (retroperitoneal/neural pain, diabetes) are misattributed

glosses.fatigue: A UK study of symptoms before diagnosis found fatigue in 51% of people with pancreatic cancer versus 26% without.
glosses.pancreas-head: UK primary-care study of symptoms in people investigated for pancreatic cancer, in which jaundice was the most discriminating later symptom and the cancer group included some ampullary and neuroendocrine tumors.

ANAT-005.citation: Wang X, Misawa R, Zielinski MC, Cowen P, Jo J, Periwal V, Ricordi C, Khan A, Szust J, Shen J, Millis JM, Witkowski P, Hara M. Regional differences in islet distribution in the human pancreas - preferential beta-cell loss in the head region in patients with type 2 diabetes. PLoS One. 2013;8(6):e67454.
ANAT-005.design: Large-scale virtual-slice immunofluorescence quantification of whole sections from head, body and tail of each donor; paired comparisons; islet yield and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion ex vivo
ANAT-005.population: Cadaveric human donor pancreata (non-diabetic n=23; type 2 diabetes n=12) plus 7 clinical islet isolations split at the neck
ANAT-005.time_frame: Donor tissue; specimens within 12 h cold ischemia
ANAT-005.finding: Endocrine area as % of pancreas: head 1.22+/-0.12%, body 1.07+/-0.12%, tail 2.37+/-0.25% (>2-fold higher in tail; paired t-test, Fig 2A). Large islets (>50 um) % of islet number: tail 41.9+/-1.3, head 34.0+/-2.2, body 32.4+/-1.3. Isolated islet yield IEQ/g: head 2,747+/-838 vs body-tail 6,422+/-1,582; stimulation index head 2.15+/-0.76 vs body-tail 1.92+/-0.35 (NS; Fig 2D). PP-cell-rich region was confined to the uncinate process (~100% PP) and excluded; cellular composition and architecture otherwise similar across regions. In T2D, preferential beta-cell loss in the head (head 0.73+/-0.08%, body 0.97, tail 2.24; Fig 3).
ANAT-005.effect: Tail islet density ~2x head/body; per-gram islet yield ~2.3x from body-tail
ANAT-005.limitations: Small T2D group; islet function tested only ex vivo; PP-rich region excluded from quantification
ANAT-005.interpretation: Descriptive anatomy; supports inference that head/uncinate resection removes a disproportionately small share of beta-cell mass but the PP-cell compartment

glosses.what-is-pdac: A study of donor human pancreases showing islet density is about twice as high in the tail as in the head or body.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Study of donor pancreata showing islets are about twice as dense in the tail as in the head or body and that pancreatic polypeptide cells cluster in the uncinate process.
glosses.pancreas-head: Study of donor pancreata showing islets are about twice as dense in the tail as in the head or body and that pancreatic polypeptide cells cluster in the uncinate process.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Study of donor pancreata showing islets are about twice as dense in the tail as in the head or body and that pancreatic polypeptide cells cluster in the uncinate process.
glosses.islets: Study of donor pancreata showing islets are about twice as dense in the tail as in the head or body and that pancreatic polypeptide cells cluster in the uncinate process.
glosses.spleen: Study of donor pancreata showing islets are about twice as dense in the tail as in the head or body and that pancreatic polypeptide cells cluster in the uncinate process.

ANAT-006.citation: Kumar AF, Gruessner RW, Seaquist ER. Risk of glucose intolerance and diabetes in hemipancreatectomized donors selected for normal preoperative glucose metabolism. Diabetes Care. 2008;31(8):1639-1643.
ANAT-006.design: Follow-up cohort with oral glucose tolerance testing 3-10 years after distal ~40-50% pancreatectomy
ANAT-006.population: Healthy living hemipancreas donors at University of Minnesota 1997-2003 selected by stringent metabolic criteria (Table 1)
ANAT-006.finding: 7/13 tested donors (54%) had abnormal glucose metabolism (2 IFG, 1 IGT, 3 both, 1 diabetes); 2 further donors on oral agents; thus >=9/21 (43%) abnormal even if all 6 lost to follow-up were normal (Fig 1). Fasting glucose 83+/-5 -> 100+/-14 mg/dl (p<0.01); 2-h glucose 77+/-17 -> 155+/-62 (p<0.05); A1C 5.1+/-0.4 -> 5.9+/-0.4% (p<0.01); fasting insulin unchanged 4.8 -> 5.5 uU/ml (Table 2). Prior series (Kendall 1990, cited) 25% abnormal at 1 year.
ANAT-006.effect: Roughly 40-55% of healthy adults develop IFG/IGT/diabetes within a decade of losing ~half the gland
ANAT-006.limitations: Small n; 6/21 lost; no pre-operative OGTT for some; no beta-cell mass measurement
ANAT-006.interpretation: Interventional (surgical) in healthy humans: direct evidence that beta-cell mass reduction alone impairs glucose tolerance

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A follow-up of healthy living pancreas donors found 40-55% developed impaired glucose handling within a decade of losing half the gland.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Follow-up of healthy living donors who gave half their pancreas, 40–55% of whom developed impaired glucose handling or diabetes within a decade.
glosses.islets: Follow-up of healthy living donors who gave half their pancreas, 40–55% of whom developed impaired glucose handling or diabetes within a decade.

ANAT-007.citation: Stauffer JA, Bridges MD, Turan N, Nguyen JH, Martin JK. Aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy and pancreaticoduodenectomy: recognition, prevalence and management. HPB (Oxford). 2009;11(2):161-165.
ANAT-007.design: Retrospective case series with blinded radiologist re-review of preoperative CT/MRI
ANAT-007.population: Consecutive pancreaticoduodenectomies at Mayo Clinic Jacksonville, Feb 2003-Jun 2007
ANAT-007.n: 191 pancreaticoduodenectomies; 31 with aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy
ANAT-007.finding: Aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 31/191 (16.2%): replaced RHA from SMA 23 (12.0%), accessory RHA from SMA 5 (2.6%), accessory RHA from GDA 1 (0.5%), replaced CHA from SMA 1 (0.5%), replaced CHA from aorta 1 (0.5%) (Table 2). Typical course (28/31): from SMA, lateral/posterior to the portal vein in the hepatoduodenal ligament, passing under the pancreatic head and bile duct. Management: preserved 24, transected+reconstructed 4, primary anastomosis 3; tumour involvement of the aberrant artery in 3; no hepatic infarction or biliary fistula; one pseudoaneurysm. Preoperative reports mentioned the variant in 9/26; blinded re-review identified it in 24/25.
ANAT-007.limitations: Retrospective; no oncologic outcome by variant; radiology re-review not fully blinded to purpose
ANAT-007.interpretation: Descriptive surgical anatomy; shows that variant arteries traverse the retropancreatic/uncinate plane where head tumours sit

glosses.what-is-pdac: A surgical series of 191 Whipple operations finding a variant right hepatic artery in 16% of patients.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Consecutive series of 191 Whipple operations finding aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 16%, most often a replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery.
glosses.pancreas-head: Consecutive series of 191 Whipple operations finding aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 16%, most often a replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery.
glosses.bile-duct-ampulla: Consecutive series of 191 Whipple operations finding aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 16%, most often a replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery.
glosses.liver: Consecutive series of 191 Whipple operations finding aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 16%, most often a replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery.
glosses.sma: Consecutive series of 191 Whipple operations finding aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 16%, most often a replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery.
glosses.celiac-hepatic-arteries: Consecutive series of 191 Whipple operations finding aberrant right hepatic arterial anatomy in 16%, most often a replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric artery.
glosses.ct-scan: A surgical series finding a variant right hepatic artery behind the pancreatic head in 16% of patients, often missed in the original CT report.
glosses.vessel-contact: A surgical series finding a variant right hepatic artery behind the pancreatic head in 16% of patients.

ANAT-008.citation: Halfdanarson TR, Rabe KG, Rubin J, Petersen GM. Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs): incidence, prognosis and recent trend toward improved survival. Ann Oncol. 2008;19(10):1727-1733.
ANAT-008.design: Population-based registry cohort; Kaplan-Meier and Cox models
ANAT-008.population: SEER registries 1973-2000, adults with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (benign insulinomas excluded)
ANAT-008.finding: Crude incidence 2.2 per million/year (1.8 F, 2.6 M), rising over time; 90.8% nonfunctional. Stage: localized 11.1%, regional 20.7%, metastatic 60.2%. Median OS 28 months overall; localized 100 months, regional 69, metastatic 17; 5-year OS 32.8% overall (Table 3). Functional vs nonfunctional median OS 54 vs 26 months (adjusted HR 0.71, p=0.004); grade 3/4 median 7.5 months (HR 2.28); age 71-95 HR 2.92 (Table 4). Survival improved across eras without stage migration (Table 5).
ANAT-008.effect: Median OS 28 months for PNET versus ~4-6 months for all-stage PDAC in contemporaneous SEER (cross-reference ANAT-030)
ANAT-008.limitations: No central pathology; functional status inferred from codes; pre-2000 data
ANAT-008.interpretation: Descriptive epidemiology; establishes that a pancreatic 'cancer' label covers biologically distinct diseases

glosses.what-is-pdac: A US population registry analysis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors showing a median survival of 28 months across all stages.
glosses.pdac-vs-other: A US population registry analysis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors showing a median survival of 28 months across all stages.
glosses.pancreas-overview: US registry analysis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors showing their rarity and a median survival of 28 months across all stages.

ANAT-009.citation: Ishiguro H, Steward MC, Naruse S, Ko SB, Goto H, Case RM, Kondo T, Yamamoto A. CFTR functions as a bicarbonate channel in pancreatic duct cells. J Gen Physiol. 2009;133(3):315-326.
ANAT-009.design: Ex vivo microperfusion with intracellular pH recording while clamping membrane potential by bath K+; pharmacological CFTR blockade; genetic CF model
ANAT-009.population: Isolated interlobular ducts from guinea pig pancreas; ducts from wild-type and CFTR deltaF508 mice
ANAT-009.n: n=4-6 ducts per condition; permeability estimates from 36 flux measurements (5 experiments)
ANAT-009.finding: Depolarization (5->70 mM K+) raised pHi only 0.10+/-0.02 in unstimulated ducts but accelerated markedly with dbcAMP; hyperpolarization lowered pHi 6.83 -> 6.72 (p<0.05) and depolarization raised it to 7.32 (p<0.01), i.e., HCO3- moves across the apical membrane down its electrochemical gradient. Fluxes independent of luminal Cl- and Na+ (excluding electrogenic Cl-/HCO3- exchange and Na+-HCO3- cotransport). CFTRinh-172 reduced the rate of pHi rise from 0.158+/-0.030 pH/min by 61+/-7% (n=6); fluxes absent in deltaF508 mouse ducts. Estimated apical HCO3- permeability 0.102+/-0.013 um/s, sufficient to account for observed secretion rates with 140 mM luminal HCO3- (Fig 6). Introduction notes human pancreas secretes ~2.5 L/day with HCO3- up to 140 mM at maximal stimulation.
ANAT-009.effect: 61% inhibition of apical HCO3- flux by CFTR blocker; complete loss in CF model
ANAT-009.limitations: Animal ducts; indirect flux estimation from pHi; small n
ANAT-009.interpretation: Perturbation (pharmacological + genetic) in a preparation: establishes CFTR as the apical bicarbonate exit path during stimulated secretion

glosses.what-is-pdac: An experimental study in isolated animal pancreatic ducts showing that CFTR acts as the bicarbonate channel of duct cells.
glosses.digestion-enzymes: A physiology study showing that pancreatic duct cells secrete bicarbonate through the CFTR channel.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Experiments in isolated animal pancreatic ducts showing that the CFTR channel itself conducts bicarbonate across the duct cell's apical membrane.
glosses.duct-cells: Experiments in isolated animal pancreatic ducts showing that the CFTR channel itself conducts bicarbonate across the duct cell's apical membrane.

ANAT-010.citation: Stapley S, Peters TJ, Neal RD, Rose PW, Walter FM, Hamilton W. The risk of pancreatic cancer in symptomatic patients in primary care: a large case-control study using electronic records. Br J Cancer. 2012;106(12):1940-1944.
ANAT-010.design: Matched case-control (year of birth, sex, practice); conditional logistic regression; Bayesian PPVs
ANAT-010.population: UK General Practice Research Database, patients >=40 with pancreatic cancer 2000-2009 and matched controls
ANAT-010.finding: Frequencies cases vs controls: abdominal pain 42.4% vs 6.1%; jaundice 30.5% vs 0.1% (LR 503); weight loss 9.7% vs 0.6%; back pain 12.4% vs 6.1%; nausea/vomiting 16.2% vs 2.5%; new-onset diabetes 22.1% vs 7.3%; abnormal liver function 50.5% vs 9.2% (Table 2). Multivariable OR: jaundice 1000 (430-2500); weight loss 15 (11-22); abdominal pain 5 (4.4-5.6); nausea/vomiting 4.5; constipation 2.2; malaise 2.4; diarrhoea 1.9; back pain 1.4 (1.1-1.7); diabetes 2.1 (1.7-2.5) (Table 3). PPV for age >=60: jaundice 22% (14-52); all other single symptoms <1%; cases consulted median 18 vs 9 times in the prior year.
ANAT-010.effect: Jaundice PPV 22%; back pain OR only 1.4
ANAT-010.limitations: No histology or stage; symptoms recorded by GPs only
ANAT-010.interpretation: Observational association; quantifies how anatomy-driven signs (jaundice) versus non-specific symptoms translate into diagnostic probability

glosses.jaundice: A large UK primary-care case-control study measured how strongly each recorded symptom predicted a later pancreatic cancer diagnosis; jaundice was by far the strongest.
glosses.pain: A large UK primary-care case-control study found back pain only weakly predicted pancreatic cancer while jaundice predicted it strongly.
glosses.obstruction-warning: A large UK primary-care case-control study found jaundice was the symptom most specific for pancreatic cancer.
glosses.pancreas-overview: UK primary-care case-control study of 3,635 pancreatic cancer patients quantifying how strongly each symptom predicts the diagnosis.
glosses.pancreas-head: UK primary-care case-control study of 3,635 pancreatic cancer patients quantifying how strongly each symptom predicts the diagnosis.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: UK primary-care case-control study of 3,635 pancreatic cancer patients quantifying how strongly each symptom predicts the diagnosis.
glosses.bile-duct-ampulla: UK primary-care case-control study of 3,635 pancreatic cancer patients quantifying how strongly each symptom predicts the diagnosis.
glosses.liver: UK primary-care case-control study of 3,635 pancreatic cancer patients quantifying how strongly each symptom predicts the diagnosis.
glosses.nerve-plexus: UK primary-care case-control study of 3,635 pancreatic cancer patients quantifying how strongly each symptom predicts the diagnosis.

ANAT-030.citation: Artinyan A, Soriano PA, Prendergast C, Low T, Ellenhorn JD, Kim J. The anatomic location of pancreatic cancer is a prognostic factor for survival. HPB (Oxford). 2008;10(5):371-376.
ANAT-030.design: Population-based registry cohort; Cox regression in resected non-metastatic subset
ANAT-030.finding: Body/tail vs head: metastatic at diagnosis 67% vs 36% (p<0.001); cancer-directed surgery 16% vs 30% (p<0.001); median survival 4 vs 6 months (p<0.001) (Table I, Fig 1). Resected: body/tail older (66.7 vs 65.1 y), fewer harvested nodes (7.7 vs 9.7), less node-positive (49.5% vs 59.9%), fewer T3/4 (69.8% vs 77.2%) (Table II). Multivariable HR body/tail 1.11 (1.00-1.23, p=0.05), lost when harvested node count added (Table V).
ANAT-030.limitations: 26% unknown/overlapping location; no margin or chemotherapy data
ANAT-030.interpretation: Population association; consistent with absence of early obstructive signs in body/tail tumours

glosses.pancreas-overview: US SEER registry of 33,752 pancreatic cancers showing body/tail tumors were more often metastatic and less often resected than head tumors.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: US SEER registry of 33,752 pancreatic cancers showing body/tail tumors were more often metastatic and less often resected than head tumors.
glosses.lymph-nodes: US SEER registry of 33,752 pancreatic cancers showing body/tail tumors were more often metastatic and less often resected than head tumors.

ANAT-011.citation: Stopczynski RE, Normolle DP, Hartman DJ, Ying H, DeBerry JJ, Bielefeldt K, Rhim AD, DePinho RA, Albers KM, Davis BM. Neuroplastic changes occur early in the development of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Res. 2014;74(6):1718-1727.
ANAT-011.design: Time-course (3-4, 6-8, 10-12, >16 weeks) histology, nerve-fibre tracing, qRT-PCR of pancreas and T9-12 dorsal root ganglia, open-field behaviour
ANAT-011.population: KPC mice (p48-Cre; LSL-KrasG12D; p53 lox) +/- tdTomato lineage label, with littermate controls
ANAT-011.n: n=4 per group for fibre quantification; behaviour cohorts 7-31 weeks
ANAT-011.finding: Focal hyperinnervation at 6-8 weeks restricted to PanIN/fibrosis areas; multifocal at 10-12 weeks. PGP9.5 fibres: total 570.5+/-151.4 (10-12 wk) and 585.3+/-118.6 (>16 wk) vs 348+/-52.4 controls (p=0.032, 0.011); density 3.83 and 3.94 vs 2.28 fibres/mm2 (p=0.03, 0.0086); fibre length 54.7 and 45.6 vs 33.4 um (p=0.0037, 0.018). Pancreatic neurotrophin mRNA: Gfr-alpha2 3.74x at 6-8 wk (p=0.008); at 10-12 wk Ngf 2.25x, Trkb 2.18x, Nrtn 1.39x, Gfr-alpha2 3.42x; >16 wk Ngf 3.6x, Trka 29.9x, Gdnf 7.1x (Fig 6). DRG: Cgrp 1.36x at 10-12 wk (p=0.043), Trpa1 1.74x and Trpv1 1.36x at >16 wk (p=0.013, 0.043) (Table 1). Vertical exploratory activity declined over time in KPC but not controls (time p=0.0006); hunching first at mean 10 weeks (PanIN stage). Lineage-labelled tumour cells found inside celiac ganglion and T10/T11 DRG in advanced mice.
ANAT-011.effect: ~1.7x nerve-fibre density and NGF 2.25x already at the PanIN stage
ANAT-011.limitations: Small n; no analgesic reversal; intrapancreatic PNI not definitively observed
ANAT-011.interpretation: Temporal ordering in a model: neural remodelling precedes invasive cancer; supports early, inflammation/neurotrophin-driven sensitisation rather than invasion-only pain

glosses.pain: A mouse study showed nerve density and nerve growth factor were already raised at the precancerous stage.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Mouse study showing nerve density and nerve growth factor rise in the pancreas at the precancerous PanIN stage.
glosses.nerves-in-tumor: A mouse time-course study showing nerve fiber density and nerve growth factor rise at the precursor stage, before invasive cancer, with normal-pancreas fiber counts for comparison.

ANAT-012.citation: Demir IE, Kujundzic K, Pfitzinger PL, Saricaoglu OC, Teller S, Kehl T, Reyes CM, Ertl LS, Miao Z, Schall TJ, Tieftrunk E, Haller B, Diakopoulos KN, Kurkowski MU, Lesina M, Kruger A, Algul H, Friess H, Ceyhan GO. Early pancreatic cancer lesions suppress pain through CXCL12-mediated chemoattraction of Schwann cells. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2017;114(1):E85-E94.
ANAT-012.design: Immunohistochemistry, 3D migration assays, conditional genetics, abdominal von Frey mechanosensitivity, spinal glia immunolabelling, pain-gene array
ANAT-012.population: Human PDAC (n=25, UICC III head tumours) and normal pancreas (n=12); human Schwann cells; KC mice with pancreas-specific CXCL12 reduction (KC12 lox/+); glia-specific CXCR4/CXCR7 knockouts
ANAT-012.n: 25 PDAC/12 NP patients; pain correlation n=10 pain vs n=11 no pain; mice KC n=3 vs KC12 n=4 for pain
ANAT-012.finding: CXCL12 IHC score PDAC 3.7+/-3.4 vs normal 0.46+/-0.46; all 8 PDAC lines secrete CXCL12 (207.5+/-12.2 pg/mL). Schwann-cell coverage of PanINs: KC 75.9+/-10.3% vs KC12 11.9+/-9.9% (GFAP/S100; 423 vs 289 PanINs; Fig 5D). Abdominal hypersensitivity score: KC 4.6+/-2.8 vs KC12 8.6+/-3.4 vs wild-type 8.4+/-2.9, i.e., KC mice are hypoalgesic and CXCL12 loss restores normal sensitivity (Fig 6A). Dorsal-horn activated astrocytes 42.3+/-7.4% (KC) vs 69.2+/-20.5% (KC12); microglia 4.3+/-1.8% vs 15.1+/-13.4% (Fig 6C). Patients: neural CXCR7 immunoreactivity 0.4+/-0.5 (no pain) vs 0.06+/-0.2 (pain); neural CXCR4 0.5+/-0.9 vs 0.02+/-0.004; fewer Schwann cells in nerves of painful patients (Fig S6). CXCL12 down-regulated 11/17 pain genes in Schwann cells (TACR1 -12.2x, P2RX3 -9.4x, GRM1 -8x, CALCA -5.1x).
ANAT-012.effect: Pain-like sensitivity nearly halved in KC vs CXCL12-deficient KC mice
ANAT-012.limitations: n=3-4 mice for pain; only stage III head tumours; cross-sectional human data
ANAT-012.interpretation: Genetic perturbation with behavioural readout plus human correlation: supports an active analgesic programme in early lesions

glosses.pain: A mouse study found early precursor lesions recruit Schwann cells through CXCL12 that reduce pain sensitivity.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Mouse and human study showing early pancreatic lesions recruit Schwann cells through CXCL12 that suppress pain sensitivity.
glosses.nerves-in-tumor: A mouse and human study showing precursor lesions secrete CXCL12 and recruit Schwann cells that coat them, with coverage falling from 75.9 to 11.9 percent when the signal was reduced.

ANAT-013.citation: Chatterjee D, Katz MH, Rashid A, Wang H, Iuga AC, Varadhachary GR, Wolff RA, Lee JE, Pisters PW, Crane CH, Gomez HF, Abbruzzese JL, Fleming JB, Wang H. Perineural and intraneural invasion in posttherapy pancreaticoduodenectomy specimens predicts poor prognosis in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Am J Surg Pathol. 2012;36(3):409-417.
ANAT-013.design: Retrospective histopathological review (mean 14 slides/case) with survival analysis
ANAT-013.population: MD Anderson pancreaticoduodenectomy specimens 1999-2007: 212 after neoadjuvant chemoradiation and 60 untreated
ANAT-013.finding: PNI in 80% (48/60) untreated vs 58% (123/212) treated specimens (p=0.002); literature range cited 70.8-93%. Among 123 PNI+ treated cases: extra-tumoral 69.9%, intra-tumoral 30.1%, intra-pancreatic only 8.9%, extra-pancreatic 91.1%, intraneural 28.5%; involved nerve diameter median 0.8 mm (0.1-4.0). Nerve >0.8 mm associated with positive margin 25.9% vs 6.2% (p=0.005). Treated group: median DFS 11.0 vs 22.0 months (p=0.002), OS 28.5 vs 56.1 months (p=0.0002) for PNI+ vs PNI-; intraneural invasion recurrence 94.3% vs 71.6% (p<0.01); PNI independent predictor of DFS and OS. Untreated: node metastasis 83% with PNI vs 42% without (p=0.006); local recurrence 31% vs 0% (p=0.03).
ANAT-013.effect: PNI in 80% of untreated resections; OS halved with PNI after neoadjuvant therapy
ANAT-013.limitations: Single centre; neoadjuvant-treated majority; no pain data
ANAT-013.interpretation: Observational pathology-outcome link; establishes nerves as the dominant extra-pancreatic spread route and the anatomical basis of positive retroperitoneal margins

glosses.what-is-pdac: A surgical pathology series finding perineural invasion in 80% of untreated resected pancreatic cancers.
glosses.pain: A US pathology study found cancer growing along nerves in 80% of untreated resected tumors, mostly in nerves outside the pancreas.
glosses.pancreas-head: Review of 272 Whipple specimens showing perineural invasion in 80% of untreated tumors, mostly in nerves outside the pancreas, with halved survival when present.
glosses.sma: Review of 272 Whipple specimens showing perineural invasion in 80% of untreated tumors, mostly in nerves outside the pancreas, with halved survival when present.
glosses.lymph-nodes: Review of 272 Whipple specimens showing perineural invasion in 80% of untreated tumors, mostly in nerves outside the pancreas, with halved survival when present.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Review of 272 Whipple specimens showing perineural invasion in 80% of untreated tumors, mostly in nerves outside the pancreas, with halved survival when present.
glosses.nerves-in-tumor: A 272-specimen pathology series finding perineural invasion in 80 percent of untreated resections, mostly outside the pancreas, and linking it to positive margins and shorter survival.

ANAT-014.citation: Aggarwal G, Ramachandran V, Javeed N, Arumugam T, Dutta S, Klee GG, Klee EW, Smyrk TC, Bamlet W, Han JJ, Rumie Vittar NB, de Andrade M, Mukhopadhyay D, Petersen GM, Fernandez-Zapico ME, Logsdon CD, Chari ST. Adrenomedullin is up-regulated in patients with pancreatic cancer and causes insulin resistance in beta cells and mice. Gastroenterology. 2012;143(6):1510-1517.e1.
ANAT-014.design: Microarray discovery, knockdown/overexpression, glucose tolerance tests, tissue expression, matched plasma case-control
ANAT-014.population: INS1 beta cells, mouse islets, athymic mice with MPanc96 xenografts, human PaC tissue (30 IHC; 121 qRT-PCR samples from 75 patients), plasma from 61 PaC and 55 non-cancer subjects
ANAT-014.n: See population; plasma groups n=27-31 each
ANAT-014.finding: PaC-conditioned media reduced INS1 glucose-stimulated insulin secretion ~30% (p=0.02). AM 1 and 20 pmol/L reduced INS1 secretion to 55%/52% (p=0.02) and mouse islet secretion to 41.6%/4.3% (p=0.009) (Fig 2). AM shRNA in PANC1 relieved inhibition (INS1 174% vs 100%, p=0.04; islets 146%, p=0.0002). Xenograft mice glucose-intolerant at 4 weeks (p<0.05); AM-overexpressing, size-matched orthotopic tumours worsened intolerance (p<0.05) (Fig 3). Tissue AM copy number: PaC 1550+/-1897 vs benign 190+/-231, CP 450+/-524, IPMN 502, PanIN 282 (p<0.0001); PaC with DM 2336 vs without 952 (p=0.01). Plasma AM (fmol/L): PaC-DM 22.9+/-10.7, PaC normal glucose 18.3+/-7.0 (p=0.057), non-cancer new-onset T2DM 14.8+/-10.7, controls 12.9+/-6.6 (p<0.001); AUC 0.77; at 16 fmol/L sensitivity 69%, specificity 81%; similar in stage I/II vs III/IV.
ANAT-014.effect: Islet insulin secretion suppressed to ~4-40% by picomolar AM; plasma AM ~1.5x in PaC-DM vs T2DM
ANAT-014.limitations: No glycemic criteria for mice; AM also raised in renal failure/sepsis; 'insulin resistance' in title but assays measure secretion
ANAT-014.interpretation: Gain/loss-of-function in cells and mice establishes sufficiency of AM to impair insulin secretion; human data correlational

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A laboratory study showed the tumor peptide adrenomedullin suppresses insulin secretion from islet cells.
glosses.islets: Laboratory study showing tumor-derived adrenomedullin suppresses insulin secretion from islet cells.

ANAT-015.citation: Pannala R, Leirness JB, Bamlet WR, Basu A, Petersen GM, Chari ST. Prevalence and clinical profile of pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes mellitus. Gastroenterology. 2008;134(4):981-987.
ANAT-015.design: Prospective case-control with FBG at recruitment; pre/post pancreaticoduodenectomy FBG in resected subset
ANAT-015.population: Mayo Clinic SPORE registry: newly diagnosed histology-confirmed PDAC before treatment and age-matched clinic controls
ANAT-015.n: 512 cases, 933 controls; 105 pancreaticoduodenectomies (41 diabetic with known duration)
ANAT-015.time_frame: Prospective registry; post-op follow-up to 1798 days
ANAT-015.finding: Diabetes (FBG>=126 or treatment) 243/512 (47.4%) vs 67/933 (7.2%), p<0.001; new-onset (<2 y) 74% vs 53% (p=0.002); normal FBG only 14% of cases vs 59%. Multivariable OR 14 (8.7-21.5). Diabetes prevalence NOT associated with tumour location (head 72% vs 66%, p=0.2), stage (I/II 47% vs III/IV 43%, p=0.2) or tumour diameter (33.5 mm in diabetic resected cases vs 32.8 overall). After pancreaticoduodenectomy, new-onset diabetes resolved in 17/30 (57%) vs 0/11 long-standing (p=0.009); FBG 174 -> 110 mg/dl (p<0.001) at median 48 days; 16/30 still non-diabetic at median 237 days; pre- and post-operative weight loss similar (8.8% vs 7.9%) (Fig 2, Table 2).
ANAT-015.effect: Diabetes prevalence 47% vs 7%; 57% resolution after head resection despite removing more gland
ANAT-015.limitations: Referral population; duration self-reported; resection subset small
ANAT-015.interpretation: Natural experiment (resection) plus absence of dose-response with tumour size/location argues against mechanical destruction and for a reversible tumour-dependent mediator

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A Mayo Clinic study of 512 newly diagnosed patients found diabetes in 47% versus 7% of controls, independent of tumor site or stage, resolving in 57% after head resection.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Mayo Clinic study of 512 newly diagnosed patients finding diabetes in 47% and its resolution after head resection in 57% of new-onset cases.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Mayo Clinic study of 512 newly diagnosed patients finding diabetes in 47% and its resolution after head resection in 57% of new-onset cases.
glosses.islets: Mayo Clinic study of 512 newly diagnosed patients finding diabetes in 47% and its resolution after head resection in 57% of new-onset cases.
glosses.diabetes-after-surgery: A Mayo Clinic case-control study in which nearly half of people with pancreatic cancer had diabetes, and new-onset diabetes resolved in 57 percent after removal of a head tumor.

ANAT-016.citation: Sharma A, Smyrk TC, Levy MJ, Topazian MA, Chari ST. Fasting blood glucose levels provide estimate of duration and progression of pancreatic cancer before diagnosis. Gastroenterology. 2018;155(2):490-500.e2.
ANAT-016.design: Retrospective temporal and cross-sectional glycemic profiling; tumour volume as scalene ellipsoid from pathology; pre/post-resection FBG
ANAT-016.population: Cohort A: Olmsted County population-based PDAC 2000-2015 (n=219) with 440 matched controls; Cohort B: Mayo resected PDAC 1976-2017 (n=526) with 1023 controls; Cohort C: 103 resected PDAC with longitudinal FBG
ANAT-016.finding: Cohort A: FBG higher than controls from 36-30 months before diagnosis, crossing 126 mg/dl ~6 months before (Fig 1); unchanged after excluding baseline diabetes (Fig 6A). Cohort B: no FBG difference for tumours <=1.0 cc; relative hyperglycemia first at 1.1-2.0 cc (105 vs 118 mg/dl, p=.02); cohort mean >=126 mg/dl at 4.1-8.0 cc; nodal involvement rises at 2.1-4.0 cc (31% vs 53%, p=.03); CA19-9 >50 at 8.1-16 cc (27% vs 75%, p=.002) (Figs 2-3). Poorly differentiated tumours hyperglycemic at 1.5 cc vs 5.8 cc for well/moderate; FBG 134 vs 118 (p=.01). Cohort C: hyperglycemia precedes diagnosis by 36-24 months for >16 cc, 24-12 for 8-16 cc, 12-0 for <8 cc (Fig 4). Resection resolved hyperglycemia regardless of head vs body/tail location or operation type (Fig 5, Supp Table 6).
ANAT-016.effect: Glycemic signal detectable at ~1-2 cc tumour volume (~4-5 doublings before typical 11.5 cc diagnosis volume); ~30-36 month hyperglycemia-defined preclinical phase
ANAT-016.limitations: Retrospective; ellipsoid volume estimates; 10% of PDAC never hyperglycemic
ANAT-016.interpretation: Dose-response (volume) and reversal after resection across locations strengthen a tumour-derived systemic cause; still observational

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A Mayo Clinic analysis showed fasting glucose rising from 36 months before diagnosis and detectable when tumors were only 1-2 cubic centimeters.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Reconstruction of fasting glucose in the years before diagnosis showing hyperglycemia begins 30–36 months early, when tumors are only 1–2 cm3.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Reconstruction of fasting glucose in the years before diagnosis showing hyperglycemia begins 30–36 months early, when tumors are only 1–2 cm3.
glosses.islets: Reconstruction of fasting glucose in the years before diagnosis showing hyperglycemia begins 30–36 months early, when tumors are only 1–2 cm3.

ANAT-017.citation: Hart PA, Kudva YC, Yadav D, Andersen DK, Li Y, Toledo FGS, Wang F, Bellin MD, Bradley D, Brand RE, Cusi K, Fisher W, Mather K, Park WG, Saeed Z, Considine RV, Graham SC, Rinaudo JA, Serrano J, Goodarzi MO. A reduced pancreatic polypeptide response is associated with new-onset pancreatogenic diabetes versus type 2 diabetes. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2023;108(5):e120-e128.
ANAT-017.design: Prospective cross-sectional standardized mixed-meal tolerance test with central PP assay; rank-sum and ANCOVA adjusted for age, sex, BMI
ANAT-017.population: DETECT study (CPDPC consortium, 9 US centres, 2018-2021): new-onset (<3 y) diabetes with PDAC (n=28; 22 proximal/6 distal tumours; 68% stage I/II; median size 3.5 cm), chronic pancreatitis (n=38), or type 2 diabetes (n=99)
ANAT-017.finding: Fasting PP median: PDAC-DM 45.3 pg/mL (24.6-110.8), CP-DM 23.9, T2DM 88.8 (52.0-141.0); p=0.01 and <0.01, adjusted p=0.00012 and <0.0001 (Fig 1). 15-min fold change: PDAC-DM 1.869 vs T2DM 3.283 (p=0.00058); CP-DM 1.813 (Fig 3). AUC of PP lower in both groups at all intervals; log-AUC differences persisted after adjustment, but the adjusted fold-change difference for PDAC-DM did not. No correlation of PP response with tumour size. PDAC-DM patients were older (69 vs 60 y), leaner (BMI 27 vs 33) with higher HbA1c (7.1% vs 6.4%).
ANAT-017.effect: Fasting PP about half of T2DM; meal-stimulated rise ~1.9x vs 3.3x
ANAT-017.limitations: Only 28 PDAC; 6 distal tumours; COVID-era under-enrolment; pilot location effect (Hart 2015, abstract-only lead ANAT-042) not formally replicated
ANAT-017.interpretation: Observational discrimination; consistent with loss of ventral-pancreas PP-cell function in head-predominant tumours but not powered for a location subgroup

glosses.pancreas-head: Multicenter US study showing the meal-stimulated pancreatic polypeptide response is blunted in diabetes caused by pancreatic cancer compared with type 2 diabetes.
glosses.islets: Multicenter US study showing the meal-stimulated pancreatic polypeptide response is blunted in diabetes caused by pancreatic cancer compared with type 2 diabetes.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Multicenter US study showing the meal-stimulated pancreatic polypeptide response is blunted in diabetes caused by pancreatic cancer compared with type 2 diabetes.

ANAT-018.citation: Saisho Y, Butler AE, Meier JJ, Monchamp T, Allen-Auerbach M, Rizza RA, Butler PC. Pancreas volumes in humans from birth to age one hundred taking into account sex, obesity, and presence of type-2 diabetes. Clin Anat. 2007;20(8):933-942.
ANAT-018.design: Cross-sectional CT volumetry (contour on each slice; parenchyma vs fat by density) with age/BMI regression; histological fat quantification
ANAT-018.population: Patients without pancreatic disease undergoing abdominal CT 2003-2006 (135 children, 1721 non-diabetic adults, 165 type 2 diabetes) plus 47 autopsy pancreata
ANAT-018.finding: Adults 20-60 y plateau: total pancreas 72.4+/-25.8 cm3, parenchyma 44.5+/-16.5 cm3, fat 27.9+/-15.7 cm3 (Table 2); males 85.2 vs females 63.0 cm3 total. Parenchymal maximum in third decade (56.4 cm3 men, 48.3 women), constant to ~60 y, then declines; fat/parenchyma ratio rises after ~50 y. Obesity: total volume 66.2/76.6/87.3 cm3 for lean/overweight/obese (+16%, +32%); parenchyma +7%/+13%; fat +32%/+68%; ~10 cm3 total and 3 cm3 parenchyma per 5 kg/m2 BMI. Childhood volume linear with age (r=0.9). Type 2 diabetes: total and parenchymal volume reduced; fat not further increased.
ANAT-018.effect: Normal adult parenchyma ~45 cm3 (range reflecting SD 16.5)
ANAT-018.limitations: Single centre; no regional (head/body/tail) breakdown; cross-sectional ageing inference

glosses.pancreas-overview: CT study of over 2,000 people without pancreatic disease measuring normal pancreas volume and fat content by age and body weight.

ANAT-019.citation: Makino I, Kitagawa H, Takei R, Kato K, Takada S, Okazaki M, Iwao Y, Nakanuma S, Ohta T, Yagi S. Status of lymph node metastasis and efficacy of lymph node dissection along the superior mesenteric artery in pancreatic head cancer: clinicopathological analysis of patients undergoing pancreatoduodenectomy with circumferential lymph nodes dissection along the superior mesenteric artery. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2026;33(5):397-405.
ANAT-019.design: Pathological mapping of SMA nodes into 5 basins; station-wise metastasis incidence; Sasako efficacy index (incidence x 5-yr OS with metastasis)
ANAT-019.population: Kanazawa University: 22 pancreatic head cancers resected with SMA (2002-2013) for anatomical mapping; 103 pancreatoduodenectomies with circumferential SMA lymphadenectomy (2011-2022; 94% after neoadjuvant therapy)
ANAT-019.finding: SMA nodes classified into basins 14R (dorsal pancreatic artery), 14L (inferior mesenteric vein), 14V (gastrocolic trunk), 14I (inferior pancreatoduodenal artery), 14D (proximal dorsal jejunal vein). In SMA-resected cases any node metastasis 16/22 (73%), SMA nodes 14/22 (64%); basin incidence 14I 45%, 14V 32%, 14D 32%, 14R 27%, 14L 23% (Table 1). In the 103-patient series: node-positive 55%; station #14 (SMA) 34%, #13 (posterior head) 32%, #17 (anterior head) 17%, #8 (common hepatic artery) 11%, #12 (hepatoduodenal ligament) 5%; efficacy index highest for #14 (10.7) and #13 (10.3) (Table 2). Median OS N0/N1/N2 115.9/55.6/24.6 months; #14-N2 14.0 months.
ANAT-019.effect: About one third of resected head cancers have SMA-station nodes involved; posterior head and SMA stations dominate
ANAT-019.limitations: Single Japanese centre; extended dissection not standard elsewhere; efficacy index is a heuristic
ANAT-019.interpretation: Descriptive anatomy of lymphatic spread in resected (selected) patients

glosses.pancreas-overview: Japanese mapping series of lymph node stations around the superior mesenteric artery in 125 resected pancreatic head cancers.
glosses.pancreas-head: Japanese mapping series of lymph node stations around the superior mesenteric artery in 125 resected pancreatic head cancers.
glosses.sma: Japanese mapping series of lymph node stations around the superior mesenteric artery in 125 resected pancreatic head cancers.
glosses.celiac-hepatic-arteries: Japanese mapping series of lymph node stations around the superior mesenteric artery in 125 resected pancreatic head cancers.
glosses.lymph-nodes: Japanese mapping series of lymph node stations around the superior mesenteric artery in 125 resected pancreatic head cancers.
glosses.pathology-report: A Japanese series mapping which lymph node stations head cancers involve and how survival falls with the number of positive nodes.

ANAT-020.citation: Yao L, Amar H, Aroori S. Incidental double duct sign: Should we be worried? Results from a long-term follow-up study. Ann Hepatobiliary Pancreat Surg. 2024;28(1):53-58.
ANAT-020.design: Retrospective cohort with risk stratification (jaundice/abnormal LFT/raised CA19-9)
ANAT-020.population: Patients with double duct sign at a UK HPB unit, 2010-2015, followed >=5 years
ANAT-020.finding: 52/103 (50.5%) malignant overall. Jaundice in 63% of malignant vs 8% non-malignant (p<0.01); abdominal pain 19% vs 59% (p<0.01); abnormal bilirubin/liver enzymes 67% vs 41% (p<0.01); abnormal CA19-9 42% vs 6% (p<0.01) (Table 3). Incidental double duct sign (no jaundice, normal LFT, normal/absent CA19-9) 20/103: 0 head/periampullary cancers in median 7.3 y (6-11); 2 chronic pancreatitis; 18 no cause. Single-positive 19: 2 (11%) periampullary cancers (cholangiocarcinoma, ampullary) at 28 and 51 days, both jaundiced. Literature cited: 58-85% malignancy in double duct sign overall; <=10% benign causes.
ANAT-020.effect: Malignancy ~50% overall, ~0% when incidental with normal biochemistry
ANAT-020.interpretation: Observational; shows the sign is an anatomical consequence of a distal common obstruction whose cause is read from accompanying cholestasis

glosses.jaundice: A single-center follow-up of 103 people with a double-duct sign found half had cancer overall but none of the 20 with normal blood tests did over seven years.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: UK cohort of 103 patients with a double-duct sign followed for at least five years, half of whom had cancer and none of the incidental cases did.
glosses.bile-duct-ampulla: UK cohort of 103 patients with a double-duct sign followed for at least five years, half of whom had cancer and none of the incidental cases did.

ANAT-021.citation: Carnie LE, Shah D, Vaughan K, Kapacee ZA, McCallum L, Abraham M, Backen A, McNamara MG, Hubner RA, Barriuso J, Gillespie L, Lamarca A, Valle JW. Prospective observational study of prevalence, assessment and treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in patients with inoperable pancreatic malignancy (PANcreatic Cancer Dietary Assessment-PanDA). Cancers (Basel). 2023;15(8):2277.
ANAT-021.clinical_status: not applicable (treatment of PEI owned by SUPP)
ANAT-021.design: Prospective observational cohort with dietitian assessment, faecal elastase-1, 13C-mixed triglyceride breath test, nutritional bloods; derivation and validation of a screening panel
ANAT-021.population: Advanced (locally advanced 30%, metastatic 68-72%) pancreatic malignancy at The Christie, Manchester, 2018-2020; 85-88% adenocarcinoma; ~50% head/neck tumours
ANAT-021.finding: PEI prevalence (dietitian-assessed) 66% demographic cohort, 64% diagnostic cohort; symptoms: weight loss 84%, flatus 84%, abdominal discomfort 50%, steatorrhoea 48%; anorexia 74%; 70% required PERT; low vitamin D 44%, vitamin A 18%. Breath test abnormal in 7/19 (36%) and predicted dietitian PEI poorly (AUC 0.4). PEI associated with shorter OS: 5.26 vs 9.46 months (univariable HR 2.05, 1.09-3.83; multivariable HR 2.28, 1.19-4.35). Screening panel (low FE-1 + low mid-upper-arm circumference) AUC 0.86; 78% of validation cohort high-risk, 89.6% of whom had dietitian-confirmed PEI.
ANAT-021.effect: ~2/3 of advanced pancreatic cancer patients have exocrine insufficiency at referral
ANAT-021.limitations: Small cohorts; heterogeneous tumour types; no location-stratified PEI rates reported in accessed text
ANAT-021.interpretation: Prevalence estimate; survival association confounded by cachexia

glosses.weight-loss-cachexia: A UK dietitian-led study found enzyme insufficiency in about two-thirds of people with advanced pancreatic cancer, with weight loss in 84%.
glosses.digestion-enzymes: A UK dietitian-led study found enzyme insufficiency in about two-thirds of people with advanced pancreatic cancer, with weight loss, flatus and vitamin deficiencies.
glosses.nausea-bowel: A UK dietitian-led study found enzyme insufficiency in about two-thirds of people with advanced pancreatic cancer.
glosses.nutrition: A UK dietitian-led study found low vitamin D in 44% and low vitamin A in 18% of people with advanced pancreatic cancer.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Prospective UK study finding exocrine insufficiency in about two-thirds of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Prospective UK study finding exocrine insufficiency in about two-thirds of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer.
glosses.acinar-cells: Prospective UK study finding exocrine insufficiency in about two-thirds of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer.

ANAT-022.citation: Keane MG, Horsfall L, Rait G, Pereira SP. A case-control study comparing the incidence of early symptoms in pancreatic and biliary tract cancer. BMJ Open. 2014;4(11):e005720.
ANAT-022.design: Matched case-control with multivariable logistic regression over 2 years pre-diagnosis; full Read-code review of a 10% PDAC subsample for symptom onset
ANAT-022.population: THIN UK primary care database 2000-2010: PDAC, biliary tract cancer and 6 matched controls each
ANAT-022.n: 2773 PDAC, 848 BTC, 15,395 controls; 296 reviewed in detail
ANAT-022.finding: PDAC patients consulted median 18 (IQR 11-27) times in the prior year. Abdominal pain in 43.9% of PDAC (OR 6.38, 5.81-7.02) vs 11.3% controls. Unique to PDAC vs BTC: back pain OR 1.33 (1.18-1.49), lethargy 1.42 (1.25-1.62), new-onset diabetes 2.46 (2.16-2.80). Onset in the 10% subsample (median days before diagnosis): abdominal pain 44%, 106 d; back pain 30%, 483 d; jaundice 35%, 31 d; pruritus 8%, 114 d; nausea/vomiting 20%, 73 d; dyspepsia 26%, 136 d; change in bowel habit 35%, 188 d; weight loss 10%, 144 d; steatorrhoea 1%, 62 d; DVT/PE 4%, 24 d; 91% symptomatic in prior 2 years (Table 1).
ANAT-022.effect: Back pain precedes diagnosis by a median 16 months; jaundice by 1 month
ANAT-022.limitations: No stage/histology; Read codes only; comparator BTC heterogeneous
ANAT-022.interpretation: Observational timing data; supports the model that duct obstruction produces late, rapid signs while retroperitoneal/systemic symptoms are early but non-specific

glosses.jaundice: A UK primary-care database study timed when symptoms first appeared before diagnosis in pancreatic versus biliary cancer; jaundice came about a month before, back pain about 16 months.
glosses.pain: A UK primary-care database study found back pain began a median 16 months before pancreatic cancer diagnosis, jaundice about one month before.
glosses.pancreas-overview: UK primary-care database study timing the onset of symptoms before pancreatic cancer diagnosis in 2,773 patients.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: UK primary-care database study timing the onset of symptoms before pancreatic cancer diagnosis in 2,773 patients.
glosses.bile-duct-ampulla: UK primary-care database study timing the onset of symptoms before pancreatic cancer diagnosis in 2,773 patients.
glosses.stomach: UK primary-care database study timing the onset of symptoms before pancreatic cancer diagnosis in 2,773 patients.
glosses.nerve-plexus: UK primary-care database study timing the onset of symptoms before pancreatic cancer diagnosis in 2,773 patients.

ANAT-023.citation: Boyd CA, Benarroch-Gampel J, Sheffield KM, Cooksley CD, Riall TS. 415 patients with adenosquamous carcinoma of the pancreas: a population-based analysis of prognosis and survival. J Surg Res. 2012;174(1):12-19.
ANAT-023.design: Registry cohort comparison; Cox regression in locoregional disease
ANAT-023.finding: Adenosquamous less often in head (44.6% vs 53.5%) and more often body/tail (29.2% vs 19.0%), p<0.0001; poorly differentiated 71.4% vs 45.0% (p<0.0001); node-positive 52.8% vs 47.1%; larger (5.7 vs 4.3 cm, p<0.0001); stage distribution similar; 2-year survival 11% in both overall; after resection 29% vs 36% (p<0.0001); resection strongest predictor in locoregional adenosquamous (HR 2.35, 1.47-3.76).
ANAT-023.effect: Body/tail predominance ~1.5x and poor differentiation 1.6x relative to PDAC

glosses.pdac-vs-other: A registry analysis of 415 adenosquamous pancreatic carcinomas showing more poorly differentiated, larger, body-tail tumors with worse resected survival than PDAC.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: US registry comparison of 415 adenosquamous pancreatic carcinomas showing body/tail predominance and poor differentiation.

ANAT-024.citation: Dreyer SB, Jamieson NB, Upstill-Goddard R, Bailey PJ, McKay CJ, Australian Pancreatic Cancer Genome Initiative, Biankin AV, Chang DK. Defining the molecular pathology of pancreatic body and tail adenocarcinoma. Br J Surg. 2018;105(2):e183-e191.
ANAT-024.design: Retrospective correlative analysis; Kaplan-Meier; gene programme/immune signature comparison
ANAT-024.population: APGI resected PDAC: 518 with clinicopathology (head 426, body/tail 92); 421 sequenced; 96 RNA-seq; 266 microarray
ANAT-024.finding: Median disease-specific survival body/tail 12.1 vs head 22.0 months (p=0.001). Body/tail more often stage IV (10% vs 0.2%) and >20 mm (87% vs 78%); node-positive 61% vs 68.5%; perineural invasion present in 324/418 (77.5%) head and 78% body/tail (Table 1). Body/tail co-segregated with the squamous subtype (RNA-seq p=0.033; microarray p<0.001); squamous body/tail tumours median survival 5.2 vs 22.0 months for the rest (p<0.001); microarray set medians 25.0/18.4/15.9/11.5 months for non-squamous head/squamous head/non-squamous body-tail/squamous body-tail (p=0.001). Body/tail enriched for EMT, inflammation, hypoxia, TP63 programmes and low dendritic-cell/type II interferon signatures.
ANAT-024.effect: Resected body/tail survival ~55% of head; squamous body/tail 5.2 months
ANAT-024.interpretation: Observational; supports a biological component to the location effect beyond stage, but cannot separate 'born different' from 'later on the molecular clock'

glosses.pdac-vs-other: A sequenced cohort of 518 resected cancers showing body and tail tumors co-segregate with the squamous molecular subtype and have shorter survival.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Sequenced cohort of 518 resected tumors showing body/tail cancers had shorter survival and were enriched for the squamous subtype.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Sequenced cohort of 518 resected tumors showing body/tail cancers had shorter survival and were enriched for the squamous subtype.

ANAT-025.citation: Javeed N, Sagar G, Dutta SK, Smyrk TC, Lau JS, Bhattacharya S, Truty M, Petersen GM, Kaufman RJ, Chari ST, Mukhopadhyay D. Pancreatic cancer-derived exosomes cause paraneoplastic beta-cell dysfunction. Clin Cancer Res. 2015;21(7):1722-1733.
ANAT-025.design: In vitro vesicle characterisation, uptake imaging, insulin secretion assays with AM receptor antagonist, ER-stress gene expression, apoptosis
ANAT-025.population: Exosomes from 5 PC cell lines and plasma of 20 PC patients (18 peripheral, 2 portal); INS-1 beta cells; human islets
ANAT-025.finding: Predominant vesicles ~100 nm (exosomes) in media and plasma; patient plasma exosomes contained CA19-9 (11/11 tested) and AM (all 20). PC exosomes entered human islets within 48 h and inhibited glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in INS-1 and human islets; exosome-depleted media had no effect; AM22-52 abrogated inhibition (Fig 2); dose-dependent inhibition with patient-plasma exosomes (Fig 2F). Uptake reduced 42.5% by amiloride and 20.5%/59.5% by nystatin 25/50 ug/mL (macropinocytosis and caveolin routes), not by chlorpromazine/nocodazole. AM raised Bip and Chop (modest Xbp-1s), increased proinsulin and Bip-proinsulin coupling, ROS/RNS and annexin-V apoptosis; all reversed by AM22-52.
ANAT-025.effect: Qualitative suppression of insulin secretion reversible by receptor blockade; magnitude in text given graphically
ANAT-025.limitations: No animal transfer; no quantification of islet exposure in vivo
ANAT-025.interpretation: Mechanistic in vitro perturbation with human-derived material; demonstrates a plausible systemic carrier but no in vivo transfer experiment

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A laboratory study showed tumor-derived vesicles carry adrenomedullin into islets and block insulin release.
glosses.islets: Laboratory study showing pancreatic cancer exosomes carry adrenomedullin into islets and suppress insulin secretion.
glosses.smv-portal-vein: Laboratory study showing pancreatic cancer exosomes carry adrenomedullin into islets and suppress insulin secretion.

ANAT-026.citation: Parajuli P, Nguyen TL, Prunier C, Razzaque MS, Xu K, Atfi A. Pancreatic cancer triggers diabetes through TGF-beta-mediated selective depletion of islet beta-cells. Life Sci Alliance. 2020;3(6):e201900573.
ANAT-026.design: Histological quantification of islet cell types and cleaved caspase-3; glucose tolerance and insulin tests at 6 months; genetic and pharmacological (anti-TGF-beta1-3 antibody, 4 months) rescue; lineage tracing
ANAT-026.population: KC (Pdx1-Cre; LSL-KrasG12D) mice; KC with Smad4 (KSC) or TGF-beta receptor II (KTC) deletion; beta-cell-specific KrasG12D (Ins2-CreERT2); HFD-obese and caerulein-pancreatitis mice; human PDAC tissue microarray n=48
ANAT-026.n: n=6 mice per group (n=3 for Smad4KO TGF-beta injection); 48 human cases
ANAT-026.finding: 6-12-month KC mice: 'remnant islets' with central loss of insulin+ cells and preserved peripheral alpha, delta and PP cells; beta-cell number and fraction markedly reduced, alpha/delta/PP unchanged (Figs 1-2). 6-month KC: severe glucose intolerance (2 g/kg) and blunted insulin response (Fig 1B-C). No remnant islets at 1-2 months (pre-PanIN) or with beta-cell-restricted KrasG12D (Fig 3); none in HFD obesity or caerulein pancreatitis despite diabetes. pSmad2 increased in islets of KC mice and in islets within human PDAC vs normal (Fig 4B). TGF-beta1 x3 days induced islet cleaved caspase-3, abolished by pancreatic Smad4 deletion (Fig 4D). Smad4 or TbRII deletion in KC background prevented beta-cell loss/apoptosis without altering alpha cells (Fig 5). Anti-TGF-beta antibody from age 2 months nearly abolished remnant islets without changing PanIN burden (Fig 6A, S7). Human TMA (n=48):…
ANAT-026.effect: Near-complete rescue of beta-cell mass with TGF-beta pathway blockade (quantified graphically)
ANAT-026.limitations: No serum insulin after rescue; TMA quantification limited; conflicts with human data showing hyperinsulinaemia/insulin resistance
ANAT-026.interpretation: Genetic and antibody rescue in vivo: establishes a sufficient and necessary pathway in the mouse for beta-cell loss; human data correlational

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A mouse study found tumor TGF-beta selectively kills insulin-producing beta cells.
glosses.islets: Mouse study showing tumor-associated TGF-beta signaling selectively depletes beta cells, which antibody blockade rescued.

ANAT-027.citation: Danai LV, Babic A, Rosenthal MH, Dennstedt EA, Muir A, Lien EC, Mayers JR, Tai K, Lau AN, Jones-Sali P, Prado CM, Petersen GM, Takahashi N, Sugimoto M, Yeh JJ, Lopez N, Bardeesy N, Fernandez-Del Castillo C, Liss AS, Koong AC, Bui J, Yuan C, Welch MW, Brais LK, Kozak MM, Chang DT, Ligorio M, Kraft P, Wolpin BM, Vander Heiden MG. Altered exocrine function can drive adipose wasting in early pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2018;558(7711):600-604.
ANAT-027.clinical_status: preclinical; enzyme replacement therapy itself is SUPP domain
ANAT-027.design: Mouse tissue-mass kinetics, metabolic cages, fecal lipid/protein/protease assays, pancreatic enzyme-supplemented and pair-fed diets, survival; human CT body composition with Cox models
ANAT-027.population: KP-/-C, KPC and KC mice; syngeneic orthotopic vs subcutaneous PDAC implants; 782 untreated PDAC patients from 5 US centres (687 with pretreatment CT)
ANAT-027.finding: Adipose mass decreased by 6 weeks in KP-/-C mice while pancreas weight unchanged; adipose loss exceeded muscle loss; 15-week KC (pre-invasive) mice also lost adipose and muscle. Same cell number orthotopic but not subcutaneous tumours caused marked adipose wasting (Fig 2c-d); circulating IL-6, TNF-alpha, PTHrP, corticosterone, amylin, IL-1beta etc. unchanged (Ext Fig 2). Early KP-/-C: lower O2 consumption and CO2 production with equal food intake and RER; lower fed insulin and glucose, no insulin-secretion defect, glucagon unchanged. Fecal lipids and protein increased, fecal protease activity decreased; orthotopic tumours raised fecal protein (Fig 3e-h). Pancreatic enzyme-supplemented diet attenuated adipose loss (also when pair-fed) and normalised fed glucose, but shortened survival (Fig 3j-k). Patients: sarcopenia 65% at diagnosis (localized 64%, locally advanced 70%, metastatic 63%,…
ANAT-027.effect: Adipose wasting present pre-invasion; rescued by enzyme replacement; 65% sarcopenia at diagnosis in patients
ANAT-027.limitations: Human exocrine function not measured; mouse models hypoglycaemic unlike hyperglycaemic patients (noted by ANAT-031 authors)
ANAT-027.interpretation: Site-controlled implantation and dietary rescue give strong causal evidence in mice for an exocrine (local) mechanism of fat loss; human data observational

glosses.weight-loss-cachexia: A mouse and human study showed fat wasting begins before invasive cancer, driven by loss of enzyme delivery, and that 65% of 782 patients were sarcopenic at diagnosis.
glosses.acinar-cells: Mouse study showing loss of pancreatic enzyme delivery drives early fat wasting that enzyme replacement reverses.

ANAT-028.citation: Yuan C, Babic A, Khalaf N, Nowak JA, Brais LK, Rubinson DA, Ng K, Aguirre AJ, Pandharipande PV, Fuchs CS, Giovannucci EL, Stampfer MJ, Rosenthal MH, Sander C, Kraft P, Wolpin BM. Diabetes, weight change, and pancreatic cancer risk. JAMA Oncol. 2020;6(10):e202948.
ANAT-028.design: Prospective cohorts with biennial questionnaires; Cox models for diabetes duration and 2-year weight change
ANAT-028.population: Nurses' Health Study (112,818 women) and Health Professionals Follow-up Study (46,207 men)
ANAT-028.time_frame: NHS 1978-2012; HPFS 1988-2012; weight measured median 1 and 3 years before diagnosis
ANAT-028.finding: Age-adjusted HR for pancreatic cancer: recent-onset diabetes 2.97 (2.31-3.82); long-standing 2.16 (1.78-2.60). Weight loss 1-4 lb HR 1.25 (1.03-1.52); 5-8 lb 1.33 (1.06-1.66); >8 lb 1.92 (1.58-2.32). Recent-onset diabetes plus weight loss 1-8 lb: 91 cases/100,000 person-years (HR 3.61, 2.14-6.10); plus >8 lb: 164/100,000 (HR 6.75, 4.55-10.00) vs 16/100,000 with neither. With BMI <25 before loss: 400/100,000; unintentional loss: 334/100,000 person-years.
ANAT-028.effect: ~10-fold absolute incidence for recent diabetes + >8 lb loss; 25-fold with prior healthy weight
ANAT-028.limitations: No tumour location or size; questionnaire-based
ANAT-028.interpretation: Prospective temporal ordering in the general population; consistent with cancer-induced prodrome but cannot separate risk-factor from consequence for long-standing diabetes

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A US cohort study found recent-onset diabetes plus weight loss carried a roughly tenfold higher incidence of pancreatic cancer.

ANAT-029.citation: Chen G, Lu W, Liu M, Ye Q, Xu Y, Zhang Y, Guo X, et al. Tumor-derived GDF15 induces CCN3+ Schwann cells to promote cancer pain in pancreatic cancer. Nat Commun. 2026;17(1):6328.
ANAT-029.clinical_status: preclinical only (GDF15/GFRAL antagonists in trials for cachexia, outside ANAT scope)
ANAT-029.design: Behavioural pain assays (von Frey, hunching, heat latency, locomotion), AAV-mediated CCN3+ Schwann-cell ablation/knockdown, GDF15/GFRAL knockdown, co-culture, metabolic assays, human correlation/ROC
ANAT-029.population: Orthotopic syngeneic K8484 PDAC mice and KPC mice; human PDAC tissue (5-12 patients per assay), public single-cell datasets (GSE212966, GSE278688); 120 PDAC patients with plasma GDF15 and NRS/VAS pain scores
ANAT-029.n: Mouse groups (n given per figure); 120 patients
ANAT-029.finding: Orthotopic PDAC mice developed mechanical allodynia, hunching, heat hyperalgesia and reduced locomotion by weeks 3-5; CCN3+ Schwann cells absent in week 1 (painless) and rose with pain severity. PGP9.5 nerve fibres and S100beta Schwann cells increased in human tumour vs adjacent tissue (n=5-8 each), with TRPV1+/CGRP+ fibres increased; nerve and Schwann-cell counts correlated in mice and patients. CCN3+ subcluster proportion increased in tumour vs adjacent in single-cell data. Ablating or knocking down CCN3+ Schwann cells reduced allodynia, hunching, heat hyperalgesia and restored locomotion. Tumour-cell GDF15 knockdown or Schwann-cell GFRAL knockdown reduced TRPV1/CGRP in co-cultured neurons, NGF/BDNF secretion and pain; Schwann PFKM over-expression restored pain after GDF15 knockdown. Patients: plasma GDF15 higher in the pain group, correlated with NRS and VAS scores, higher with…
ANAT-029.effect: Pain behaviours substantially reduced by CCN3+ Schwann-cell ablation (graphical); human correlation coefficients not fully extractable from accessed text
ANAT-029.limitations: Exact numeric values for several endpoints not retrievable from the accessed XML; single pain-score cross-section
ANAT-029.interpretation: Targeted cell ablation and ligand/receptor knockdown with behavioural readouts: strong causal evidence in mice that a Schwann-cell subset drives established-tumour pain

glosses.pain: A 2026 mouse and human study identified tumor-derived GDF15 driving a pain-promoting Schwann-cell state, with plasma GDF15 tracking pain in 120 patients.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Mouse and patient study identifying a GDF15-driven Schwann-cell population that promotes pancreatic cancer pain.
glosses.nerves-in-tumor: A 2026 study showing tumor-derived GDF15 induces a CCN3-positive Schwann-cell subset, with more nerve fibers and Schwann cells in human tumor than adjacent pancreas.

ANAT-031.citation: Sah RP, Sharma A, Nagpal S, Patlolla SH, Sharma A, Kandlakunta H, Anani V, Angom RS, Kamboj AK, Ahmed N, Mohapatra S, Vivekanandhan S, Philbrick KA, Weston A, Takahashi N, Kirkland J, Javeed N, Matveyenko A, Chari ST, Mukhopadhyay D. Phases of metabolic and soft tissue changes in months preceding a diagnosis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Gastroenterology. 2019;156(6):1742-1752.
ANAT-031.design: Retrospective temporal profiling in 6-12-month windows; serial CT at L2/L3; in vitro and mouse adipose studies
ANAT-031.population: Olmsted County PDAC 2000-2015 (n=219) with 657 matched controls; CT subcohort n=86 (68 weight-stable/losing); exosome-exposed human adipocytes; Kras/p53 mice; 5 PDAC and 4 control SAT biopsies
ANAT-031.finding: Phase 1 (-30 to -18 months): hyperglycemia only. Phase 2 (-18 to -6): fall in total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, body weight and subcutaneous fat with preserved visceral fat and muscle; body temperature rises (weight-losing 37.4 vs 37.1 C, p=0.02). Phase 3 (-6 to 0): all lipids, SAT, VAT and muscle fall while glucose keeps rising (Figs 1-4). Almost all symptoms within last 6 months (Supp Fig 1). UCP1 mRNA >20-fold in SAT of 5/5 PDAC vs 1/4 controls (p=0.047); PDAC exosomes reduced adipocyte triglyceride and induced lipolysis/browning programmes; mouse SAT fibrosis with UCP1.
ANAT-031.effect: Weight loss begins ~18 months and muscle loss ~6 months before diagnosis
ANAT-031.limitations: Retrospective; predominantly white population; small biopsy numbers
ANAT-031.interpretation: Temporal ordering plus mechanistic suggestion (browning); retrospective

glosses.weight-loss-cachexia: A US population study traced the metabolic changes in the three years before diagnosis: first high glucose, then fat loss, then muscle loss.
glosses.fatigue: A US population study found a raised body temperature and fat-tissue browning during the weight-losing phase before diagnosis.

ANAT-032.citation: Lillemoe KD, Cameron JL, Hardacre JM, Sohn TA, Sauter PK, Coleman J, Pitt HA, Yeo CJ. Is prophylactic gastrojejunostomy indicated for unresectable periampullary cancer? A prospective randomized trial. Ann Surg. 1999;230(3):322-328.
ANAT-032.clinical_status: surgical practice question owned by SURG/SUPP
ANAT-032.design: Single-centre randomized trial (prophylactic retrocolic gastrojejunostomy vs none)
ANAT-032.population: Johns Hopkins 1994-1998: 194 patients found unresectable at laparotomy; 107 judged at significant risk of outlet obstruction received gastrojejunostomy; 87 randomized
ANAT-032.finding: Presenting symptoms (randomized groups): obstructive jaundice 70-80%, weight loss 56-57%, nausea/vomiting 7-9%; 95-98% pancreatic primaries; unresectability from vascular invasion 47-57%, liver metastases 34-47%. Late gastric outlet obstruction in 8/43 (19%) without prophylactic bypass vs 0/44 with (p<0.01), at mean 5.1+/-2.3 months (1-16); 7/8 were pancreatic head tumours; additional 7% late nausea/vomiting not needing intervention; mean survival 8.3 months in both arms; morbidity 32% vs 33%.
ANAT-032.effect: 19% late outlet obstruction over ~8 months of survival; 55% (107/194) judged at risk at laparotomy
ANAT-032.limitations: Single centre; pre-chemotherapy era; periampullary (not only PDAC)
ANAT-032.interpretation: Randomized for the surgical question (SURG domain); natural-history arm gives incidence

ANAT-033.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Increased neural density and hypertrophy found only in PCa and CP, associated with GAP-43 over-expression and abdominal pain; pancreatic neuritis most severe in PCa; neural invasion aggressiveness related to neuropathic changes, desmoplasia and pain; severe/enduring pain associated with poor prognosis.

ANAT-034.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Neurolytic celiac plexus block vs opioids alone (denervation experiment supporting the celiac plexus as the pain pathway); results summarised in abstract (pain relief greater with block; no QOL/survival advantage).

ANAT-035.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Intraoperative 50% alcohol splanchnicectomy lowered mean pain scores at 2, 4, 6 months (p<0.05), delayed/prevented onset of pain in those without preoperative pain, reduced existing pain, and improved survival in those with pre-existing pain (p<0.0001).

ANAT-036.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Fasting glucose 4.9 -> 5.4 mmol/L (p<0.003); 2-h glucose 6.5 -> 8.7 (p<0.001); fasting insulin 38.4 -> 33.0 pmol/L; insulin AUC 76,230 -> 52,554 pmol/L/min; 7/28 abnormal glucose tolerance at 1 year.

ANAT-044.citation: Wisnoski NC, Townsend CM Jr, Nealon WH, Freeman JL, Riall TS. 672 patients with acinar cell carcinoma of the pancreas: a population-based comparison to pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Surgery. 2008;144(2):141-148.
ANAT-044.population: SEER 1988-2003: 672 acinar cell carcinoma vs 58,526 adenocarcinoma
ANAT-044.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): ACC younger (56 vs 70 y), 58% distant at diagnosis vs 57%; 5-year survival 42.8% (median 47 months) vs 3.8% (median 4 months); resected 72% vs 16.3%.
ANAT-044.effect: not reported in accessed text beyond abstract
ANAT-044.limitations: Full methods/results not examined; retained as lead, not counted

glosses.pdac-vs-other: A population-based comparison, recorded from its abstract, of 672 acinar cell carcinomas against ductal cancer showing far higher resection rates and longer survival.
glosses.pancreas-overview: Abstract of a US registry comparison showing acinar cell carcinoma affects younger people and has far longer survival than ductal adenocarcinoma.
glosses.acinar-cells: Abstract of a US registry comparison showing acinar cell carcinoma affects younger people and has far longer survival than ductal adenocarcinoma.

ANAT-045.citation: Owyang C, Louie DS, Tatum D. Feedback regulation of pancreatic enzyme secretion. Suppression of cholecystokinin release by trypsin. J Clin Invest. 1986;77(6):2042-2047.
ANAT-045.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Intraduodenal trypsin (>=0.5 g/L) suppressed phenylalanine-, oleate- and meal-stimulated chymotrypsin/lipase output (max 35+/-4% suppression at 1 g/L) and returned plasma CCK (basal 0.9 -> 5.3-7.2 pM after nutrients) to basal: CCK-mediated negative feedback exists in humans.
ANAT-045.effect: not reported in accessed text beyond abstract
ANAT-045.limitations: Full methods/results not examined; retained as lead, not counted

glosses.acinar-cells: Abstract of a human study showing trypsin in the duodenum suppresses cholecystokinin and enzyme secretion by negative feedback.
glosses.duodenum: Abstract of a human study showing trypsin in the duodenum suppresses cholecystokinin and enzyme secretion by negative feedback.

ANAT-046.citation: Beglinger C, Fried M, Whitehouse I, Jansen JB, Lamers CB, Gyr K. Pancreatic enzyme response to a liquid meal and to hormonal stimulation. Correlation with plasma secretin and cholecystokinin levels. J Clin Invest. 1985;75(5):1471-1476.
ANAT-046.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Secretin dose-dependently increased bicarbonate but not trypsin output; caerulein (CCK analogue) increased both; postprandial trypsin 29.1 IU/min (55% of maximal caerulein response; peak 90%); CCK release accounts for postprandial enzyme secretion, secretin does not.
ANAT-046.effect: not reported in accessed text beyond abstract
ANAT-046.limitations: Full methods/results not examined; retained as lead, not counted

glosses.acinar-cells: Abstract of a human study showing secretin drives bicarbonate output while cholecystokinin drives enzyme output after a meal.
glosses.duct-cells: Abstract of a human study showing secretin drives bicarbonate output while cholecystokinin drives enzyme output after a meal.
glosses.duodenum: Abstract of a human study showing secretin drives bicarbonate output while cholecystokinin drives enzyme output after a meal.

ANAT-047.citation: Marino CR, Matovcik LM, Gorelick FS, Cohn JA. Localization of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator in pancreas. J Clin Invest. 1991;88(2):712-716.
ANAT-047.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): CFTR (155-170 kD) localized to the apical domain of centroacinar and intralobular duct cells; no conclusive acinar staining.
ANAT-047.effect: not reported in accessed text beyond abstract
ANAT-047.limitations: Full methods/results not examined; retained as lead, not counted

glosses.acinar-cells: Abstract localizing the CFTR channel to centroacinar and small duct cells in human pancreas.
glosses.duct-cells: Abstract localizing the CFTR channel to centroacinar and small duct cells in human pancreas.

ANAT-048.citation: Seaquist ER, Robertson RP. Effects of hemipancreatectomy on pancreatic alpha and beta cell function in healthy human donors. J Clin Invest. 1992;89(6):1761-1766.
ANAT-048.population: Hemipancreas donors cross-sectional and 8 prospective (15+/-2 months)
ANAT-048.finding: ABSTRACT ONLY (full text not retrievable from this environment; publisher page blocked): Reduced glucose- and arginine-induced insulin and glucagon secretion; maximal acute insulin response 666+/-84 vs 1,772+/-234 pM in controls; fasting glucose/insulin unchanged; glucose disposal maintained.
ANAT-048.effect: not reported in accessed text beyond abstract
ANAT-048.limitations: Full methods/results not examined; retained as lead, not counted

glosses.islets: Abstract showing reduced insulin and glucagon responses in healthy donors after removal of half the pancreas.

ORIG-001.citation: Braxton AM, Kiemen AL, Grahn MP, et al. 3D genomic mapping reveals multifocality of human pancreatic precancers. Nature. 2024;629(8012):679-687.
ORIG-001.design: Quantitative 3D histological reconstruction at single-cell resolution (machine-learning pipeline) with 3D-model-guided multi-region microdissection plus targeted and whole-exome sequencing
ORIG-001.population: Grossly normal human pancreas tissue (46 large samples)
ORIG-001.n: 46 large samples of grossly normal human pancreas
ORIG-001.finding: Abstract reports a mean burden of 13 PanINs per cm3, extrapolating to hundreds of PanINs in the normal intact adult pancreas, 'almost all with oncogenic KRAS hotspot mutations'. Most PanINs originated as independent clones with distinct somatic mutation profiles. Some spatially continuous PanINs contained multiple different KRAS mutations localizing to distinct cell subpopulations, indicating polyclonal origin. Figure/table locations not available from the abstract.
