ORIG-001.limitations: Abstract only in this run — numbers above are the authors' summary statements, not figures/tables I examined. No progression follow-up.
ORIG-001.interpretation: Establishes baseline prevalence and clonal architecture of the putative precursor in people without pancreatic cancer; cross-sectional so it cannot establish progression rates.

glosses.what-is-pdac: A three-dimensional mapping study estimating hundreds of KRAS-mutant precursor lesions in a normal adult pancreas.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Abstract of a 3D mapping study finding hundreds of KRAS-mutant PanIN lesions in ordinary adult pancreata.
glosses.acinar-cells: Abstract of a 3D mapping study finding hundreds of KRAS-mutant PanIN lesions in ordinary adult pancreata.
glosses.duct-cells: Abstract of a 3D mapping study finding hundreds of KRAS-mutant PanIN lesions in ordinary adult pancreata.
glosses.growth-control: A 3D mapping study (abstract only) estimating hundreds of KRAS-mutant precursor lesions in a normal adult pancreas.
glosses.kras: A 3D mapping study (abstract only) estimating hundreds of KRAS-mutant precursor lesions in a normal adult pancreas.
glosses.panin: A 3D mapping study (abstract only) estimating 13 PanINs per cubic centimeter and hundreds per adult pancreas, nearly all KRAS-mutant.

ORIG-002.citation: Kanda M, Matthaei H, Wu J, et al. Presence of somatic mutations in most early-stage pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia. Gastroenterology. 2012;142(4):730-733.e9.
ORIG-002.design: Laser-capture microdissection of graded PanIN lesions followed by ultrasensitive mutation detection (pyrosequencing; plus digital ligation and a second ultrasensitive platform in an independent validation set)
ORIG-002.population: Human PanIN lesions microdissected from resected pancreata
ORIG-002.n: 169 microdissected PanINs (50 PanIN-1A, 52 PanIN-1B, 45 PanIN-2, 22 PanIN-3); independent validation set of 37 further PanINs (11 PanIN-1, 20 PanIN-2, 7 PanIN-3)
ORIG-002.finding: KRAS codon 12 mutations detected in 46/50 (92.0%) PanIN-1A, 48/52 (92.3%) PanIN-1B, 42/45 (93.3%) PanIN-2 and 21/22 (95.4%) PanIN-3 (Supplementary Table 2). Occasional codon 13 and 61 mutations also found. Including KRAS, GNAS, p16/CDKN2A and BRAF, >99% of PanIN-1 lesions carried at least one mutation (Figure 2). p16/CDKN2A mutations were found in only 17/147 (11.5%) PanIN-1/2 lesions but were commoner in KRAS-wild-type than KRAS-mutant PanINs (P=0.0209); a similar trend for GNAS (P=0.088). Critically, in the earliest lesions mutant KRAS was present in only a fraction of the cells comprising the lesion, and the mutant-KRAS cell fraction rose progressively with PanIN grade and into invasive carcinoma (Figure 2, lower panel).
ORIG-002.effect: KRAS codon 12 mutation prevalence 92.0-95.4% across grades; >99% of PanIN-1 with >=1 driver mutation; p16 mutation only 11.5% of PanIN-1/2
ORIG-002.limitations: PanINs came from resected pancreata, most with an associated cancer, so lesions may not represent PanIN in cancer-free pancreata; small numbers at the highest grade (n=22).
ORIG-002.interpretation: Establishes temporal ordering of genetic events within the precursor sequence (KRAS first, near-universal; CDKN2A rare early); mutant-cell-fraction gradient supports a model in which mutant cells recruit/expand among non-mutant neighbours.

glosses.what-is-pdac: A pathology study finding KRAS mutations in 92-95% of precursor lesions at every grade.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Sequencing of 147 PanIN lesions showing KRAS mutations in over 90% of even the lowest-grade lesions.
glosses.acinar-cells: Sequencing of 147 PanIN lesions showing KRAS mutations in over 90% of even the lowest-grade lesions.
glosses.duct-cells: Sequencing of 147 PanIN lesions showing KRAS mutations in over 90% of even the lowest-grade lesions.
glosses.growth-control: A study of 147 precursor lesions finding KRAS mutations in over 90 percent at every grade.
glosses.kras: A study of 147 precursor lesions finding KRAS codon-12 mutations in 92 to 95 percent at every grade.
glosses.cdkn2a: A study of 147 precursor lesions in which p16 point mutations were found in only 11.5 percent of low-grade lesions.
glosses.panin: A study of 147 precursor lesions finding KRAS mutations in 92 to 95 percent at every grade and p16 mutations in only 11.5 percent of low-grade lesions.

ORIG-003.citation: Ferreira RMM, Sancho R, Messal HA, et al. Duct- and acinar-derived pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas show distinct tumor progression and marker expression. Cell Rep. 2017;21(4):966-978.
ORIG-003.design: Cell-type-specific conditional oncogene activation with Rosa26-LSL-YFP lineage tracing: duct-targeted Ck19-CreER (KFCk: Kras-LSL-G12D; Fbw7 F/F) and acinar-targeted Ela1-CreERT2 (KFE, with cerulein-induced pancreatitis); confirmatory KPCk/KPEY models substituting p53 loss; orthotopic allografts of…
ORIG-003.population: Mouse (conditional Cre-ER lineage tracing); plus human PDAC tissue microarrays
ORIG-003.n: >=7 animals per time point for duct time-course (4 sections each); quantifications with n=3 KFE vs n=11 KFCk mice (Fig 3D) and n=3 KFEY vs n=10 KFCk mice (Fig 3F); 4 duct-OA and 3 acinar-OA tumours…
ORIG-003.time_frame: Day 0 to 6 months post-tamoxifen; allografts analysed 20 days post-transplant; chimeras at 4 months
ORIG-003.finding: Duct-targeted KFCk mice developed carcinoma ~2 months after oncogene activation. Time course (Fig 2C-D): no change at day 0; by day 14 ducts hyperplastic with 15% showing luminal cell expansion; by day 21 >20% of ducts with cell expansion and ~4% with dysplasia (tufting, shedding); carcinoma in situ features by 1 month. Mucinous PanIN lesions were NOT detectable at early stages in duct-driven models (also in KPCk, Fig S3B), indicating the PanIN-independent route is due to ductal origin rather than Fbw7 loss. Acinar-targeted KFE mice developed PDAC by 6 months, with low-grade PanIN-like lesions readily identified at 1 month, well before carcinoma (Fig 3C); acinar-derived carcinoma had significantly more such lesions than duct-derived (Fig 3D, Welch's t test). Lineage tracing (Fig 3F): in KFEY most PanIN-like lesions were YFP+/AB-PAS+ (minority untraced), whereas in KFCkY NONE of the…
ORIG-003.effect: Latency ~2 months (duct) vs ~6 months (acinar) to PDAC; 0% of duct-model PanIN-like lesions lineage-traced vs majority traced in acinar model
ORIG-003.limitations: Mouse models with engineered alleles and supraphysiologic recombination; the human arm is marker correlation (AGR2) only — authors state proof of cellular origin in human PDAC is not yet possible. Small n in several quantifications (n=3 per arm).
ORIG-003.interpretation: Cell-type-restricted perturbation with lineage tracing — strong causal inference about which cell of origin produces which lesion sequence, in a mouse preparation. The chimera and YFP-sorted allograft experiments are a clean natural-experiment test that separates 'precursor' from 'bystander'.

glosses.acinar-cells: Mouse study showing duct-derived cancers arise faster and without mucinous PanIN compared with acinar-derived ones.
glosses.duct-cells: Mouse study showing duct-derived cancers arise faster and without mucinous PanIN compared with acinar-derived ones.
glosses.panin: A mouse lineage-tracing study showing an established tumor induces PanIN-like lesions in genetically normal neighboring tissue.
glosses.cell-of-origin: A mouse lineage-tracing study showing duct and acinar cells give rise to pancreatic cancer by distinct routes, plus host-derived bystander lesions.

ORIG-004.citation: Canto MI, Almario JA, Schulick RD, et al. Risk of neoplastic progression in individuals at high risk for pancreatic cancer undergoing long-term surveillance. Gastroenterology. 2018;155(3):740-751.e2.
ORIG-004.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice for high-risk individuals (US); not applicable to average-risk adults
ORIG-004.design: Prospective longitudinal surveillance cohort with multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis
ORIG-004.population: Asymptomatic adults at high risk of PDAC by family history or germline variant (Cancer of the Pancreas Screening, CAPS, cohorts at US tertiary academic centres)
ORIG-004.n: 354 high-risk individuals; 97% familial-PC relatives; 16% with a known deleterious germline variant; mean baseline age 56.4 years (range 22-81, Table 1); 48% male; 94% White
ORIG-004.finding: Over 16 years of the programme, pancreatic lesions with worrisome features or rapid cyst growth (>4 mm/year) were detected in 68/354 (19%). 24/354 (7%) had neoplastic progression — 14 PDAC and 10 high-grade dysplasia — a rate of 1.6% per year; 93% had detectable worrisome-feature lesions before the PDAC/HGD diagnosis. 9 of the 10 PDACs detected during routine surveillance were resectable. 3-year survival was 85% in patients with resectable PDAC vs 25% in the 4 subjects with symptomatic unresectable PDAC that developed outside surveillance (log-rank P<.0001). Neoplastic progression occurred at median age 67; median time from baseline screening to PDAC diagnosis 4.8 years (IQR 1.6-6.9). Progressors were significantly older at baseline than non-progressors (P<.0001; Table 1), and age >60 was associated with progression (P=0.009).
ORIG-004.effect: 7% progression over up to 16 years; 1.6%/year; 3-year survival 85% vs 25%
ORIG-004.limitations: No randomised or external average-risk comparator; small event numbers; predominantly White familial-risk population limits generalisability; 'worrisome features' were defined and acted on by the same expert team.
ORIG-004.interpretation: Prospective cohort; establishes incidence of progression and stage/resectability of surveillance-detected disease. Comparison to out-of-surveillance cases is non-randomised and vulnerable to lead-time and length bias, so it cannot by itself establish mortality benefit.

glosses.hereditary-risk: A 16-year US surveillance cohort with 7 percent neoplastic progression, 1.6 percent per year, and most cancers resectable.

ORIG-005.citation: Overbeek KA, Levink IJM, Koopmann BDM, et al. Long-term yield of pancreatic cancer surveillance in high-risk individuals. Gut. 2022;71(6):1152-1160.
ORIG-005.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice for high-risk individuals (intl/Europe); authors conclude imaging surveillance yields suboptimal results and biomarkers are needed
ORIG-005.design: Prospective surveillance cohort; annual EUS AND MRI/MRCP at every visit; univariable predictor analysis; modality-sensitivity comparison
ORIG-005.population: Asymptomatic individuals with estimated >=10% lifetime PDAC risk after clinical-genetics evaluation and genetic testing (Dutch Familial Pancreatic Cancer surveillance study)
ORIG-005.n: 366 individuals from 214 families; 165 (45%) proven mutation carriers (96 CDKN2A p16, 45 BRCA2 with >=2 affected blood relatives, 7 BRCA1, 9 STK11/LKB1, 5 TP53, 2 PALB2 — Table 1) and 201 (55%)…
ORIG-005.finding: Mean follow-up 63 months (SD 43.2). Ten individuals developed PDAC. Cumulative PDAC incidence was 9.3% in mutation carriers and 0% in mutation-negative FPC kindreds (p<0.001). Four of 10 presented as symptomatic metastasised INTERVAL carcinomas, at 1, 3, 5 and 17 months after the last surveillance visit; at that prior visit one had no visible abnormality and three were presumed to have unchanged multifocal branch-duct IPMN. Resectability was 60% (6/10) overall and 50% (4/8) for incident cases; only 3/10 (30%) were detected at T1N0M0 with R0 resection (2/8, 25%, of incident cases). Median survival 18 months overall (range 1-32), 12 months for the 8 incident cases. Surgery was performed in 17 individuals (overall surgery rate 4.6%) at median age 51; pathology yielded 6 PDAC, 7 low-grade precursor lesions, 2 neuroendocrine tumours <2 cm, 1 autoimmune pancreatitis and 1 with no…
ORIG-005.effect: Cumulative PDAC incidence 9.3% (carriers) vs 0% (FPC kindreds); 30% early-stage detection; 11/17 operations found no cancer; 64% exocrine insufficiency among those
ORIG-005.limitations: Small event numbers (10 PDAC); single-country programme; 'mutation-negative FPC kindred' classification was uncertain in 27% where it could not be retrieved who had been tested and 4% untested; no unscreened comparator.
ORIG-005.interpretation: Prospective cohort with pre-specified dual-modality protocol — strong evidence on achievable yield and on harms; it stratifies risk by genotype, which is causally informative. Not a mortality trial.

glosses.genome-evolution: A Dutch high-risk surveillance cohort in which four of ten cancers appeared as symptomatic interval cancers within months of a reassuring visit.
glosses.panin: A Dutch high-risk surveillance cohort in which 11 of 17 operations found no cancer and 7 found low-grade precursors.
glosses.cysts-ipmn-mcn: A Dutch high-risk surveillance cohort reporting interval cancers in presumed-stable IPMN and exocrine insufficiency after non-cancer resections.
glosses.hereditary-risk: A Dutch high-risk surveillance cohort with lower early-stage yield, interval cancers and non-therapeutic surgery.
glosses.mri: A surveillance cohort of high-risk relatives in which MRI/MRCP found cysts well but solid lesions poorly compared with endoscopic ultrasound.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A surveillance cohort of high-risk relatives in which EUS found solid lesions far better than MRI/MRCP.

ORIG-006.citation: Hu C, Hart SN, Polley EC, et al. Association between inherited germline mutations in cancer predisposition genes and risk of pancreatic cancer. JAMA. 2018;319(23):2401-2409.
ORIG-006.clinical_status: germline testing guideline-recommended for all PDAC patients (US, NCCN since 2018, per this paper's discussion); therapeutic implications owned by GENE domain
ORIG-006.design: Case-control analysis of germline panel sequencing (21 cancer predisposition genes, custom multiplex PCR panel) with logistic regression and multiple-comparison correction; longitudinal survival analysis of cases
ORIG-006.population: Adults with pancreatic cancer in a Mayo Clinic registry; public exome reference controls
ORIG-006.n: 3030 patients with pancreatic cancer (43.2% female; 95.6% non-Hispanic White; mean age at diagnosis 65.3, SD 10.7) vs 123,136 gnomAD and 53,105 ExAC reference controls
ORIG-006.time_frame: Enrolment 12 Oct 2000 to 31 Mar 2016; last follow-up 22 Jun 2017
ORIG-006.finding: Deleterious germline mutations were identified in 249/3030 patients (8.2%; 95% CI 7.26-9.25%) across 19 of the 21 genes (253 mutations). Highest individual-gene prevalences: ATM 2.28% (95% CI 1.78-2.87%; n=69), BRCA2 1.95% (1.49-2.50%), CHEK2 1.09%. Six genes were significantly associated with pancreatic cancer vs gnomAD controls: CDKN2A 0.30% of cases vs 0.02% of controls (OR 12.33; 95% CI 5.43-25.61); TP53 0.20% vs 0.02% (OR 6.70; 2.52-14.95); MLH1 0.13% vs 0.02% (OR 6.66; 1.94-17.53); BRCA2 1.9% vs 0.3% (OR 6.20; 4.62-8.17); ATM 2.3% vs 0.37% (OR 5.71; 4.38-7.33); BRCA1 0.6% vs 0.2% (OR 2.58; 1.54-4.05). In aggregate these 6 genes accounted for 167/3030 (5.5%; 95% CI 4.7-6.4%) of patients — 27/343 (7.9%; 5.3-11.2%) of those WITH a family history of pancreatic cancer and 140/2687 (5.2%; 4.4-6.1%) of those WITHOUT one (Table 4). Only CDKN2A carriers were more likely to have a…
ORIG-006.effect: 8.2% any panel-gene mutation; 5.5% in the 6 associated genes; ORs 2.58-12.33; most carriers (140/167) had NO pancreatic cancer family history
ORIG-006.limitations: 95.6% non-Hispanic White — ancestry generalisability poor; PALB2 and STK11 did not reach significance here, likely a power limitation rather than absence of risk; authors call for replication in other populations.
ORIG-006.interpretation: Case-control with very large external control set gives robust relative-risk estimates for rare variants; germline genotype precedes disease, so confounding by reverse causation is implausible. It gives ORs, not absolute lifetime risks.

glosses.cdkn2a: A 3,030-patient germline study in which CDKN2A carried the highest odds ratio, 12.33, of any gene tested.
glosses.tp53: A 3,030-patient germline study in which inherited TP53 variants were found in 0.20 percent with an odds ratio of 6.70.
glosses.risk-factors: A 3,030-patient germline study finding risk variants in 5.5 percent, most without a family history.
glosses.hereditary-risk: A 3,030-patient germline study finding six associated genes with odds ratios from 2.58 to 12.33, present in 5.5 percent of patients, most without family history.
glosses.atm-noncore: A 3,030-patient germline study in which inherited ATM variants were the commonest risk finding, 2.28 percent, odds ratio 5.71.

ORIG-007.citation: Amundadottir L, Kraft P, Stolzenberg-Solomon RZ, et al. Genome-wide association study identifies variants in the ABO locus associated with susceptibility to pancreatic cancer. Nat Genet. 2009;41(9):986-990.
ORIG-007.clinical_status: not applicable (no clinical test based on this variant); research finding
ORIG-007.design: Two-stage genome-wide association study (558,542 SNPs) with combined analysis adjusted for study, sex, ancestry and five principal components
ORIG-007.population: Adults of European background from twelve prospective cohorts plus one hospital-based case-control study (PanScan), with a 'Fast Track' replication in eight further case-control studies
ORIG-007.n: Stage 1: 1,896 incident cases and 1,939 controls; plus Fast Track replication in 8 case-control studies (4 hospital-based, 4 population-based)
ORIG-007.time_frame: Prospective cohorts with incident case ascertainment; replication case-control studies
ORIG-007.finding: The strongest association was at chromosome 9q34 within the first intron of ABO, marked by rs505922: P=5.37x10^-8 (trend model), heterozygous OR 1.20 (95% CI 1.12-1.28) and a higher homozygous OR. The protective (T) allele of rs505922 is in complete linkage disequilibrium (r2=1.0) with the O allele of the ABO locus, i.e. blood group O is the lower-risk state. Three regions were carried into Fast Track replication (9q34/ABO with rs505922, rs495828, rs657152, rs630014 ranked 2, 3, 8 and 17 in the initial scan; 7q36 including Sonic Hedgehog; and a third region). Authors note ABO intron-1 variation has also been linked to circulating TNF-alpha, soluble ICAM-1 and alkaline phosphatase, but state the direction for TNF-alpha is discordant with their risk direction.
ORIG-007.effect: Per-genotype OR_het 1.20 (95% CI 1.12-1.28) for rs505922; genome-wide significant at P=5.37x10^-8
ORIG-007.limitations: European-ancestry only; effect size small (OR ~1.2), so of no individual predictive value; mechanism linking ABO glycosyltransferase activity to pancreatic carcinogenesis unresolved.
ORIG-007.interpretation: Germline variants are randomised at conception relative to lifestyle, so a GWAS association is largely free of reverse causation and confounding by behaviour — but the causal gene/mechanism within the locus is not established by the association.

glosses.risk-factors: A genome-wide association study showing the ABO blood-group variant shifts risk with an odds ratio near 1.2.

ORIG-008.citation: Arslan AA, Helzlsouer KJ, Kooperberg C, et al. Anthropometric measures, body mass index, and pancreatic cancer: a pooled analysis from the Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Consortium (PanScan). Arch Intern Med. 2010;170(9):791-802.
ORIG-008.clinical_status: not applicable (risk factor); weight management is general preventive advice, not a PDAC-specific intervention
ORIG-008.design: Pooled nested case-control analysis with unconditional logistic regression on cohort-specific quartiles and conventional BMI categories; sequential adjustment models
ORIG-008.population: Adults aged 37-94 in 12 prospective cohorts (ATBC, CLUE II, CPS II, EPIC, HPFS, Mayo, NYUWHS, NHS and others); 86% aged >=60; majority White
ORIG-008.time_frame: Prospective cohorts with baseline anthropometry and incident case ascertainment; follow-up durations vary by cohort
ORIG-008.finding: Adjusted OR for highest vs lowest BMI quartile was 1.33 (95% CI 1.12-1.58; P for trend <0.001) in model 1 (adjusted for cohort, age, sex, BMI source and smoking) — Table 4. Among men the top-vs-bottom quartile OR was 1.33 (1.04-1.69; P trend <0.03); among never-smoking men a significant increasing trend persisted (P trend=0.007) and estimates were higher after excluding current smokers (model 4). Waist-to-hip ratio showed a top-vs-bottom quartile OR of 1.71 and waist circumference 1.23 (0.94-1.62) after additional adjustment for diabetes history and height (model 2). Further adjustment for diabetes history attenuated estimates but trends for BMI quartiles and categories remained statistically significant. BMI distribution: 36% of cases vs 39% of controls normal, 41% vs 39% overweight, 21% of cases obese. Height, weight and BMI were self-reported in ~50% of subjects, measured in 29%,…
ORIG-008.effect: OR 1.33 (1.12-1.58) highest vs lowest BMI quartile; WHR top-vs-bottom OR 1.71
ORIG-008.limitations: Half of anthropometry self-reported; single baseline measurement, no trajectory; mostly older White participants; central-adiposity estimates imprecise (waist CI crosses 1).
ORIG-008.interpretation: Prospective exposure measurement before diagnosis reduces recall bias and limits reverse causation relative to case-control designs; pooling improves precision. Residual confounding by smoking and the mediating role of diabetes remain.

glosses.risk-factors: A pooled cohort analysis giving an odds ratio of 1.33 for the highest versus lowest body-mass-index quartile.

ORIG-009.citation: Chari ST, Leibson CL, Rabe KG, et al. Probability of pancreatic cancer following diabetes: a population-based study. Gastroenterology. 2005;129(2):504-511.
ORIG-009.clinical_status: not a stand-alone screening indication in the US; new-onset diabetes raises risk only modestly per USPSTF 2019 scope
ORIG-009.design: Population-based incidence cohort with observed-to-expected comparison against the Iowa SEER registry, plus a nested case-control analysis of BMI and smoking
ORIG-009.population: Rochester, Minnesota residents aged >=50 first meeting standardized diabetes criteria (Rochester Diabetes Incidence Cohort)
ORIG-009.n: 2,122 subjects with incident diabetes; 18 developed pancreatic cancer; nested case-control 18 cases vs 72 controls
ORIG-009.time_frame: Diabetes incidence 1 Jan 1950 - 31 Dec 1994; cancers ascertained within 3 years of diabetes diagnosis
ORIG-009.finding: 18/2,122 (0.85%) were diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within 3 years of first meeting diabetes criteria; 10 of those 18 (56%) were diagnosed <6 months after meeting criteria, and only 3 were resected. Crude 3-year incidence was 310/100,000 person-years. Observed-to-expected ratio 7.94 (95% CI 4.70-12.55) overall (Table 2), with 5.23 (1.70-12.20) in those <70 years and 9.91 (5.26-16.96) in those >=70; 5.83 (2.14-12.68) in women and 9.69 (5.01-16.92) in men. Within the diabetes cohort, those who developed pancreatic cancer were more likely to have met diabetes criteria at or after age 70 (OR 4.52; 95% CI 1.61-12.74); male sex OR 2.01 (0.75-5.38, NS). Smoking: 12/13 (92.3%) of cases with smoking data were ever-smokers vs 38/55 (69.1%) of controls — OR 5.37 (95% CI 0.65-44.66; P=.16), and 5.84 (0.62-55.43) in conditional logistic regression, i.e. imprecise and not significant. BMI did not…
ORIG-009.effect: ~1% 3-year pancreatic cancer risk after new-onset diabetes at age >=50; O/E 7.94 (4.70-12.55)
ORIG-009.limitations: Only 18 events; smoking data missing in ~26%; historical cohort (1950-1994) with older diabetes criteria and imaging; single predominantly White community; the authors explicitly state the usefulness of new-onset diabetes as an early marker 'needs further evaluation'.
ORIG-009.interpretation: Population-based denominators with complete record linkage give an unbiased absolute risk estimate for a defined clinical state. The 56% of cancers diagnosed within 6 months argues the diabetes is largely a CONSEQUENCE (paraneoplastic) rather than a cause — a direction-of-causation inference the design supports.

glosses.glucose-diabetes: A Minnesota population study found about 1% of people developing diabetes after 50 were diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within three years, most within six months.
glosses.islets: Minnesota population study showing about 1% of people with new diabetes after age 50 were diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within three years.
glosses.risk-factors: A population study in which about 1 percent of people over 50 with new-onset diabetes were diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within three years, over half within six months.

ORIG-010.citation: Bosetti C, Lucenteforte E, Silverman DT, et al. Cigarette smoking and pancreatic cancer: an analysis from the International Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium (Panc4). Ann Oncol. 2012;23(7):1880-1888.
ORIG-010.clinical_status: not applicable (risk factor); smoking cessation is established preventive practice (US)
ORIG-010.design: Pooled analysis of individual-level data; study-specific ORs combined with random-effects models; stratified analyses and cumulative meta-analysis
ORIG-010.population: Adults in 12 case-control studies within PanC4 (in-person interviews except the Ontario study)
ORIG-010.n: 6,507 cases of exocrine pancreatic adenocarcinoma and 12,890 controls
ORIG-010.time_frame: 12 case-control studies spanning roughly 1994-2010 publication era
ORIG-010.finding: Compared with never smokers, pooled ORs (Table 3) were 1.40 (95% CI 1.24-1.55) for ever cigarette smokers, 1.17 (1.02-1.34) for former smokers and 2.20 (1.71-2.83) for current smokers, with a significant trend by intensity (OR 3.4 for >=35 cigarettes/day; P for trend <0.0001) and increasing risk with duration up to 40 years. Study-specific ORs for ever-smoking showed significant heterogeneity (Figure 2). A cumulative meta-analysis (Figure 1) showed the current-vs-never OR rising with publication era: 1.74 in the initial 1994 study, 1.75 through 2007, and 2.2 once 2007-2010 studies were added. Cases were older than controls and more often non-Hispanic White, more educated, with higher BMI and more frequent history of diabetes and pancreatitis (Table 2), and study-specific ORs were adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education and BMI.
ORIG-010.effect: Current smokers OR 2.20 (1.71-2.83); >=35 cigarettes/day OR 3.4; former smokers OR 1.17 (1.02-1.34)
ORIG-010.limitations: Significant between-study heterogeneity in ever-smoking ORs; retrospective exposure assessment; the rising OR by publication era may reflect changing comparison populations as smoking prevalence fell rather than a changing biological effect.
ORIG-010.interpretation: Dose-response by intensity and duration, plus a cessation gradient (former << current), are Hill-type criteria strengthening causal interpretation beyond simple association.

glosses.risk-factors: A pooled case-control consortium (6,507 cases) giving a current-smoking odds ratio of 2.20 with a dose gradient.

ORIG-011.citation: Fan X, Alekseyenko AV, Wu J, et al. Human oral microbiome and prospective risk for pancreatic cancer: a population-based nested case-control study. Gut. 2018;67(1):120-127.
ORIG-011.clinical_status: not applicable; association only, no screening or preventive use
ORIG-011.design: Nested case-control study using PRE-DIAGNOSTIC oral wash samples; bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequencing; conditional logistic regression with LASSO; sensitivity analysis excluding cases diagnosed within 2 years of sample collection
ORIG-011.population: Adults in two large US prospective cohorts: American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II and the NCI Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) Screening Trial
ORIG-011.n: 361 incident pancreatic adenocarcinoma cases and 371 matched controls
ORIG-011.time_frame: Samples collected before diagnosis; time-to-diagnosis stratified, with a >2-year exclusion sensitivity analysis
ORIG-011.finding: Carriage of Porphyromonas gingivalis was associated with higher risk (adjusted OR for presence vs absence 1.60; 95% CI 1.15-2.22) and Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans likewise (OR 2.20; 95% CI 1.16-4.18). In the opposite direction, greater abundance of phylum Fusobacteria was associated with DECREASED risk (adjusted OR per percent increase in relative abundance 0.94; 95% CI 0.89-0.99), as was its genus Leptotrichia (Table 3). Associations for P. gingivalis and Leptotrichia persisted after excluding cases diagnosed within two years of sample collection (Table 4), reducing the likelihood that the tumour altered the oral flora.
ORIG-011.effect: P. gingivalis OR 1.60 (1.15-2.22); A. actinomycetemcomitans OR 2.20 (1.16-4.18); Fusobacteria OR 0.94 per percent abundance (0.89-0.99)
ORIG-011.limitations: Single oral wash per participant; 16S gives genus-level resolution at best; relative (not absolute) abundance; no pancreatic tissue microbiome measured; associations are modest.
ORIG-011.interpretation: Pre-diagnostic sampling plus the 2-year exclusion materially weakens reverse causation, but this remains an observational association: no mechanism, no perturbation, and the oral cavity is remote from the pancreas.

glosses.risk-factors: A prospective study associating certain gum-disease bacteria with higher pancreatic cancer risk and one group with lower risk.

ORIG-012.citation: Kopp JL, von Figura G, Mayes E, et al. Identification of Sox9-dependent acinar-to-ductal reprogramming as the principal mechanism for initiation of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Cell. 2012;22(6):737-750.
ORIG-012.design: Cell-type-restricted Kras-G12D activation with R26R-YFP tracing (Ptf1a-CreER for acinar, Sox9-CreER for ductal/centroacinar), whole-pancreas Alcian-blue area quantification on sections every 140 um, caerulein pancreatitis challenge, Sox9 conditional deletion, and Sox9 overexpression…
ORIG-012.population: Mouse, tamoxifen-inducible lineage tracing and conditional gain/loss of function
ORIG-012.n: PanIN incidence by genotype (Table 1): Ptf1a-CreER;Kras;R26R-YFP 12/12 mice (100%) with PanIN vs Sox9-CreER;Kras;R26R-YFP 8/14 (57%); caerulein arms Ptf1a 4/4 (100%) vs Sox9 3/5 (40%); saline Sox9…
ORIG-012.time_frame: Tamoxifen at postnatal day 10-25; caerulein at 6 weeks; analysis 48 h to 21 days post-injury, and up to ~8-16 weeks for lesion counts
ORIG-012.finding: Pancreatic histology was largely normal in Sox9-CreER;Kras;R26R-YFP mice: of 14 mice, 6 had NO detectable PanINs and the rest had no more than 10 PanINs per mouse (Table 1, Table S1), versus abundant lesions from acinar targeting (Fig 2C,G,M). Acute caerulein pancreatitis promoted Kras-driven PanIN formation from acinar but NOT from ductal/centroacinar cells (Fig 3). Sox9 is normally restricted to ductal/CAC cells but was induced in Kras-expressing acinar cells before ADM (Fig 4A-D). Concomitant Sox9 deletion with Kras activation COMPLETELY blocked Kras-mediated changes including ADM and PanIN (Fig 4E-Q). Forced Sox9 expression in acinar cells induced ductal genes (Cpa1/CK19 co-expression; Fig 5A-F, I) and potentiated Kras-driven PanIN formation; Ptf1a-Cre;Sox9-OE mice developed exocrine insufficiency after 3 weeks. Boundary condition: pancreatitis still caused ADM in Sox9-deleted…
ORIG-012.effect: PanIN incidence 100% (12/12) acinar vs 57% (8/14) ductal targeting, and <=10 lesions/mouse in the ductal arm; complete block of ADM/PanIN with Sox9 deletion
ORIG-012.limitations: Mouse only; Kras alone without p53/CDKN2A loss, so it models initiation not progression to carcinoma; PanIN counts per mouse are small-number data.
ORIG-012.interpretation: Necessity (conditional knockout) plus sufficiency-direction (overexpression) plus cell-type restriction — the strongest form of causal evidence available in a mouse preparation for the ADM->PanIN step.

glosses.what-is-pdac: A mouse lineage-tracing study showing most KRAS-driven precursor lesions arise from acinar cells reprogrammed into a duct-like state.
glosses.acinar-cells: Mouse study showing acinar cells are the main source of PanIN through Sox9-dependent acinar-to-ductal reprogramming.
glosses.duct-cells: Mouse study showing acinar cells are the main source of PanIN through Sox9-dependent acinar-to-ductal reprogramming.
glosses.kras: A mouse lineage-tracing study showing acinar cells reprogram to a duct-like state through Sox9 when Kras is activated.
glosses.cell-of-origin: A mouse study identifying Sox9-dependent acinar-to-ductal metaplasia as the main route to Kras-driven precursor lesions.

ORIG-013.citation: Lee AYL, Dubois CL, Sarai K, et al. Cell of origin affects tumour development and phenotype in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Gut. 2019;68(3):487-498.
ORIG-013.design: Sox9-CreER;Kras-LSL-G12D;Trp53-flox/flox;R26R-YFP ('Duct:KP cKO') vs Ptf1a-CreER;Kras-LSL-G12D;Trp53-flox/flox;R26R-YFP ('Acinar:KP cKO'), tamoxifen at 3-4 weeks; survival cohorts plus staged time-course histology, mPanIN grading, p53 IHC, Ki67, and mucin (Alcian blue, Muc5AC) phenotyping
ORIG-013.population: Mouse, tamoxifen-inducible cell-type-restricted Kras activation plus Trp53 ablation with YFP lineage tracing
ORIG-013.n: Survival cohorts: Duct:KP cKO n=19, Acinar:KP cKO n=9; tumour-area quantification n=8 per genotype; time-course n=4 per genotype per time point (2,4,6,8 weeks for duct; 4,6,8,12,16 weeks for acinar)
ORIG-013.time_frame: Tamoxifen at 3-4 weeks of age; staged analysis 2-16 weeks post-induction; survival to humane endpoint
ORIG-013.finding: Both models developed PDAC, but Duct:KP cKO mice developed PDAC EARLIER than Acinar:KP cKO mice and tumour development was associated with high-grade mPanIN. Duct:KP cKO mice developed ONLY high-grade mPanIN — no mPanIN1 lesions were observed (Fig 5A-B) — whereas Acinar:KP cKO mice developed the full spectrum: numerous low-grade mPanIN from 4 weeks post-injection increasing over time, plus high-grade lesions from 4 weeks rising to approximately twenty mPanIN3 lesions per section. Tumour burden at humane endpoint was equivalent (66.0% +/- 8.7% vs 60.0% +/- 9.7% of pancreatic area, p=0.4; Fig 2), so the difference is in timing and lesion sequence, not final extent. Differential Trp53 recombination was excluded by p53 IHC (both ductal- and acinar-derived mPanIN3 were p53-negative). Cell death (cleaved caspase 3) was minimal and Ki67 fractions were examined in mPanIN3 of both origins.…
ORIG-013.effect: Earlier PDAC onset and absence of low-grade mPanIN in the ductal arm; equivalent final tumour area (66.0% vs 60.0%, p=0.4)
ORIG-013.limitations: Small cohorts (n=9-19); Trp53 is fully ablated rather than point-mutated as in most human PDAC; no human validation; the senescence explanation is proposed, not tested here.
ORIG-013.interpretation: Isolates a single variable (cell of origin) against a fixed genotype, which is exactly the comparison Ferreira's asymmetric design (cerulein only in the acinar arm) could not make. Independent replication of the 'ductal route skips low-grade PanIN' claim in a different lab with different alleles.

glosses.acinar-cells: Mouse study showing duct-targeted mutations produce only high-grade precursors and earlier cancer than acinar-targeted ones.
glosses.duct-cells: Mouse study showing duct-targeted mutations produce only high-grade precursors and earlier cancer than acinar-targeted ones.
glosses.panin: A mouse study in which duct-cell origin produced only high-grade lesions and reached cancer sooner than acinar origin.
glosses.cell-of-origin: A second mouse study, from an independent laboratory, showing duct-cell origin skips low-grade PanIN and reaches cancer sooner.

ORIG-014.citation: Guerra C, Collado M, Navas C, et al. Pancreatitis-induced inflammation contributes to pancreatic cancer by inhibiting oncogene-induced senescence. Cancer Cell. 2011;19(6):728-739.
ORIG-014.clinical_status: preclinical; no anti-inflammatory agent is approved or recommended in the US for pancreatic cancer chemoprevention
ORIG-014.design: Temporally controlled oncogene activation in adult (>=P60) acinar cells, factorial combination with tumour suppressor loss and with caerulein-induced episodic (non-acute) pancreatitis; senescence and proliferation marker immunostaining; a pharmacological anti-inflammatory intervention (sulindac,…
ORIG-014.population: Mouse (doxycycline-controlled Elas-tTA/tetO-Cre acinar targeting of endogenous Kras-G12V, with conditional p16Ink4a/p19Arf or Trp53 ablation); plus human chronic pancreatitis surgical specimens
ORIG-014.n: Mouse survival and lesion-count cohorts of n=4-5 per genotype for the quantified comparisons (e.g. Fig 2B: n=5 p16/p19Arf-lox/lox, n=4 heterozygous, plus wild-type controls); human arm: nine…
ORIG-014.time_frame: Oncogene activation at P60; caerulein for 1-3 months; sacrifice 6-18 months after activation; human specimens cross-sectional
ORIG-014.finding: Adult acinar cells were resistant to transformation by Kras-G12V expression AND by loss of p16Ink4a/p19Arf or Trp53. Compound Kras-G12V;p16Ink4a/p19Arf-lox/lox and Kras-G12V;Trp53-lox/lox mice induced at P60 showed NORMAL parenchyma with no mPanIN lesions one year after oncogene activation (Fig 1A-B). Conversely, Kras-wild-type mice with p16Ink4a/p19Arf or Trp53 ablation plus three months of caerulein showed normal parenchyma with no mPanIN 8 months after treatment ended (Fig 1C-D), whereas Kras-G12V control mice under the same protocol developed abundant mPanIN surrounded by fibrosis and inflammatory infiltrate (Fig 1E). Episodic, non-acute pancreatitis was therefore both necessary and sufficient to unlock mPanIN and mPDAC in adult Kras-expressing acinar cells (Fig 3A-C, with one- vs three-month caerulein exposures and sacrifice 6, 12 and 18 months after oncogene activation).…
ORIG-014.effect: Zero mPanIN at one year with Kras + p16/p19Arf or Trp53 loss in the absence of pancreatitis, versus abundant mPanIN/mPDAC with episodic pancreatitis; sulindac reduced lesion development
ORIG-014.limitations: Nine human patients, cross-sectional, no outcomes; mouse Kras-G12V from endogenous promoter differs from human KRAS-G12D dominance; the authors' own framing that anti-inflammatory treatment 'may reduce risk' is explicitly a concept, not a tested clinical claim.
ORIG-014.interpretation: A factorial perturbation with a rescue-like arm (anti-inflammatory drug) plus a timing manipulation (adult vs embryonic activation) — this is strong causal evidence in mice that inflammation is the permissive variable, not merely a correlate. The human arm is a small cross-sectional correlation and does not establish that anti-inflammatory…

glosses.acinar-cells: Mouse study showing pancreatitis releases oncogene-induced senescence to let Kras-mutant acinar cells progress.
glosses.growth-control: A mouse study in which adult cells with mutant Kras stayed dormant unless pancreatitis released a senescence brake.
glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: A mouse study in which adult Kras-mutant pancreatic cells stayed senescent unless pancreatitis released the brake.
glosses.cdkn2a: A mouse study in which adult Kras-mutant pancreatic cells stayed senescent unless pancreatitis released the brake, with p16 loss accelerating progression.
glosses.genome-evolution: A mouse study in which adult Kras-mutant pancreatic cells stayed senescent unless pancreatitis released the brake.
glosses.panin: A mouse study in which adult Kras-mutant acinar cells formed no lesions for a year unless pancreatitis released a senescence brake.
glosses.cell-of-origin: A mouse study in which adult Kras-mutant acinar cells formed no lesions for a year unless pancreatitis released a senescence brake.
glosses.risk-factors: A mouse study in which pancreatitis released a senescence brake and an anti-inflammatory drug reduced lesion development.

ORIG-015.citation: Dbouk M, Katona BW, Brand RE, et al. The Multicenter Cancer of Pancreas Screening Study: impact on stage and survival. J Clin Oncol. 2022;40(28):3257-3266.
ORIG-015.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice for high-risk individuals (US); surveillance of average-risk adults recommended AGAINST by USPSTF (Grade D, 2019)
ORIG-015.design: Prospective multicentre cohort; primary endpoint the stage distribution of detected PDAC (stage I vs higher); Kaplan-Meier overall survival; Cox comparison of screen-detected vs outside-surveillance PDAC with adjustment for age and risk group
ORIG-015.population: High-risk individuals recommended for pancreas surveillance at eight US academic medical centres (CAPS5), plus the pooled CAPS1-5 programme
ORIG-015.n: CAPS5: 1,461 high-risk individuals enrolled 2014-June 2021, 48.5% with a pathogenic variant in a PDAC-susceptibility gene (18.4% BRCA2, 6.4% ATM); ~one third with a personal cancer history (breast…
ORIG-015.time_frame: CAPS5 enrolment 2014 to June 2021; CAPS1-5 programme 1998-2021; median follow-up 2.8 years
ORIG-015.finding: In CAPS5, nine patients had screen-detected PDAC and one presented with symptomatic metastatic PDAC four years after baseline, the only surveillance visit. Of the nine, 7 (77.8%) were stage I by surgical pathology, one stage II and one stage III; 88.9% had resectable disease. PDAC incidence was one per 160 person-years. Seven of nine were alive with median overall survival to date 3.84 years; two died (one stage IB BRCA1, one stage III familial-risk). Eight further patients had resections for concerning cystic lesions: three had high-grade dysplasia (in high-grade PanIN or IPMN) and the remaining FIVE had only low-grade dysplasia. Overall 10 of the 18 patients (56%) identified with PDAC or resected met the recommended goals of surveillance. During the CAPS5 period 73 patients under surveillance were diagnosed with OTHER cancers (1.68 per 100 patient-years). Across CAPS1-5, 26 patients…
ORIG-015.effect: 77.8% stage I among screen-detected PDAC; HR 0.13 (0.03-0.50) unadjusted for survival; 5-year OS 73.3%; 5 of 8 cyst resections found only low-grade dysplasia
ORIG-015.limitations: Relatively short CAPS5 follow-up; very small event numbers driving wide confidence intervals (adjusted HR lower bound 0.004); expert high-volume centres; no randomised comparison and none planned.
ORIG-015.interpretation: Prospective multicentre cohort with a pre-specified stage endpoint; the within-cohort comparator (those who left surveillance) is better than an external one but still not randomised. The authors themselves state that long-term outcomes are needed to minimise confounding from lead-time bias, which is the correct reading: a stage shift is…

glosses.panin: The US CAPS5 surveillance cohort, in which five of eight cyst resections found only low-grade dysplasia.
glosses.cysts-ipmn-mcn: The US CAPS5 surveillance cohort, in which five of eight cyst resections found only low-grade dysplasia.
glosses.hereditary-risk: The US CAPS5 surveillance cohort, 77.8 percent of screen-detected cancers at stage I with 73.3 percent five-year survival.

ORIG-016.citation: Klatte DCF, Meziani J, Cahen DL, et al. Pancreatic cancer surveillance: risk stratification of individuals with a germline CDKN2A pathogenic variant. United European Gastroenterol J. 2024;12(10):1374-1383.
ORIG-016.clinical_status: not implemented; authors state the model is not yet clinically useful
ORIG-016.design: Prospective-cohort data used to develop a clinical prediction model for PDAC within 20 years of surveillance enrolment, with non-PDAC death handled as a competing event via a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model; discrimination by c-statistic with bootstrap internal validation and a calibration…
ORIG-016.population: Individuals with a proven germline CDKN2A pathogenic variant in two Dutch pancreatic cancer surveillance programmes (Leiden University Medical Center, started 2000; Dutch Familial Pancreatic Cancer study, started 2006, three university hospitals)
ORIG-016.n: 506 germline CDKN2A pathogenic variant carriers: 107 (21.1%) from the FPC cohort and 399 (78.9%) from the LUMC cohort; median age at start of surveillance 49.9 years (IQR 44.8-56.7); 43.5% male
ORIG-016.time_frame: Surveillance enrolment from 2000 (LUMC) and 2006 (FPC); follow-up evaluated to July 2023; 20-year prediction horizon
ORIG-016.finding: In the multivariable Fine-Gray model (Table 2), having a first-degree relative with PDAC (B=0.7256) and a smoking history (B=0.4776) raised the probability of developing PDAC, whereas having a second-degree relative with PDAC or a relative affected before age 50 did not contribute. Worked example from the paper: an individual with an FDR with PDAC at 40, an SDR with PDAC at 50, and current smoking had a predicted 20-year PDAC risk of 31.7%. Discrimination was poor: the model c-statistic was 0.64 (95% CI 0.57-0.71) at 20 years, falling to 0.59 (0.46-0.71) after bootstrap internal validation — a confidence interval that includes 0.50, i.e. no better than chance. The authors conclude the study highlights the high lifetime PDAC risk in CDKN2A carriers while showing that their prediction model has limited precision and that additional factors such as biomarkers are needed before tailored…
ORIG-016.effect: Smoking and FDR history are significant predictors; but bootstrap-validated 20-year c-statistic only 0.59 (0.46-0.71)
ORIG-016.limitations: Internal validation only, no external cohort; single-country and largely a founder p16-Leiden population, so transportability to other CDKN2A variants is unknown; the model is not usable clinically as the authors state.
ORIG-016.interpretation: Prognostic modelling within a genetically defined cohort; it can establish predictive discrimination (and here establishes its absence) but not causation. The competing-risks handling matters because this population has high non-PDAC mortality, principally melanoma-associated.

glosses.cdkn2a: A study of 506 germline CDKN2A carriers in which a risk model performed no better than chance after validation.
glosses.hereditary-risk: A study of 506 germline CDKN2A carriers in which a risk model performed no better than chance after validation.

ORIG-017.citation: Mino-Kenudson M, Fernandez-del Castillo C, Baba Y, et al. Prognosis of invasive intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm depends on histological and precursor epithelial subtypes. Gut. 2011;60(12):1712-1720.
ORIG-017.clinical_status: informs surgical selection for IPMN (guideline-informing pathology); SURG/TX domains own management
ORIG-017.design: Retrospective clinicopathological cohort with central re-review classifying intraductal components into four epithelial subtypes (gastric, intestinal, pancreatobiliary, oncocytic) by H&E morphology and mucin glycoprotein immunoreactivity, and invasive components into tubular, colloid and oncocytic…
ORIG-017.population: Patients undergoing pancreatic resection for IPMN-associated invasive adenocarcinoma or for conventional PDAC at a single tertiary centre
ORIG-017.n: 61 invasive IPMN (histology tubular 38 (62%), colloid 16 (26%), oncocytic 7 (12%)) compared with a conventional PDAC cohort at the same institution
ORIG-017.time_frame: Retrospective resection series; survival measured from resection
ORIG-017.finding: Patients with invasive IPMN were more often male (61% vs 47%, p=0.043) and presented on average five years later than PDAC patients (70.6 +/- 9.6 vs 65.8 +/- 10.4 years, p=0.0006). Median survival after resection was 58 months for invasive IPMN versus 18 months for PDAC (Figure 3A); 5- and 10-year overall survival for invasive IPMN were 47% and 34%. Unadjusted mortality was markedly lower for invasive IPMN (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.26-0.54; Table 2), and the advantage persisted in the stage-matched multivariate model (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.39-0.86), i.e. it is not merely earlier-stage detection. Invasive IPMNs also had a lower incidence of adverse pathological features. By histological subtype, median survival after resection was 35 months for tubular adenocarcinoma, 95 months for colloid carcinoma and 132 months for oncocytic carcinoma — so the tubular type behaves much like conventional PDAC…
ORIG-017.effect: Median survival 58 vs 18 months; stage-matched multivariate HR 0.58 (0.39-0.86); subtype medians 35 / 95 / 132 months
ORIG-017.limitations: Single institution, retrospective, modest numbers in the favourable subtypes (7 oncocytic); staging era predates the AJCC 8th edition used by later surveillance studies; no molecular profiling.
ORIG-017.interpretation: Stage-matched multivariate adjustment is the key design feature: it separates 'detected earlier' from 'biologically different', supporting a genuine biological distinction rather than a lead-time artefact. Being retrospective and single-centre, it cannot exclude residual selection.

glosses.what-is-pdac: A surgical series showing invasive cancer arising in an IPMN has better stage-matched survival than conventional PDAC.
glosses.pdac-vs-other: A surgical series showing invasive cancer arising in an IPMN has better stage-matched survival than conventional PDAC, with the size of the advantage set by precursor subtype.
glosses.cysts-ipmn-mcn: A surgical series showing invasive cancer arising in an IPMN has better stage-matched survival than conventional pancreatic cancer, varying by epithelial subtype.
glosses.hereditary-risk: A surgical series showing IPMN-derived cancers, which surveillance preferentially catches, have better stage-matched survival.

ORIG-018.citation: Kobayashi G, Fujita N, Maguchi H, et al. Natural history of branch duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm with mural nodules: a Japan Pancreas Society multicenter study. Pancreas. 2014;43(4):532-538.
ORIG-018.clinical_status: informs international consensus (Fukuoka) guidance on observing small-mural-nodule BD-IPMN; management owned by SURG/DIAG
ORIG-018.design: Multicentre observational follow-up cohort (Japan Pancreas Society working group); EUS-based morphological monitoring every 3-6 months with US/MRCP/CT; comparison of patients with vs without mural nodules; univariate analysis of predictors of concomitant PDAC
ORIG-018.population: Patients with branch-duct IPMN (BD-IPMN) under long-term non-operative follow-up at 10 Japanese institutions (5 university hospitals, 5 tertiary referral centres)
ORIG-018.n: 402 analysable registered BD-IPMN patients on long-term follow-up (from 417 collected, 15 excluded); of these, 53 had mural nodules (MNs) <10 mm in height on endosonography; 28 men, 25 women, mean…
ORIG-018.time_frame: Follow-up >=1 year required; mean 42.4 months, up to 196 months
ORIG-018.finding: Mean follow-up was 42.4 months (SD 22.2; range 12-196). Median MN height at initial diagnosis was 3 mm (range 1-8 mm). During follow-up, 12/53 (23%) showed an increase in MN height; 4/53 (7.5%) showed enlargement of the cystic branch (none of whom had MN growth); and 4/53 (8%) showed progression of main pancreatic duct dilation — all four of these also had MN growth (3->6 mm, 8->13 mm, 4->8 mm, 5->8 mm). Six patients underwent surgery because of increasing MN height, yielding high-grade dysplasia in 1. Across the 53 MN patients, PDAC DERIVED from IPMN developed in 0 patients, PDAC CONCOMITANT with (but separate from) the IPMN in 1 (1.9%), and high-grade dysplasia in 1 (1.9%). Surgery was performed in 10/53 with MNs versus 29/349 without. In the earlier 2011 report of the 349 patients without MNs, IPMN-derived PDAC occurred in 0.3% and a distinct separate PDAC in 2.0%. Univariate…
ORIG-018.effect: 0/53 IPMN-derived PDAC with MN <10 mm over mean 42 months; 1.9% concomitant separate PDAC; MN growth in 23%; in MN-free patients 0.3% IPMN-derived and 2.0% distinct PDAC
ORIG-018.limitations: Modest numbers (53 with MNs); monitoring modality was at each institution's discretion so surveillance intensity varied; comparison group drawn from a previously published report rather than concurrent analysis; follow-up of ~3.5 years is short relative to IPMN natural history.
ORIG-018.interpretation: Observational natural history with imaging denominators — establishes absolute progression rates for a defined, guideline-selected low-risk cyst phenotype. It cannot establish what would have happened to resected patients, and it is not a test of surgical thresholds.

glosses.pdac-vs-other: A Japanese multicenter series following 53 branch-duct IPMNs with small nodules in which none developed an IPMN-derived cancer over a mean of 42 months.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Japanese multicenter follow-up of branch-duct IPMN cysts with small nodules showing no cyst-derived cancer over a mean of 42 months.
glosses.cysts-ipmn-mcn: A ten-center registry of branch-duct IPMN in which no IPMN-derived cancer arose among 53 cysts with small nodules, but 1.9 percent developed a separate cancer.

ORIG-019.citation: LaPelusa M, Shen C, Arhin ND, et al. Trends in the incidence and treatment of early-onset pancreatic cancer. Cancers (Basel). 2022;14(2):283.
ORIG-019.design: Retrospective population-based registry analysis of SEER-18 (2004-2016), covering ~35% of the US population; delay-adjusted annual age-adjusted incidence rates (AAIR) with annual percent change (APC) by sex and race/ethnicity; stage at presentation and treatment patterns by stage
ORIG-019.population: US population-based cancer registry cases of pancreatic cancer in adults aged under 50 (early-onset pancreatic cancer, EOPC)
ORIG-019.n: Annual EOPC case counts ranged from 515 (7.0% of all pancreatic cancer cases) in 2014 to 634 (8.7%) in 2009 (Table 1)
ORIG-019.finding: The age-adjusted incidence rate of EOPC increased over the study period (Figure 1). Although AAIR was higher in males, the rate of increase was faster in FEMALES: annual percent change 0.9 in males versus 2.2 in females. AAIR was highest in non-Hispanic Black patients; Hispanic patients experienced the fastest increase among the groups examined. Stage distribution (Figure 2a): distant-stage disease accounted for the highest percentage of diagnoses in every year of the study period, and localized-stage disease the lowest percentage in every year — i.e. no stage migration toward earlier disease across 2004-2016. For context the authors note that among all ages in the US, localized-stage pancreatic cancer incidence is approximately 1 per 100,000 while distant-stage incidence is far higher, and that pancreatic cancer incidence among all age groups was higher in African American than…
ORIG-019.effect: APC +0.9 (males) and +2.2 (females) in under-50 incidence 2004-2016; EOPC 7.0-8.7% of all cases; distant stage predominant in every year
ORIG-019.limitations: SEER covers ~35% of the US and lacks data on obesity, smoking, diabetes and germline status, so no risk-factor attribution is possible; APC values are reported by subgroup rather than a single overall figure; ends in 2016.
ORIG-019.interpretation: Population-based registry with near-complete ascertainment in its catchment — good for describing trends and absolute burden. Purely descriptive: it cannot attribute the trend to any cause, and the authors only hypothesise about obesity.

glosses.risk-factors: A US registry analysis showing rising incidence under age 50, faster in women, still under 10 percent of cases.

ORIG-020.citation: Naudin S, Wang M, Dimou N, et al. Alcohol intake and pancreatic cancer risk: an analysis from 30 prospective studies across Asia, Australia, Europe, and North America. PLoS Med. 2025;22(5):e1004590.
ORIG-020.clinical_status: not applicable (risk factor); alcohol reduction is general preventive advice, not a PDAC-specific intervention
ORIG-020.design: Pooled analysis of harmonised INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL data with multivariable Cox proportional hazards models on the aggregated dataset; follow-up time as the primary time scale; stratified analyses by sex, smoking status, geographic region and beverage type
ORIG-020.population: Adults without cancer at baseline in 30 prospective cohorts across Asia, Australia, Europe and North America (Pooling Project on Alcohol and Cancer, PPAC, within the Dietary Cancer Pooling Project)
ORIG-020.n: 2,494,432 participants (62% women, 84% European ancestries, 70% alcohol drinkers defined as >=0.1 g/day, 47% never smokers), with 10,067 incident pancreatic cancer cases; median baseline age 57
ORIG-020.finding: Each 10 g/day increase in alcohol intake was associated with a 3% increase in pancreatic cancer risk. In women, HRs versus the 0.1-<5 g/day reference were 0.91 (95% CI 0.84-0.99) for 5-<15 g/day, 1.12 (1.00-1.25) for 15-<30 g/day and 1.13 (0.99-...) for >=30 g/day (Fig 1); in men, intakes of 30-60 and >60 g/day were associated with 15% and 36% increased risk respectively. The association did NOT differ by smoking status (Fig 2): HR per 10 g/day was 1.03 (1.01-1.06) in never smokers (3,801 cases), 1.02 (1.00-1.04) in former smokers (3,490 cases) and 1.03 (1.01-1.04) in current smokers (2,573 cases). By region, positive associations were seen in Europe-Australia (HR per 10 g/day 1.03, 1.00-1.05) and North America (1.03, 1.02-1.05) but NO association in Asia, the region with the fewest drinkers. By beverage, positive associations for beer (1.02, 1.00-1.04) and spirits/liquor (1.04,…
ORIG-020.effect: HR 1.03 per 10 g/day (approx. 1 drink); men >60 g/day +36%; women 15-<30 g/day +12%; null in Asia and for wine
ORIG-020.limitations: Baseline-only exposure, no trajectory; 84% European ancestry despite the multi-continent framing; the Asian null may be a power or exposure-range issue rather than true absence of effect; effect sizes are small enough that residual confounding cannot be excluded.
ORIG-020.interpretation: Prospective individual-level pooling with very large case numbers permits dose-response modelling and formal effect-modification testing by smoking — the key confounder. Independence from smoking strengthens causal interpretation; residual confounding by diet, adiposity and unmeasured pancreatitis remains.

glosses.risk-factors: An analysis of 30 prospective studies showing alcohol raises risk about 3 percent per 10 grams per day above sex-specific thresholds.

ORIG-021.citation: Habbe N, Shi G, Meguid RA, et al. Spontaneous induction of murine pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (mPanIN) by acinar cell targeting of oncogenic Kras in adult mice. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2008;105(48):18913-18918.
ORIG-021.design: Bitransgenic lineage-restricted oncogene activation: Ela-CreERT2;LSL-Kras-G12D and Mist1-CreERT2;LSL-Kras-G12D mice induced with tamoxifen at 6 weeks of age, with serial harvest across six time points from 2 to 12 months post-induction; non-induced littermates as controls; histological mPanIN…
ORIG-021.population: Mouse, adult acinar-cell-restricted tamoxifen-inducible Cre with endogenous conditional Kras-G12D
ORIG-021.n: Cohorts harvested at six time points from 2 to 12 months post-induction, with two non-induced bitransgenic littermates killed at each of the six time points as controls
ORIG-021.time_frame: Tamoxifen at 6 weeks; serial harvest 2 to 12 months post-induction
ORIG-021.finding: Targeting Kras-G12D to mature adult acinar cells produced SPONTANEOUS mPanIN lesions without imposed injury: low-grade mPanIN-1A lesions were present as early as 2 months post-tamoxifen (Fig 2A-B), and the ENTIRE histological spectrum of mPanINs was observed over the time course, including high-grade mPanIN-2 at 12 months post-induction arising on a background of lobulocentric parenchymal change (Fig 3A). Acinar-ductal metaplastic lesions bridging the parenchyma were observed at 6 months post-induction, together with biphenotypic differentiation (co-expression of acinar and ductal markers) within acinar-derived mPanIN lesions (Fig 4A) — i.e. ADM lesions were morphologically intermediate. Aberrant Notch pathway activation was identified as an early molecular alteration: no discernible N1-ICD expression was seen in uninvolved acinar parenchyma distant from lesions in a 4-month-old…
ORIG-021.effect: Low-grade mPanIN by 2 months and high-grade mPanIN-2 by 12 months after adult acinar Kras activation with NO injury stimulus
ORIG-021.limitations: Progression stopped at high-grade mPanIN within 12 months — invasive mPDAC was not the reported endpoint, so this models initiation only; time points are sparse with small numbers of control animals (2 per time point); Notch finding is descriptive immunofluorescence, not a perturbation.
ORIG-021.interpretation: Cell-type- and time-restricted oncogene activation in adults with an explicit no-injury arm — this directly tests the necessity of pancreatitis claimed by Guerra. Because the two studies use different Kras alleles (G12D here vs endogenous G12V-geo there) and different Cre systems, the discrepancy is interpretable as an allele/dose effect rather…

glosses.acinar-cells: Mouse study showing Kras activation in adult acinar cells produced PanIN lesions without any injury stimulus.
glosses.panin: A mouse study in which mutant Kras in adult acinar cells produced the full PanIN spectrum without any injury stimulus.
glosses.cell-of-origin: A mouse study in which mutant Kras in adult acinar cells produced the full PanIN spectrum without any injury stimulus.

ORIG-022.citation: Kastrinos F, Mukherjee B, Tayob N, et al. Risk of pancreatic cancer in families with Lynch syndrome. JAMA. 2009;302(16):1790-1795.
ORIG-022.clinical_status: Lynch syndrome is not by itself a standard indication for pancreatic surveillance in the US absent additional family history; germline testing is guideline-recommended for PDAC patients
ORIG-022.design: Family-based penetrance study using MODIFIED SEGREGATION ANALYSIS by maximum likelihood (implemented in MENDEL v3.3.5) to estimate age-specific pancreatic cancer incidence in MMR carriers, with correction for ascertainment by conditioning on the genotype and phenotype of the proband and the…
ORIG-022.population: Families with confirmed germline mismatch repair (MMR) gene mutations in two US hereditary colorectal cancer registries (Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, n=80 families; University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center)
ORIG-022.n: 6,342 individuals from 147 families with deleterious MLH1, MSH2 or MSH6 mutations: 147 probands, 1,017 first-degree relatives and 5,178 more distant relatives on the affected side
ORIG-022.time_frame: Families enrolled before June 2008; lifetime (to age 70) risk horizon
ORIG-022.finding: 21% of families (31/147) reported at least one case of pancreatic cancer; 47 pancreatic cancers were reported in total (21 male, 26 female), with no sex difference in age at diagnosis (51.5 vs 56.5 years). Of the 31 affected families, 18 reported one case, 10 reported two and 3 reported three. Approximately 4% of individuals in these MMR-mutation families were estimated to be diagnosed with pancreatic cancer by age 70, with the increase in risk more pronounced after age 40 (Table 3, Figure 1 penetrance curves plotted at 5-year intervals from 20 to 70 years with 95% CIs shown for ages 50-70). Thirty-one of the 47 cases were reported in families with an MSH2 mutation. Verification was a major limitation the authors quantify explicitly: diagnoses could be confirmed with additional records in only 3/23 University of Michigan and 7/24 Dana-Farber cases; in 20/23 and 17/24 respectively the…
ORIG-022.effect: ~4% cumulative pancreatic cancer risk by age 70 in MMR-mutation families; risk rises after age 40; 21% of families reported >=1 case
ORIG-022.limitations: Most diagnoses unverified by records or pathology (the authors' own tabulation above); gene-specific risks not separately estimable with precision; three MMR genes pooled and PMS2 not included; US registry families, mostly of European ancestry.
ORIG-022.interpretation: Segregation analysis with explicit ascertainment correction is the appropriate design for converting registry family data into penetrance; germline genotype precedes disease so direction of causation is secure. The estimate is only as good as the reported pedigree phenotypes.

glosses.hereditary-risk: A study of Lynch-syndrome families estimating about 4 percent cumulative pancreatic cancer risk by age 70.

ORIG-023.citation: Hata T, Suenaga M, Marchionni L, et al. Genome-wide somatic copy number alterations and mutations in high-grade pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia. Am J Pathol. 2018;188(7):1723-1733.
ORIG-023.clinical_status: not applicable (pathology/genomic analysis); informs early-detection marker development
ORIG-023.design: Whole-genome copy number analysis by SNP microarray (log R ratio and B allele frequency, GC-content corrected) plus targeted next-generation sequencing (Ion Torrent AmpliSeq custom panel of 11 genes: KRAS, GNAS, CDKN2A, TP53, SMAD4, RNF43, ARID1A, BRAF, FBXW7, PIK3CA, TGFBR2); chromothripsis…
ORIG-023.population: Microdissected human PanIN lesions from fresh-frozen resected pancreata
ORIG-023.n: 11 microdissected high-grade PanIN (HG-PanIN) and 2 low-grade PanIN (PanIN-2) lesions; two patients had HG-PanIN WITHOUT an associated PDAC (one resected for ampullary carcinoma), the remainder came…
ORIG-023.finding: Somatic copy number alterations were observed in ALL 11 HG-PanIN lesions and in one of the two LG-PanINs (patient 45T). On average there were 2.7 regions of somatic copy number GAIN and 4.3 regions of copy number LOSS per PanIN (Table 2). The most common regions of alteration were 9p21 (the CDKN2A locus), 17p (TP53 locus) and 18q (SMAD4 locus), with per-lesion alteration lists showing recurrent involvement of 9p, 17p, 18q and 19p across lesions, and focal segments reported at 9p24.3-p21.3, 9p21.3 and 17p13.2-p11.2. The targeted panel covered the 11 genes most commonly mutated in pancreatic cancer alongside the array data for the same lesions.
ORIG-023.effect: Copy number alterations in 11/11 HG-PanIN and 1/2 LG-PanIN; mean 2.7 gains and 4.3 losses per lesion; recurrent 9p21 (CDKN2A), 17p (TP53), 18q (SMAD4)
ORIG-023.limitations: Very small n (11 HG-PanIN, 2 LG-PanIN) — the authors note it is rare to find HG-PanIN in fresh-frozen sections without an associated PDAC; one patient had neoadjuvant therapy; targeted panel of only 11 genes; no matched normal sequencing detail reported in the portion examined.
ORIG-023.interpretation: Direct genomic comparison across lesion grades in human tissue establishes the ORDER of events (near-universal KRAS mutation first, then chromosomal loss of CDKN2A/TP53/SMAD4 by high grade). Being cross-sectional, it cannot show that a given lesion with these losses would have progressed.

glosses.what-is-pdac: A genomic study of high-grade precursor lesions showing chromosomal losses at CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 in every lesion examined.
glosses.cdkn2a: A genomic study finding copy-number loss at the CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 regions in all 11 high-grade precursor lesions examined.
glosses.tp53: A genomic study finding copy-number loss at the TP53 region in all 11 high-grade precursor lesions examined.
glosses.smad4: A genomic study finding copy-number loss at the SMAD4 region in all 11 high-grade precursor lesions examined.
glosses.genome-evolution: A genomic study finding copy-number loss at the CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 regions in all 11 high-grade precursor lesions examined.
glosses.panin: A genomic study finding copy-number loss at the CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 regions in all 11 high-grade PanINs examined.

ORIG-024.citation: Kiemen AL, Almagro-Perez C, Matos V, et al. Quantitative 3D histology reveals localized immune remodeling during early pancreatic cancer progression. Cell Press Blue. 2026;1:100008.
ORIG-024.design: Extension of CODA, a cellular-resolution 3D histology pipeline, to co-register multiplexed serial histology: FFPE tissue serially sectioned at 4 um with every third section H&E-stained and digitised at 20x, intervening sections in a subset stained for CD45 and CD3/FOXP3; deep-learning semantic…
ORIG-024.population: Grossly normal human pancreas tissue, harvested as normal-adjacent tissue after surgical pancreatectomy; samples with significant fibrosis, atrophy or cancer in the normal-adjacent region, or from patients diagnosed with acute or chronic pancreatitis, were EXCLUDED
ORIG-024.n: 48 cm3-scale samples of grossly normal human pancreas; more than 1,000 pancreatic precancers mapped; IMC applied to 3 samples; 34 individual PanIN lesions analysed for immune composition in one…
ORIG-024.finding: PanIN was the MOST inflamed structure in the grossly normal pancreas, followed by normal pancreatic ducts and stroma (Figures 2B and 5B). Samples resected from the pancreatic head were significantly more inflamed than those from the tail (p=0.03, Wilcoxon rank-sum, n=48); no significant difference by patient diagnosis, age or sex. The central finding is extreme spatial heterogeneity: local immune cell density decayed by 50% within 10 serial sections (40 um), so bulk 2D radial profiles average away the structure entirely. Bulk pancreatic inflammation correlated strongly with PanIN burden but EQUALLY strongly with acinar content/atrophy and stromal density (Figure 3C), implying inflammation responds to ductal obstruction and acinar dropout as much as to neoplasia. Discrete immune HOTSPOTS contained more high-grade dysplasia, reactive stroma and acinar-to-ductal metaplasia, whereas cold…
ORIG-024.effect: 50% decay in local immune density within 40 um; FOXP3+ fraction of CD3+ cells 9% (small PanIN) vs 40% (large PanIN); pancreatic head more inflamed than tail, p=0.03
ORIG-024.limitations: Authors state a key limitation themselves: the study uses surgical resections, and organ-donor work suggests the microenvironment around PanINs in healthy pancreata differs from that in tissue from patients diagnosed with PDAC — extension to organ-donor pancreata is called crucial. Immune density was largely inferred from H&E stromal cell density calibrated on only two IHC-stained samples; FOXP3 composition analysis rests on n=1 sample for the…
ORIG-024.interpretation: High-resolution spatial correlation in human tissue at the level of individual lesions. It identifies a candidate gating variable and shows that the standard measurement modality cannot resolve it, but it is observational: it cannot determine whether the immunosuppressive niche causes the higher grade or is a response to it.

glosses.panin: A 3D immune-mapping study showing PanIN is the most inflamed structure in normal pancreas and that immune density halves within 40 micrometers.

ORIG-025.citation: Min J, Schweizer L, Zonderland G, et al. AI-powered Deep Visual Proteomics reveals critical molecular transitions in pancreatic cancer precursors. Cancer Discov. 2026. doi:10.1158/2159-8290.CD-25-1119.
ORIG-025.clinical_status: not applicable (discovery resource for candidate biomarkers)
ORIG-025.design: Deep Visual Proteomics (DVP): H&E imaging, AI-based phenotype clustering with a pathology foundation model (H-optimus-0) plus pathologist annotation, targeted laser microdissection (Leica LMD7) of defined cell populations, and ultrasensitive mass spectrometry; seven biological groups profiled…
ORIG-025.population: Human FFPE pancreas: cancer-free organ donors (incidental lesions, prefix 'i') and patients with PDAC (cancer-associated lesions, prefix 'c')
ORIG-025.n: 115 discrete histologically annotated and microdissected regions from 20 individuals, including 10 cancer-free organ donors
ORIG-025.finding: Quality control confirmed detection of peptides for PDAC drivers KRAS and TP53 and for HMGA2 and the stem cell marker DCLK1 (Fig 1G). PCA across all regions separated the tumour proteome from normal ducts, iADM and PanINs, with HG-cPanIN occupying a position INTERMEDIATE between LG-cPanIN and tumours (Fig 3A). Elevated TP53 appeared specifically in tumours and HG-cPanINs, consistent with mutant protein stabilisation (Supplementary Fig S5A); DCLK1 increased from LG-cPanIN to tumour. Restricting to non-tumour lesions, lesion morphology AND disease association were the dominant factors shaping the molecular landscape, with dimension 1 (14.4% of total variance) separating histologic classifications (Fig 3C). The two key context comparisons: despite MATCHED morphology, cNormal ducts differed from iNormal ducts by 192 proteins, 68% (131) of them increased in cNormal — a cancer-associated…
ORIG-025.effect: 192 proteins differ between histologically identical normal ducts from cancer-bearing vs cancer-free pancreata (68% up); 301 proteins differ between histologically identical LG-PanIN by context (88% up in cancer-associated)
ORIG-025.limitations: 20 individuals and 115 regions is small for the number of comparisons; FFPE proteomics has limited depth and is sensitive to pre-analytical variables; no HG-iPanIN group (high-grade lesions in cancer-free donors are very rare), so the most informative cell of the design is empty; the ~60% incidental PanIN prevalence figure is cited from prior work, not measured here.
ORIG-025.interpretation: The organ-donor comparison is the critical design element: it holds morphology constant and varies disease context, which is the only way with human tissue to ask whether identical-looking precursors are molecularly different. It establishes a correlate of context, not a cause of progression — the field effect could be a consequence of the tumour…

glosses.tp53: A proteomic study of precursor lesions in which raised p53 protein appeared specifically in tumors and high-grade lesions.
glosses.epigenetic: A proteomic study showing histologically normal ducts differ by 192 proteins between cancer-bearing and cancer-free pancreases.
glosses.panin: A proteomic study placing high-grade PanIN between low-grade PanIN and tumor, with p53 protein rising at the high-grade stage.
glosses.cysts-ipmn-mcn: A proteomic study showing histologically normal ducts differ by 192 proteins between cancer-bearing and cancer-free pancreases.

GENE-001.citation: Jones S, Zhang X, Parsons DW, et al. Core signaling pathways in human pancreatic cancers revealed by global genomic analyses. Science. 2008;321(5897):1801-1806.
GENE-001.design: Discovery sequencing of protein-coding exons of 20,735 genes (219,229 amplicons; Sanger dye-terminator), matched normal DNA confirmation of somatic status; SNP arrays (1,069,688 SNPs) for homozygous deletions/amplifications; SAGE transcriptome; gene-set/pathway statistics against an estimated…
GENE-001.population: Human PDAC: 24 advanced pancreatic adenocarcinomas passaged as cell lines or nude-mouse xenografts (to remove non-neoplastic cells), plus a 90-tumour prevalence screen; microdissected normal duct epithelium and HPV-immortalised HPDE cells as controls.
GENE-001.n: 24 discovery tumours (23,219 transcripts / 20,661 genes with mutation data); 90-tumour prevalence screen; 39 genes taken forward
GENE-001.time_frame: Cross-sectional; samples from advanced disease; published 2008
GENE-001.finding: Mean 63 genetic alterations per tumour, majority point mutations. 198 homozygous deletions across 24 tumours, mean size 335,000 bp, averaging 8.3 per tumour (range 2-20); ~10 genes eradicated per typical tumour. 144 focal high-copy amplifications. Deletion targets included CDKN2A (p16), SMAD4 and TP53. Prevalence screen: 255 nonsilent somatic mutations across 23 genes; nonsilent rate excluding KRAS/TP53/CDKN2A/SMAD4 was 3.6 vs 1.47 mutations/Mb in discovery (P<0.001). 69 gene sets altered in the majority of tumours; 31 collapsed into 12 core signalling pathways/processes each altered in 67-100% of the 24 cancers (Table 2, Fig 3A). The 31 core gene sets were more enriched for differentially expressed genes than the remaining 3,041 sets (P<0.001). Fig 3B/3C show two tumours each hitting most core pathways but through largely different genes (one SMAD4, one BMPR2).
GENE-001.effect: 12 core pathways each altered in 67-100% of tumours; mean 63 alterations/tumour; 8.3 homozygous deletions/tumour
GENE-001.limitations: Only 24 discovery tumours; coding exons only (no introns, regulatory regions, or structural variants); single-copy losses deliberately not pursued; Sanger-era sensitivity; authors state they cannot be certain every assigned mutation is functional in the pathway named.
GENE-001.interpretation: Descriptive/associational at genome scale. Supports inference that selection acts at the level of pathways rather than individual genes; cannot establish that any single mutation is causal.

glosses.what-is-pdac: The first genome-wide analysis of pancreatic cancer, finding about 63 alterations per tumor grouped into 12 core pathways.
glosses.growth-control: The 2008 exome study of 24 pancreatic cancers that found about 63 alterations per tumor clustering into 12 core pathways.
glosses.cdkn2a: The 2008 exome study of 24 pancreatic cancers identifying CDKN2A, SMAD4 and TP53 as targets of homozygous deletion.
glosses.tp53: The 2008 exome study identifying TP53, CDKN2A and SMAD4 as targets of homozygous deletion.
glosses.smad4: The 2008 exome study identifying the TGF-β pathway as one of 12 core processes broken at different points in different tumors.

GENE-002.citation: Witkiewicz AK, McMillan EA, Balaji U, et al. Whole-exome sequencing of pancreatic cancer defines genetic diversity and therapeutic targets. Nat Commun. 2015;6:6744.
GENE-002.clinical_status: BRAF V600E targeting is an approved tumour-agnostic approach in the US for some settings; in PDAC this remains off-label/trial territory (checked 2026-10-08). KRAS allele-specific prognostication is not standard practice.
GENE-002.design: Whole-exome sequencing of 109 tumour/normal pairs with microdissection to raise tumour cellularity; MutSigCV significance testing; GISTIC copy-number analysis; affinity-propagation clustering; survival correlation; IHC validation; drug sensitivity to the BRAF inhibitor PLX-4032 (vemurafenib).
GENE-002.population: Human PDAC: 109 micro-dissected cases with tumour/normal pairs and outcome data; separate IHC cohort of 296 PDAC for ARID1A; patient-derived BRAF V600E cell line (PDA_014); comparator lines PL45 (KRAS-mutant) and MNT1 (BRAF V600E melanoma).
GENE-002.n: 109 tumour/normal exome pairs; 296-case IHC validation cohort; 248 mutations Sanger-validated across 132 genes (92% confirmation, 95% CI 87.64-94.58%)
GENE-002.time_frame: Cross-sectional sequencing with retrospective survival follow-up; published 2015
GENE-002.finding: KRAS mutated in 92% of cases (Fig 4a), majority codon 12, also codons 13 and 61. 24 significantly mutated genes at >3.5% frequency (MutSigCV, Fig 3a) including KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A, SMAD4. KRAS codon-61 cases had markedly better survival than codon-12 cases (Fig 4d, Cox) and showed less ERK activation by pERK IHC (Fig 4e). BRAF V600E in 3% of cases, mutually exclusive with KRAS (Suppl Fig 29); the patient-derived BRAF V600E line was as sensitive to PLX-4032 as BRAF V600E melanoma cells while KRAS-driven PL45 was resistant (Fig 4g-i). MYC (8q24) amplification was the only locus uniquely associated with poor outcome (Fig 2e) and was over-represented in adenosquamous histology; MYC amplification also found in associated PanIN lesions. Pathway-level alterations: DNA repair >35%, SWI/SNF chromatin remodelling 42%, TGF-beta disrupted via SMAD4 plus mutually exclusive TGFBR1/2 and ACVR1B…
GENE-002.effect: KRAS 92%; BRAF V600E 3%; SWI/SNF 42%; DNA repair >35%; codon-61 KRAS survival advantage with lower pERK
GENE-002.limitations: Exome only (deletions of CDKN2A/SMAD4 captured by GISTIC but point-mutation frequencies alone understate them); microdissection improves but does not guarantee purity; single BRAF V600E line tested for drug response; multiple-testing burden across many survival comparisons.
GENE-002.interpretation: Human cohort association for frequencies and prognosis; the PLX-4032 experiment gives a perturbation-level causal link between BRAF V600E and drug sensitivity in one patient-derived line.
