glosses.what-is-pdac: Whole-exome sequencing of 109 pancreatic cancers finding KRAS mutated in 92% and defining the other recurrently mutated genes.
glosses.growth-control: A whole-exome study of 109 microdissected pancreatic cancers reporting KRAS mutation in 92 percent.
glosses.kras: A whole-exome study of 109 microdissected pancreatic cancers with KRAS mutated in 92 percent.
glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A whole-exome study of 109 tumors in which codon-61 KRAS mutants had less ERK activation and better survival.
glosses.epigenetic: A whole-exome study of 109 tumors finding SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling genes altered in 42 percent.
glosses.fusions-rare-targets: A whole-exome study of 109 tumors in which BRAF V600E occurred in 3 percent, mutually exclusive with KRAS.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: A 109-tumor exome study finding BRAF V600E in 3 percent of pancreatic cancers, mutually exclusive with KRAS, and a V600E line sensitive to a BRAF inhibitor.

GENE-003.citation: Notta F, Chan-Seng-Yue M, Lemire M, et al. A renewed model of pancreatic cancer evolution based on genomic rearrangement patterns. Nature. 2016;538(7625):378-382.
GENE-003.clinical_status: not applicable (changes the explanatory model; no direct clinical action)
GENE-003.design: Whole-genome sequencing with purpose-built informatics: CELLULOID (tumour ploidy and copy-number estimation from WGS) and Chrom-AL (distinguishes chromothripsis from gradually accumulated focal changes); mutation-timing analysis relative to polyploidisation; rearrangement-based reconstruction of…
GENE-003.population: Human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: over 100 whole genomes from tumour-enriched primary and metastatic specimens (107 evaluable for ploidy/chromothripsis calls).
GENE-003.time_frame: Cross-sectional WGS of primary and metastatic specimens; event ordering inferred computationally; published 2016
GENE-003.finding: 45% (48/107) of tumours showed copy-number patterns consistent with polyploidisation; of these 88% (42/48) tetraploid, rest hexaploid. Mean ploidy 1.95 (diploid) vs 3.03 (duplicated, relative to 4) and 5.21 (triplicated, relative to 6), implying large genome loss after duplication. Polyploid tumours were enriched for TP53 mutation (P=0.02, Fisher) and carried ~1.5-fold more copy-number alterations (median 112 vs 77, P=0.003, t-test). Most point mutations preceded polyploidisation while most copy-number losses and gains followed it (losses P=4.3x10^-7; gains P=0.003, t-test; Fig 1c). 65.4% (70/107) harboured at least one chromothripsis event; a common site was chr18, producing SMAD4 loss accompanied by gain of a chr18 region containing GATA6. Chromothripsis was associated with worse overall survival (P=0.025, log-rank). Rearrangement patterns in 16% of cases (17/107) combined allelic…
GENE-003.effect: Polyploidisation 45% (48/107); chromothripsis 65.4% (70/107); simultaneous multi-driver alteration 16% (17/107); chromothripsis OS P=0.025
GENE-003.limitations: No serial sampling, so timing is reconstructed rather than measured; precursor lesions were not sequenced in this cohort (the stepwise model it challenges was built on PanIN data); survival association from a modest number of events.
GENE-003.interpretation: Observational but mechanism-constraining: the structure of the rearrangements themselves orders events, so the inference that several drivers were lost in one catastrophe does not depend on clinical staging.

glosses.what-is-pdac: Whole-genome sequencing of 107 pancreatic cancers showing chromosome shattering in 65% and genome doubling in 45%.
glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: Whole-genome sequencing of 107 pancreatic cancers showing genome doubling in 45 percent and chromosome shattering in 65 percent.
glosses.tp53: Whole-genome sequencing of 107 tumors showing genome-doubled cancers were enriched for TP53 mutation.
glosses.smad4: Whole-genome sequencing of 107 tumors showing chromosome 18 shattering that removes SMAD4 and duplicates GATA6.
glosses.genome-evolution: Whole-genome sequencing of 107 pancreatic cancers showing genome doubling in 45 percent, chromothripsis in 65 percent and multi-driver single events in 16 percent.

GENE-004.citation: Moffitt RA, Marayati R, Flate EL, et al. Virtual microdissection identifies distinct tumor- and stroma-specific subtypes of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Nat Genet. 2015;47(10):1168-1178.
GENE-004.clinical_status: Subtyping is not standard-of-care for PDAC treatment selection in the US (checked 2026-10-08); used as a stratification variable in research.
GENE-004.design: Blind source separation by non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) to decompose bulk expression into tumour, stromal and normal components; subtype assignment; Kaplan-Meier and multivariable survival analysis; single-sample cross-platform classifier trained across PDAC/bladder/breast data.
GENE-004.population: Human PDAC gene-expression microarray compendium spanning primary tumours, metastases, normal pancreas and cell lines; validation in the ICGC PDAC microarray dataset; cross-tissue comparison with TCGA bladder and Perou breast cancer data.
GENE-004.n: Not fully enumerated in the accessed text for every cohort; survival subgroups reported include classical+normal-stroma n=24 and basal-like+activated-stroma n=26
GENE-004.time_frame: Retrospective expression compendium with survival follow-up; published 2015
GENE-004.finding: Two tumour-intrinsic subtypes recovered after removing stromal and normal signal: basal-like and classical. Basal-like tumours had median overall survival 11 months with 44% 1-year survival versus 19 months and 70% 1-year survival for classical (P=0.007, Fig 3b); validated in ICGC data (Fig 3c,d). Basal-like genes (laminins, keratins) overlapped basal subtypes of bladder and breast cancer; the cross-platform basal-like classifier achieved 93% cross-validation accuracy and 92% accuracy on external TCGA breast data. Separately, two stromal subtypes: activated stroma median survival 15 months / 60% 1-year vs normal stroma 24 months / 82% 1-year (Fig 2b); both absent from cell lines (Fig 2c). Tumour and stromal subtype effects were cumulative: classical tumour with normal stroma had the lowest hazard ratio 0.39 (95% CI 0.21-0.73, n=24) and basal-like tumour with activated stroma the…
GENE-004.effect: Basal-like vs classical median OS 11 vs 19 months (P=0.007); combined tumour+stroma HR range 0.39 to 2.28
GENE-004.limitations: Microarray-era data from heterogeneous sources; no serial sampling, so stability of subtype over time is untested; the stromal subtypes are the TME domain's material and are recorded here only because they were derived in the same decomposition.
GENE-004.interpretation: Observational and computational. Establishes that a reproducible tumour-cell-intrinsic expression axis exists and tracks outcome; says nothing about whether subtype causes outcome or is reversible.

glosses.sub-environments: The study that separated tumor from stromal gene signal and defined basal-like and classical subtypes, with median survival 11 versus 19 months.
glosses.cell-states: The virtual-microdissection study that defined basal-like and classical subtypes, with median survival 11 versus 19 months.

GENE-005.citation: Philip PA, Azar I, Xiu J, et al. Molecular Characterization of KRAS Wild-type Tumors in Patients with Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma. Clin Cancer Res. 2022;28(12):2704-2714.
GENE-005.clinical_status: NTRK and RET fusion inhibitors and pembrolizumab for MSI-H/dMMR are tumour-agnostic FDA approvals in the US; NRG1-fusion and FGFR2-fusion targeting in PDAC remains investigational (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-005.design: Retrospective analysis of clinical next-generation DNA and RNA sequencing with fusion detection (RNA from FFPE, >=10% tumour content required for microdissection), MSI/MMR determination, TMB, PD-L1 IHC, transcriptomic immune-cell deconvolution, plus real-world survival comparisons by treatment…
GENE-005.population: Human pancreatic adenocarcinoma specimens submitted to a commercial reference laboratory (Caris Life Sciences): 2,483 patients, 53.7% male, median age 66; PDAC 92.5% of samples, remainder mucinous, adenosquamous, sarcomatoid, acinar and solid-pseudopapillary.
GENE-005.n: 2,483 patients total; 266 (10.7%) KRAS wild-type; oncoprint shown for 233 KRAS-WT PDAC
GENE-005.time_frame: Retrospective commercial-laboratory series; real-world survival follow-up; published 2022
GENE-005.finding: 266/2,483 (10.7%) were KRAS wild-type; restricted to PDAC histology the rate was 10.1%; 11% in men and 10% in women; median age 66 (WT) vs 67 (MT). Acinar cell carcinomas were 82% KRAS-WT; both solid-pseudopapillary tumours were WT. KRAS mutation spectrum: G12D 43%, G12V 31%. In KRAS-WT PDAC the most frequently mutated gene was TP53 (44.5%), then BRAF (13.0%); only ~37% of those BRAF mutations were class 1 V600, with RAS-independent class 2 most common (43%) and class 3 least common. Other KRAS-WT mutation frequencies: ARID1A 11.6%, CDKN2A 10.3%, PBRM1 5.6%, BRCA2 5.2%, ATM 4.7%, ARID2 3.9%, KMT2C 3.8%, KMT2D 3.4%, BAP1 2.9%, RAD50 2.3%, SMARCA4 2.2%, FANCE 2.1%, PALB2 2.1%, SETD2 1.8%. Amplifications in KRAS-WT: FGF3 3%, ERBB2 2.2%, FGFR3 1.8%, NTRK 1.8%, MET 1.3%. Gene fusions were found in 21% of KRAS-WT tumours (50/233) involving BRAF 6.6%, FGFR2 5.2%, ALK 2.6%, RET 1.3%, NRG1…
GENE-005.effect: KRAS-WT 10.7% of all, 10.1% of PDAC; fusions in 21% of KRAS-WT; MSI-H 4.7% vs 0.7%; TMB-H 4.5% vs 1%; ERBB2 amplification 2.2% of KRAS-WT
GENE-005.limitations: No central pathology review reported in accessed text; histology mix includes non-PDAC entities (acinar, pseudopapillary) that are biologically distinct and drive part of the KRAS-WT enrichment; treatment data are real-world and incomplete.
GENE-005.interpretation: Prevalence and association only. Establishes how often alternative drivers exist; does not show that targeting them helps.

glosses.kras: A 2,483-patient commercial sequencing series giving the KRAS allele distribution and characterizing the wild-type tenth.
glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A 2,483-patient commercial sequencing series characterizing the 10.7 percent of tumors that are KRAS wild-type.
glosses.msi-mmr: A 2,483-patient sequencing series showing mismatch-repair deficiency in 4.7 percent of KRAS wild-type versus 0.7 percent of mutant tumors.
glosses.fusions-rare-targets: A 2,483-patient sequencing series showing fusions in 21 percent of KRAS wild-type tumors and listing the specific genes and amplifications.
glosses.molecular-testing: A 2,483-patient sequencing series showing fusions, detected by RNA sequencing, are concentrated in KRAS wild-type tumors.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: A 2,483-patient molecular series in which MSI-high was found in 4.7 percent of KRAS-wild-type and 0.7 percent of KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancers.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: A 2,483-patient molecular series giving fusion frequencies in KRAS-wild-type pancreatic cancer: 21 percent overall, led by BRAF, FGFR2, ALK, RET and NRG1.
glosses.kras-g12d-inhibitors: A 2,483-patient reference-laboratory series of pancreatic adenocarcinoma in which G12D was the commonest KRAS allele, at 43 percent of KRAS-mutated tumors.

GENE-006.citation: Hu ZI, Shia J, Stadler ZK, et al. Evaluating Mismatch Repair Deficiency in Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: Challenges and Recommendations. Clin Cancer Res. 2018;24(6):1326-1336.
GENE-006.clinical_status: Pembrolizumab is FDA-approved in the US for unresectable/metastatic MSI-high or dMMR solid tumours after prior treatment (as described in the accessed text); detailed approval terms belong to the TX domain (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-006.design: Retrospective consecutive-cohort review with multimodal MMR/MSI assessment: MMR protein immunohistochemistry, MSI PCR (Bethesda panel plus mononucleotide markers), MSIsensor computational MSI scoring from next-generation sequencing, tumour mutational burden, and germline testing; case-level…
GENE-006.population: Human PDAC: 833 consecutive patients treated at a single tertiary cancer centre (MSKCC) between 2006 and 2017, with institutional tumour registry and ICD billing database review.
GENE-006.n: 833 consecutive PDAC patients; 7 MMR-deficient cases identified
GENE-006.finding: 7 of 833 patients (0.8%) had MMR-deficient PDAC. These cases were associated with germline mismatch-repair gene mutations, loss of MMR protein expression by IHC, higher mutational loads and elevated MSIsensor scores. The paper documents that MSI PCR using the Bethesda panel (BAT-25, BAT-26, D5S346, D2S123, D17S250, supplemented with NR-21, NR-24, MONO-27; MSI-high defined as instability at >=2 loci) and IHC can disagree, and notes that MLH1 promoter hypermethylation is an alternative sporadic cause (citing a prior series in which 6 of 13 sporadic MSI-high PDACs had MLH1 hypermethylation). One MMR-deficient case also carried a B2M mutation, a described immune-evasion mechanism via MHC class I loss. The authors propose a testing algorithm recommending germline testing consideration for all PDAC patients and NGS for metastatic or locally advanced disease.
GENE-006.limitations: Hybrid article: contains an original 833-patient prevalence analysis but also substantial review and recommendation content, so only the cohort findings are treated as primary here. Very small numerator (7 cases) gives a wide true confidence interval. Survival and immunotherapy-response inferences from 7 cases are anecdotal.
GENE-006.interpretation: Prevalence estimate from a consecutive series; the assay-comparison component is methodological rather than causal.

glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: A consecutive series of 833 patients in which 7 (0.8 percent) had mismatch-repair-deficient tumors.
glosses.epigenetic: A consecutive series of 833 patients that also documents MLH1 promoter methylation as a sporadic cause of mismatch-repair deficiency.
glosses.msi-mmr: A consecutive series of 833 patients in which 7 (0.8 percent) had mismatch-repair-deficient tumors, all Lynch-associated, and which documents assay disagreement and MLH1 methylation.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: A consecutive series of 833 pancreatic cancers in which 7 (0.8 percent) were mismatch-repair deficient, all with Lynch syndrome.

GENE-007.citation: Mueller S, Engleitner T, Maresch R, et al. Evolutionary routes and KRAS dosage define pancreatic cancer phenotypes. Nature. 2018;554(7690):62-68.
GENE-007.clinical_status: preclinical and cross-sectional human genomics; KRAS allele dosage is not measured in routine US clinical testing (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-007.design: Multiplex FISH, whole-exome sequencing and array CGH of mouse PDAC lines; allele-specific Kras G12D mRNA quantification by amplicon RNA-seq plus qRT-PCR; phenotype correlation (morphology, histopathology, metastasis); functional studies of alternative oncogenic gains; amplicon-based deep…
GENE-007.population: Mouse: large panel of primary PDAC cell cultures from Kras G12D-driven mice (PK mice, initial panel n=38) plus metastatic mouse PDAC lines; cross-species comparison with human microdissected PDAC datasets and 20 microdissected human PanIN lesions.
GENE-007.n: 38 primary mouse PDAC cultures classified by Kras dosage state; 26 Kras-iGD vs 12 Kras-HET tumours compared; 20 microdissected human PanINs; human PDAC comparison groups n=38…
GENE-007.time_frame: Mouse tumours collected at endpoint; human PanIN and PDAC specimens cross-sectional; published 2018
GENE-007.finding: Mouse PDAC Kras G12D dosage states: focal gain 7.9%, arm-level gain 23.7%, copy-number-neutral loss of wild-type Kras 36.8%, no change 31.6% - so roughly two-thirds had allelic imbalance increasing mutant Kras dosage. Allele-specific Kras G12D mRNA was higher in iGD (n=26) than HET (n=12) tumours (P=0.02, two-sided Mann-Whitney). Macro/micro-metastasis prevalence was markedly higher in Kras G12D-iGD (n=26) than Kras G12D-HET (n=12) tumours (P=0.001, two-sided Fisher). Highest Kras mutant levels underlay aggressive undifferentiated phenotypes. Kras dosage gain was tightly linked to Cdkn2a status: Kras-iGD occurred in 23/27 Cdkn2a-homozygously-deleted cancers versus predominantly HET (8/11) in Cdkn2a heterozygous/wild-type cancers (P=0.001, Fisher, OR 15.3, 95% CI 2.8-83.9). The same relationship held in human data: KRAS mutant variant allele frequencies were higher in CDKN2A…
GENE-007.effect: ~two-thirds of mouse PDAC with increased Kras dosage; metastasis prevalence iGD vs HET P=0.001; Cdkn2a-deletion/Kras-iGD association OR 15.3 (95% CI 2.8-83.9)
GENE-007.limitations: Phenotyping relies substantially on cultured lines to escape stromal contamination, which may bias dosage distributions; human PanIN sample is small (n=20); the human arm reuses published copy-number data rather than new sequencing.
GENE-007.interpretation: Strong for the mouse: genetically defined dosage states with matched phenotype and metastasis read-outs, plus functional substitution experiments with alternative oncogenes. Human component is cross-sectional association, so the dosage-to-metastasis link is causal in the mouse preparation and correlational in people.

glosses.growth-control: A mouse and human study showing that extra copies of mutant KRAS drive metastasis and are licensed by CDKN2A loss.
glosses.kras: A mouse and human study showing extra copies of mutant KRAS drive metastasis and are licensed by CDKN2A loss.
glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A mouse and human study showing extra copies of mutant KRAS drive metastasis and are licensed by CDKN2A loss.
glosses.cdkn2a: A mouse and human study showing extra copies of mutant KRAS drive metastasis and are licensed by CDKN2A loss.

GENE-008.citation: McDonald OG, Li X, Saunders T, et al. Epigenomic reprogramming during pancreatic cancer progression links anabolic glucose metabolism to distant metastasis. Nat Genet. 2017;49(3):367-376.
GENE-008.clinical_status: preclinical only; oxPPP inhibition is not a clinical therapy in PDAC (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-008.design: Chromatin immunostaining (H3K9me2/3) across matched tumour sections; genome-wide chromatin and expression mapping across euchromatin and large organized chromatin K9-modified (LOCK) heterochromatin domains; metabolic flux and metabolite measurements; perturbations - glucose deprivation, RNAi…
GENE-008.population: Human PDAC subclones from rapid-autopsy patients whose subclonal genetic architecture had already been defined (founder clone, regional/peritoneal subclones, distant liver and lung metastatic subclones, all sharing identical driver mutations); HPDE immortalised normal duct epithelial cells as…
GENE-008.n: Matched primary and metastatic subclone series from rapid-autopsy patients (exact n not enumerated in accessed text); transcriptional comparisons involve 1,968 6AN-downregulated and 2,192…
GENE-008.time_frame: Autopsy-derived subclones (natural, largely untreated disease history); in-vitro perturbations over days; published 2017
GENE-008.finding: Patients with regional (peritoneal) metastatic disease showed uniform, diffusely positive (>80%) H3K9me2/3 staining across all tumour sections, whereas patients with distant (liver, lung) metastases showed progressive loss of H3K9me2/3 during subclonal evolution - heterogeneous staining in primary subclones followed by diffusely negative (<20%) or heterogeneous staining in the metastases (Fig 1a,b). Reprogramming targeted thousands of large chromatin domains including LOCKs and large hypomethylated blocks, which together occupy over half the genome. Distant metastatic subclones acquired dependence on the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway: glucose deprivation, PGD RNAi and 6AN all reversed the reprogrammed chromatin state of distant metastatic subclones while having no effect on the peritoneal subclone. PGD RNAi had minimal effect on HPDE sphere formation or regional PDAC tumour…
GENE-008.effect: H3K9me2/3 >80% positive (regional) vs <20% (distant metastases); 52% overlap between 6AN-downregulated and subclone-overexpressed genes; PGD knockdown selectively blocked distant-metastatic tumour formation
GENE-008.limitations: Small number of patients, with much of the mechanistic work resting on one patient's subclone pair (A38Per vs A38Lg); 'distant' vs 'regional' grouping is coarse; reversal of chromatin state is not the same as reversal of metastatic behaviour in vivo.
GENE-008.interpretation: High for the preparation: matched subclones with identical drivers isolate the non-genetic variable, and three independent perturbations (nutrient, genetic, pharmacological) converge on the same reversal, which is a strong causal design.

glosses.recurrence-meaning: A study of matched primary and metastatic subclones showing distant metastasis can arise without new driver mutations through chromatin and metabolic reprogramming.
glosses.kras: A study of human metastatic subclones showing a lung metastasis that had lost KRAS dependence without changing its mutation.
glosses.genome-evolution: A study of human metastatic subclones showing distant metastasis arose through chromatin and metabolic reprogramming without new driver mutations.
glosses.epigenetic: A study of human metastatic subclones showing distant metastasis arose through loss of H3K9 chromatin marks and oxidative pentose phosphate dependence, without new mutations.

GENE-009.citation: Chou A, Froio D, Nagrial AM, et al. Tailored first-line and second-line CDK4-targeting treatment combinations in mouse models of pancreatic cancer. Gut. 2018;67(12):2142-2155.
GENE-009.clinical_status: preclinical; CDK4/6 inhibitors are FDA-approved in the US for certain breast cancers but not for PDAC (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-009.design: In-vitro sensitivity screening to the CDK4/6 inhibitor PD-0332991 (palbociclib) correlated with protein and genomic data to find response biomarkers; in-vivo efficacy of monotherapy and combinations across primary growth, recurrence (second-line) and metastatic settings; mechanistic analysis of…
GENE-009.population: Human patient-derived PDAC cell lines (n=19 primary lines, genome-sequenced); mouse xenograft models - subcutaneous, intrasplenic and orthotopic - derived from sequenced patient specimens plus a genetically engineered mouse model; independent human PDAC patient cohorts for biomarker validation…
GENE-009.n: 19 patient-derived lines for biomarker discovery; >500 human PDAC specimens for biomarker prevalence/prognosis; multiple in-vivo cohorts
GENE-009.time_frame: Preclinical experiments over weeks of treatment; retrospective human cohorts with survival follow-up; published 2018
GENE-009.finding: Palbociclib sensitivity across 19 patient-derived lines tracked with RB protein status rather than CDKN2A/p16 status. Subtype-specific in-vivo efficacy was demonstrated at multiple stages: primary tumour growth, recurrence after first-line therapy, and the metastatic setting, with activity concentrated in RB-high models. Palbociclib disrupted surrounding extracellular-matrix organisation, increased quiescence and apoptosis, improved chemosensitivity, and decreased invasion, metastatic spread and disease progression in vivo; it also reduced circulating tumour cells and delayed progression in metastatic RB-high models. In the human validation cohorts (>500 specimens), RB protein was prevalent in both primary operable and metastatic PDAC; retained RB correlated with significantly improved survival and lower tumour grade, and RB loss was an independent poor prognostic factor for…
GENE-009.effect: RB loss independent poor prognostic factor HR 1.552 (P=0.0148); p16 expression not prognostic
GENE-009.limitations: Biomarker discovery in only 19 lines; mouse models do not reproduce human immune context; RB immunohistochemistry thresholds are assay-dependent; CDK4/6 inhibitors have not shown benefit in PDAC trials, so the preclinical promise is unconfirmed clinically.
GENE-009.interpretation: Interventional in animals (randomised-by-allocation preclinical efficacy across several settings), observational for the human prognostic biomarker. Supports a conditional causal claim: CDK4/6 inhibition works where RB is retained.

glosses.growth-control: Patient-derived models and more than 500 human specimens showing RB, not p16, tracks CDK4/6-inhibitor sensitivity and prognosis.
glosses.cdkn2a: Patient-derived models and over 500 human specimens showing RB, not p16, tracks CDK4/6-inhibitor sensitivity and prognosis.

GENE-010.citation: Hobbs GA, Baker NM, Miermont AM, et al. Atypical KRAS(G12R) Mutant Is Impaired in PI3K Signaling and Macropinocytosis in Pancreatic Cancer. Cancer Discov. 2020;10(1):104-123.
GENE-010.clinical_status: preclinical only (checked 2026-10-08); KRAS-allele-specific therapy selection beyond G12C is the RAS domain's territory
GENE-010.design: Comparative signalling and phenotype analysis across KRAS-allele-defined PDAC models; effector-binding assays for p110alpha (PI3Kalpha); X-ray crystallography of GDP-bound KRAS G12V, G12R and Q61L; macropinocytosis assays; MYC dependence tests; PI3Kgamma (p110gamma) involvement tests; drug…
GENE-010.population: Human PDAC cell lines and models stratified by KRAS allele (G12R vs G12D/G12V); recombinant KRAS proteins; X-ray crystallography of KRAS mutant structures.
GENE-010.n: Not enumerated as a single n in the accessed text; panel of PDAC lines plus 525-compound drug screen
GENE-010.finding: KRAS G12R is rare in lung and colorectal cancer (~1%) but relatively common in PDAC (~20%), and G12R is the third most common KRAS mutation in PDAC; across cancers 84% of KRAS mutations are at G12, with G12D most predominant (42%) followed by G12V, G12C, G12A, G12S and G12R. KRAS G12D/V but not G12R drove macropinocytosis; MYC was essential for macropinocytosis in G12D/V but not in G12R-mutant PDAC. KRAS G12R was defective for interaction with the key effector p110alpha PI3K, attributable to structural perturbation of the switch II region shown crystallographically (G12R, unlike G12D, disrupts switch II). Instead, upregulated KRAS-independent PI3Kgamma (p110gamma) activity supported macropinocytosis in G12R-mutant PDAC. G12R-mutant PDAC showed a distinct drug-sensitivity profile from G12D-mutant PDAC with only limited preferential sensitivity to MEK/ERK inhibitor monotherapy, but was…
GENE-010.effect: G12R ~20% of PDAC vs ~1% of lung/colorectal; G12R fails to bind p110alpha; macropinocytosis MYC-dependent only in G12D/V
GENE-010.limitations: No in-vivo or patient-level validation of the G12R drug-sensitivity profile; macropinocytosis assays are in-vitro surrogates for nutrient scavenging in a stroma-rich tumour; KRAS allele frequencies are quoted from prior datasets rather than measured here.
GENE-010.interpretation: Strong mechanistic causality within the preparation: structure plus binding assay plus phenotype plus isoform rescue, each independently testing the same claim. No human outcome data.

glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A cell and structural study showing KRAS G12R cannot bind the PI3K subunit p110-alpha and does not drive macropinocytosis.

GENE-011.citation: Zafra MP, Parsons MJ, Kim J, et al. An In Vivo Kras Allelic Series Reveals Distinct Phenotypes of Common Oncogenic Variants. Cancer Discov. 2020;10(11):1654-1671.
GENE-011.design: CRISPR-engineered endogenous allelic series; induction in murine pancreas or colon; quantitative histopathology measuring relative area of normal acini, acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) and PanIN at 12 and 50-60 weeks (plus 24 weeks and 1 year for G12R); whole-pancreas transcriptome and…
GENE-011.population: Mouse: new conditional LSL-Kras allelic series (G12C, G12R, G13D alongside the standard G12D) generated by high-fidelity CRISPR homology-directed repair in genetically engineered embryonic stem cells; pancreas-specific and colon induction; mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs); pancreatic organoid…
GENE-011.n: Allelic series across four Kras genotypes plus wild-type controls; cohorts aged to 12, 24, 50-60 weeks and 1 year (per-genotype n not enumerated in accessed text)
GENE-011.time_frame: Mouse cohorts followed 4 weeks to 1 year; published 2020
GENE-011.finding: Striking quantitative and qualitative differences between Kras mutants in driving early transformation. In low-serum MEFs, only KRAS G12D showed clear MEK/ERK/AKT activation; G12C and G13D showed lower pMEK/pERK than G12D but above wild-type; KRAS G12R MEFs showed pMEK/pERK levels similar to KRAS wild-type cultures. In pancreas at 12 weeks, KC-G12D pancreata were predominantly PanIN (>90%) with little normal acinar tissue; KC-G13D pancreata appeared predominantly histologically normal with less than one third showing ADM or PanIN transition, though the PanINs that did form resembled G12D/G12C lesions with increased Alcian blue and KRT19. KC-G12R pancreata showed no Alcian blue staining and epithelium co-expressing acinar (CPA1) and ductal (KRT19) markers, indicating progression stalled at ADM; this lack of progression persisted at 24 weeks and 1 year, so it was not merely a latency…
GENE-011.effect: KC-G12D >90% PanIN area at 12 weeks vs KC-G13D <1/3 ADM-or-PanIN and KC-G12R stalled at ADM through 1 year
GENE-011.limitations: No metastasis or survival endpoints reported in accessed text for all genotypes; these are initiation models in otherwise wild-type pancreas, without the Trp53 or Cdkn2a lesions that accompany human G12R disease; per-genotype animal numbers not enumerated in the accessed text.
GENE-011.interpretation: Strong: endogenous, single-nucleotide-defined alleles on an otherwise identical background, with time-course histology - as close to a controlled experiment on allele identity as is available.

glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A mouse allelic series in which G12D drove rapid PanIN formation while G12R stalled at an early stage for a year.
glosses.cdkn2a: A mouse allelic series in which G12R stalled at an early stage for a year while G12D drove rapid lesion formation.

GENE-012.citation: Ying H, Kimmelman AC, Lyssiotis CA, et al. Oncogenic Kras maintains pancreatic tumors through regulation of anabolic glucose metabolism. Cell. 2012;149(3):656-670.
GENE-012.clinical_status: preclinical; provides the rationale for KRAS-directed therapy, whose clinical status belongs to the RAS domain (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-012.design: Inducible oncogene extinction: Kras G12D expression switched off by doxycycline withdrawal in advanced tumours (assessed at 9 weeks after induction), with serial MRI and FDG-PET imaging, histopathology, proliferation and apoptosis read-outs; transcriptome and metabolomic profiling; isotope-tracing…
GENE-012.population: Mouse: doxycycline-inducible Kras G12D-driven PDAC model (iKras) with established, advanced tumours; primary tumour cell cultures from these mice.
GENE-012.n: Not enumerated as a single n in the accessed text; cohorts of iKras mice with established tumours plus derived primary cultures
GENE-012.time_frame: Tumours established over 9 weeks; regression measured over 48 hours to 1 week; published 2012
GENE-012.finding: Advanced PDAC remained strictly dependent on Kras G12D expression. Kras G12D extinction caused rapid tumour regression with morphological deterioration of tumour cells and rapid degeneration of stromal elements beginning at 48 hours and peaking at 72 hours after doxycycline withdrawal. After one week of withdrawal, MRI showed regression and FDG-PET showed complete loss of fluorodeoxyglucose uptake (Fig 1D,E). Histologically, virtually all malignant components regressed, leaving pancreata with collagen deposition around a few remnant ductal structures (Fig 1C); regression was accompanied by decreased proliferation and increased apoptosis, paralleled in culture by loss of clonogenic growth (Fig S2B). Mechanistically, Kras G12D controlled tumour metabolism by stimulating glucose uptake and channelling glucose intermediates into hexosamine biosynthesis and the pentose phosphate pathway,…
GENE-012.effect: Complete regression of established tumours within ~1 week of Kras extinction; loss of FDG uptake; apoptosis onset 48-72 h
GENE-012.limitations: Transgenic rather than endogenous allele; single genetic background; no immune-competent therapeutic translation; non-oxidative pentose phosphate routing is measured in mouse tumours and may differ in human disease - notably the related distant-metastatic human subclones in GENE-008 depend on the OXIDATIVE branch instead.
GENE-012.interpretation: Very strong within the preparation: reversible genetic perturbation in established disease is the cleanest available test of oncogene maintenance, and the imaging read-out is quantitative.

glosses.growth-control: A mouse study in which switching off mutant Kras made established pancreatic tumors regress within about a week.
glosses.kras: A mouse study in which switching off mutant Kras made established tumors regress within about a week.
glosses.epigenetic: A mouse study showing mutant Kras routes glucose into the non-oxidative pentose phosphate pathway in primary tumors.
glosses.pet-scan: A mouse study in which switching off mutant KRAS abolished FDG uptake within a week, showing the oncogene drives the tumor's glucose uptake.

GENE-013.citation: Kapoor A, Yao W, Ying H, et al. Yap1 activation enables bypass of oncogenic Kras addiction in pancreatic cancer. Cell. 2014;158(1):185-197.
GENE-013.clinical_status: preclinical; relevance to clinical KRAS inhibitor resistance is the RAS domain's territory (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-013.design: Oncogene extinction followed by long-term surveillance for spontaneous relapse with serial MRI; molecular characterisation of relapse tumours for transgene expression and canonical MAPK signalling; copy-number and expression analysis identifying Yap1 amplification; functional studies of Yap1 and…
GENE-013.population: Mouse: doxycycline-inducible Kras G12D (iKras) PDAC model, monitoring tumours at least 8 mm in diameter at the time of doxycycline withdrawal; relapse tumours and derived cells; corroboration in human PDAC models.
GENE-013.n: 28 iKras mice followed after doxycycline withdrawal; 20 relapsed
GENE-013.time_frame: Relapse observed 9-47 weeks after oncogene extinction; published 2014
GENE-013.finding: Consistent with prior work, doxycycline withdrawal produced tumour regression detectable by MRI by three weeks (Fig 1A). However, 70% of mice (20/28) escaped doxycycline withdrawal with evidence of relapse between 9 and 47 weeks, and median survival was 36.6 weeks versus 15.4 weeks for iKras mice maintained on continuous doxycycline (P<0.0001, Fig 1B). Approximately half of the relapse tumours examined re-expressed the iKras transgene with restored canonical downstream signalling ('iKras+ relapse tumours'); the remainder were devoid of Kras G12D expression and of downstream canonical MAPK signalling and instead showed amplification and overexpression of the transcriptional co-activator Yap1. Functional studies established that Yap1 and the transcription factor Tead2 drive Kras G12D-independent tumour maintenance, with the Yap1/Tead2 complex acting cooperatively with E2F transcription…
GENE-013.effect: Relapse in 70% (20/28) of mice after Kras extinction; median survival 36.6 vs 15.4 weeks (P<0.0001); roughly half of relapses Kras-independent with Yap1 amplification
GENE-013.limitations: Transgenic inducible model, not a drug; complete and instantaneous oncogene removal is more absolute than any pharmacological KRAS inhibition, so the escape route observed may not be the one that dominates under partial drug inhibition in patients; human corroboration is in models, not patients.
GENE-013.interpretation: Strong within the preparation: the relapse is a natural experiment inside a controlled genetic system, and the Yap1/Tead2 requirement was tested functionally rather than only inferred from correlation.

glosses.growth-control: A mouse study in which 70 percent of tumors relapsed after Kras was switched off, half of them using YAP1 instead.
glosses.kras: A mouse study in which 70 percent of tumors relapsed after Kras extinction, half via YAP1 amplification.

GENE-014.citation: Raghavan S, Winter PS, Navia AW, et al. Microenvironment drives cell state, plasticity, and drug response in pancreatic cancer. Cell. 2021;184(25):6119-6137.e26.
GENE-014.clinical_status: not applicable (reframes subtype as a state); subtype-directed therapy is not standard US practice (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-014.design: Paired single-cell profiling of patient tissue and derived organoids; benchmarking of model systems against the in-vivo reference map; principal-component and signature-correlation analysis of malignant cells; copy-number confirmation of malignancy in organoid cells; perturbation of organoid…
GENE-014.population: Human metastatic PDAC: single-cell RNA sequencing of metastatic biopsies from 23 patients (13 male, 10 female) collected October 2018 to December 2020, with matched patient-derived organoid models; earlier organoid cohort for bulk genomic/transcriptomic analysis collected May 2015 to January 2018;…
GENE-014.n: 23 patients for single-cell profiling; matched organoid models; serial samples in at least one patient (PANFR0489)
GENE-014.time_frame: Biopsies collected Oct 2018-Dec 2020; culture perturbations over passages; published 2021
GENE-014.finding: Published bulk PDAC signatures clustered mainly into classical-like (clade 1) and basal-like (clade 2) groups (Fig 1C). Model systems were strongly biased: primary and metastatic tissues contained both classical-like and basal-like tumours, whereas cell lines were predominantly basal-like and organoids were nearly entirely classical-like. At single-cell resolution scBasal and scClassical programmes were NOT mutually exclusive: the authors identified cells intermediate for both signatures, co-expressing features of each to varying degrees and poorly described by prior bulk subtypes, defining a new intermediate co-expressor (IC) state and a tripartite cell-state framework (Fig 2B, S3A, S3B, S3F). Basal-like cells associated with TGF-beta signalling, WNT signalling, EMT and cell-cycle progression; classical-like cells with epithelial and pancreatic lineage programmes and AKT-associated…
GENE-014.effect: Organoids nearly entirely classical-like vs cell lines predominantly basal-like despite tissues containing both; TGF-beta exposure shifts organoids toward IC/basal states
GENE-014.limitations: 23 patients, predominantly liver metastases, limiting site-specific generalisation (acknowledged by the authors); no lineage tracing, so transitions are inferred; the microenvironmental and immune mapping components overlap the TME domain and are cited rather than claimed here.
GENE-014.interpretation: Mixed and unusually informative: observational for the in-vivo state map, but interventional for plasticity, since changing the culture environment changed the state. That makes the plasticity claim causal in the preparation.

glosses.sub-environments: A single-cell study of 23 patients' metastases showing an intermediate cell state and showing experimentally that TGF-beta and culture conditions move cells between states.
glosses.smad4: A single-cell study of 23 patients' metastases and organoids showing TGF-β shifts tumor cells toward basal-like states.
glosses.cell-states: A single-cell study of 23 patients' metastases and matched organoids defining an intermediate state and showing culture and TGF-β move cells between states.
glosses.epigenetic: A single-cell study showing culture conditions and TGF-β move pancreatic cancer cells between classical and basal states.

GENE-015.citation: Shin JH, Kim SY, Lee J, et al. Mutant p53 regulates reversible subtype plasticity in pancreatic cancer. Cell Mol Life Sci. 2025;83(1):31.
GENE-015.design: Organoid experiments comparing growth and transcriptional programmes under normal versus acute environmental stress conditions; transcriptomic profiling with subtype scoring using an integrated marker set derived from the intersection of human and mouse PDAC subtype gene sets (classical 143 genes;…
GENE-015.population: Genetically defined pancreatic cancer organoid models differing in p53 status (missense mutant p53 versus p53-deficient/control), with validation against public human and mouse PDAC expression datasets.
GENE-015.n: Not enumerated as a single n in the accessed text; genetically defined organoid lines with replicate conditions
GENE-015.time_frame: Short-term organoid culture experiments (acute stress and recovery); published 2025
GENE-015.finding: Mutant p53 conferred a selective growth advantage specifically under acute environmental stress and drove a molecular transition toward a basal-like state. Transcriptomic analysis showed that under stress, organoids expressing mutant p53 adopted a basal-like gene expression programme - the poor-prognosis PDAC subtype. Critically, the molecular subtype reverted to classical once organoids were returned to normal growth conditions, establishing that the transcriptional plasticity arises from acute changes in the tissue microenvironment rather than from a fixed genetic switch. The authors situate this within the established subtype biology: classical PDAC retains epithelial identity and highly expresses endodermal lineage transcription factors such as GATA6 and HNF4A, while basal-like PDAC activates squamous-lineage programmes with upregulation of deltaNp63 (a TP63 isoform) and a YAP/TEAD…
GENE-015.effect: Direction and reversibility established; quantitative effect sizes not enumerated in the accessed text
GENE-015.limitations: Organoid-only; no in-vivo or patient validation; the specific stressors and TP53 missense alleles used are not fully characterised in the accessed text; effect sizes not reported numerically in the accessed abstract/results text.
GENE-015.interpretation: Interventional within the preparation and, unusually, bidirectional: the same cells were pushed into and out of the basal state, which is the design that most firmly separates plasticity from clonal selection.

glosses.tp53: An organoid study in which mutant p53 drove a reversible shift to the basal-like state under stress.
glosses.cell-states: An organoid study in which mutant p53 drove a reversible shift to the basal-like state under stress.
glosses.epigenetic: An organoid study in which mutant p53 drove a reversible shift to the basal-like state under stress.

GENE-016.citation: Park W, Chen J, Chou JF, et al. Genomic Methods Identify Homologous Recombination Deficiency in Pancreas Adenocarcinoma and Optimize Treatment Selection. Clin Cancer Res. 2020;26(13):3239-3247.
GENE-016.clinical_status: Germline BRCA1/2 testing in PDAC is guideline-recommended practice in the US and supports platinum and maintenance PARP-inhibitor decisions; the PARP-inhibitor trial evidence itself belongs to the TX domain (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-016.design: Retrospective cohort with progression-free and overall survival analysis by homologous-recombination mutation (HRm) status, grouped three ways: germline versus somatic; core (BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2) versus non-core (the other 14 of 17 genes, including ATM, BAP1, BARD1, BLM, BRIP1, CHEK2, FAM175A,…
GENE-016.population: Human advanced-stage PDAC: 262 patients who had both germline and somatic targeted gene sequencing (MSK-IMPACT platform).
GENE-016.n: 262 patients; 50 (19%) with HRD; biallelic HRm n=29, monoallelic n=21, wild-type n=212; core HRm n=31 (biallelic core n=22); germline biallelic n=23; somatic HRm n=10
GENE-016.finding: Among 262 patients, 50 (19%) had HRD - 15% germline and 4% somatic. Germline and somatic groups were analysed together because they did not differ in genomic instability or outcome. Median follow-up 21.9 months (95% CI 1.4-57.0). For the whole cohort median overall survival was 15.5 months (95% CI 14.6-19) and median progression-free survival 7 months (95% CI 6.1-8.1). Patients with HRD had improved PFS versus no HRD when treated with first-line platinum (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.67, P<0.01) but NOT with first-line non-platinum therapy. On multivariable analysis HRD patients had improved OS regardless of first-line treatment, though most had platinum exposure at some point. Zygosity and gene class mattered: biallelic HRm (n=29) had higher LST scores than both wild-type (n=212, P=0.0006) and monoallelic HRm (n=21, P=0.005); both core HRm (n=31, P=0.04) and biallelic core HRm (n=22,…
GENE-016.effect: HRD prevalence 19% (15% germline, 4% somatic); PFS benefit with first-line platinum HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.29-0.67, P<0.01); biallelic and core HRm enriched for instability and benefit
GENE-016.limitations: Authors note that computing mutational signatures or structural variants from targeted sequencing has known limitations and that low mutation numbers in PDAC made Sig3/LST assessment difficult, limiting the clinical applicability of signature approaches on targeted panels; they also acknowledge possible survivorship bias. Somatic HRD subgroup was small (n=10). Single-institution platform.
GENE-016.interpretation: Observational treatment comparison. The internal contrast (HRD benefit appears with platinum but not with non-platinum therapy) is the strongest causal signal available short of randomisation, because it shows treatment-specificity rather than general prognosis.

glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: A 262-patient study of advanced disease in which 19 percent had homologous-recombination deficiency and platinum benefit tracked biallelic and core-gene loss.
glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: A 262-patient study in which 19 percent had homologous-recombination deficiency and platinum benefit tracked biallelic and core-gene loss.
glosses.atm-noncore: A 262-patient study showing biallelic and core-gene loss, not gene label, track genomic instability and platinum benefit.
glosses.oxaliplatin: A cohort of 262 people with advanced pancreatic cancer in which homologous-recombination defects predicted benefit from platinum but not from non-platinum chemotherapy.
glosses.olaparib: A 262-patient study of advanced pancreatic cancer in which 19 percent had homologous-recombination deficiency and benefit tracked biallelic and core-gene loss rather than gene name.

GENE-017.citation: Golan T, Kanji ZS, Epelbaum R, et al. Overall survival and clinical characteristics of pancreatic cancer in BRCA mutation carriers. Br J Cancer. 2014;111(6):1132-1138.
GENE-017.clinical_status: Platinum-based chemotherapy in germline BRCA-mutated advanced PDAC is widely practised in the US and underpins maintenance PARP-inhibitor eligibility; the randomised PARP-inhibitor evidence belongs to the TX domain (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-017.design: Retrospective multi-institution cohort of BRCA carriers with pancreatic cancer; overall survival from diagnosis to death, censored at last follow-up; comparison of patients exposed to platinum-based treatment at any point versus those receiving only non-platinum chemotherapy, analysed within and…
GENE-017.population: Human pancreatic cancer in germline BRCA mutation carriers: 71 participants (69% BRCA2 n=49, 30% BRCA1 n=21, 1% both n=1); mean age at diagnosis 60.3 years (range 33-83); 81.7% (n=58) with any family history of malignancy; 30% (n=21) underwent primary resection; Jewish and non-Jewish patients…
GENE-017.n: 71 participants; 58 evaluable for OS after excluding 12 who received experimental therapy and 1 with missing data; stage 3/4 platinum n=22 versus non-platinum n=21
GENE-017.time_frame: Retrospective; diagnosis dates not enumerated in accessed text; published 2014
GENE-017.finding: Median OS for the 58 evaluable patients was 14 months (95% CI 10-23). No significant difference between Jewish patients (13 months, 95% CI 5-22) and non-Jewish patients (15 months, 95% CI 8-60). By stage and treatment: stage 3 patients treated with platinum (n=8) had median OS over 48 months versus 10 months for non-platinum (n=7), P=0.205 - not significant. Stage 4 platinum-treated (n=14) median OS 15 months versus 7 months for non-platinum (n=14), P=0.276 - not significant. Only when stages 3 and 4 were combined did the difference reach significance: median OS 22 months for platinum-exposed (n=22) versus 9 months for non-platinum (n=21), P<0.039 (Fig 2C, Table 4). Patients treated with PARP inhibitors on unpublished clinical trials were excluded from the OS analysis.
GENE-017.effect: Pooled stage 3+4: median OS 22 vs 9 months (P<0.039); stage-specific comparisons not significant (P=0.205 and P=0.276)
GENE-017.limitations: Retrospective, multi-institution with heterogeneous regimens; very small strata; platinum exposure defined as any time during the disease course rather than first line; 13 of 71 patients excluded from OS analysis including 12 on experimental (PARP-inhibitor) therapy, which plausibly removes some of the best responders.
GENE-017.interpretation: Weak-to-moderate. Non-randomised exposure comparison in small strata; the direction is consistent and biologically expected but the magnitude is unreliable.

glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: The founding 71-patient BRCA cohort in which platinum-exposed carriers lived a median 22 versus 9 months, significant only when stages were pooled.

GENE-018.citation: Peeters SLJ, de With M, Imholz ALT, et al. Survival of patients with colorectal or pancreatic cancer who received UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan in the Netherlands (2017-2024): a retrospective, multicentre cohort study. Lancet Reg Health Eur. 2026;64:101629.
GENE-018.clinical_status: UGT1A1-guided irinotecan dose reduction is recommended in the US label for poor metabolisers (see regulatory_checks); routine pre-emptive genotyping is more established in the Netherlands than in the US (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-018.design: Retrospective multicentre cohort study. Inclusion required irinotecan dosed according to UGT1A1 genotype in at least cycle 1 - initial dose intensity 100% plus or minus 10% for intermediate/normal metabolisers (IM/NM) and 70% plus or minus 10% for poor metabolisers (PM). Kaplan-Meier estimates and…
GENE-018.population: Human: patients with pancreatic cancer or colorectal cancer treated with UGT1A1 genotype-guided irinotecan dosing at six Dutch hospitals between August 2017 and April 2024. Primary analysis 779 patients, of whom 396 had pancreatic cancer (including 41 poor metabolisers) and 383 had colorectal…
GENE-018.n: 779 patients in primary analysis (76, 9.8%, poor metabolisers); 210 additional patients excluded from the primary analysis
GENE-018.time_frame: Treatment August 2017 to April 2024; median follow-up 27.8 months; published 2026
GENE-018.finding: Of 779 patients, 76 (9.8%) were poor metabolisers. Median follow-up 27.8 months (95% CI 15.2-31.6). No significant differences in PFS or OS between 30% dose-reduced PMs and fully dosed IM/NMs (stratified log-rank PFS P=0.54; OS P=0.42). In stratified Cox regression the adjusted hazard ratio for PMs versus IM/NMs was 1.02 (95% CI 0.78-1.32, P=0.90) for PFS and 1.10 (95% CI 0.82-1.48, P=0.51) for OS. Severe toxicity rates were comparable between 30% dose-reduced PMs and fully dosed IM/NMs (P=0.59) - that is, the dose reduction brought high-risk patients down to the toxicity level of normal metabolisers. No significant PFS or OS differences between dose-reduced PMs and fully dosed IM/NMs were seen in the standard FOLFIRINOX or modified FOLFIRINOX subgroups (Suppl Fig S5, Tables S13/S14), nor between intermediate and normal metabolisers.
GENE-018.effect: PFS adjusted HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.78-1.32); OS adjusted HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.82-1.48); severe toxicity equalised (P=0.59)
GENE-018.limitations: Retrospective; 210 patients excluded from primary analysis; mixed tumour types and regimens; toxicity captured only for the first three cycles; no untreated-genotype control arm receiving full dose (by design, since genotype-guided dosing was standard in these hospitals).
GENE-018.interpretation: Observational non-inferiority-style comparison. It cannot prove equivalence, but the confidence intervals bound any survival penalty from a 30% reduction as small, which is the practical question.

glosses.nausea-bowel: A Dutch study of 779 patients found UGT1A1 genotype-guided irinotecan dose reduction equalized severe toxicity without worsening survival.
glosses.fever-infection: A Dutch study of 779 patients found UGT1A1 genotype-guided irinotecan dose reduction equalized severe toxicity without worsening survival.
glosses.ugt1a1-dpyd: A 779-patient cohort in which a 30 percent irinotecan reduction normalized toxicity in UGT1A1 poor metabolizers without a survival cost.
glosses.nalirifox: Dutch cohort of 779 patients, about half with pancreatic cancer, in which a 30% irinotecan dose cut for UGT1A1 poor metabolizers equalized severe toxicity without a survival penalty.
glosses.irinotecan: A Dutch cohort of 779 people, half with pancreatic cancer, in which 30% dose reduction for UGT1A1 poor metabolizers equalized toxicity without a survival penalty.
glosses.growth-factor-support: A Dutch multicenter cohort of 779 people, 396 with pancreatic cancer, in which UGT1A1 poor metabolizers given 30 percent less irinotecan had toxicity and survival similar to fully dosed normal metabolizers.

GENE-019.citation: Gambron M, Deslandes B, Lamoril J, et al. DPYD and UGT1A1 Genotype-Based Dosing for Fluoropyrimidines and Irinotecan Chemotherapy: A Real-World Variant-Specific Analysis. Int J Cancer. 2026;159(10):2512-2524.
GENE-019.clinical_status: DPYD and UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing is recommended by EMA and Dutch guidance as described in the accessed text; current US labelling for capecitabine directs pre-treatment DPYD testing while noting no FDA-authorised DPYD test exists (see regulatory_checks, checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-019.design: Retrospective real-world cohort comparing a standard-of-care group genotyped AFTER treatment (n=97, therefore dosed without genotype information) against a genotype-driven group genotyped BEFORE treatment with Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group-driven dosing (n=81). Endpoints: clinically…
GENE-019.population: Human: 178 unselected cancer patients carrying a matched actionable DPYD and/or UGT1A1 genotype and treated with fluoropyrimidines and/or irinotecan. Variants: DPYD rs3918290 (*2A, c.1905+1G>A), rs55886062 (*13, c.1679T>G), rs67376798 (c.2846A>T), rs56038477 (c.1236G>A, HapB3, tagging…
GENE-019.finding: Genotype-driven dosing significantly reduced overall clinically relevant toxicity: 16.0% versus 43.3% (P<0.001). Variant-specific results diverged sharply. DPYD c.1905+1G>A heterozygotes: clinically relevant toxicities occurred only in the standard-of-care group (61.5% versus 0%, P=0.007), with lower RDI in standard of care despite the full starting dose (41%, IQR 13-62, versus 48%, IQR 46-50; P=0.425) - i.e. toxicity forced dose cuts anyway. DPYD c.2846A>T heterozygotes: standard of care had slightly higher RDI (63%, IQR 54-80, versus 50%, IQR 43-50; P=0.007) but double the toxicity rate (67% versus 27%, P=0.092). UGT1A1 *28 homozygotes: genotype-driven dosing reduced toxicity (21.1% versus 45.7%, P=0.086) while preserving comparable RDI (58%, IQR 50-69, versus 61%, IQR 41-76; P=0.906). By contrast, DPYD c.1236G>A (HapB3) heterozygotes showed no clear toxicity benefit from…
GENE-019.effect: Overall clinically relevant toxicity 16.0% vs 43.3% (P<0.001); HapB3 heterozygotes: no toxicity benefit but RDI 50% vs 82% (P<0.001)
GENE-019.limitations: Small per-variant subgroups; mixed cancer types and regimens (not PDAC-specific); retrospective; RDI is a proxy for exposure, not a pharmacokinetic measurement; multiple comparisons without stated adjustment.
GENE-019.interpretation: Observational with a useful quasi-control: the comparator group was genotyped only after treatment, so genotype did not influence their dosing, which approximates an untreated-information control. Still subject to era and centre effects.

glosses.nausea-bowel: A French real-world study found DPYD and UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing cut clinically relevant toxicity from 43.3% to 16.0%.
glosses.fever-infection: A French real-world study found DPYD and UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing cut clinically relevant toxicity from 43.3% to 16.0%.

GENE-020.citation: Weissmueller S, Manchado E, Saborowski M, et al. Mutant p53 drives pancreatic cancer metastasis through cell-autonomous PDGF receptor beta signaling. Cell. 2014;157(2):382-394.
GENE-020.clinical_status: preclinical; PDGFRB inhibition is not an established PDAC therapy in the US (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-020.design: Loss-of-function of mutant p53 by shRNA in cells that retain it; motility and inverted collagen-gel invasion assays; transcriptional profiling to find mutant-p53-dependent genes; targeted shRNA mini-screen of upregulated genes to find those that phenocopy loss of invasion; mechanistic dissection…
GENE-020.population: Mouse: KPC pancreatic cancer cell lines (Kras G12D plus mutant p53) with stable shRNA knockdown of mutant p53 versus control shRNA targeting Renilla, compared against a p53-null KP(fl)C line (Pdx-Cre; LSL-Kras G12D/+; LSL-p53 loxP/+); in-vivo lung colonisation assays; human expression datasets for…
GENE-020.n: Three independent KPC+sh.Ctrl lines versus mutant-p53 knockdown; 441 differentially expressed genes identified; in-vivo cohorts not enumerated in accessed text
GENE-020.time_frame: In-vitro assays over days; in-vivo lung colonisation over weeks; published 2014
GENE-020.finding: Sustained mutant p53 expression was required to maintain the pro-metastatic phenotype. Knockdown of mutant p53 in KPC cells reduced motility to the level of p53-null KP(fl)C cells (Fig 1A) and significantly abrogated the enhanced invasiveness seen in control KPC cells in an inverted collagen invasion assay (Fig 1B). Transcriptional profiling identified 441 genes significantly up- or down-regulated on depletion of endogenous mutant p53, with pathway analysis showing about 20% of affected genes in the 'cellular movement' functional class. An shRNA mini-screen of upregulated genes identified PDGF receptor beta (PDGFRB) as both necessary and sufficient to mediate the effects. Mutant p53 induced PDGFRB cell-autonomously by inhibiting a p73/NF-Y complex that represses PDGFRB in p53-deficient, non-invasive cells. Blocking PDGFRB by RNA interference or small-molecule inhibition prevented…
GENE-020.effect: Mutant p53 knockdown reduces motility to p53-null levels; crenolanib reduces lung nodules in mutant-p53 but not p53-null cells; ~20% of 441 mutant-p53-dependent genes in the 'cellular movement' class
GENE-020.limitations: Mouse cell lines; experimental metastasis assays rather than spontaneous metastasis endpoints for the drug experiment; human PDGFRB survival correlation is observational; specific TP53 missense alleles tested are limited.
GENE-020.interpretation: Strong and well-controlled: the p53-null comparator is the key control, since it shows the drug effect is not a general anti-metastatic action but is contingent on mutant p53. Necessity and sufficiency were both tested.

glosses.tp53: A mouse-cell study showing mutant p53 drives invasion and metastasis through PDGFR-beta, reversed by removing the mutant protein.

GENE-021.citation: Martinelli P, Carrillo-de Santa Pau E, Cox T, et al. GATA6 regulates EMT and tumour dissemination, and is a marker of response to adjuvant chemotherapy in pancreatic cancer. Gut. 2017;66(9):1665-1676.
GENE-021.clinical_status: GATA6 immunohistochemistry is not standard-of-care for adjuvant regimen selection in the US (checked 2026-10-08); used as a research stratifier.
GENE-021.design: Combined loss- and gain-of-function manipulation of GATA6 in PDAC cell lines with GATA6 ChIP-seq and RNA-seq to define direct targets; in-vivo cell dissemination assays; immunohistochemical GATA6 histoscoring in primary tumours with survival analysis; biomarker-by-treatment interaction analysis in…
GENE-021.population: Human PDAC cell lines with GATA6 silencing and overexpression; primary human patient samples, a subset of which came from the ESPAC-3 randomised adjuvant trial comparing 5-fluorouracil/leucovorin with gemcitabine; in-vivo dissemination models.
GENE-021.n: ESPAC-3 subset and additional primary cohorts (exact n not enumerated in accessed text); GATA6 survival strata reported as low/medium/high
GENE-021.time_frame: ESPAC-3 adjuvant trial specimens with trial follow-up; in-vitro experiments over days; published 2017
GENE-021.finding: GATA6 inhibited epithelial-mesenchymal transition in vitro and cell dissemination in vivo, with a unique pro-epithelial and anti-mesenchymal function; its transcriptional regulation was direct and also indirect through other EMT transcription factors. GATA6 is lost in tumours, in association with altered differentiation and acquisition of a basal-like molecular phenotype, which the authors describe as an epithelial-to-epithelial (ET2) transition rather than a classical EMT. Survival: patients with GATA6-medium and GATA6-high tumours had similar survival (12.7 versus 13.1 months) and both significantly longer than GATA6-low tumours (4.6 months, P=0.003, Fig 6A,B); low GATA6 was associated with significantly increased death risk on univariable analysis (HR 5.39, 95% CI 2.3 to 12.x as reported in the accessed text). GATA6 levels were not significantly associated with the…
GENE-021.effect: GATA6-low median OS 4.6 months vs 12.7-13.1 months for medium/high (P=0.003); univariable HR 5.39; GATA6 predicts outcome in the 5-FU/leucovorin arm only
GENE-021.limitations: Specimen subset of a randomised trial rather than the full trial population; immunohistochemical histoscore cut-points are assay-dependent; the dissociation between the patient-level predictive signal and the absent cell-level causal effect is unresolved; exact sample numbers not enumerated in the accessed text.
GENE-021.interpretation: Mixed. Causal in the preparation for GATA6's control of the epithelial programme and dissemination (bidirectional manipulation plus ChIP-seq). For the treatment interaction it is a biomarker analysis nested in a randomised trial, which is stronger than a single-arm correlation but still a subgroup analysis. The authors' own negative in-vitro…

glosses.cell-states: A study showing GATA6 maintains the classical state, that GATA6-low tumors had 4.6-month median survival, and that GATA6 predicted 5-FU but not gemcitabine outcome in trial specimens.
glosses.epigenetic: A study showing GATA6 directly maintains the classical epithelial program and suppresses dissemination.

GENE-022.citation: Aguirre AJ, Nowak JA, Camarda ND, et al. Real-time Genomic Characterization of Advanced Pancreatic Cancer to Enable Precision Medicine. Cancer Discov. 2018;8(9):1096-1111.
GENE-022.clinical_status: Germline and somatic profiling of advanced PDAC is guideline-recommended practice in the US (checked 2026-10-08); the specific matched therapies vary in approval status.
GENE-022.design: Prospective IRB-approved biopsy protocol for time-sensitive whole-exome and RNA sequencing from small-volume needle biopsies (~15-20 mg tissue per biopsy), with an initial 10-patient workflow optimisation phase followed by 69 patients sequenced in a CLIA-certified laboratory and return of selected…
GENE-022.population: Human advanced PDAC: 79 patients biopsied on the prospective PancSeq protocol between March 2015 and June 2017; median age 64; 96% metastatic; most treatment-naive. Biopsies percutaneous by interventional radiology (n=72), endoscopic ultrasound (n=6) or intraoperative (n=1), median 5 cores (range…
GENE-022.n: 79 patients biopsied; actionability denominators reported as 71
GENE-022.finding: Therapeutically relevant genomic alterations were identified in 48% (34/71) of patients and pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline alterations in 18% (13/71). Turnaround in the CLIA phase averaged 39 days (range 16-67) from clinically indicated biopsies and 28 days (range 15-51) for research-only biopsies. Complication rate was low, with one self-limited hepatic subcapsular haematoma. Pathological and sequencing-based tumour cellularity estimates correlated only moderately (0.386, 95% CI 0.195-0.548, P=0.00016), consistent with other studies. Illustrative cases included a patient with KRAS p.G12R, TP53 p.M246fs and somatic BRCA2 p.LS298fs who received first-line FOLFIRINOX with CA19-9 normalisation and a complete radiographic response within 5 months, and a patient treated with the ERK1/2 inhibitor ulixertinib under a single-patient IND in whom cfDNA droplet-digital PCR showed rapid…
GENE-022.effect: Therapeutically relevant alterations 48% (34/71); pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline 18% (13/71); median turnaround 28-39 days
GENE-022.limitations: Single institution; 79 patients; no outcome comparison between those who received matched therapy and those who did not; turnaround times of 28-39 days are long relative to PDAC tempo (testing logistics proper belong to the DIAG domain); case reports cannot establish efficacy.
GENE-022.interpretation: Descriptive yield estimate from a prospective protocol. The individual-patient pharmacodynamic cases are anecdotal but mechanistically informative.

glosses.molecular-testing: A prospective sequencing program finding therapeutically relevant alterations in 48 percent and germline variants in 18 percent.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A prospective biopsy-to-sequencing protocol in advanced pancreatic cancer showing moderate agreement between pathologist and sequencing estimates of tumor content.

GENE-023.citation: Winter JM, Tang LH, Klimstra DS, et al. Failure patterns in resected pancreas adenocarcinoma: lack of predicted benefit to SMAD4 expression. Ann Surg. 2013;258(2):331-335.
GENE-023.clinical_status: SMAD4 status is not used in the US to select local versus systemic therapy intensification (checked 2026-10-08); the idea that it could be remains investigational.
GENE-023.design: Retrospective tissue-microarray immunohistochemistry study. SMAD4 expression scored as present or lost in tumour cells; conventional pathological features recorded (lymph node metastases, positive resection margin, poor grade, tumour size); recurrence pattern determined from medical records and…
GENE-023.population: Human resected PDAC: tissue microarray of 127 patients selected for either short (<12 months) or long (>30 months) survival after resection.
GENE-023.n: 127 resected patients (56 short survivors, 71 long survivors); 12 patients without recurrence excluded from the regression
GENE-023.time_frame: Retrospective with post-resection follow-up imaging; published 2013
GENE-023.finding: Loss of SMAD4 expression was identified in 40 of 127 patients (32%). Recurrence patterns for the whole cohort: local only n=15 (12%), distant only n=42 (33%), both local and distant n=58 (46%), no recurrence n=12 (9%); the majority failed outside the retroperitoneum (n=100, 79%). SMAD4 loss occurred in 27% of patients with isolated local recurrence, 33% with distant recurrence, 33% with both local and distant recurrence, and 25% of patients without recurrence - no association (Fisher exact, P=0.9). The same null result held in the subgroup of short survivors, whose aggressive phenotype most resembles the advanced-disease populations in which the association was originally reported. On multivariable analysis, regional lymph node metastasis was the only factor associated with development of distant metastases (odds ratio 4.7). For the separate question of distinguishing short from long…
GENE-023.effect: SMAD4 loss 32% (40/127); no association with recurrence pattern (P=0.9); nodal status OR 4.7 for distant metastasis
GENE-023.limitations: Single-institution; 127 patients with extreme-survivor selection; recurrence pattern ascertained retrospectively from records and imaging with variable surveillance intensity; no genotyping, only protein immunohistochemistry as a surrogate for DPC4 genetic status.
GENE-023.interpretation: Negative observational test. A null result in a selected cohort cannot disprove the original association but does bound its generalisability to the resected setting.

glosses.recurrence-meaning: A 127-patient resected series finding no association between SMAD4 loss and the pattern of recurrence.
glosses.smad4: A 127-patient resected series in which SMAD4 loss (32 percent) showed no association with the pattern of recurrence.
glosses.pathology-report: A 127-patient resected series in which SMAD4 loss showed no relationship to the pattern of recurrence.

GENE-024.citation: Witz A, Conroy T, Bazire L, et al. Impact of Tumor Genomic Profile on Adjuvant Chemotherapy Efficacy in Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Molecular Analysis of the PRODIGE-24/CCTG PA6 Trial. J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(26):2517-2528.
GENE-024.clinical_status: mFOLFIRINOX remains the standard adjuvant regimen for fit patients with resected PDAC in the US; this analysis supports no change to that practice (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-024.design: Retrospective molecular analysis nested within a randomised controlled trial. Tumour DNA sequencing of four key PDAC driver genes and 24 homologous-recombination-repair (HRR)-associated genes; single-base-substitution (SBS) mutational signature analysis; transcriptomic subtyping with the PurIST…
GENE-024.population: Human resected PDAC: tumours from patients enrolled in the randomised phase III PRODIGE-24/CCTG PA6 adjuvant trial; tumour DNA sequencing successful in 317 of 350 tumours (168 modified FOLFIRINOX, 149 gemcitabine).
GENE-024.time_frame: Adjuvant trial with DFS/CSS follow-up; molecular analysis published 2026
GENE-024.finding: KRAS mutations were detected in 87.4% of tumours (277/317), with 12.6% KRAS wild-type; 12.6% of KRAS-mutated cases (35/277) had variant read counts below 20. KRAS G12D was the commonest allele at 43.7% (121/277). Other drivers by mutation only: TP53 53.6% (170/317), SMAD4 9.1% (29/317), CDKN2A 6.6% (21/317) - the authors explicitly note that their panel did not call deletions, that CDKN2A deletions are frequent and biologically relevant in PDAC, and that this omission contributed to underestimating SMAD4 and CDKN2A, in agreement with prior work. In the mFFX group the PurIST subtype was prognostic: classical tumours had superior DFS to basal-like tumours (stratified HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.31-0.77). Treatment interaction by KRAS status was significant: among KRAS-mutated patients mFFX significantly improved DFS versus GEM (stratified HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.45-0.79, P<0.001) while no benefit was…
GENE-024.effect: PurIST classical vs basal-like DFS sHR 0.48 (0.31-0.77); mFFX vs GEM in KRAS-mutant sHR 0.60 (0.45-0.79), interaction P=0.010; HRR interaction P=0.568, BRCA interaction P=0.785
GENE-024.limitations: Panel called mutations but not deletions, systematically undercounting CDKN2A and SMAD4; 33 of 350 tumours failed sequencing; subgroup analyses with multiple interaction tests; resected (not advanced) disease, so results do not transfer directly to metastatic treatment selection; gene-level HR annotation without zygosity resolution.
GENE-024.interpretation: Highest in this domain for predictive claims: treatment was randomised, so a biomarker-by-treatment interaction test is interpretable rather than confounded by fitness. Still retrospective and subgroup-based, so it is hypothesis-testing for the pre-specified markers and hypothesis-generating for KRAS.

glosses.what-is-pdac: Sequencing of 317 tumors from a randomized adjuvant trial finding KRAS mutations in 87% and G12D as the commonest allele.
glosses.growth-control: A molecular analysis of 317 resected tumors from a randomized adjuvant trial, with KRAS mutated in 87.4 percent.
glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: A randomized-trial molecular analysis of 317 resected tumors in which TP53 was mutated in 53.6 percent and repair-gene status did not predict mFOLFIRINOX benefit.
glosses.kras: A randomized-trial molecular analysis of 317 resected tumors, 87.4 percent KRAS-mutant, in which only KRAS-mutant patients benefited from adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX over gemcitabine.
glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A randomized-trial molecular analysis in which 12.6 percent were KRAS wild-type and showed no benefit from adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX over gemcitabine.
glosses.cdkn2a: A randomized-trial molecular analysis whose mutation-only panel reported CDKN2A in 6.6 percent, an acknowledged undercount.
glosses.tp53: A randomized-trial molecular analysis of 317 resected tumors, TP53 mutated in 53.6 percent with no prognostic or predictive value.
glosses.smad4: A randomized-trial molecular analysis whose mutation-only panel reported SMAD4 in 9.1 percent, an acknowledged undercount.
glosses.cell-states: A randomized-trial molecular analysis in which classical tumors had better disease-free survival than basal-like within the mFOLFIRINOX arm.
glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: A randomized adjuvant-trial analysis in which repair-gene and BRCA status did not predict mFOLFIRINOX benefit while KRAS status did.
glosses.atm-noncore: A randomized adjuvant-trial analysis in which repair-gene status did not predict mFOLFIRINOX benefit.
glosses.molecular-testing: A randomized-trial molecular analysis whose mutation-only panel under-reported CDKN2A and SMAD4 because it did not call deletions.
glosses.folfirinox: Genomic analysis of 317 PRODIGE 24 tumors: adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX benefit was confined to KRAS-mutated tumors, while BRCA and other repair-gene status did not predict benefit.

GENE-025.citation: Huffman BM, Aguirre AJ, Perez K, et al. A Phase II Trial of Niraparib in Patients with Advanced Pancreatic Cancer Harboring Pathogenic Variants in Homologous Recombination Repair Genes. Clin Cancer Res. 2026;32(9):1666-1677.
GENE-025.clinical_status: phase 2, reported; niraparib is not FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer in the US (checked 2026-10-08). Olaparib maintenance for germline BRCA-mutated metastatic PDAC after platinum is an approved US indication whose trial evidence belongs to the TX domain.
GENE-025.design: Multicentre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial. Niraparib 200 or 300 mg once daily, initial dose determined by weight and platelet count. Primary endpoint 6-month progression-free survival against a pre-established threshold of 17%; secondary endpoints median PFS and objective response rate;…
GENE-025.population: Human advanced pancreatic cancer with germline or somatic pathogenic variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, ATM and/or CHEK2; patients with prior progression on platinum-based therapy were excluded. 32 patients enrolled, 10 women (31%), median age 67.
GENE-025.n: 32 patients: ATM n=14, BRCA2 n=10, CHEK2 n=4, PALB2 n=3, BRCA1 n=2
GENE-025.time_frame: Prospective single-arm trial; longest exposures exceeded 1 year; published 2026
GENE-025.finding: The 6-month PFS was 25% (90% CI 13-41%) for the overall population, exceeding the pre-established 17% threshold and so meeting the primary endpoint. However, median PFS for the entire population was only 2.0 months (95% CI 1.4-3.8) and the objective response rate was 14% (95% CI 4-33%) - a bimodal pattern of mostly rapid progression with a minority of durable benefit. The discriminating finding: all six patients with 6 months or more of PFS and evaluable tumour zygosity had BIALLELIC inactivation of a DNA repair gene. Three patients with biallelic inactivation of ATM and no progression on prior chemotherapy received niraparib for more than one year. The authors conclude that niraparib produced clinically meaningful benefit in a subset and that the prolonged PFS in patients with biallelic ATM loss warrants further investigation.
GENE-025.effect: 6-month PFS 25% (90% CI 13-41%); median PFS 2.0 months (95% CI 1.4-3.8); ORR 14% (95% CI 4-33%); 6/6 durable responders with evaluable zygosity were biallelic
GENE-025.limitations: 32 patients, single arm, no randomisation; 6-month PFS reported with a 90% (not 95%) confidence interval per the trial's design; zygosity was evaluable only in a subset; ATM-dominant enrolment (14/32) limits inference about the other genes; the biallelic-ATM signal rests on three patients.
GENE-025.interpretation: Prospective interventional with a pre-specified endpoint, so the overall activity estimate is sound. The zygosity finding is post-hoc and based on six patients, so it is a strong hypothesis rather than an established selection rule - but it is the right kind of evidence, because it tests the mechanism (biallelic loss) rather than the proxy (gene…

glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: A 32-patient phase 2 trial of niraparib in which all durable responders had lost both copies of a repair gene.
glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: A 32-patient phase 2 niraparib trial in which all durable responders had biallelic loss of a repair gene.
glosses.atm-noncore: A 32-patient phase 2 niraparib trial, median progression-free survival 2.0 months, in which all durable responders had biallelic repair-gene loss, including three with biallelic ATM loss.
glosses.olaparib: A 32-patient phase 2 niraparib trial in which median progression-free survival was 2.0 months and all durable responders had biallelic loss of a repair gene.

GENE-026.citation: Bouchart C, Navez J, Closset J, et al. Favorable histo-molecular remodeling of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma after neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX and stereotactic body radiation therapy. Br J Cancer. 2026;134(5):721-734.
GENE-026.clinical_status: Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX is used in the US for borderline-resectable and locally advanced PDAC; adding SBRT remains investigational, and this analysis is explicitly hypothesis-generating for prospective trials (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-026.design: Comparative histo-molecular characterisation of resected specimens across three treatment exposures using RNA sequencing plus immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence including multiplex panels; transcriptional signature scoring for tumour subtype (classical, basal-like) and stromal state…
GENE-026.population: Human non-metastatic PDAC: residual tumour tissue from 56 resected patients - 17 upfront surgery, 17 neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX (FFX) alone, and 22 FFX followed by radiotherapy (16 stereotactic body radiation therapy, 6 radiochemotherapy).
GENE-026.n: 56 patients (17 upfront surgery, 17 FFX alone, 22 FFX plus radiotherapy of which 16 SBRT)
GENE-026.time_frame: Residual tumour assessed at resection after neoadjuvant therapy; published 2026
GENE-026.finding: Addition of SBRT to FOLFIRINOX favourably remodelled PDAC across stromal, immune, metabolic and molecular features, and unlike radiochemotherapy, SBRT counteracted several detrimental effects induced by FFX alone. Most relevant to tumour-cell biology: FFX plus SBRT enriched tumours for 'Classical' and 'Inactive stroma' signatures - both linked to better prognosis - while REDUCING 'Basal-like' cell enrichment. SBRT promoted COL1A1-driven stromal remodelling while globally preserving T-lymphocyte infiltration including cytotoxic T cells, which remained in close proximity to tumour cells despite increased desmoplasia. The authors identified key SBRT-induced transcriptional alterations as candidate combination targets and conclude the data support prospective validation of this combination in non-metastatic PDAC.
GENE-026.effect: Direction established: FFX+SBRT enriched classical and depleted basal-like signatures relative to comparator exposures; numeric effect sizes per signature not enumerated in the accessed text
GENE-026.limitations: 56 patients across three non-randomised groups; no paired pre- and post-treatment biopsies from the same tumour, so within-tumour change is not demonstrated; the stromal, immune and spatial findings belong substantively to the TME domain and are cited rather than claimed here; signature-level effect sizes not reported numerically in the accessed text.
