GENE-026.interpretation: Observational across non-randomised treatment groups, so the subtype shift is associational at patient level. Its value is as a boundary condition: it demonstrates that measured subtype differs systematically by treatment received, which is what undermines treating subtype as a fixed trait.

glosses.cell-states: A 56-patient resected series in which tumors exposed to FOLFIRINOX plus stereotactic radiotherapy were enriched for classical signatures.

GENE-027.citation: Hunter JC, Manandhar A, Carrasco MA, et al. Biochemical and Structural Analysis of Common Cancer-Associated KRAS Mutations. Mol Cancer Res. 2015;13(9):1325-1335.
GENE-027.design: In-vitro biochemistry and structural biology: substrate binding kinetics, intrinsic and GAP-stimulated GTPase activity, and RAF effector interaction across common KRAS mutants; high-resolution X-ray structures
GENE-027.population: Recombinant human KRAS mutant proteins; X-ray crystallography
GENE-027.n: Panel of common KRAS mutants (G12V, G12R, G13D, Q61L and others)
GENE-027.finding: From the abstract: different KRAS mutations have distinct biochemical behaviours. KRAS G13D showed rapid nucleotide exchange kinetics compared with other mutants analysed, explained by G13D-induced changes in the electrostatic charge distribution of the active site as shown by X-ray crystallography. High-resolution structures were reported for GDP-bound KRAS G12V, G12R and Q61L. The authors state that measurable biochemical properties provide clues for identifying KRAS-driven tumours that preferentially signal through particular effector routes. Numeric kinetic constants were not available in the accessed abstract.
GENE-027.effect: not reported in accessed text (abstract only)
GENE-027.limitations: Abstract only; full text not retrieved, so kinetic values, methods detail and limitations stated by the authors were not examined. Does not count toward phase minimums.
GENE-027.interpretation: Direct biochemical measurement of protein behaviour; no cellular or clinical inference.

glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A biochemical and structural study (abstract only) showing that different KRAS mutants, notably G13D, have distinct nucleotide-exchange behavior.

GENE-028.citation: Iacobuzio-Donahue CA, Fu B, Yachida S, et al. DPC4 gene status of the primary carcinoma correlates with patterns of failure in patients with pancreatic cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2009;27(11):1806-1813.
GENE-028.clinical_status: not applicable; SMAD4-directed treatment intensification remains investigational (checked 2026-10-08)
GENE-028.design: Rapid-autopsy case series correlating end-stage histological features and pattern of failure with KRAS2, TP53 and DPC4 (SMAD4) gene status, assessed in part by Dpc4 immunolabelling as a surrogate for DPC4 genetic status
GENE-028.population: Human pancreatic cancer: rapid autopsies performed on 76 patients with documented pancreatic cancer
GENE-028.finding: From the abstract: at autopsy, 30% of patients died with locally destructive pancreatic cancer and 70% died with widespread metastatic disease. These divergent patterns were unrelated to clinical stage at initial presentation, treatment history, or histopathological features. However, Dpc4 immunolabelling status of carcinoma tissue harvested at autopsy - described as a sensitive marker of DPC4 genetic status - was highly correlated with the presence of widespread metastasis but not with the locally destructive pattern. Exact correlation statistics were not available in the accessed abstract.
GENE-028.effect: 30% locally destructive versus 70% widespread metastatic at autopsy; correlation statistics not reported in accessed text
GENE-028.limitations: Abstract only; full text not retrieved (PMC deposit is PDF-only), so the correlation statistics, immunolabelling criteria and author-stated limitations were not examined. Does not count toward phase minimums. Directly contradicted in the resected setting by GENE-023.
GENE-028.interpretation: Observational association in terminal disease; cannot establish that SMAD4 loss causes the metastatic pattern.

glosses.smad4: A 76-patient rapid-autopsy series (abstract only) linking SMAD4 protein loss to widespread metastatic rather than local disease.
glosses.pathology-report: An abstract-only autopsy series in which SMAD4 loss correlated with widespread metastatic rather than locally destructive disease.

GENE-029.citation: Pishvaian MJ, Blais EM, Brody JR, et al. Overall survival in patients with pancreatic cancer receiving matched therapies following molecular profiling: a retrospective analysis of the Know Your Tumor registry trial. Lancet Oncol. 2020;21(4):508-518.
GENE-029.clinical_status: Molecular profiling of advanced PDAC is guideline-recommended practice in the US; the survival benefit of matched therapy in PDAC has not been demonstrated in a randomised trial (checked 2026-10-08).
GENE-029.design: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively enrolled registry. Commercial molecular profiling with molecular tumour board review (Perthera report) classifying findings as actionable; treating physicians chose therapy. Overall survival calculated from the date of initial diagnosis of…
GENE-029.population: Human pancreatic cancer: patients enrolled in the Know Your Tumor (KYT) registry programme with biopsy-confirmed cancers originating in the pancreas (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, or acinar cell carcinoma); pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours excluded. 1,856 patients…
GENE-029.n: 1,856 referred; 1,082 (58%) received a Perthera report; 189 patients with actionable alterations and adequate follow-up, of whom 46 (24%) received matched therapy and 143 (76%) did not; 488 patients…
GENE-029.time_frame: Registry enrolment with retrospective survival follow-up measured from diagnosis of advanced disease; published 2020
GENE-029.finding: Of more than 1,000 patients tested, the molecular tumour board assessed 26% of molecular profiles as harbouring actionable findings. Median overall survival was significantly longer in the matched-therapy group than the unmatched-therapy group: 2.58 years (95% CI 2.39 to not reached) versus 1.51 years (95% CI 1.33-1.87); HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.26-0.68), P=0.0004 (Fig 2). The no-marker group (n=488) had median overall survival 1.32 years (95% CI 1.25-1.47). Among patients who received two or more lines of therapy, the matched group (n=39) had median OS 1.81 years (95% CI 1.58 to not reached) versus 0.85 years (95% CI 0.63-1.08) for the unmatched group (n=83); HR 0.37 (95% CI 0.22-0.63), P=0.0002 (Fig 3A); the no-marker group with two or more lines (n=288) had 0.73 years (95% CI 0.67-0.84). Progression-free survival in that subgroup was 10.93 months (95% CI 7.83 to not reached) for matched…
GENE-029.effect: Matched vs unmatched median OS 2.58 vs 1.51 years, HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.26-0.68), P=0.0004; DDR with PARP/ATR inhibitor 3.81 vs 1.71 years, HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.24-0.94); 26% actionable; 46/1,856 (2%) actually received matched therapy
GENE-029.limitations: Retrospective, no randomisation, no preplanned analysis; actionability defined by a proprietary molecular tumour board; matched-therapy definition for DDR excluded platinum chemotherapy; heterogeneous treatment lines and eras; 2% of referred patients drive the headline result.
GENE-029.interpretation: Weak for the survival claim. This is a non-randomised comparison among a 2% subset selected by physician choice and survival long enough to be profiled, reported, and then treated. The authors themselves label the analyses post hoc and exploratory. Its solid contribution is the denominators: how often profiling is completed and acted upon.

glosses.molecular-testing: The Know Your Tumor registry in which 26 percent of profiles were actionable but only 2 percent of referred patients received matched therapy.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: The Know Your Tumor registry analysis, in which matched therapy was associated with longer survival in an unplanned comparison among 2 percent of referred patients.

TME-001.citation: Olive KP, Jacobetz MA, Davidson CJ, Gopinathan A, McIntyre D, Honess D, et al. Inhibition of Hedgehog signaling enhances delivery of chemotherapy in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer. Science. 2009;324(5933):1457-1461.
TME-001.clinical_status: Rationale for IPI-926 and vismodegib trials that were subsequently negative/terminated; hedgehog inhibition is not an approved PDAC therapy (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-001.design: Preclinical perturbation and pharmacokinetic study: perfusion imaging (lectin/doxorubicin IF, contrast ultrasonography, DCE-MRI), HPLC measurement of gemcitabine active metabolite, and randomised survival intervention
TME-001.population: KPC autochthonous mouse PDAC (Kras-LSL-G12D/+;Trp53-LSL-R172H/+;Pdx1-Cre); transplanted-tumour comparators; human PDAC tissue for vascular comparison
TME-001.n: Perfusion cohorts n=6-8 per model; survival cohorts of KPC mice (vehicle vs gemcitabine vs IPI-926 vs IPI-926+gem)
TME-001.time_frame: 8-12 day pharmacodynamic treatment; survival followed from enrolment at defined tumour size until death
TME-001.finding: KPC tumours were poorly perfused: only 32% of CD31+ vessels were lectin-labelled vs 78% in transplanted tumours and 100% in normal pancreas (Fig 2, fig S). DCE-MRI showed reduced Gd-DTPA extravasation in KPC (n=6) vs transplanted (n=6) tumours (Fig 2E,F). The active gemcitabine metabolite dFdCTP was detectable in transplanted tumours and control tissues but undetectable in KPC tumours (table S1). IPI-926 reduced desmoplastic stroma and transiently increased CD31+ content (by day 4), with a significant increase in proliferating endothelial cells; combination IPI-926/gemcitabine increased intratumoral gemcitabine concentration and cleaved caspase-3 (Fig 3-4). Median survival with IPI-926/gem was 25 days vs 11 days with gemcitabine from enrolment (P=.001 log-rank; HR 0.157).
TME-001.effect: Median survival 11 to 25 days from enrolment (HR 0.157); vessel patency 32% vs 78-100%; dFdCTP undetectable vs detectable
TME-001.limitations: Short treatment window; benefit explicitly transient; survival measured from enrolment with large established tumours; single mouse model; no human efficacy data
TME-001.interpretation: Interventional in a genetically faithful autochthonous model: supports a causal chain from stromal content to perfusion to drug delivery to transient tumour response, in mice

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study showing pancreatic tumors arising in their own pancreas were poorly perfused and contained no detectable active gemcitabine, and that a short course of a hedgehog-pathway inhibitor transiently improved delivery and survival.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Mouse study showing pancreatic tumors arising in their own pancreas were poorly perfused and contained no detectable active gemcitabine, and that a short course of a hedgehog-pathway inhibitor transiently improved delivery and survival.
glosses.stroma-lessons: The founding mouse study showing pancreatic tumors are poorly perfused and that a hedgehog-pathway drug transiently raised chemotherapy levels and survival.

TME-002.citation: Rhim AD, Oberstein PE, Thomas DH, Mirek ET, Palermo CF, Sastra SA, et al. Stromal elements act to restrain, rather than support, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Cell. 2014;25(6):735-747.
TME-002.clinical_status: Preclinical; retrospectively explains the failure of hedgehog-inhibitor trials in PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-002.design: Genetic deletion plus pharmacologic replication and a randomised antiangiogenic intervention; lineage tracing (YFP) to separate epithelial from stromal compartments
TME-002.population: Autochthonous mouse PDAC: Pdx1-Cre;Kras-LSL-G12D/+;p53-fl/+;Rosa26-LSL-YFP (PKCY) with epithelial Shh deletion (ShhPKCY); KPC mice for pharmacologic arm; human PDAC tissue for vascular density
TME-002.n: Survival cohorts of PKCY vs ShhPKCY vs Shh-fl/+ PKCY; IPI-926 vs vehicle KPC cohorts; DC101 trial: PKCY n=10 DC101/n=11 IgG, ShhPKCY n=13 DC101/n=10 IgG
TME-002.time_frame: Lifetime survival studies; DC101 from ultrasound-detected tumour to death
TME-002.finding: ShhPKCY median survival 3.61 +/- 1.97 months vs 6.17 +/- 2.65 months for PKCY (p<0.001 log-rank); heterozygous Shh-fl/+ PKCY 4.14 +/- 1.57 months (p=0.004). Mean survival from first tumour detection 6.5 +/- 2.7 vs 19.2 +/- 5.27 days (p<0.001); gross metastasis 43.4% vs 15.3% (p=0.039). Stroma was reduced (fewer YFP-negative aSMA+ myofibroblasts, 3.7 +/- 0.7 vs higher in controls) and CD45+ myeloid cells fell. CD31+ vessels rose to 32.4 +/- 7.2 vs 11.2 +/- 3.8 per high-power field, with better doxorubicin delivery, reduced LC3+ autophagy and increased proliferation. Chronic IPI-926 alone shortened KPC survival to 121 vs 156 days (p<0.0001) despite identical model, drug, dose, route and schedule to the earlier study. DC101 did not affect PKCY survival but improved ShhPKCY survival from 12.5 to 22.4 days from enrolment (p=0.028) with large necrosis, fewer CD31+ vessels and more LC3+…
TME-002.effect: Median survival 6.17 to 3.61 months with Shh deletion; 156 to 121 days with chronic IPI-926; vessel density ~2.9-fold higher; metastasis 15.3% to 43.4%
TME-002.limitations: Mouse only; Gli1 fell but Ptch1 was unchanged, so Hh pathway suppression was partial; no difference in tumour VEGF expression was found, leaving the mechanism of increased angiogenesis unexplained
TME-002.interpretation: Genetic loss-of-function plus independent pharmacologic replication in the same model, with lineage labelling; strong causal evidence that Hh-driven stroma restrains progression in mice, and a documented failed replication of the earlier intervention result

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study in which deleting the hedgehog signal from cancer cells, or blocking the pathway continuously, reduced the stroma, increased blood-vessel density and shortened survival with more metastasis.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Mouse study in which deleting the hedgehog signal from cancer cells, or blocking the pathway continuously, reduced the stroma, increased blood-vessel density and shortened survival with more metastasis.
glosses.stroma-lessons: The mouse study that reversed the picture: deleting the hedgehog signal or blocking it long-term shortened survival and increased metastasis.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A mouse study showing that reducing hedgehog-driven stroma shortened survival and roughly tripled metastasis, which retrospectively explains why hedgehog-inhibitor trials failed.

TME-003.citation: Provenzano PP, Cuevas C, Chang AE, Goel VK, Von Hoff DD, Hingorani SR. Enzymatic targeting of the stroma ablates physical barriers to treatment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Cell. 2012;21(3):418-429.
TME-003.clinical_status: Basis for PEGPH20 trials; the confirmatory phase 3 (HALO-301) was negative and PEGPH20 is not FDA-approved (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-003.design: In vivo physiological measurement (needle-guided pressure transducer), intravital multiphoton imaging, vascular morphometry, and a randomised survival intervention
TME-003.population: KC (Kras-G12D;Pdx1-Cre) and KPC autochthonous mouse PDAC; normal mouse pancreas; human PDAC tissue for HA and vascular morphometry
TME-003.n: IFP: normal pancreas n=8, KPC n=7, KC n=4; doxorubicin delivery n=3-4 per group; survival: control n=16, gemcitabine n=16, PEGPH20 n=15, gemcitabine+PEGPH20 n=14
TME-003.time_frame: Acute (2-24 h) pressure and delivery endpoints; survival from enrolment to death
TME-003.finding: Normal pancreas interstitial fluid pressure 8-13 mmHg (mean 10.4, n=8); PDAC IFP 75-130 mmHg (mean 99 mmHg KPC n=7; 87 mmHg KC n=4), exceeding typical arteriolar (40-80) and capillary (15-40) pressures (Fig 2D). Over 80% of normal pancreatic vessels had patent lumens vs ~25% in PDAC; after PEGPH20 ~71% of CD31+ vessels had discernible lumens with increased diameter (Fig 2G). A single IV dose lowered IFP significantly within 2 h, approaching normal by 24 h, and produced a >6.5-fold increase in doxorubicin fluorescence intensity (p=0.013 KPC n=4/group; p=0.04 KC n=3/group). Median overall survival from enrolment: gemcitabine 55.5 days vs gemcitabine+PEGPH20 91.5 days (p=0.004); PEGPH20 alone 63 days (p=0.1, not significant). Metastatic burden was lower with the combination (p=0.014).
TME-003.effect: IFP ~10 to ~99 mmHg in tumour; ~6.5-fold increase in drug delivery; median survival 55.5 to 91.5 days with added PEGPH20
TME-003.limitations: Mouse models; PEGPH20 monotherapy was not significantly beneficial; no human pressure measurements; survival from enrolment not from birth
TME-003.interpretation: Direct physiological measurement plus acute enzymatic perturbation with immediate reversal: strong causal support that HA-dependent pressure limits perfusion and drug delivery in mice

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study that measured interstitial pressure of 75-130 mmHg in pancreatic tumors against 8-13 mmHg in normal pancreas and showed a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme lowered it, reopened vessels and improved drug delivery and survival.
glosses.matrix-pressure: Mouse study that measured interstitial pressure of 75-130 mmHg in pancreatic tumors against 8-13 mmHg in normal pancreas and showed a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme lowered it, reopened vessels and improved drug delivery and survival.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Mouse study that measured interstitial pressure of 75-130 mmHg in pancreatic tumors against 8-13 mmHg in normal pancreas and showed a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme lowered it, reopened vessels and improved drug delivery and survival.
glosses.stroma-lessons: The mouse study measuring interstitial pressures of 75 to 130 mmHg in tumors against 8 to 13 in normal pancreas, reversed by a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme.

TME-004.citation: Van Cutsem E, Tempero MA, Sigal D, Oh DY, Fazio N, Macarulla T, et al. Randomized phase III trial of pegvorhyaluronidase alfa with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine for patients with hyaluronan-high metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. J Clin Oncol. 2020;38(27):3185-3194.
TME-004.clinical_status: Negative phase 3; PEGPH20 development in PDAC discontinued and the drug is not FDA-approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-004.design: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, 2:1 allocation, stratified by geographic region; hierarchical testing of OS, then PFS, then ORR
TME-004.population: Adults with untreated, metastatic, hyaluronan-high pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1, at least one measurable metastasis
TME-004.n: 494 randomly assigned; 492 in intention-to-treat (327 PEGPH20 + nab-paclitaxel/gemcitabine, 165 placebo + AG); safety population 325 vs 156; 330 deaths at cutoff
TME-004.time_frame: Enrolment 14 March 2016 to 26 December 2018; analysis at 330 deaths
TME-004.finding: Median OS 11.2 months (PEGPH20+AG) vs 11.5 months (placebo+AG); stratified HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.80-1.27), P=.97. Median PFS 7.1 vs 7.1 months, HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.75-1.26). ORR 47% vs 36% (ORR ratio 1.29, 95% CI 1.03-1.63). Any-grade events more frequent with PEGPH20: peripheral oedema 61.8% vs 33.3%, muscle spasms 51.4% vs 9.6%, myalgia 28.9% vs 14.7%, arthralgia 19.4% vs 11.5%. Grade >=3 with >=2% excess: fatigue 16.0% vs 9.6%, muscle spasms 6.5% vs 0.6%, hyponatraemia 8.0% vs 3.8%; musculoskeletal events any grade 75.4% vs 46.2%, grade >=3 13.2% vs 5.1%. The trial assumed a placebo median OS of 8.5 months and was powered (93%) for HR 0.67.
TME-004.effect: HR for death 1.00 (95% CI 0.80-1.27); absolute ORR difference +11 percentage points with no survival difference
TME-004.limitations: 2:1 allocation reduces comparator precision; the placebo arm outperformed the historical assumption (11.5 vs 8.5 months), reducing power to detect a modest effect; no on-treatment pressure or perfusion measurements in patients
TME-004.interpretation: Randomised, placebo-controlled, biomarker-selected phase 3: the strongest available clinical test of the HA/pressure/delivery model, and it excludes a clinically meaningful survival benefit

glosses.clear-scan: The randomized HALO-301 trial in which adding hyaluronidase raised the response rate from 36% to 47% with no survival difference.
glosses.reading-trial-results: The randomized HALO-301 trial in which adding hyaluronidase raised the response rate from 36% to 47% with a hazard ratio for death of 1.00.
glosses.matrix-pressure: Double-blind phase 3 trial in 492 people with hyaluronan-high metastatic pancreatic cancer: adding pegvorhyaluronidase alfa raised the response rate from 36% to 47% but gave a hazard ratio for death of 1.00 with substantially more musculoskeletal toxicity.
glosses.nutrient-scavenging: The randomized phase 3 HALO-301 trial of a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme added to chemotherapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer, which raised response rate without improving survival.
glosses.stroma-lessons: The randomized phase 3 trial in 492 patients showing hyaluronidase added to chemotherapy gave more tumor shrinkage and no survival difference, with added side effects.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: The randomized HALO-301 trial in which hyaluronidase raised the response rate from 36% to 47% with a hazard ratio for death of 1.00.

TME-005.citation: Ohlund D, Handly-Santana A, Biffi G, Elyada E, Almeida AS, Ponz-Sarvise M, et al. Distinct populations of inflammatory fibroblasts and myofibroblasts in pancreatic cancer. J Exp Med. 2017;214(3):579-596.
TME-005.clinical_status: Preclinical; no CAF-state-directed therapy is approved (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-005.design: Tissue spatial profiling (immunofluorescence, RNA in situ hybridisation) plus a three-dimensional organoid/stellate-cell co-culture and trans-well system with secretome, ELISA, qPCR and RNA-seq readouts
TME-005.population: Human PDAC tissue (n=3-4 per stain), KPC and KPCY mouse tumours, murine pancreatic stellate cells, mouse and patient-derived tumour organoids
TME-005.n: Human PDAC n=3-4 per assay; co-culture experiments 2-4 biological replicates per condition
TME-005.finding: In human PDAC most FAP+ fibroblasts expressed low aSMA, while a FAP+ aSMA-high subpopulation formed a periglandular ring in direct contact with cancer-cell clusters (Fig 1A-B); the same gradient occurred in KPC mice. YFP lineage labelling in KPCY mice showed these aSMA-high cells were not epithelium-derived, excluding EMT (Fig 1E). In 3D co-culture, direct contact induced aSMA-high IL-6-low myCAFs, whereas trans-well (no contact) culture induced aSMA-low IL-6-high iCAFs secreting IL-6, IL-11 and LIF (Figs 2-3; flow gating of aSMA-high/IL-6-low vs aSMA-low/IL-6-high populations). Co-culture conditioned media activated STAT3 in organoids, and pSTAT3 was detectable in KPC tumour tissue (Fig 3G).
TME-005.effect: Reported as fold change in myCAF/iCAF induction relative to PSC monoculture and as ELISA concentrations; the qualitative switch depends on physical proximity rather than dose
TME-005.limitations: Small human sample numbers; no in vivo manipulation of CAF state; functional consequences for tumour growth not tested here
TME-005.interpretation: Controlled perturbation of a single variable (physical contact vs diffusible signals only) in a reductionist co-culture, mapped back onto spatial anatomy in human and mouse tissue: supports causation for state induction in a preparation

glosses.fibroblast-states: Organoid and stellate-cell co-culture study showing direct contact produces myofibroblastic fibroblasts while separation by a membrane produces inflammatory, cytokine-secreting ones, with the same spatial pattern in human tumors.
glosses.sub-environments: A culture and tissue study showing that pancreatic fibroblasts adopt a myofibroblastic state on direct contact with cancer cells and an inflammatory state at a distance.

TME-006.citation: Balachandran VP, Luksza M, Zhao JN, Makarov V, Moral JA, Remark R, et al. Identification of unique neoantigen qualities in long-term survivors of pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2017;551(7681):512-516.
TME-006.clinical_status: Biomarker/target-discovery stage; informs neoantigen vaccine development (owned by the IMMUNE domain); no approved application (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-006.design: Retrospective comparative cohort with whole-exome sequencing, in silico neoantigen prediction, 9-parameter multiplexed immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence on tissue microarrays, T-cell receptor sequencing, ex vivo T-cell reactivity assays, and a prespecified neoantigen fitness (quality) model…
TME-006.population: Treatment-naive, surgically resected human PDAC: stage-matched long-term survivors (LTS, median survival 6 years, n=82) vs short-term survivors (STS, median survival 0.8 years, n=68), MSKCC cohort, with validation in an independent dataset
TME-006.n: n=82 LTS and n=68 STS in the primary cohort; one rapid-autopsy patient for clonal dynamics
TME-006.time_frame: Resected primaries with long-term follow-up (LTS median 6 years); autopsy sampling at death
TME-006.finding: Median 38 predicted neoantigens per tumour (Extended Data Fig 3a). Patients with BOTH the highest predicted neoantigen number and either the greatest CD3+CD8+ infiltrate or the most polyclonal T-cell repertoire had the longest survival (median not reached); neither parameter alone stratified survival (Fig 2a), and this held independent of adjuvant chemotherapy (Extended Data Fig 3d). The neoantigen quality model, but not the quantity model, significantly separated LTS from STS independent of confounders and adjuvant chemotherapy (Fig 2b) and did so in two independent datasets. LTS were enriched for high-quality neoantigens and for neoantigens in MUC16/CA125. More than 94% of intratumoral T-cell clones were unique to tumours (Fig 1d). Intratumoral and lasting circulating T-cell reactivity to high-quality and MUC16 neoantigens was detected in LTS, including clones cross-reactive with…
TME-006.effect: Survival stratification required the conjunction of high neoantigen number and high CD8 infiltrate (median survival not reached vs 0.8 years in STS); quality model significant, quantity model not
TME-006.limitations: Retrospective; selection of exceptional survivors; prediction algorithms rather than measured HLA-peptide presentation for most antigens; immunoediting inference from n=1
TME-006.interpretation: Human observational with mechanistic corroboration (T-cell reactivity ex vivo, clonal loss at metastasis): establishes association and makes immunoediting plausible, but does not prove that immunity caused the long survival

glosses.t-cells: A comparison of 82 long-term and 68 short-term survivors of resected pancreatic cancer showing that long survival went with the conjunction of high-quality predicted neoantigens and a dense CD8 T-cell infiltrate.
glosses.antigen-presentation: A comparison of 82 long-term and 68 short-term survivors of resected pancreatic cancer showing that long survival went with the conjunction of high-quality predicted neoantigens and a dense CD8 T-cell infiltrate.
glosses.cea-ca125: A study of long-term survivors enriched for immune responses against neoantigens in MUC16, the molecule measured as CA-125.

TME-007.citation: O'Reilly EM, Oh DY, Dhani N, Renouf DJ, Lee MA, Sun W, et al. Durvalumab with or without tremelimumab for patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a phase 2 randomized clinical trial. JAMA Oncol. 2019;5(10):1431-1438.
TME-007.clinical_status: Negative phase 2; checkpoint inhibitors are not approved for mismatch-repair-proficient PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-007.design: Randomised, open-label, two-arm phase 2 trial with a prespecified response-rate gate for expansion to part B
TME-007.population: Adults with metastatic PDAC after exactly one prior fluorouracil- or gemcitabine-based line, enrolled at 21 sites in 6 countries
TME-007.n: 65 patients randomised (32 combination, 32 monotherapy evaluable for safety; 64 treated); median age 61 years; 34 of 65 (52%) men
TME-007.time_frame: Enrolment 26 November 2015 to 23 March 2017; treatment up to 12 months
TME-007.finding: Objective response rate 3.1% (95% CI 0.08-16.22) with durvalumab plus tremelimumab and 0% (95% CI 0.00-10.58) with durvalumab monotherapy, against a prespecified 10% gate; part B was therefore not conducted. Median PFS was 1.5 months in both arms (95% CI 1.2-1.5 and 1.3-1.5). Median OS 3.1 months (95% CI 2.2-6.1) combination vs 3.6 months (95% CI 2.7-6.1) monotherapy. Grade >=3 treatment-related adverse events in 7 of 32 (22%) combination vs 2 of 32 (6%) monotherapy; 4 of 64 (6%) discontinued for treatment-related adverse events.
TME-007.effect: ORR 3.1% vs 0%; median PFS 1.5 months in both arms; median OS 3.1 vs 3.6 months
TME-007.limitations: Small, open-label, no chemotherapy comparator arm, pretreated population, no biomarker selection; cannot exclude benefit in selected subgroups (e.g., MMR-deficient)
TME-007.interpretation: Randomised clinical trial with a prespecified futility gate: excludes a clinically meaningful single-agent or dual-checkpoint effect in this (pretreated, unselected) population

glosses.t-cells: A randomized phase 2 trial in 65 patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer after one prior line, in which durvalumab with or without tremelimumab produced a 3.1 percent response rate and no survival benefit.

TME-008.citation: Commisso C, Davidson SM, Soydaner-Azeloglu RG, Parker SJ, Kamphorst JJ, Hackett S, et al. Macropinocytosis of protein is an amino acid supply route in Ras-transformed cells. Nature. 2013;497(7451):633-637.
TME-008.clinical_status: Preclinical; no macropinocytosis-directed drug approved (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-008.design: Cell-biological and metabolic-tracing perturbation study plus in vivo xenograft pharmacologic intervention
TME-008.population: Human pancreatic (MIA PaCa-2, BxPC-3) and bladder carcinoma cell lines with mutant versus wild-type RAS; K-Ras-V12-transformed NIH 3T3 cells; mouse PDAC xenografts and an autochthonous mouse pancreatic cancer model
TME-008.n: Cell experiments in replicate; xenograft arms treated 7 days (MIA PaCa-2 and BxPC-3 tumours, waterfall plots of volume change)
TME-008.finding: Oncogenic RAS-expressing pancreatic and bladder lines showed elevated fluid-phase (TMR-dextran) uptake, inhibited dose-dependently by EIPA and attenuated by K-Ras knockdown; T24 (H-Ras-G12V) exceeded wild-type 5637 cells. Macropinocytosis occurred in vivo in both xenograft and autochthonous pancreatic tumours. Internalised protein was proteolysed to amino acids including glutamine that entered central carbon metabolism. Albumin supplementation rescued proliferation under subphysiological glutamine, and this rescue was abolished by EIPA (Fig 4a); the antiproliferative effect of EIPA was reversed by added glutamine or by 7 mM dimethyl alpha-ketoglutarate (Fig 4b). EIPA treatment for 7 days reduced tumour volume change versus vehicle in MIA PaCa-2 and BxPC-3 xenografts (Fig 4e waterfall plots).
TME-008.effect: Reported as fold changes in uptake and relative proliferation; in vivo effect reported as percent change in tumour volume over 7 days rather than a single summary statistic in the accessed text
TME-008.limitations: Mostly cell lines and NIH 3T3 models; no human clinical data; no selective macropinocytosis inhibitor
TME-008.interpretation: Pharmacologic and genetic loss-of-function with metabolic rescue: establishes that protein macropinocytosis supplies amino acids and supports growth in a preparation, with in vivo plausibility

glosses.nutrient-scavenging: A cell-biology and metabolic-tracing study showing that mutant RAS drives cells to drink extracellular protein and digest it into usable amino acids, with the same gulping seen in mouse pancreatic tumors.

TME-009.citation: Erkan M, Reiser-Erkan C, Michalski CW, Deucker S, Sauliunaite D, Streit S, et al. Cancer-stellate cell interactions perpetuate the hypoxia-fibrosis cycle in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Neoplasia. 2009;11(5):497-508.
TME-009.clinical_status: Not applicable (mechanistic/pathology study); antiangiogenic therapy is not standard in PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-009.design: Quantitative immunohistochemical morphometry of human tissue plus normoxia/hypoxia monoculture and coculture experiments with ELISA, immunoblot, qPCR and endothelial growth assays
TME-009.population: Human pancreatic tissue: normal pancreas, chronic pancreatitis and PDAC; primary human pancreatic stellate cells and pancreatic cancer cell lines
TME-009.n: Human tissue cohorts for microvessel density across the three diagnoses (per-group numbers not stated in the accessed text); in vitro assays in replicate
TME-009.time_frame: Cross-sectional human tissue; in vitro exposures of hours to days
TME-009.finding: Microvessel density by CD31 was five-fold lower in fibrotic chronic pancreatitis (P<.001) and four-fold lower in PDAC (P<.01) than in normal pancreas (Fig 2D). At the invasive front, stellate cells deposited a periostin-rich matrix around periacinar capillaries, and periostin expression preceded aSMA expression. Hypoxia increased stellate-cell activity and roughly doubled secretion of periostin, type I collagen, fibronectin and VEGF. Cancer cells induced stellate-cell VEGF secretion to 390 +/- 60% of baseline (P<.001), while stellate cells increased cancer-cell endostatin production to 210 +/- 14% (P<.001) via matrix-metalloproteinase-dependent cleavage. Stellate cells promoted endothelial cell growth in vitro, whereas cancer cells alone or cocultured with stellate cells suppressed it.
TME-009.effect: 4-5 fold reduction in microvessel density in diseased pancreas; VEGF 390% and endostatin 210% of baseline in coculture
TME-009.limitations: Group sizes not stated in accessed text; no in vivo perturbation; antibody-based quantification; older cohort without molecular subtyping
TME-009.interpretation: Human observational morphometry plus in vitro perturbation: establishes the hypovascular/hypoxic phenotype in human tissue and provides a candidate mechanism, without proving directionality in patients

glosses.desmoplasia: Human tissue study finding four- to fivefold lower microvessel density in pancreatic cancer and chronic pancreatitis than in normal pancreas, with hypoxia increasing stellate-cell matrix and VEGF secretion.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Human tissue study finding four- to fivefold lower microvessel density in pancreatic cancer and chronic pancreatitis than in normal pancreas, with hypoxia increasing stellate-cell matrix and VEGF secretion.

TME-010.citation: Carstens JL, Correa de Sampaio P, Yang D, Barua S, Wang H, Rao A, et al. Spatial computation of intratumoral T cells correlates with survival of patients with pancreatic cancer. Nat Commun. 2017;8:15095.
TME-010.clinical_status: Not applicable (prognostic/pathology study); no approved spatial-immune biomarker in PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-010.design: Retrospective multiplexed immunofluorescence of a tissue microarray (8 markers: aSMA, collagen-I, cytokeratin 8, CD3, CD8, CD4, Foxp3, DAPI) with spatial point-process statistics (L-function area under curve within defined radii) correlated to overall survival
TME-010.population: 132 patients with PDAC who underwent pancreatectomy with curative intent at MD Anderson without neoadjuvant therapy; uninvolved pancreatic tissue as comparator
TME-010.time_frame: Resected primaries with post-operative survival follow-up; cross-sectional tissue
TME-010.finding: Over 80% of CD3+ cells were CD4+ or CD8+ in both tumour and uninvolved tissue, but the CD8 proportion of CD3+ cells fell from 67% in uninvolved to 47% in tumour (P<0.001) while CD4 rose from 17% to 36% (P<0.001) (Fig 3e). High infiltration of cytotoxic T cells and of CD4+ effector T cells correlated with significantly longer survival, whereas Treg or 'other' T-cell infiltration did not (Fig 4b-g). Using the spatial L-function, high cytotoxic T-cell infiltration specifically within a 20 um radius of cytokeratin-8+ cancer cells significantly correlated with prolonged survival. Collagen-I deposition did not reduce cytotoxic T-cell infiltration; higher collagen-I correlated with the presence of T-cell subpopulations, so the desmoplastic reaction as measured by aSMA and collagen-I appeared to have little impact on cytotoxic T-cell infiltration.
TME-010.effect: Reported as Kaplan-Meier separation on median-dichotomised spatial AUC; CD8 fraction 67% to 47% and CD4 17% to 36% between uninvolved and tumour tissue
TME-010.limitations: Single-centre retrospective; no functional or exhaustion markers; dichotomisation at median; resected (earlier-stage) patients only
TME-010.interpretation: Human observational with quantitative spatial statistics: supports that proximity (not just abundance) of cytotoxic T cells tracks outcome, and provides a negative test of the collagen-exclusion hypothesis

glosses.t-cells: A spatial analysis of 132 resected human pancreatic tumors showing that cytotoxic T cells close to cancer cells tracked longer survival and that collagen density did not reduce their infiltration.

TME-011.citation: Biffi G, Oni TE, Spielman B, Hao Y, Elyada E, Park Y, Preall J, Tuveson DA. IL1-induced JAK/STAT signaling is antagonized by TGFbeta to shape CAF heterogeneity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Discov. 2019;9(2):282-301.
TME-011.clinical_status: Preclinical; IL-1 blockade in PDAC is investigational, not approved (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-011.design: Ligand/receptor expression mapping in sorted cells, organoid-PSC co-culture with cytokine addition and neutralisation, CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of IL-1alpha in organoids and of IL-1R1 in stellate cells, and in vivo orthotopic transplantation
TME-011.population: Mouse and human pancreatic stellate cells; mouse and human PDAC tumour organoids; KPC mouse tumours (sorted CAFs and epithelium, single-cell RNA-seq); orthotopically grafted organoids in nu/nu mice
TME-011.n: Sorted CAF/epithelial populations from KPC tumours; three independent IL-1alpha knockout organoid lines versus Rosa26-targeted controls in orthotopic grafts
TME-011.finding: Il1a and Tnf were higher in sorted KPC epithelial cancer cells than CAFs, whereas Il1r1 and Tnfrsf1a were predominantly in CAFs; flow cytometry confirmed higher IL-1R1 protein on CAFs (Fig 1A-B). Tumour and metastatic organoids and KPC monolayers secreted detectable IL-1alpha and TNF-alpha by ELISA; fibroblast-conditioned media did not. IL-1alpha induced Il1a, Il6, Lif, Cxcl1 and Csf3 in mouse and human stellate cells while reducing myofibroblastic genes Ctgf and Acta2 (Fig 2A); IL-1beta and TNF-alpha did the same. IL-1alpha neutralisation reduced iCAF marker induction by organoid-conditioned media, partly restored myofibroblastic genes (Fig 2B) and impaired proliferation of iCAF-cultured but not myCAF-cultured stellate cells (Fig 2C). IL-1alpha-knockout organoids induced significantly lower iCAF markers and significantly higher aSMA in co-cultured stellate cells (Fig 2D); IL-1R1…
TME-011.effect: Reported as significant differences in marker gene expression and in orthotopic tumour size across three independent knockout lines; absolute effect sizes not given as single summary statistics in the accessed text
TME-011.limitations: Immunodeficient recipients for the key in vivo experiment; no survival endpoint; collagen and aSMA unchanged in vivo despite a growth effect, leaving the in vivo mediator uncertain
TME-011.interpretation: Converging genetic (two independent knockouts, ligand and receptor side), pharmacologic (neutralising antibody) and in vivo transplantation evidence: strong causal support for IL-1 as the iCAF-inducing signal and TGF-beta as its antagonist, in a preparation

glosses.fibroblast-states: Mouse and human cell study identifying tumor-derived interleukin-1 as the signal that induces inflammatory fibroblasts, and TGF-beta as the signal that blocks it by removing the interleukin-1 receptor.
glosses.smad4: A mouse and cell study showing TGF-β drives fibroblasts into the myofibroblast state and blocks the inflammatory fibroblast route.

TME-012.citation: Ozdemir BC, Pentcheva-Hoang T, Carstens JL, Zheng X, Wu CC, Simpson TR, et al. Depletion of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts and fibrosis induces immunosuppression and accelerates pancreas cancer with reduced survival. Cancer Cell. 2014;25(6):719-734.
TME-012.clinical_status: Preclinical; anti-CTLA-4 has no approved role in mismatch-repair-proficient PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-012.design: Conditional genetic cell-ablation at two disease stages (PanIN and established PDAC), with histopathology, hypoxia staining, flow cytometry/RNA-seq immune profiling, and rescue experiments using gemcitabine or anti-CTLA-4
TME-012.population: PKT (Ptf1a-Cre;Kras-G12D;Tgfbr2-fl) and KPC autochthonous mouse PDAC crossed to aSMA-tk mice for ganciclovir-inducible ablation of proliferating aSMA+ myofibroblasts; resected human PDAC for aSMA scoring
TME-012.n: Multiple mouse cohorts across early and late depletion settings; human cohort of resected untreated PDAC scored for interstitial aSMA (Table S1)
TME-012.time_frame: Depletion from PanIN stage or from established PDAC until death; rescue therapy during depletion
TME-012.finding: Ablation achieved ~80% depletion of proliferating myofibroblasts and ~80% of total myofibroblasts (Fig 1F-G) without depleting aSMA+ cells in kidney, lung, bowel, heart or liver (Fig S1D-E). Depletion at either the PanIN or the PDAC stage produced significantly more invasive, undifferentiated, necrotic tumours and significantly reduced survival in both early and late depletion groups (Fig 1B-E, 1H). Tumour weight fell and pulmonary emboli were more frequent (Fig S1F-H). Pericyte number (NG2) and vascular leakage (FITC-dextran) were unchanged, but pimonidazole-adduct hypoxia increased dramatically (Fig 4B-C, S4E-F), with EMT and cancer-stem-cell features. Immune profiling showed reduced overall immune infiltration but a significant fall in CD4+Foxp3- effector T cells and rise in CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs, lowering the Teff/Treg ratio (Fig 6B-D), with increased Foxp3 and Ctla4 expression (Fig 6E,…
TME-012.effect: ~80% myofibroblast depletion; significantly shortened survival at both depletion stages; hypoxia markedly increased; anti-CTLA-4 reversed the survival deficit
TME-012.limitations: Thymidine-kinase ablation requires cell proliferation so quiescent CAFs persist; no distinction between myCAF and iCAF states; human analysis retrospective with semi-quantitative scoring
TME-012.interpretation: Targeted genetic cell ablation with a pharmacologic rescue that reverses the phenotype: strong causal evidence in mice that myofibroblasts restrain PDAC via immune-mediated mechanisms, plus a human correlative anchor

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study in which ablating about 80% of proliferating myofibroblasts made tumors more invasive and more hypoxic, expanded regulatory T cells and shortened survival, with low stromal alpha-smooth-muscle actin also marking worse survival in resected human tumors.
glosses.fibroblast-states: Mouse study in which ablating about 80% of proliferating myofibroblasts made tumors more invasive and more hypoxic, expanded regulatory T cells and shortened survival, with low stromal alpha-smooth-muscle actin also marking worse survival in resected human tumors.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Mouse study in which ablating about 80% of proliferating myofibroblasts made tumors more invasive and more hypoxic, expanded regulatory T cells and shortened survival, with low stromal alpha-smooth-muscle actin also marking worse survival in resected human tumors.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A mouse study in which ablating most myofibroblasts made tumors more aggressive and shortened survival, with the harm reversed by blocking CTLA-4.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A mouse study in which depleting about 80 percent of myofibroblasts shortened survival, increased hypoxia and expanded regulatory T cells, with the survival loss reversed by anti-CTLA-4.

TME-013.citation: Steele NG, Biffi G, Kemp SB, Zhang Y, Drouillard D, Syu L, et al. Inhibition of hedgehog signaling alters fibroblast composition in pancreatic cancer. Clin Cancer Res. 2021;27(7):2023-2037.
TME-013.clinical_status: Preclinical; sonidegib is FDA-approved for basal cell carcinoma, not PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-013.design: Pharmacologic Smoothened inhibition plus gain- and loss-of-function genetics, with CyTOF, flow cytometry, single-cell RNA-seq, Gli1-lacZ lineage reporting and immunohistochemistry
TME-013.population: Orthotopic 7940b murine PDAC in C57BL/6J and Gli1-lacZ reporter mice; KPC mice; iKC-Shh inducible Shh-overexpression mice; human PDAC single-cell RNA-seq fibroblasts
TME-013.n: Orthotopic cohorts (5x10^4 cells implanted, 12 days of gavage from day 6); KPC cohorts treated 2 weeks with ultrasound tumour-volume monitoring; human scRNA-seq fibroblast dataset
TME-013.finding: Hedgehog target genes (GLI1, PTCH1, PTCH2, HHIP) plus SMO, GAS1, CDON and BOC were enriched in PDAC fibroblasts rather than epithelium, and were higher in myCAFs than iCAFs in both mouse and human single-cell data. SHH overexpression promoted tumour growth; LDE225 impaired tumour growth. LDE225 reduced myCAF numbers and increased iCAF numbers. Immune profiling after 2 weeks of LDE225 in KPC mice showed significantly increased Ly6C+Ly6G- monocytic immature myeloid cells, PD-L1+ macrophages and CD206+ macrophages (Fig 5B, S5A). Total CD3+, CD4+ and CD8+ infiltration trended lower without reaching significance (Fig S5C), but as a percentage of CD3+ cells, CD8+ T cells significantly decreased while CD4+ and CD25+CD4+ cells increased (Fig 5C); immunohistochemistry confirmed fewer CD8+ T cells and more FOXP3+ Tregs in LDE225-treated KPC tumours (Fig 5D-G).
TME-013.effect: Direction and significance reported per population; absolute percentages not given as summary statistics in the accessed text
TME-013.limitations: Short treatment windows; no survival endpoint in the orthotopic arm; immune analysis in KPC only; apCAF population not separately perturbed
TME-013.interpretation: Pharmacologic perturbation with matched genetic gain/loss of function and single-cell resolution: supports a causal link from hedgehog signalling to CAF state to immune composition in mice, with human expression correspondence

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study showing hedgehog target genes are concentrated in myofibroblastic fibroblasts and that blocking the receptor Smoothened shifted fibroblast composition towards the inflammatory state while reducing CD8 T cells and increasing regulatory T cells.
glosses.fibroblast-states: Mouse study showing hedgehog target genes are concentrated in myofibroblastic fibroblasts and that blocking the receptor Smoothened shifted fibroblast composition towards the inflammatory state while reducing CD8 T cells and increasing regulatory T cells.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A mouse study showing Smoothened inhibition shifts fibroblasts from the myofibroblastic to the inflammatory state and reduces CD8 T cells.

TME-014.citation: DuFort CC, DelGiorno KE, Carlson MA, Osgood RJ, Zhao C, Huang Z, et al. Interstitial pressure in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is dominated by a gel-fluid phase. Biophys J. 2016;110(9):2106-2119.
TME-014.clinical_status: Not applicable (physiological measurement study); informs but does not change clinical practice (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-014.design: Paired, simultaneous in vivo pressure measurement by two physically distinct methods (modified wick-in-needle for free fluid; Millar piezoelectric pressure-catheter transducer, 330-460 um, range -50 to 300 mmHg, for either phase), with enzymatic depletion and a cardiac-cessation control
TME-014.population: Normal mouse tissues (pancreas head and tail), autochthonous KPC mouse PDAC, allografts of primary KPC-derived cell lines, and BxPC3/HAS3 hyaluronan-synthase-overexpressing xenografts
TME-014.n: Autochthonous PDA: pressure-catheter n=7, wick-in-needle n=5; normal pancreas head n=6 (PC) and n=8 (WN), tail n=4 each; allografts from two independently derived cell lines
TME-014.time_frame: Acute measurements; PEGPH20 effects within 2 h to steady state
TME-014.finding: In the same autochthonous KPC tumours, the pressure catheter recorded 76 +/- 4.2 mmHg (n=7) while the wick-in-needle recorded only 12 +/- 3.0 mmHg (n=5). Normal pancreas pressure-catheter values were 2.6 +/- 0.44 mmHg (head, n=6) and -0.73 +/- 0.6 mmHg (tail, n=4); wick-in-needle values were -0.22 +/- 0.33 and -0.60 +/- 0.55 mmHg. Autochthonous KPC tumours had significantly higher catheter-measured pressure than allografts of their own derived cell lines (43 +/- 9.0 and 44 +/- 5.3 mmHg for two lines). Cardiac cessation changed catheter pressure by only -3.5 +/- 1.1 mmHg (autochthonous) and -2.1 +/- 0.5 mmHg (xenograft), showing the pressure is not vascular in origin. PEGPH20 depleted interstitial HA, eliminated the gel-fluid phase, significantly reduced tumour water content at 2 h, and equalised the two measurement methods at steady state (final catheter pressures 2.1 and 1.9 mmHg).…
TME-014.effect: 76 vs 12 mmHg between methods in the same tumours; pressure falls to ~2 mmHg after HA depletion; <4 mmHg of the pressure is vascular
TME-014.limitations: No human measurements; anaesthetised laparotomy conditions; probe diameter large relative to interstitial structures; does not address solid stress from cells, which a separate literature attributes the compression to
TME-014.interpretation: Method-discriminating paired measurement plus enzymatic removal of the candidate molecule and a cardiac-arrest control: strong causal and mechanistic identification of HA-dependent gel fluid as the pressure source, in mice

glosses.matrix-pressure: Mouse measurement study showing the interstitial pressure of pancreatic tumors is carried by a hyaluronan-held gel rather than free fluid, reading 76 mmHg by one probe and 12 mmHg by another in the same tumors.

TME-015.citation: Chauhan VP, Martin JD, Liu H, Lacorre DA, Jain SR, Kozin SV, et al. Angiotensin inhibition enhances drug delivery and potentiates chemotherapy by decompressing tumour blood vessels. Nat Commun. 2013;4:2516.
TME-015.clinical_status: Losartan is FDA-approved for hypertension (US), not for PDAC; oncologic use is investigational, checked 2026-10-08
TME-015.design: Correlative matrix-versus-perfusion morphometry across models, then pharmacologic intervention with mechanistic readouts (solid stress, perfused vessel fraction, drug and nanoparticle delivery, hypoxia) and efficacy/survival experiments
TME-015.population: Orthotopic AK4.4 murine pancreatic tumours and E0771/4T1 murine breast tumours; aSMA-promoter-dsRed reporter mice for CAF sorting; multiple orthotopic models for the matrix-perfusion correlation
TME-015.n: Multiple orthotopic tumour cohorts; CAFs sorted from losartan- versus saline-treated AK4.4 tumours
TME-015.time_frame: 7-day treatment for delivery/stress endpoints; survival followed to death or excessive tumour burden
TME-015.finding: Hyaluronan and collagen area fractions were each inversely associated with perfused vessel fraction, and their mean correlated more strongly, with HA compressing vessels only in collagen-rich tumours. Losartan reduced CAF-derived profibrotic signalling: TGF-beta1 (P=0.048 E0771; P=0.044 AK4.4), CCN2 (P=0.044; P=0.046), collagen I area fraction (P=0.040; P=0.022), hyaluronan area fraction (P=0.048; P=0.019) and aSMA+ CAF density (P=0.019; P=0.040). Lisinopril reduced collagen I and hyaluronan less than losartan. Solid stress fell (P=0.049 E0771; P=0.043 AK4.4). Perfused vessel fraction rose from 21% to 45% in AK4.4 pancreatic tumours (and 23% to 43% in E0771). 5-FU accumulation in AK4.4 tumours rose 74% (P=0.0063) without changing normal-organ accumulation, and vessel permeability to nanoparticles of all sizes increased. 5-FU alone and losartan alone produced no significant growth…
TME-015.effect: Perfused vessel fraction 21% to 45% in the pancreatic model; +74% intratumoral 5-FU; combination survival benefit with no monotherapy effect
TME-015.limitations: No autochthonous PDAC model; short treatment; solid stress measured ex vivo by tissue-slicing deformation; no human data in this report
TME-015.interpretation: Pharmacologic intervention with a mechanistically matched comparator (ACE inhibitor), a measured intermediate (solid stress, perfusion), a measured downstream (drug concentration) and an efficacy endpoint: strong mechanistic chain in mice; the cross-model correlation supplies the discriminating observation about collagen dependence

glosses.matrix-pressure: Mouse study across tumor models showing hyaluronan compresses vessels only where collagen is abundant, and that losartan lowered both, raised the perfused vessel fraction from 21% to 45% and increased intratumoral fluorouracil by 74%.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A mouse study in which losartan lowered matrix content and mechanical stress, raising perfused vessels from 21 to 45 percent and intratumoral fluorouracil by 74 percent.

TME-016.citation: Murphy JE, Wo JY, Ryan DP, Clark JW, Jiang W, Yeap BY, et al. Total neoadjuvant therapy with FOLFIRINOX in combination with losartan followed by chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced pancreatic cancer: a phase 2 clinical trial. JAMA Oncol. 2019;5(7):1020-1027.
TME-016.clinical_status: Phase 2 complete, hypothesis-generating; losartan is not approved as PDAC therapy and a randomised confirmation has not established benefit (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-016.design: Single-arm, open-label phase 2 trial; primary endpoint margin-negative (R0) resection rate
TME-016.population: 49 patients with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma by multidisciplinary review, ECOG 0-1, adequate organ function, at one large academic hospital
TME-016.n: 49 patients (26 women, 23 men), median age 63 years (range 42-78)
TME-016.time_frame: Enrolment 22 August 2013 to 22 May 2018; median follow-up 17.1 months
TME-016.finding: 39 of 49 patients completed 8 cycles; 10 did not because of progression (5), losartan intolerance (3) or toxicity (2). Chemoradiotherapy was short-course in 7 (16%) and long-course in 38 (84%). 42 patients (86%) underwent attempted surgery. The accessed text is internally inconsistent on the primary endpoint: the abstract Results state R0 resection in 34 of 49 (69%; 95% CI 55%-82%), while the Key Points and Conclusions state an R0 rate of 61% with 34 of 49 resected and 30 of 49 achieving R0. Overall median progression-free survival was 17.5 months (95% CI 13.9-22.7) and median overall survival 31.4 months (95% CI 18.1-38.5). Among resected patients, median progression-free survival was 21.3 months (95% CI 16.6-28.2) and median overall survival 33.0 months (95% CI 31.4 to not reached). Median follow-up was 17.1 months (range 5.0-53.7) among 27 patients alive at study completion.
TME-016.effect: R0 resection rate 61%-69% (text inconsistent); median overall survival 31.4 months in locally advanced disease
TME-016.limitations: Single arm, single centre, no losartan-free control, small n, no on-treatment measurement of tumour stiffness, perfusion or matrix content to confirm the proposed mechanism; internally inconsistent reporting of the primary endpoint in the accessed text
TME-016.interpretation: Single-arm phase 2: establishes feasibility and an outcome signal but cannot attribute benefit to losartan, since FOLFIRINOX plus chemoradiotherapy and patient selection could account for all of it

glosses.matrix-pressure: Single-arm phase 2 trial of FOLFIRINOX plus losartan then chemoradiotherapy in 49 people with locally advanced pancreatic cancer, with a median overall survival of 31.4 months and no control group or on-treatment matrix measurement.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A single-arm phase 2 trial of 49 patients with locally advanced disease given FOLFIRINOX plus losartan then chemoradiotherapy, internally inconsistent on its own margin-negative resection rate.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A single-arm phase 2 of FOLFIRINOX plus losartan then chemoradiotherapy in 49 patients with locally advanced disease, reporting a margin-negative resection rate of 61 to 69 percent and median survival of 31.4 months with no control arm.

TME-017.citation: Elyada E, Bolisetty M, Laise P, Flynn WF, Courtois ET, Burkhart RA, et al. Cross-species single-cell analysis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma reveals antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts. Cancer Discov. 2019;9(8):1102-1123.
TME-017.clinical_status: Preclinical; no apCAF-directed therapy exists (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-017.design: Droplet single-cell RNA sequencing (10x Genomics) of whole viable and fibroblast-enriched fractions with unsupervised clustering, cross-species comparison, and a functional antigen-presentation assay
TME-017.population: 6 human PDAC surgical resections and 2 adjacent-normal pancreata; tumours from 4 KPC mice; sorted CAFs; OT-II TCR-transgenic CD4 T cells
TME-017.n: 6 human PDAC + 2 adjacent-normal specimens; 4 KPC mice; 15 clusters identified (mean 5,246 transcripts and 1,576 genes per cluster); fibroblasts ~2% of all cells in both human and mouse tumours
TME-017.finding: Clustering identified iCAFs and myCAFs in human PDAC, and in KPC mice a third population expressing MHC class II and CD74 without classical co-stimulatory molecules, termed apCAFs. In the OT-II assay, both professional antigen-presenting cells and apCAFs induced the early TCR-ligation markers CD25 and CD69 in CD4 T cells in an OVA-specific manner, whereas myCAFs did not (Fig 7B-D). Ductal sub-clustering mapped classical-signature genes (TFF1, TFF2, LYZ, VSIG2, CEACAM6) to specific sub-clusters, showing classical/basal programmes coexist within tumours. CD4 T cells and Tregs (expressing CTLA4 and TIGIT) came almost exclusively from tumour rather than adjacent-normal samples. apCAFs converted into myofibroblasts under suitable culture conditions, indicating interconvertible states. The authors propose, as a hypothesis, that apCAF MHC class II acts as a decoy that anergises CD4 T cells or…
TME-017.effect: Antigen-specific CD25/CD69 induction by apCAFs versus no induction by myCAFs; fibroblasts ~2% of cells in both species
TME-017.limitations: Small human n; no in vivo apCAF perturbation; decoy hypothesis untested; dissociation bias in single-cell methods
TME-017.interpretation: Discovery-scale transcriptomics plus one targeted functional test: establishes the existence and antigen-presenting capacity of apCAFs in a preparation; the immunosuppressive consequence is proposed, not demonstrated

glosses.fibroblast-states: Single-cell sequencing study across human and mouse pancreatic tumors that identified a fibroblast state carrying antigen-presenting machinery without co-stimulatory molecules, and showed it engages CD4 T-cell receptors specifically.
glosses.t-cells: A single-cell survey of six human and four mouse pancreatic tumors that identified an antigen-presenting fibroblast state carrying MHC class II without classical co-stimulatory molecules.
glosses.antigen-presentation: A single-cell survey of six human and four mouse pancreatic tumors that identified an antigen-presenting fibroblast state carrying MHC class II without classical co-stimulatory molecules.

TME-018.citation: Ene-Obong A, Clear AJ, Watt J, Wang J, Fatah R, Riches JC, et al. Activated pancreatic stellate cells sequester CD8+ T cells to reduce their infiltration of the juxtatumoral compartment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Gastroenterology. 2013;145(5):1121-1132.
TME-018.clinical_status: Preclinical/translational; ATRA stromal reprogramming has been tested in early-phase PDAC trials but is not approved for this use (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-018.design: Compartment-resolved immunohistochemical tissue microarray analysis (juxtatumoral defined as <100 um from tumour cells versus panstromal) with survival correlation, plus in vitro transwell migration/adhesion assays, CXCL12 siRNA knockdown, and an in vivo ATRA intervention in KPC mice
TME-018.population: Human tissue microarrays across pancreatico-biliary diseases (PDAC, ampullary carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, mucinous cystic neoplasm, chronic inflammation, chronic pancreatitis) in two independent patient groups; KPC mice; primary human pancreatic stellate cells and patient CD8 T cells
TME-018.n: Two independent PDAC tissue microarray cohorts (the second composed mainly of advanced cancers); 6 cores per patient; in vitro assays with 1x10^5 sorted cells per transwell
TME-018.time_frame: Cross-sectional human tissue with survival follow-up; 4-8 h migration assays; in vivo ATRA treatment course
TME-018.finding: In PDAC, juxtatumoral compartments contained more myeloperoxidase+ and CD68+ cells but fewer CD8+, FoxP3+, CD56+ and CD20+ cells than panstromal compartments; this compartment difference was absent in ampullary carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma, making it PDAC-specific. Patients whose tumours had high juxtatumoral CD8+ density survived longer. Patient-derived CD8+ T cells showed increased chemotaxis towards activated (versus quiescent) stellate cells or tumour cells, and this was reversed by CXCL12 knockdown or by ATRA treatment of the stellate cells. In KPC mice, ATRA increased CD8+ T-cell numbers in the juxtatumoral compartment.
TME-018.effect: Direction and significance reported per marker and compartment; exact fold differences and hazard ratios not stated in the accessed text
TME-018.limitations: Semi-quantitative immunohistochemistry; survival analysis without multivariable detail in the accessed text; no functional T-cell assays in situ
TME-018.interpretation: Human compartment-resolved observation plus a mechanistic in vitro loss-of-function and an in vivo pharmacologic reversal: supports causation for stellate-cell-mediated CD8 retention, in a preparation and in mice

glosses.t-cells: A compartment-by-compartment analysis of human pancreatic tumors showing CD8 T cells held in the wider stroma away from cancer cells by CXCL12 from activated stellate cells, reversible in mice.

TME-019.citation: Feig C, Jones JO, Kraman M, Wells RJ, Deonarine A, Chan DS, et al. Targeting CXCL12 from FAP-expressing carcinoma-associated fibroblasts synergizes with anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2013;110(50):20212-20217.
TME-019.clinical_status: Preclinical; CXCR4 inhibitors are not approved for PDAC (US); plerixafor is approved for stem-cell mobilisation only, checked 2026-10-08
TME-019.design: Conditional cell-depletion and pharmacologic blockade experiments with ultrasound tumour-volume endpoints, antibody-mediated T-cell depletion controls, and loss-of-heterozygosity readout of cancer-cell elimination
TME-019.population: KPC autochthonous mouse PDAC and KPCD mice carrying a FAP-diphtheria-toxin-receptor BAC transgene for conditional depletion of FAP+ cells; single-cell tumour suspensions
TME-019.n: Antibody arms: anti-PD-L1 n=6, anti-CTLA-4 n=6, control n=4; diphtheria-toxin arms n=6 (PBS) and n=13 (DTx across experiments); AMD3100 arms n=5 (PBS) upward; FAP mRNA quantification PBS n=5
TME-019.finding: Six days of anti-PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4 did not reduce the ~80% increase in tumour volume seen with control IgG, confirming checkpoint inertness in this model. Depletion of FAP+ cells permitted immune control of tumour growth and, combined with anti-CTLA-4 or anti-PD-L1, further reduced growth. T cells were absent from cancer-cell-containing regions; cancer cells were coated with CXCL12; and the FAP+ CAF was the principal tumoral source of CXCL12. AMD3100 induced rapid T-cell accumulation among cancer cells and synergised with anti-PD-L1 to greatly diminish cancer cells, identified by Trp53 loss of heterozygosity, leaving residual tumour composed only of premalignant epithelial and inflammatory cells. The effect required CD4/CD8 T cells.
TME-019.effect: Checkpoint antibodies alone: no change from ~80% volume increase; AMD3100 plus anti-PD-L1: near-elimination of malignant cells
TME-019.limitations: Volume rather than survival endpoints; single model; no human validation; depletion of FAP+ cells conflicts in direction with aSMA+ depletion studies (TME-012), which the study does not reconcile
TME-019.interpretation: Conditional genetic depletion plus a pharmacologic phenocopy plus an immune-cell-depletion control: strong causal chain from FAP+ CAF-derived CXCL12 to T-cell exclusion to checkpoint resistance, in mice

glosses.t-cells: A mouse study in which depleting FAP-positive fibroblasts, or blocking the CXCL12 receptor, let anti-PD-L1 and anti-CTLA-4 antibodies work in a pancreatic cancer model where they are otherwise inert.
glosses.myeloid-cells: A mouse study in which depleting FAP-positive fibroblasts, or blocking the CXCL12 receptor, let anti-PD-L1 and anti-CTLA-4 antibodies work in a pancreatic cancer model where they are otherwise inert.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A mouse study in which blocking the CXCL12 signal from FAP-expressing fibroblasts plus anti-PD-L1 nearly eliminated malignant cells, the opposite direction from bulk fibroblast depletion.

TME-020.citation: Zhu Y, Knolhoff BL, Meyer MA, Nywening TM, West BL, Luo J, et al. CSF1/CSF1R blockade reprograms tumor-infiltrating macrophages and improves response to T-cell checkpoint immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer models. Cancer Res. 2014;74(18):5057-5069.
TME-020.clinical_status: Preclinical; no CSF1R inhibitor is approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-020.design: Pharmacologic and antibody-based receptor/ligand blockade with flow cytometry, qRT-PCR, antigen-presentation assays and combination-therapy efficacy experiments
TME-020.population: Syngeneic orthotopic murine PDAC (KI and KC tumour cells implanted surgically into the pancreas of syngeneic mice); sorted tumour-associated macrophages and lymphoid dendritic cells
TME-020.n: Treatment cohorts of orthotopic tumour-bearing mice (immune-phenotyping groups n=6-7 per arm); macrophage/dendritic-cell isolations after 8 days of treatment
TME-020.time_frame: 6 hours to 8 days for pharmacodynamics; multi-week efficacy experiments
TME-020.finding: CSF1/CSF1R blockade reduced tumour-associated macrophage numbers and reprogrammed the remaining macrophages towards antigen presentation (higher MHC-II+ TAM and lymphoid dendritic-cell frequencies after 8 days), lowering immune suppression and raising interferon responses. CSF1R blockade also upregulated the T-cell checkpoint molecules PD-L1 and CTLA-4, restraining its own benefit. Anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 had limited single-agent efficacy. Combining CSF1 blockade with anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 and gemcitabine produced complete tumour regression in 30% of animals and an average tumour regression of about 85% (Fig 7D), including in well-established tumours; similar results were obtained in orthotopic KC tumours and with the less potent inhibitor GW2580.
TME-020.effect: Complete regression in 30% of animals; mean tumour regression ~85% with the triple combination
TME-020.limitations: No autochthonous model; regression measured by tumour volume/weight rather than survival; the clinical CSF1R-inhibitor programmes in PDAC have not reproduced these results
TME-020.interpretation: Converging pharmacologic and antibody approaches with mechanistic intermediates and a combination test that reverses the induced resistance: strong causal support in mouse orthotopic models

glosses.myeloid-cells: A mouse study showing that blocking CSF1R reduced and reprogrammed tumor macrophages but raised PD-L1 and CTLA-4, with regression only when checkpoint antibodies and gemcitabine were added.

TME-021.citation: Steele CW, Karim SA, Leach JDG, Bailey P, Upstill-Goddard R, Rishi L, et al. CXCR2 inhibition profoundly suppresses metastases and augments immunotherapy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Cell. 2016;29(6):832-845.
TME-021.clinical_status: Preclinical; no CXCR2 inhibitor is approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-021.design: Expression mapping in human tissue, germline genetic deletion, pharmacologic inhibition, antibody-mediated neutrophil ablation, and combination immunotherapy survival experiments
TME-021.population: Human PDAC expression data; KPC autochthonous mice with and without germline Cxcr2 deletion; KPC mice treated with a clinical-grade CXCR2 inhibitor; neutrophil-ablation cohorts
TME-021.n: Survival cohorts: KPC and KPC-Cxcr2-/- untreated or gemcitabine-treated, n=21, 24, 10, 13; neutrophil ablation: isotype control n=11 versus anti-Ly6G (1A8) n=15
TME-021.time_frame: Treatment from 10 weeks of age for prevention arms; 2-week priming then combination in established disease
TME-021.finding: CXCR2 signalling was upregulated in human PDAC predominantly in neutrophil/myeloid-derived suppressor cells and rarely in tumour cells. Genetic ablation or pharmacologic inhibition of CXCR2 abrogated metastasis, but only pharmacologic inhibition slowed primary tumorigenesis and prolonged tumour-free survival, revealing differential effects in early versus late tumours. Neutrophil/MDSC depletion also suppressed metastasis, indicating CXCR2 is needed to establish and maintain the metastatic niche. Loss or inhibition of CXCR2 improved T-cell entry into tumours. In KPC mice with established late-stage tumours, CXCR2 inhibitor plus anti-PD-1 significantly extended survival beyond vehicle plus anti-PD-1 (anti-PD-1 being previously ineffective as a single agent in this model), with two mice living 100 days beyond treatment start before dying of pancreatic tumours.
TME-021.effect: Metastasis significantly inhibited by genetic or pharmacologic CXCR2 targeting; survival extension with CXCR2 inhibitor plus anti-PD-1 including two long survivors beyond 100 days
TME-021.limitations: Survival curves for the genetic cohorts were not significant on log-rank; no human trial data; mechanism of improved T-cell entry not fully resolved
TME-021.interpretation: Germline deletion plus pharmacologic inhibition plus cell-ablation, with a stage-dependent dissociation between the two approaches: strong causal support with an explicit boundary condition

glosses.myeloid-cells: A mouse and human expression study showing CXCR2 signaling in neutrophils and myeloid suppressor cells is required for metastasis, and that blocking it made anti-PD-1 extend survival.

TME-022.citation: Jiang H, Hegde S, Knolhoff BL, Zhu Y, Herndon JM, Meyer MA, et al. Targeting focal adhesion kinase renders pancreatic cancers responsive to checkpoint immunotherapy. Nat Med. 2016;22(8):851-860.
TME-022.clinical_status: Preclinical rationale; FAK inhibitors remain investigational and none is approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-022.design: Human correlative pathology plus pharmacologic and genetic (shFAK1) FAK inhibition with survival, fibrosis, immune-phenotyping, gene-array and combination-immunotherapy experiments
TME-022.population: Human PDAC tissue (p-FAK1, collagen and CD8 immunohistochemistry with outcome data); KPC (p48-Cre/LSL-Kras-G12D/p53-flox/+) and KPPC autochthonous mice; orthotopic KI and KP tumours; KP-OVA adoptive-transfer model
TME-022.n: Human cohort for p-FAK1/CD8/collagen scoring with survival; mouse immune-phenotyping n=6-7 per group; survival cohorts in KPC, KPPC and orthotopic models
TME-022.time_frame: 10-14 days for pharmacodynamics; 1.5 months for fibrosis assessment; lifetime survival studies
TME-022.finding: In human PDAC, FAK activity was elevated and correlated with high fibrosis (total collagen by Sirius Red and collagen I by immunohistochemistry) and poor CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell infiltration; high p-FAK1 with low CD8 marked poor clinical outcome. Single-agent VS-4718 significantly limited tumour progression and doubled survival in KPC mice, with similar extension in the aggressive KPPC model, whereas gemcitabine had no survival effect in these models; the mechanism was prolonged tumour stasis rather than regression. Ten days of FAK inhibition decreased tumour-infiltrating MDSCs, CD206+ TAMs and CD4+FOXP3+ Tregs without altering bone-marrow or blood myelopoiesis. FAK inhibition decreased fibrosis. FAKi plus gemcitabine more than doubled median survival. FAK inhibition rendered the previously unresponsive KPC model responsive to anti-PD-1 and to adoptive T-cell therapy.
TME-022.effect: Doubling of median survival with single-agent FAK inhibition; more than doubling with FAKi plus gemcitabine; conversion from checkpoint-refractory to checkpoint-responsive
TME-022.limitations: Mouse survival benefit is stasis not regression; the human arm is observational; clinical FAK-inhibitor combinations in PDAC have not reproduced the preclinical magnitude
TME-022.interpretation: Human correlative anchor plus pharmacologic and genetic perturbation in autochthonous models with immunologic rescue experiments: strong causal support in mice for FAK as a shared node linking matrix and myeloid suppression

glosses.myeloid-cells: A study pairing human tissue, in which focal adhesion kinase activity went with dense collagen and few CD8 cells, with mouse experiments where inhibiting it doubled survival and restored checkpoint responsiveness.

TME-023.citation: Beatty GL, Chiorean EG, Fishman MP, Saboury B, Teitelbaum UR, Sun W, et al. CD40 agonists alter tumor stroma and show efficacy against pancreatic carcinoma in mice and humans. Science. 2011;331(6024):1612-1616.
TME-023.clinical_status: Hypothesis-generating; no CD40 agonist is approved for PDAC (US) and the randomised test did not meet its endpoint (see TME-024), checked 2026-10-08
TME-023.design: Open-label clinical trial of an agonist CD40 antibody plus gemcitabine with FDG-PET and RECIST readouts, paired with mechanistic dissection in a genetically engineered mouse model
TME-023.population: 21 patients with chemotherapy-naive, surgically incurable PDAC (90% metastatic); KPC autochthonous mice; clodronate-liposome and T-cell-depletion experiments
TME-023.n: 21 patients (2 not evaluable for response); mouse cohorts treated with FGK45 with or without gemcitabine, with or without CD4/CD8 depletion, with or without macrophage depletion
TME-023.time_frame: 28-day cycles with imaging after two cycles; interim survival analysis August 2010; mouse treatments over days to weeks
TME-023.finding: Human: metabolic responses on FDG-PET/CT in 88% of patients evaluated after two cycles; by RECIST 4 of 21 partial responses, 11 stable disease, 4 progressive disease. Median progression-free survival 5.6 months (95% CI 4.0 to not estimable) and median overall survival 7.4 months (95% CI 5.5-12.8) on interim data as of 25 August 2010 with 6 of 21 alive. Regressing human tumours showed necrosis with a macrophage-dominated infiltrate and an absence of lymphocytes. Mouse: FGK45 plus gemcitabine induced regression in 30% of mice; FGK45 alone gave the same regression rate while gemcitabine alone gave none. Regression occurred at the same rate in mice depleted of CD4+, CD8+ or both. Clodronate-liposome macrophage depletion abolished the regression. CD40-activated macrophages rapidly infiltrated tumours, became tumoricidal and facilitated depletion of tumour stroma.
TME-023.effect: 4 of 21 RECIST partial responses and 88% metabolic responses in patients; 30% regression rate in mice, abolished by macrophage depletion and unaffected by T-cell depletion
TME-023.limitations: Small uncontrolled human cohort; interim survival data; mouse regression measured by ultrasound over short intervals; the macrophage-dependent mechanism conflicts with the T-cell rationale used in subsequent trial design
TME-023.interpretation: Combination of an uncontrolled human trial (association only) with mouse depletion experiments that identify the necessary effector cell: strong mechanistic inference in mice, weak efficacy inference in humans

glosses.myeloid-cells: A 21-patient trial of a CD40 agonist with gemcitabine alongside mouse experiments showing the regressions it caused required macrophages rather than T cells or chemotherapy.
glosses.pet-scan: A 21-patient CD40 antibody trial in which 88% had a metabolic response on PET while few shrank by size and median survival was 7.4 months.

TME-024.citation: Padron LJ, Maurer DM, O'Hara MH, O'Reilly EM, Wolff RA, Wainberg ZA, et al. Sotigalimab and/or nivolumab with chemotherapy in first-line metastatic pancreatic cancer: clinical and immunologic analyses from the randomized phase 2 PRINCE trial. Nat Med. 2022;28(6):1167-1177.
TME-024.clinical_status: Randomised phase 2 did not meet its endpoint for sotigalimab arms; no CD40 agonist is FDA-approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-024.design: Randomised phase 2 (following a phase 1b dose-finding portion), three arms, with a prespecified primary endpoint of 1-year overall survival rate per arm tested against a historical control of 35%, plus extensive tumour and circulating immune biomarker analyses
TME-024.population: Adults with untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1, measurable disease, at seven US academic hospitals (PRINCE / PICI0002)
TME-024.n: 129 enrolled overall; 105 analysed for efficacy in the randomised portion: nivolumab/chemotherapy n=34 (registry: 37 started), sotigalimab/chemotherapy n=36 (registry: 31 started in phase 2),…
TME-024.time_frame: Phase 1b enrolment 22 August 2017 to 10 July 2018; primary completion 11 February 2021; 1-year survival endpoint
TME-024.finding: 1-year overall survival: nivolumab/chemotherapy 57.7% (one-sided P=0.006, one-sided 95% lower bound 41.7%) - endpoint met; sotigalimab/chemotherapy 48.1% (one-sided P=0.062, lower bound 33.7%) - not met; sotigalimab/nivolumab/chemotherapy 41.3% (one-sided P=0.223 or 0.233 as reported, lower bound 27.0%) - not met. Median overall survival 16.7 months (95% CI 9.8-18.4), 11.4 months (95% CI 7.2-20.1) and 10.1 months (95% CI 7.9-13.2) respectively. Posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT03214250 give the same 1-year rates with two-sided intervals: 0.577 (0.384-0.729), 0.481 (0.309-0.634), 0.413 (0.244-0.575). The authors note that a later phase 3 reported a 1-year survival of approximately 40-45% for chemotherapy alone, and that their own synthetic control arm gave 45%, which narrows any apparent benefit. Relatively few tumour or circulating immune biomarkers associated with survival,…
TME-024.effect: 1-year overall survival 57.7% / 48.1% / 41.3% versus a 35% historical and a 45% synthetic control; adding CD40 agonism to chemotherapy plus nivolumab lowered survival relative to chemotherapy plus nivolumab
TME-024.limitations: No concurrent control; single historical benchmark chosen before contemporary chemotherapy results; phase 2 size; biomarker analyses exploratory and largely null
TME-024.interpretation: Randomised allocation across three experimental arms but with a historical rather than concurrent control: permits comparison between arms and excludes a large CD40 effect, while leaving the absolute benefit of any arm uncertain

glosses.myeloid-cells: The randomized phase 2 PRINCE trial in 105 patients with untreated metastatic pancreatic cancer, in which only the chemotherapy-plus-nivolumab arm met its one-year survival endpoint and both CD40 arms missed.
glosses.immune-combinations: The randomized PRINCE trial, in which only the chemotherapy-plus-nivolumab arm met its one-year survival target and both arms containing the CD40 agonist sotigalimab did not.

TME-025.citation: Yang S, Wang X, Contino G, Liesa M, Sahin E, Ying H, et al. Pancreatic cancers require autophagy for tumor growth. Genes Dev. 2011;25(7):717-729.
