TME-025.clinical_status: Rationale for hydroxychloroquine trials, which were negative or mixed (see TME-026, TME-027); chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine are not approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-025.design: Baseline autophagy measurement (GFP-LC3 puncta, electron microscopy, immunohistochemistry), genetic inhibition by ATG5 siRNA, pharmacologic inhibition by chloroquine, and in vivo survival/regression experiments
TME-025.population: Human PDAC primary tumours (ATG7 immunohistochemistry in 80 tumours) and cell lines, with HPDE (immortalised normal ductal), MCF7 (breast) and H460 (lung) comparators; PDAC xenografts; genetic mouse models of pancreatic cancer
TME-025.n: ATG7 immunohistochemistry: elevated in 57 of 80 tumours; xenograft treatment groups of 10 mice each; genetic mouse model cohort of 8 control versus 8 chloroquine-treated
TME-025.time_frame: Days (in vitro); up to ~180 days (mouse survival)
TME-025.finding: PDAC primary tumours and cell lines showed elevated basal autophagy by GFP-LC3 puncta, with electron microscopy showing autophagosomes fusing with lysosomes, and ATG7 elevated in 57 of 80 tumours. Chloroquine IC50 was much lower across a panel of PDAC lines than in MCF7 or H460 cells. ATG5 siRNA suppressed ATG5 protein, inhibited autophagy, and reduced soft-agar growth of 8988T cells by more than 50% without significantly affecting H460 cells. Autophagy inhibition increased reactive oxygen species, DNA damage (increased comet tail moments and gamma-H2AX) and reduced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. In the genetic mouse model, all 8 control mice died of PDAC by 140 days (median 117 days) whereas only 1 of 8 chloroquine-treated animals had died by termination at approximately 180 days (P=0.0012 log-rank).
TME-025.effect: Soft-agar growth reduced >50% by ATG5 knockdown; 8 of 8 control deaths by 140 days versus 1 of 8 with chloroquine by ~180 days (P=0.0012)
TME-025.limitations: Human arm is expression-only; small mouse cohorts; no measurement of tumour autophagy inhibition in patients; translation assumed rather than tested
TME-025.interpretation: Genetic and pharmacologic loss-of-function with a mechanistic intermediate (reactive oxygen species, DNA damage, oxidative phosphorylation) and in vivo survival endpoints: strong causal support in preparations and mice

glosses.nutrient-scavenging: A study establishing that pancreatic cancer cells run high baseline autophagy and depend on it, with chloroquine causing regression and markedly longer survival in a genetic mouse model.

TME-026.citation: Wolpin BM, Rubinson DA, Wang X, Chan JA, Cleary JM, Enzinger PC, et al. Phase II and pharmacodynamic study of autophagy inhibition using hydroxychloroquine in patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Oncologist. 2014;19(6):637-638.
TME-026.clinical_status: Negative phase 2 for single-agent hydroxychloroquine; not approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-026.design: Single-arm phase 2 trial at two dose levels with a prespecified primary endpoint and an embedded pharmacodynamic substudy in peripheral-blood lymphocytes
TME-026.population: 20 patients with previously treated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma; plus mice treated with chloroquine for pharmacodynamic marker validation
TME-026.n: 20 patients (n=10 at 400 mg twice daily, n=10 at 600 mg twice daily)
TME-026.time_frame: Primary endpoint at 2 months; survival followed to death
TME-026.finding: 2 of 20 patients (10%) were free of progression at 2 months, the primary endpoint. Median progression-free survival was 46.5 days and median overall survival 69.0 days. Treatment-related grade 3/4 events were lymphopenia (n=1) and alanine aminotransferase elevation (n=1); tolerability and efficacy were similar at both dose levels. In mice receiving chloroquine at doses sufficient to inhibit tumour autophagy and cause tumour regression, LC3-II (but not p62) rose in peripheral lymphocytes and hepatocytes, validating LC3-II as a pharmacodynamic marker. In patients, LC3-II analysis in peripheral lymphocytes showed inconsistent autophagy inhibition at 800 or 1,200 mg daily. The authors concluded the 10% two-month progression-free rate was inadequate to justify further single-agent study.
TME-026.effect: 2-month progression-free rate 10% (2/20); median progression-free survival 46.5 days; median overall survival 69.0 days
TME-026.limitations: Very small, single-arm, pretreated population; surrogate pharmacodynamic tissue; brief report format
TME-026.interpretation: Single-arm trial with a target-engagement measurement: excludes meaningful single-agent activity and, because autophagy inhibition was inconsistent, leaves the mechanism itself untested in humans

glosses.nutrient-scavenging: A 20-patient single-arm trial of hydroxychloroquine alone in pretreated metastatic pancreatic cancer, in which only two patients were progression-free at two months and autophagy inhibition was inconsistent.
glosses.antigen-presentation: A 20-patient single-arm trial of hydroxychloroquine alone in pretreated metastatic pancreatic cancer, in which only two patients were progression-free at two months and autophagy inhibition was inconsistent.

TME-027.citation: Karasic TB, O'Hara MH, Loaiza-Bonilla A, Reiss KA, Teitelbaum UR, Borazanci E, et al. Effect of gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel with or without hydroxychloroquine on patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: a phase 2 randomized clinical trial. JAMA Oncol. 2019;5(7):993-998.
TME-027.clinical_status: Negative for the primary survival endpoint; hydroxychloroquine is not approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-027.design: Open-label, randomised (1:1) phase 2 trial; primary endpoint overall survival at 12 months
TME-027.population: 112 patients with previously untreated metastatic or advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1, adequate marrow and organ function, at the University of Pennsylvania, HonorHealth and Johns Hopkins
TME-027.n: 112 randomised: 55 to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel plus hydroxychloroquine, 57 to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel
TME-027.time_frame: Enrolment 18 March 2013 to 16 November 2017; primary endpoint at 12 months
TME-027.finding: Overall survival at 12 months was 41% (95% CI 27%-53%) with hydroxychloroquine versus 49% (95% CI 35%-61%) without - the primary endpoint was not met. Median progression-free survival was 5.7 months (95% CI 4.0-9.3) versus 6.4 months (95% CI 4.5-7.6); median overall survival 11.1 months (95% CI 9.0-14.2) versus 12.1 months (95% CI 9.3-15.5). Overall response rate was significantly higher with hydroxychloroquine: 38.2% (n=21) versus 21.1% (n=12), P=.047. The authors suggest the response-rate gain may have a role in the locally advanced setting where tumour response can permit resection.
TME-027.effect: 12-month overall survival 41% versus 49% (no benefit); overall response rate 38.2% versus 21.1% (P=.047)
TME-027.limitations: Open-label; phase 2 size; no measurement of intratumoral autophagy inhibition; survival numerically worse with the experimental arm
TME-027.interpretation: Randomised concurrent-control trial: excludes a survival benefit of this magnitude while establishing a real effect on tumour shrinkage

glosses.reading-trial-results: A randomized phase 2 trial in which adding hydroxychloroquine raised the response rate from 21% to 38% while one-year survival was numerically worse.
glosses.nutrient-scavenging: A randomized phase 2 trial in 112 patients in which hydroxychloroquine added to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel raised the response rate significantly but did not improve twelve-month survival.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A randomized phase 2 trial in which adding hydroxychloroquine raised response rates but did not improve 12-month survival.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: A randomized phase 2 trial in which hydroxychloroquine raised the response rate from 21% to 38% while 12-month survival was numerically worse.

TME-028.citation: Kamphorst JJ, Nofal M, Commisso C, Hackett SR, Lu W, Grabocka E, et al. Human pancreatic cancer tumors are nutrient poor and tumor cells actively scavenge extracellular protein. Cancer Res. 2015;75(3):544-553.
TME-028.clinical_status: Not applicable (mechanistic human-tissue study); no scavenging-directed therapy approved (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-028.design: Quantitative metabolomics of human tumour versus adjacent benign tissue by LC-MS, plus stable-isotope (13C,15N) tracing in culture that separates protein-derived from monomer-derived amino acids, and amino-acid dropout growth experiments
TME-028.population: Resected human PDAC tumours with matched adjacent benign pancreas (freeze-clamped intraoperatively); human PDAC tissue for macropinocytosis staining; murine KRPC (KRAS-G12D, p53-silenced) and human MIA PaCa-2 and E3 pancreatic cancer cell lines
TME-028.n: Paired human tumour and adjacent benign specimens (exact n not stated in the accessed text); multiple cell lines in replicate
TME-028.time_frame: Intraoperative tissue sampling; 24 h to several doublings in culture
TME-028.finding: Relative to adjacent benign tissue, PDAC tumours were consistently low in both glucose and glutamine, with an amino-acid pattern consistent with reliance on protein scavenging. Macropinocytosis was detectable in human pancreatic tumour tissue. With physiological albumin, cultured murine PDAC cells grew indefinitely in media lacking individual essential amino acids and replicated once in the complete absence of free amino acids. After 24 h in leucine-free medium with 5% albumin, intracellular leucine was about 12.5 pmol/uL cell volume - roughly 100-fold lower than in complete medium but twice as high as without albumin. Albumin contributed to intracellular amino-acid pools in MIA PaCa-2 and E3 human cells. Growth on albumin as sole amino-acid source was associated with glutamine depletion and essential-amino-acid accumulation. The authors note that, assuming 75 g/L total plasma protein,…
TME-028.effect: Glucose and glutamine consistently lower in tumour than adjacent benign tissue; albumin doubled intracellular leucine under leucine deprivation; ~200-fold more amino-acid equivalents in plasma protein than as free amino acids
TME-028.limitations: No in vivo quantification of the scavenged fraction; compartment ambiguity in human measurements; cell-line dependence; freeze-clamping is not clinically practicable
TME-028.interpretation: Human quantitative measurement establishes the nutrient environment; isotope tracing with albumin dependence establishes the scavenging route in a preparation. The link between the two is inference, not demonstration

glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Human tissue study showing pancreatic tumors are depleted of glucose and glutamine compared with each patient's own adjacent pancreas, with cancer cells able to scavenge amino acids from protein.
glosses.nutrient-scavenging: Quantitative metabolomics of resected human pancreatic tumors against adjacent benign pancreas, showing both glucose and glutamine depleted and tumor cells actively scavenging extracellular protein.
glosses.t-cells: Quantitative metabolomics of resected human pancreatic tumors against adjacent benign pancreas, showing both glucose and glutamine depleted and tumor cells actively scavenging extracellular protein.

TME-029.citation: Sousa CM, Biancur DE, Wang X, Halbrook CJ, Sherman MH, Zhang L, et al. Pancreatic stellate cells support tumour metabolism through autophagic alanine secretion. Nature. 2016;536(7617):479-483.
TME-029.clinical_status: Preclinical; no alanine-transfer-directed therapy exists (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-029.design: Metabolite profiling of conditioned media (about 200 metabolites), oxygen-consumption-rate measurement, U-13C glucose/glutamine isotope tracing with media transfer, and in vivo co-injection of genetically manipulated (autophagy-incompetent) stellate cells
TME-029.population: Human and murine pancreatic stellate cells and PDAC cell lines, including cells derived from murine autochthonous PDAC models; subcutaneous and orthotopic co-injection mouse models
TME-029.n: Approximately 200 metabolites screened; 14 amino acids measured kinetically; multiple co-injection cohorts (subcutaneous and orthotopic)
TME-029.time_frame: 24 h (secretion); days (proliferation and tracing); weeks (in vivo growth and tumour-free survival)
TME-029.finding: Of about 200 metabolites screened, only the non-essential amino acids alanine and aspartate followed the pattern of stellate-cell secretion and tumour-cell uptake. Only alanine raised PDAC oxygen consumption to a degree comparable with full stellate-cell conditioned medium. Secreted alanine reached millimolar concentration in stellate-cell medium within 24 h, and alanine was secreted faster than any of the other 13 amino acids measured and faster even than lactate. Alanine was one of only two amino acids to accumulate in PDAC cells, with greater than fivefold enrichment. Alanine carbon outcompeted glucose- and glutamine-derived carbon in fuelling the TCA cycle and downstream non-essential amino acid and lipid biosynthesis. Alanine secretion depended on stellate-cell autophagy, which cancer cells stimulated. Conditioned medium increased PDAC proliferation significantly only under…
TME-029.effect: >5-fold intracellular alanine enrichment; millimolar secreted alanine within 24 h; fastest secretion of 14 amino acids; significant attenuation of tumour take and growth with autophagy-deficient stellate cells
TME-029.limitations: No autochthonous genetic test of stellate-cell autophagy; alanine levels not measured in human tumour interstitium; graft models
TME-029.interpretation: Unbiased metabolite screen narrowed to a single mediator, with isotope tracing, a genetic loss-of-function in the supplying cell type, and in vivo co-injection: strong causal support for a stroma-to-tumour nutrient transfer, in preparations and mouse grafts

glosses.nutrient-scavenging: A metabolite screen and mouse co-injection study identifying alanine, secreted by stellate cells through their own autophagy, as a fuel pancreatic cancer cells prefer over glucose and glutamine.

TME-030.citation: Saloman JL, Albers KM, Li D, Hartman DJ, Crawford HC, Muha EA, et al. Ablation of sensory neurons in a genetic model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma slows initiation and progression of cancer. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2016;113(11):3078-3083.
TME-030.clinical_status: Preclinical; denervation is not a PDAC therapy (celiac plexus block is used for pain only; see ANAT), checked 2026-10-08
TME-030.design: Neonatal chemical denervation (capsaicin) followed by lifetime histological and survival follow-up, with central and peripheral nervous-system inflammation readouts and perineural invasion assessment
TME-030.population: PKC and related autochthonous mouse PDAC models (PKCT, PKCY); cerulein-induced acute pancreatitis as an inflammation comparator; dorsal root ganglia and spinal cord tissue
TME-030.n: Mouse cohorts for capsaicin versus vehicle with survival follow-up; the subgroup with >80% neuronal ablation followed to 18 months
TME-030.finding: Inflammation and neuronal damage in both peripheral and central nervous systems appeared as early as the PanIN2 stage, with astrocyte reactivity elevated in the spinal cord at PanIN and cancer stages. Also at PanIN2, pancreas acinar-derived cells frequently invaded along sensory neurons into the spinal cord and migrated caudally to lower thoracic and upper lumbar regions. Sensory-neuron ablation prevented perineural invasion, astrocyte activation and neuronal damage. Neuron ablation significantly delayed PanIN formation and prolonged survival: median survival 7.8 versus 4.5 months (P=0.001). Animals with the greatest degree of ablation (>80%) did not develop cancer up to 18 months when they were euthanised for analysis, whereas more than 90% of untreated mice died of PDAC within 6 months.
TME-030.effect: Median survival 4.5 to 7.8 months (P=0.001); no cancer by 18 months in the >80%-ablation subgroup versus >90% mortality within 6 months in controls
TME-030.limitations: Prevention not treatment; no pharmacologic denervation in established disease; mouse only; no human correlate
TME-030.interpretation: Permanent loss-of-function of a defined cell population before disease onset, with a dose-response (degree of ablation) and a benign-inflammation comparator: strong causal support in mice that sensory innervation accelerates initiation

glosses.pain: A mouse study in which pancreatic sensory nerves were ablated before disease onset found slower cancer development and longer survival.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Mouse study showing ablating pancreatic sensory neurons before disease onset delayed precursor lesions and extended survival.
glosses.nerves-in-tumor: A mouse experiment in which ablating sensory neurons before disease onset prevented perineural invasion and raised median survival from 4.5 to 7.8 months.

TME-031.citation: Renz BW, Tanaka T, Sunagawa M, Takahashi R, Jiang Z, Macchini M, et al. Cholinergic signaling via muscarinic receptors directly and indirectly suppresses pancreatic tumorigenesis and cancer stemness. Cancer Discov. 2018;8(11):1458-1473.
TME-031.clinical_status: Preclinical; muscarinic agonists are not used as PDAC therapy (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-031.design: Surgical denervation (subdiaphragmatic vagotomy with pyloroplasty) and pharmacologic receptor agonism, with histology, qPCR, immunohistochemistry, cancer-stem-cell assays and ultrasound-guided randomised survival experiments
TME-031.population: KC (LSL-Kras-G12D;Pdx1-Cre) and KPC (LSL-Kras-G12D;LSL-Trp53-R172H;Pdx1-Cre) autochthonous mice; PDAC cell lines for receptor-pathway work
TME-031.n: KC arms: KC+PP, KC+VxPP, KC+VxPP+bethanechol (n=3 per group for macrophage quantification); KPC survival arms: gemcitabine n=15 versus gemcitabine plus bethanechol n=10
TME-031.time_frame: Vagotomy at 8 weeks with assessment at 20 weeks; KPC survival from 3-5 mm tumour enrolment to moribund
TME-031.finding: Subdiaphragmatic vagotomy in KC mice accelerated PDAC development, and bethanechol restored the normal KC phenotype, suppressing the vagotomy-induced acceleration. Vagotomised pancreata showed significantly increased Chrm1 (muscarinic type 1 receptor) expression (P<0.05) at 20 weeks, with no change in other muscarinic receptors. In KPC mice enrolled with ultrasound-confirmed 3-5 mm tumours, bethanechol added to gemcitabine significantly extended overall survival (Fig 2B; numeric medians not reported in the accessed text). Mechanistically, effects were mediated in part through CHRM1, which inhibited downstream MAPK/EGFR and PI3K/AKT signalling in PDAC cells. Enhanced cholinergic signalling suppressed the cancer-stem-cell compartment, CD11b+ myeloid cells, TNF-alpha levels and hepatic metastatic growth.
TME-031.effect: Acceleration with vagotomy, reversal with bethanechol, and significant survival extension in KPC mice on gemcitabine; exact medians not reported in the accessed text
TME-031.limitations: No numeric survival medians in the accessed text; small group sizes for mechanistic readouts; no human data; this article later carried an Editor's Note (Cancer Discov. 2026;16(8):1711), which should be consulted before relying on specific figures
TME-031.interpretation: Surgical loss-of-function with pharmacologic rescue in the same model, plus a therapeutic arm in established disease: strong causal support in mice for a tumour-restraining cholinergic input

glosses.nerve-plexus: Mouse study showing cutting the vagus accelerated tumor development while a cholinergic drug suppressed it.
glosses.nerves-in-tumor: A mouse experiment in which vagotomy accelerated tumor development and a muscarinic agonist reversed it; an Editor's Note was later attached to this paper.

TME-032.citation: Hwang WL, Jagadeesh KA, Guo JA, Hoffman HI, Yadollahpour P, Reeves JW, et al. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptome profiling of pancreatic cancer identifies multicellular dynamics associated with neoadjuvant treatment. Nat Genet. 2022;54(8):1178-1191.
TME-032.clinical_status: Not applicable (molecular pathology); no spatial-community-based clinical decision is standard (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-032.design: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing combined with whole-transcriptome digital spatial profiling of matched specimens, with consensus non-negative matrix factorisation to define expression programmes, spatial community detection, receptor-ligand analysis and survival modelling in independent cohorts
TME-032.population: 43 of 48 patients with primary resected PDAC (18 treatment-naive, 25 after neoadjuvant therapy, including 5 on the losartan chemoradiotherapy trial NCT01821729 and 2 on NCT03563248), with banked frozen specimens stored up to five years
TME-032.time_frame: Cross-sectional resected specimens (treated and untreated) with survival follow-up; banked tissue up to five years old
TME-032.finding: Fourteen malignant programmes were identified, reflecting lineage (classical-like, squamoid, basaloid, mesenchymal, acinar-like, neuroendocrine-like, neural-like progenitor) or state (cycling-S, cycling-G2/M, MYC, interferon, TNF-NFkB, ribosomal, adhesive), plus four CAF programmes (myofibroblastic progenitor, neurotropic, immunomodulatory, adhesive). The ACTA2-enriched myofibroblastic progenitor programme overlapped the published myCAF signature, while the neurotropic, immunomodulatory and adhesive programmes overlapped the iCAF signature, suggesting iCAF subsets; the immunomodulatory programme included CXCL12, CCL19 and CCL21. Malignant-cell proportions were significantly lower after neoadjuvant therapy, and the CD8+ T-cell fraction was higher after chemoradiotherapy plus losartan. A newly identified neural-like progenitor malignant programme was enriched after chemotherapy and…
TME-032.effect: Adhesive CAF programme HR 1.84 (1.04-3.25) and classical programme HR 0.73 (0.56-0.95) for overall survival; three reproducible spatial communities
TME-032.limitations: Modest n for survival modelling; resected (more favourable) patients only; treatment heterogeneity including two small trial subgroups; no functional perturbation
TME-032.interpretation: Human observational multi-omic and spatial profiling: establishes co-organisation and prognostic association; treatment comparisons are non-randomised, so treatment-associated programmes could be selection of resistant pre-existing states rather than induction

glosses.fibroblast-states: Single-nucleus and spatial profiling of 43 resected human pancreatic tumors that resolved four fibroblast programs and three recurring tissue neighborhoods, one fibroblast program tracking with shorter survival.
glosses.sub-environments: A single-nucleus and spatial study of 43 resected tumors defining fourteen tumor and four fibroblast programs, three recurring tissue neighborhoods, and their survival associations.
glosses.cell-states: A spatial and single-nucleus study mapping classical and basal programs to distinct tissue neighborhoods, with classical cells associated with lower mortality.

TME-033.citation: Jacobetz MA, Chan DS, Neesse A, Bapiro TE, Cook N, Frese KK, et al. Hyaluronan impairs vascular function and drug delivery in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer. Gut. 2013;62(1):112-120.
TME-033.clinical_status: Preclinical; the strategy failed in phase 3 (see TME-004), checked 2026-10-08
TME-033.design: Short-term pharmacodynamic studies (vessel patency by lectin perfusion, vessel luminal area, HPLC measurement of active gemcitabine metabolite) plus a four-arm survival study with serial three-dimensional ultrasonography
TME-033.population: KPC autochthonous mouse PDAC; syngeneic subcutaneous tumours as comparators
TME-033.n: Vessel patency n=4 mice per cohort with >100 vessels per mouse; survival arms: vehicle n=8, gemcitabine n=15, PEGPH20 n=12, gemcitabine plus PEGPH20 n=10; mice enrolled with tumours of 270 +/- 100…
TME-033.time_frame: 3-day pretreatment for pharmacodynamics; survival from enrolment at ~270 mm^3 to death, with ultrasound every 3 days
TME-033.finding: Three days of PEGPH20 increased tumour vascular patency from 30% to 70% (P=0.0286) and significantly increased mean vessel luminal area (P=0.0085), while mean vessel density was unchanged (Fig S1) - so increased perfusion is attributable to decompression of existing vessels. Mice given gemcitabine after a single PEGPH20 dose had significantly higher intratumoral gemcitabine triphosphate (dFdCTP) than vehicle-pretreated controls (P=0.0053, Fig 2D). In the survival study, gemcitabine plus PEGPH20 significantly increased survival relative to gemcitabine alone, whereas PEGPH20 alone or gemcitabine alone had insignificant effects versus vehicle (Fig 4C).
TME-033.effect: Vessel patency 30% to 70% (P=0.0286); significant increase in dFdCTP (P=0.0053); significant survival gain only for the combination
TME-033.limitations: No numeric median survivals in the accessed text; mouse only; same single agent and model family as TME-003
TME-033.interpretation: Independent replication with a mechanism-discriminating negative control (unchanged vessel density): strengthens the decompression interpretation in mice

glosses.matrix-pressure: Mouse study showing a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme raised tumor vessel patency from 30% to 70% without changing vessel number, and increased the active gemcitabine metabolite inside tumors.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Mouse study showing a hyaluronan-degrading enzyme raised tumor vessel patency from 30% to 70% without changing vessel number, and increased the active gemcitabine metabolite inside tumors.
glosses.stroma-lessons: An independent mouse study confirming that removing hyaluronan raised vessel patency from 30 to 70 percent and increased intratumoral chemotherapy.

TME-034.citation: Chen Y, Kim J, Yang S, Wang H, Wu CJ, Sugimoto H, LeBleu VS, Kalluri R. Type I collagen deletion in alphaSMA+ myofibroblasts augments immune suppression and accelerates progression of pancreatic cancer. Cancer Cell. 2021;39(4):548-565.e6.
TME-034.clinical_status: Preclinical; no collagen- or CXCR2/CCR2-directed therapy approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-034.design: Cell-type-specific gene deletion in an autochthonous model with survival, histopathology, single-cell transcriptomics, mechanistic epithelial signalling experiments and a pharmacologic rescue
TME-034.population: Dual-recombinase autochthonous mouse PDAC: FSF-Kras-G12D/+;Trp53-frt/frt;Pdx1-Flp;alphaSMA-Cre;Col1a1-loxP/loxP (KPPF;Col1-smaKO) versus KPPF controls; single-cell RNA sequencing of tumour stroma
TME-034.n: Survival cohorts KPPF n=20 versus KPPF;Col1-smaKO n=18
TME-034.time_frame: Lifetime survival study in an autochthonous model
TME-034.finding: Deleting type I collagen specifically in alphaSMA+ myofibroblasts significantly reduced total stromal collagen content, accelerated the emergence of PanINs and PDAC, and significantly decreased overall survival (Fig 3A; KPPF n=20 versus KPPF;Col1-smaKO n=18). Mechanistically, collagen loss upregulated Cxcl5 in cancer cells via SOX9. Increased CXCL5 was associated with recruitment of CD206+F4/80+ARG1+ myeloid-derived suppressor cells and suppression of CD8+ T cells. Combined suppression of CXCR2 and CCR2 attenuated the myeloid recruitment and restrained PDAC progression.
TME-034.effect: Significantly shortened survival with myofibroblast collagen deletion; myeloid recruitment reversed by dual CXCR2/CCR2 blockade
TME-034.limitations: Single model; collagen deletion from the outset rather than in established tumours; no human validation of the SOX9-CXCL5 axis
TME-034.interpretation: Cell-type-restricted deletion of a single matrix gene in an autochthonous model, with an identified intermediate (SOX9-CXCL5) and a pharmacologic rescue: strong causal support in mice that myofibroblast-derived collagen restrains PDAC through immune composition

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study in which deleting type I collagen only in myofibroblasts, leaving the cells in place, reduced stromal collagen, accelerated cancer formation and shortened survival through myeloid-cell recruitment.

TME-035.citation: Royal RE, Levy C, Turner K, Mathur A, Hughes M, Kammula US, et al. Phase 2 trial of single agent ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4) for locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. J Immunother. 2010;33(8):828-833.
TME-035.clinical_status: Negative phase 2; ipilimumab is not approved for PDAC (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-035.design: Single-arm phase 2 trial stratified into locally advanced and metastatic cohorts, with RECIST response and toxicity as outcomes; progression alone did not mandate treatment cessation, allowing delayed responses to be observed
TME-035.population: 27 adults with locally advanced (n=7) or metastatic (n=20) pancreatic adenocarcinoma with measurable disease, good performance status (26 of 27 ECOG 0-1) and minimal comorbidities; median age 55 years (range 27-68)
TME-035.time_frame: Dosing every 3 weeks; delayed response observed after documented progression
TME-035.finding: There were no responders by RECIST criteria. One subject experienced a significant delayed response after initial progressive disease. Three subjects had grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse events: colitis (1), encephalitis (1) and hypophysitis (1). The authors concluded that single-agent ipilimumab at 3.0 mg/kg per dose is ineffective for advanced pancreatic cancer, while noting that the delayed response suggests immunotherapeutic approaches deserve further exploration.
TME-035.effect: 0 of 27 RECIST responses; 1 delayed response after initial progression; 3 of 27 with grade >=3 immune-mediated toxicity
TME-035.limitations: Small, single-arm, no biomarker selection, single dose level, response-only primary outcome
TME-035.interpretation: Single-arm phase 2: excludes a meaningful single-agent response rate; the one delayed response is a hypothesis-generating observation, not evidence of efficacy

glosses.t-cells: A 27-patient single-arm phase 2 trial in which single-agent ipilimumab produced no responses by standard criteria, with one delayed response and grade 3 or worse immune toxicity in three patients.

TME-036.citation: Hutton C, Heider F, Blanco-Gomez A, Banyard A, Kononov A, Zhang X, et al. Single-cell analysis defines a pancreatic fibroblast lineage that supports anti-tumor immunity. Cancer Cell. 2021;39(9):1227-1244.e20.
TME-036.clinical_status: Preclinical; no lineage-selective CAF therapy exists (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-036.design: Mass cytometry (CyTOF) of the mesenchymal stroma with bulk RNA sequencing of sorted subsets, followed by subcutaneous co-transplantation of tumour cells with each fibroblast lineage into immunocompetent and immunodeficient hosts
TME-036.population: Murine normal and tumour-bearing pancreas (19 PDA tumour samples analysed by mass cytometry), murine and human healthy tissues and tumours; sorted pancreatic fibroblasts (PaFs); syngeneic C57BL/6 recipients plus Rag1-/-, NOD-scid-Il2rg-/- (NSG) and Batf3-/- hosts
TME-036.n: 19 PDA tumours for CyTOF; co-transplantation of 10^5 PDA cells alone or with 10^5 CD105-positive or CD105-negative PaFs; immunodeficient arms n=6 per condition
TME-036.time_frame: Subcutaneous co-transplant growth over about 10 days to endpoint; cross-sectional CyTOF
TME-036.finding: Unlike most CAF markers, CD105 (encoded by Eng, a TGF-beta receptor co-receptor) cleanly separated two discrete fibroblast populations in all 19 tumour samples and in most normal and tumour-bearing tissues of mouse and human; CD105-positive cells were typically more abundant (about a 7:3 ratio), with the ratio varying widely between tumours. The two lineages were stable, differed in S-phase and apoptotic fractions and in aSMA, MHC-II and CD74 positivity, and diverged in their response to microenvironmental regulatory signals; their abundance correlated with distinct immune populations in PDA tumours. CD105-positive fibroblasts were permissive for tumour growth in vivo, whereas CD105-negative fibroblasts potently restricted it. In NSG mice (lacking innate and adaptive immunity) and in Rag1-/- mice (lacking mature T and B cells), co-injection with either lineage did not affect tumour…
TME-036.effect: Opposite directions of tumour growth from two fibroblast lineages at the same cell dose; restriction abolished in Rag1-/- and NSG hosts and blunted in Batf3-/- hosts; CD105-positive:negative ratio about 7:3
TME-036.limitations: Subcutaneous rather than orthotopic/autochthonous for the functional arm; human data limited to marker presence, not function; no therapeutic manipulation of the ratio in vivo
TME-036.interpretation: Cell-transfer experiment with matched doses of two prospectively isolated lineages across four host genotypes: strong causal support that fibroblast identity, not fibroblast amount, determines the direction of effect, and that the mechanism is immune

glosses.fibroblast-states: Mass cytometry and transplantation study showing the marker CD105 separates two stable pancreatic fibroblast lineages with opposite effects on tumor growth at matched dose, the restraining effect depending entirely on adaptive immunity.
glosses.blood-supply-hypoxia: Mass cytometry and transplantation study showing the marker CD105 separates two stable pancreatic fibroblast lineages with opposite effects on tumor growth at matched dose, the restraining effect depending entirely on adaptive immunity.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A mouse and human study showing two pancreatic fibroblast lineages with opposite effects on tumor growth, the suppressive one requiring adaptive immunity.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A single-cell and transplantation study showing CD105 separates two stable pancreatic fibroblast lineages with opposite effects on tumor growth, the restraining effect depending entirely on adaptive immunity.

TME-037.citation: Krishnamurty AT, Shyer JA, Thai M, Gandham V, Buechler MB, Yang YA, et al. LRRC15+ myofibroblasts dictate the stromal setpoint to suppress tumour immunity. Nature. 2022;611(7934):148-154.
TME-037.clinical_status: Preclinical; LRRC15-directed agents are investigational and none is approved (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-037.design: In vivo genetic lineage and signalling experiments: tamoxifen-inducible deletion of Tgfbr2 in dermatopontin-positive universal fibroblasts, and diphtheria-toxin-mediated selective depletion of LRRC15+ CAFs, with single-cell RNA sequencing, tumour growth and checkpoint-blockade combination endpoints
TME-037.population: Mouse models of pancreatic cancer (KPR3070 subcutaneous implantation); Dpt-IresCreERT2;Tgfbr2-fl/fl inducible conditional-knockout mice; newly generated Lrrc15-DTR-GFP knock-in mice; human bulk RNA-seq associations from prior anti-PD-L1 cohorts
TME-037.n: Depletion tumour-growth cohorts n=9-11 mice per group; conditional-knockout and control cohorts on matched tamoxifen regimens
TME-037.time_frame: Tamoxifen and diphtheria-toxin regimens over days to weeks; single-cell kinetics over the first two weeks of depletion
TME-037.finding: TGF-beta receptor 2 signalling in healthy dermatopontin+ universal fibroblasts was shown by in vivo genetic deletion to be essential for the development of cancer-associated LRRC15+ myofibroblasts; TGFbetaR2 on PDPN+ CAFs from conditional-knockout tumours was reduced by about 90%. Selective depletion of LRRC15+ CAFs markedly reduced total tumour fibroblast content, with total PDPN+ fibroblast numbers significantly reduced by about 70% in diphtheria-toxin-treated DTR+ mice. Tumour growth was significantly slowed following sustained LRRC15+ CAF depletion compared with DTR-negative controls (Fig 2f, n=9-11 per group). Single-cell analysis showed that after depletion, Lrrc15+ cells were absent for the first two weeks while Pi16+ universal-like fibroblasts (a subset also expressing Cxcl12) increased, so depletion recalibrated the remaining CAFs towards a universal fibroblast-like state.…
TME-037.effect: About 70% reduction in total fibroblasts with LRRC15+ depletion; significantly slowed tumour growth; augmented regression with anti-PD-L1
TME-037.limitations: Implanted tumours; growth rather than survival endpoints; human relevance inferred from signature associations rather than tested; depletion duration limited
TME-037.interpretation: Two independent in vivo genetic manipulations (upstream signalling knockout and downstream subtype ablation) with an immunologic mechanism and a therapy-combination endpoint: strong causal support that a defined pro-tumour CAF subtype suppresses CD8 function in mice

glosses.desmoplasia: Mouse study showing LRRC15-marked myofibroblasts arise from resting universal fibroblasts via TGF-beta receptor 2, suppress CD8 T-cell function, and that depleting them slowed growth and improved the response to anti-PD-L1.
glosses.fibroblast-states: Mouse study showing LRRC15-marked myofibroblasts arise from resting universal fibroblasts via TGF-beta receptor 2, suppress CD8 T-cell function, and that depleting them slowed growth and improved the response to anti-PD-L1.
glosses.t-cells: A mouse study showing that selectively depleting LRRC15-positive myofibroblasts relieved their direct suppression of CD8 T cells and improved the response to anti-PD-L1.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A mouse study showing that depleting one defined pro-tumor myofibroblast subtype slowed growth and improved anti-PD-L1 response.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A mouse study in which selectively depleting LRRC15-positive myofibroblasts slowed growth, relieved CD8 suppression and improved anti-PD-L1 response, with TGF-beta signaling in resident fibroblasts shown to create them.

TME-038.citation: Sherman MH, Yu RT, Engle DD, Ding N, Atkins AR, Tiriac H, et al. Vitamin D receptor-mediated stromal reprogramming suppresses pancreatitis and enhances pancreatic cancer therapy. Cell. 2014;159(1):80-93.
TME-038.clinical_status: Preclinical; vitamin D analogues are not approved as PDAC therapy and paricalcitol combinations remain investigational (US), checked 2026-10-08
TME-038.design: Transcriptome analysis of stellate-cell activation with and without VDR ligand, chromatin/transcriptional characterisation of VDR as a regulator of the activation network, plus in vivo pancreatitis and KPC survival/pharmacokinetic experiments
TME-038.population: Primary mouse pancreatic stellate cells (pre-activated 3-day versus culture-activated 7-day), cancer-associated stellate cells, human pancreatic tumour stroma for VDR expression, a murine pancreatitis model, and KPC autochthonous mice
TME-038.n: KPC survival arms (gemcitabine versus gemcitabine plus calcipotriol) with medians reported; transcriptome and histology cohorts not numerically specified in the accessed text
TME-038.time_frame: 3- and 7-day stellate-cell activation cultures; KPC survival from treatment start to death
TME-038.finding: VDR was unexpectedly expressed at high levels in pancreatic stellate cells, including cancer-associated stellate cells, and in stroma from human pancreatic tumours. Transcriptomics of activation showed loss of lipid-storage and lipid-metabolism gene expression, and the activation and cancer stromal signatures overlapped a previously published stromal signature predicting poor survival and chemoresistance. Calcipotriol markedly reduced markers of inflammation and fibrosis in a pancreatitis model and in human tumour stroma, acting through VDR as a master transcriptional regulator that reprises the quiescent stellate-cell state. In KPC mice, gemcitabine plus calcipotriol increased intratumoral gemcitabine, increased CD31 positivity and apparent vessel patency, reduced tumour volume, and significantly prolonged survival versus chemotherapy alone: median survival 14 days with gemcitabine…
TME-038.effect: Median survival 14 to 22 days (+57%); 29% long-term survivors (>30 days, mean 52.8 days) in the combination arm; no effect of calcipotriol monotherapy
TME-038.limitations: Mouse only in the efficacy arm; the human component is expression, not outcome; monotherapy inactive so the strategy is strictly adjunctive; small absolute survival differences
TME-038.interpretation: Pharmacologic reprogramming with transcriptional mechanism, a measured delivery intermediate and a survival endpoint in an autochthonous model: strong causal support in mice that reprogramming rather than ablating stellate cells improves chemotherapy response

glosses.desmoplasia: Study finding the vitamin D receptor is abundant in pancreatic stellate cells and that a vitamin D analog returned activated cells towards quiescence, improving drug delivery and survival in mice only when combined with chemotherapy.
glosses.stroma-lessons: A mouse study in which a vitamin D analog returned stellate cells toward quiescence, raised intratumoral gemcitabine and extended median survival from 14 to 22 days.
glosses.stroma-reprogramming: A study showing a vitamin D analog reprogrammed stellate cells toward quiescence, raised intratumoral gemcitabine and extended median mouse survival from 14 to 22 days, with no effect as a single agent.

DIAG-001.citation: Tran Cao HS, Balachandran A, Wang H, et al. Radiographic tumor-vein interface as a predictor of intraoperative, pathologic, and oncologic outcomes in resectable and borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. J Gastrointest Surg. 2014;18(2):269-278.
DIAG-001.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice (degree-of-contact CT reporting is embedded in US resectability classifications)
DIAG-001.design: Retrospective cohort with blinded re-review of preoperative CT; tumour-vein interface (TVI) with the SMV-PV classified as none, <=180 degrees, >180 degrees, or occlusion; correlated with need for venous resection, histologic vein invasion, margin status and survival (ROC analysis).
DIAG-001.population: 254 patients with PDAC of the pancreatic head who underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy at MD Anderson 2004-2011 with pancreatic-protocol CT within 3 months of surgery; 76.4% had received neoadjuvant chemoradiation.
DIAG-001.n: 254 (TVI none n=62; <=180 n=154; >180 n=28; occlusion n=10)
DIAG-001.time_frame: Surgery 2004-2011; median follow-up of survivors 47.1 months.
DIAG-001.finding: SMV-PV resection performed in 98/254 (39.6%). By TVI category, vein resection: 8/62 (12.9%), 56/154 (36.4%), 25/28 (89.3%), 9/10 (90.0%), p<0.001; histologic vein invasion: 2 (3.3%), 34 (22.7%), 20 (71.4%), 8 (80.0%), p<0.001 (Table 2). R0 rate did not differ across categories: 61 (98.4%), 141 (91.6%), 26 (92.9%), 10 (100%), p=0.25. Threshold 'any interface' for predicting vein resection: sensitivity 91.8%, NPV 87.1%, specificity 34.6%; threshold >180 degrees: specificity 97.4%, PPV 89.5%, sensitivity 34.7%; AUC 0.734. Median OS for cohort 33.1 months (95% CI 29.8-40.4); vein resection associated with shorter OS (27.8 vs 44.5 months, p=0.002) and PFS (16.1 vs 19.6 months, p=0.013); TVI <=180 degrees associated with better OS than greater interface.
DIAG-001.effect: Histologic vein invasion rises from 3% (no interface) to 71-80% (>180 degrees/occlusion); >180-degree threshold PPV 89.5% for vein resection; R0 unchanged across categories (p=0.25).
DIAG-001.limitations: Retrospective; head tumours only; arterial contact not analysed; reference standard (histologic vein invasion) only available when the vein was resected.
DIAG-001.interpretation: Observational association between an imaging measurement and a pathologic reference standard; supports the inference that contact angle tracks true invasion probabilistically, not deterministically, and that margin status depends on surgical strategy (planned vein resection) rather than on the angle itself.

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: A 254-patient study showing the degree of tumor-vein contact on CT predicts vein resection and invasion but not margin status.
glosses.resectability-categories: A 254-patient study showing the degree of tumor-vein contact on CT predicts vein invasion and the need for vein resection but not margin status.
glosses.pancreas-neck: MD Anderson series of 254 head cancers relating CT tumor–vein contact to true vein invasion, vein resection and margin status.
glosses.smv-portal-vein: MD Anderson series of 254 head cancers relating CT tumor–vein contact to true vein invasion, vein resection and margin status.
glosses.sma: MD Anderson series of 254 head cancers relating CT tumor–vein contact to true vein invasion, vein resection and margin status.
glosses.ct-scan: A 254-patient series showing that the degree of tumor-vein contact on CT predicts vein invasion and the need for vein resection but not whether the margin will be clear.
glosses.vessel-contact: A 254-patient series showing that the degree of tumor-vein contact on CT predicts vein invasion and the need for vein resection but not whether the margin will be clear.
glosses.vascular-resection: An MD Anderson series of 254 Whipples showing that the degree of tumor-vein contact on CT predicts vein resection and invasion but not margin status.

DIAG-002.citation: Gudmundsdottir H, Yonkus JA, Alva-Ruiz R, et al. Yield of Staging Laparoscopy for Pancreatic Cancer in the Modern Era: Analysis of More than 1,000 Consecutive Patients. J Am Coll Surg. 2023;237(1):49-57.
DIAG-002.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort; yield defined as positive laparoscopy (gross metastases and/or positive peritoneal cytology); multivariable logistic regression for risk factors.
DIAG-002.population: 1,004 patients with radiographically localized PDAC undergoing staging laparoscopy at Mayo Clinic 2017-2021; CT in all, MRI in 723 (72%), FDG-PET (CT or MRI) in 845 (84%); neoadjuvant therapy started or completed before laparoscopy in 507 (51%).
DIAG-002.finding: Positive laparoscopy in 180/1,004 (18%): gross metastases n=140 and/or positive cytology n=96. Lower after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (14% vs 22%, p=0.002). Among chemo-naive patients with lavage, 95/419 (23%) positive. Multivariable predictors (Table 3): age <=60 (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.19-2.79), distal body/tail location (OR 2.78, 1.84-4.21), tumour 21-40 mm (OR 2.33, 1.25-4.32) and >40 mm (OR 2.28, 1.14-4.56) vs <=20 mm, indeterminate extrapancreatic lesion on imaging (OR 6.84, 4.19-11.17), elevated CA 19-9 >=35 U/mL (OR 1.69, 1.02-2.81); neoadjuvant therapy OR 0.72 (0.47-1.10, p=0.13) after adjustment; peritoneal CEA elevated OR 2.94 (1.45-5.93). In patients with no indeterminate lesions, positive-laparoscopy rate ranged from 1.6% (no risk factors) to 42% (all four). Serum CA 19-9 elevated in 612 (61%); 66 patients (6.6%) were non-secretors. Peritoneal CA 19-9 elevated: sensitivity 60%,…
DIAG-002.effect: 18% positive laparoscopy overall despite CT +/- MRI +/- PET; 1.6% to 42% depending on risk factors; neoadjuvant therapy lowered yield from 22% to 14%.
DIAG-002.limitations: Retrospective; evolving practice during the study period (laparoscopy with planned same-anaesthetic resection fell over time); no long-term outcome data on cytology-positive patients.
DIAG-002.interpretation: Descriptive yield study; establishes the magnitude of imaging-invisible disease and its correlates; cannot establish whether lower yield after neoadjuvant therapy reflects eradication or selection.

glosses.why-plans-change: A 1,004-patient series in which staging laparoscopy found hidden spread in 18% of patients with radiographically localized disease.
glosses.clear-scan: A 1,004-patient series in which staging laparoscopy found hidden spread in 18% of patients with radiographically localized disease.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Mayo Clinic series of 1,004 staging laparoscopies finding hidden spread in 18% despite modern imaging.
glosses.peritoneum: Mayo Clinic series of 1,004 staging laparoscopies finding hidden spread in 18% despite modern imaging.
glosses.ct-scan: A 1,004-patient series in which staging laparoscopy found hidden spread in 18% of patients whose scans showed localized disease.
glosses.mri: A 1,004-patient series in which an indeterminate lesion outside the pancreas on imaging raised the odds of hidden spread nearly seven-fold.
glosses.pet-scan: A 1,004-patient series in which staging laparoscopy found hidden spread in 18% despite CT, MRI and usually PET.
glosses.staging-laparoscopy: A 1,004-patient series in which staging laparoscopy found hidden spread in 18% of patients whose scans showed localized disease, with yield from 1.6% to 42% by risk factors.
glosses.restaging: A 1,004-patient series in which staging laparoscopy yield fell from 22% to 14% after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
glosses.ca19-9: A 1,004-patient series in which 6.6% were non-secretors and an elevated CA 19-9 raised the odds of hidden spread at laparoscopy.
glosses.cea-ca125: A 1,004-patient laparoscopy series in which elevated CEA in peritoneal washings raised the odds of hidden metastases nearly three-fold.
glosses.liver-lesions: A 1,004-patient series in which an indeterminate lesion outside the pancreas on imaging raised the odds of hidden spread at laparoscopy nearly seven-fold.
glosses.distal-pancreatectomy: A Mayo Clinic series of 1,004 staging laparoscopies in which body-or-tail location nearly tripled the odds of hidden metastases.

DIAG-003.citation: Allen PJ, Kuk D, Castillo CF, et al. Multi-institutional Validation Study of the American Joint Commission on Cancer (8th Edition) Changes for T and N Staging in Patients With Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma. Ann Surg. 2017;265(1):185-191.
DIAG-003.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice (AJCC 8th edition in US use since 2018)
DIAG-003.design: Retrospective pooled cohort; random split into training (n=1,551) and test sets; recursive partitioning to find size and nodal cutoffs; concordance probability estimate (CPE) for 7th vs 8th edition staging.
DIAG-003.population: 2,318 patients with R0-resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma from Memorial Sloan Kettering (n=1,050), Massachusetts General Hospital (n=731) and Johns Hopkins (n=537) with dedicated GI-pathology review; median age 68; 77% pancreaticoduodenectomy; median tumour diameter 3 cm.
DIAG-003.time_frame: Institutional databases through ~2014; survival from surgery.
DIAG-003.finding: Recursive partitioning identified size cutoffs of <2.2 cm and >=4.8 cm and nodal cutoffs of 0, 1-3 and >=4 positive nodes, supporting the 8th-edition definitions. Under 7th-edition T3N0, median survival differed by institution (24 vs 37 vs 29 months, p=0.054), a difference absent when T3N0 was defined by 8th-edition size criteria. In the test set, 68% of patients fell into 7th-edition stage IIB with CPE 0.57; under the 8th edition no stage held a majority and CPE was 0.58.
DIAG-003.effect: CPE 0.57 (7th) vs 0.58 (8th); 13-month inter-institutional difference in 7th-edition T3N0 median survival eliminated by size-based T staging.
DIAG-003.limitations: High-volume academic centres only; R0 restriction; modest concordance overall (0.58), meaning stage explains a minority of survival variation.
DIAG-003.interpretation: Prognostic-model validation; shows that the size/node thresholds are statistically defensible and that extrapancreatic-extension-based T staging was non-reproducible across pathologists; does not show improved discrimination (CPE nearly unchanged).

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: A multi-institutional validation deriving the eighth-edition size and node cut points and showing improved consistency between hospitals.
glosses.lymph-nodes: Multi-institutional validation of the AJCC 8th edition showing cut-points in the number of positive nodes separate survival.
glosses.pathology-report: A 2,318-patient validation of the current staging edition's size and node cut-offs, with modest overall discrimination.

DIAG-004.citation: Ferrone CR, Marchegiani G, Hong TS, et al. Radiological and surgical implications of neoadjuvant treatment with FOLFIRINOX for locally advanced and borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. Ann Surg. 2015;261(1):12-17.
DIAG-004.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice (exploration after neoadjuvant therapy in the absence of progression)
DIAG-004.design: Retrospective cohort with blinded radiologic re-review (senior pancreatic surgeon blinded to timing) of pre- and post-FOLFIRINOX CT/MRI using AHPBA/SSO/SSAT criteria; comparison of operative and pathologic outcomes.
DIAG-004.population: Massachusetts General Hospital, April 2011-March 2014: 188 PDAC resections; 40 locally advanced/borderline patients resected after neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX (47 explored) compared with 87 upfront-resectable patients who had no neoadjuvant therapy.
DIAG-004.n: 40 FOLFIRINOX-treated resections (47 explored) vs 87 no-neoadjuvant resections
DIAG-004.time_frame: 2011-2014; median follow-up 13 months in FOLFIRINOX group.
DIAG-004.finding: Blinded re-review pre-treatment: 26 locally advanced (LA), 14 borderline; post-treatment: 19 LA, 9 borderline, 12 resectable (Table). Tumour board called complete response 6, partial 30, stable 4, no progression. Median CA 19-9 fell 169 to 16 U/mL (<40 U/mL in 72% vs 31% pre-treatment); median CT diameter 3.6 to 2.2 cm. Of 47 explored: 3 metastatic, 4 unresectable, 40 resected. R0 92% (vs 86% upfront, p=NS); node-positive 35% vs 79% (p<0.001); perineural invasion 72% vs 95%; 4 patients <1 mm residual cancer and 2 pathologic complete response. Morbidity 36% vs 63%; no pancreatic fistulas in FOLFIRINOX group. Median follow-up 11 months; OS longer with FOLFIRINOX (p=0.008). Authors state pathology showed fibrosis without viable cancer where imaging showed persistent vessel contact.
DIAG-004.effect: 28 of 40 resected tumours (70%) still classified LA/borderline on post-treatment imaging; R0 rate 92%.
DIAG-004.limitations: Small single-centre series; no formal quantification of fibrosis vs tumour at the interface; survival comparison confounded by selection.
DIAG-004.interpretation: Human observational; establishes that post-treatment vessel contact on imaging no longer implies unresectability; mechanism (fibrosis replacing tumour) inferred from pathology description, not quantified.

glosses.resectability-categories: A surgical series in which 70% of tumors resected after FOLFIRINOX still looked unresectable on scans, yet 92% were removed with clear margins.
glosses.why-plans-change: A surgical series in which 70% of tumors resected after FOLFIRINOX still looked unresectable on scans, yet 92% were removed with clear margins.
glosses.why-chemo-first: A surgical series showing node positivity of 35% after FOLFIRINOX against 79% in untreated controls.
glosses.clear-scan: A surgical series in which 70% of tumors resected after FOLFIRINOX still looked unresectable on scans, yet 92% were removed with clear margins.
glosses.pancreas-neck: Massachusetts General Hospital series showing most tumors removed with clear margins after FOLFIRINOX still looked unresectable on CT.

glosses.vessel-contact: A surgical series in which 70% of tumors resected after FOLFIRINOX still looked unresectable on scans, yet 92% were removed with clear margins.
glosses.restaging: A surgical series in which 70% of tumors resected after FOLFIRINOX still looked unresectable on scans, yet 92% were removed with clear margins.
glosses.ca19-9: A surgical series in which CA 19-9 fell from 169 to 16 U/mL after FOLFIRINOX while scans still showed vessel contact.
glosses.pathology-report: A surgical series in which node positivity fell from 79% to 35% and perineural invasion from 95% to 72% after FOLFIRINOX.
glosses.vascular-resection: A Massachusetts General Hospital series showing that after FOLFIRINOX most resected tumors still looked unresectable on scans yet 92% had clear margins.

DIAG-005.citation: Ferrone CR, Finkelstein DM, Thayer SP, et al. Perioperative CA19-9 levels can predict stage and survival in patients with resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. J Clin Oncol. 2006;24(18):2897-2902.
DIAG-005.design: Retrospective cohort; survival from first post-operative CA 19-9 (median 39 days); multivariate failure-time model including clinical, pathologic and adjuvant variables.
DIAG-005.population: 424 consecutive resections for pancreatic adenocarcinoma at Massachusetts General Hospital 1985-2004; 176 with bilirubin <2 mg/dL and preoperative CA 19-9; 111 with paired pre- and post-operative values.
DIAG-005.finding: Median preoperative CA 19-9 by stage: IA 20.5, IB 86, IIA 105, IIB 164, IV 182 U/mL (Table 2); N0 vs N1 90 vs 164 U/mL (p=0.06); T1/T2 vs T3 41 vs 162 U/mL (p=0.03). Preoperative <1,000 vs >=1,000 U/mL: median survival 2.3 vs 1.0 years (p=0.01; Table 3). Post-operative CA 19-9 <200 U/mL strongest univariate predictor (p<0.0001; Fig 2). Multivariate: decrease in CA 19-9 (p=0.0005), negative nodes (p=0.001), lower T stage (p=0.0008), post-operative CA 19-9 <200 U/mL (p=0.0007). Actuarial survival 1/3/5-year 70%/36%/30%.
DIAG-005.effect: Median survival 2.3 vs 1.0 years for preoperative <1,000 vs >=1,000 U/mL; post-operative decrease and <200 U/mL independent of stage.
DIAG-005.limitations: Single centre over 19 years; no Lewis phenotyping; cut points chosen partly from prior literature.
DIAG-005.interpretation: Observational prognostic association; by excluding hyperbilirubinaemia it isolates tumour-derived from obstruction-derived CA 19-9.

glosses.clear-scan: A single-center study showing CA 19-9 rises with stage and that a postoperative fall predicts survival independently of stage.
glosses.ca19-9: A single-center study showing CA 19-9 rises with stage and that a postoperative fall predicts survival independently of stage.

DIAG-006.citation: Bettegowda C, Sausen M, Leary RJ, et al. Detection of circulating tumor DNA in early- and late-stage human malignancies. Sci Transl Med. 2014;6(224):224ra24.
DIAG-006.design: Cross-sectional detection study using digital PCR / Safe-SeqS for tumour-specific mutations (mostly KRAS) in plasma; detection fraction by tumour type and stage; ctDNA vs circulating tumour cells comparison.
DIAG-006.population: 640 patients with various cancers; 410 non-brain patients characterised (Table 1) of whom 155 (37.8%) had pancreatic cancer; stages I-IV.
DIAG-006.finding: ctDNA detectable in >75% of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer and in 48% of patients with localized pancreatic cancer (abstract; Fig 3A). Across the four types with localized and metastatic cases (breast, colon, pancreas, gastro-oesophageal), 49-78% of localized and 86-100% of metastatic tumours had detectable ctDNA. Across all types, detection by stage was 47% (stage I), 55% (II), 69% (III), 82% (IV) (Somers Dxy 0.337); plasma concentration rose with stage (Fig 3C). ctDNA often present when circulating tumour cells were absent.
DIAG-006.limitations: Heterogeneous collection; pancreatic stage-specific counts not reported in accessed text; single draw per patient.
DIAG-006.interpretation: Descriptive; establishes that tumour burden (stage) drives plasma mutant-fragment concentration and detectability; does not establish shedding mechanism.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A foundational study finding circulating tumor DNA in more than 75% of advanced but only 48% of localized pancreatic cancers.
glosses.clear-scan: A foundational study finding circulating tumor DNA in more than 75% of advanced but only 48% of localized pancreatic cancers.
glosses.molecular-testing: A study showing ctDNA is detectable in about 48 percent of localized but over 75 percent of metastatic pancreatic cancers.
glosses.ctdna: A foundational study finding circulating tumor DNA in more than 75% of advanced but only 48% of localized pancreatic cancers.

DIAG-007.citation: Groot VP, Mosier S, Javed AA, et al. Circulating Tumor DNA as a Clinical Test in Resected Pancreatic Cancer. Clin Cancer Res. 2019;25(16):4973-4984.
DIAG-007.clinical_status: not FDA-approved; laboratory-developed test in a CLIA setting (checked 2026-10-08: no pancreatic ctDNA companion diagnostic on FDA list)
DIAG-007.design: Prospective cohort with analytic validation (ddPCR for KRAS G12D/G12V/G12R/Q61H; limit of detection 1:10,000) in a CLIA laboratory; recurrence-free and overall survival by ctDNA status; longitudinal surveillance (277 samples from 46 patients, median 5 per patient).
DIAG-007.population: 59 patients with resected PDAC at Johns Hopkins; 290 plasma samples (preoperative and longitudinal post-operative); treating clinicians blinded to ctDNA.
DIAG-007.n: 59 patients; 41 with immediate post-operative sample; 46 with follow-up samples
DIAG-007.finding: Preoperative ctDNA detected in 29/59 (49%); 21% after neoadjuvant chemotherapy vs 69% chemo-naive (p<0.001). Preoperative ctDNA: median RFS 8 vs 19 months (26/29 vs 15/30 recurred, p<0.001); multivariable HR for RFS 2.67 (p=0.011), OS 2.37 (p=0.048). Immediate post-operative sample (median day 24): ctDNA persisted or emerged in 11/41; 10/11 (91%) recurred, median RFS 5 vs 15 months (p<0.001). Surveillance: 27/30 (90%) of recurrences had ctDNA detected (sensitivity 90%, 95% CI 74-98%); 14/16 non-recurrers never positive (specificity 88%, 95% CI 62-98%); PPV 93%, NPV 82%; median lead time over clinical recurrence 84 days (IQR 25-146). Table 2: 3 of 17 patients negative throughout follow-up recurred. Median OS 17 months with surveillance ctDNA vs not reached at 30 months without (p=0.011). Turnaround 1-2 weeks.
DIAG-007.effect: Post-operative ctDNA positivity: 91% recurrence, median RFS 5 vs 15 months; surveillance sensitivity 90%, NPV 82%; neoadjuvant therapy reduced pre-op positivity 69% to 21%.
DIAG-007.limitations: Small cohort; single institution; recurrence defined radiographically; no tumour-informed comparator.
DIAG-007.interpretation: Prospective prognostic association with blinded clinicians; the neoadjuvant effect is a natural experiment on detectability but cannot separate reduced burden from reduced shedding.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A 59-patient study in which tumor DNA detected shortly after surgery was followed by recurrence in 10 of 11 patients.
glosses.clear-scan: A 59-patient study in which postoperative tumor DNA had 90% sensitivity for later recurrence.
glosses.restaging: A 59-patient study in which preoperative tumor DNA was detectable in 21% after chemotherapy against 69% without.
glosses.ctdna: A 59-patient study in which postoperative tumor DNA had 90% sensitivity and 82% negative predictive value for later recurrence.

DIAG-008.citation: Yokose T, Kitago M, Matsusaka Y, et al. Usefulness of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography for predicting the prognosis and treatment response of neoadjuvant therapy for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Cancer Med. 2020;9(12):4059-4068.
DIAG-008.clinical_status: PET response assessment not standard of care in US guidelines for PDAC restaging (checked 2026-10-08: ASCO 2020 guideline text makes no PET restaging recommendation)
DIAG-008.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort; RECIST (CT size) vs PERCIST (SUL-peak based) vs pathologic treatment response (Evans grading); PET parameters (SUVmax, SULpeak, metabolic tumour volume MTV, total lesion glycolysis) and their reduction rates versus RFS/OS.
DIAG-008.population: 42 consecutive PDAC patients treated with neoadjuvant therapy then pancreatectomy at Keio University 2014-2018; 22 had FDG-PET/CT before and after therapy with the same protocol.
DIAG-008.finding: RECIST: stable disease 20/22, partial response 2/22. PERCIST: stable metabolic disease 8, partial metabolic response 9, complete metabolic response 5. Pathologic response G3/G2/G1 in 8/12/2. Concordance with pathologic response: PERCIST 72.7% (16/22) vs RECIST 36.4% (8/22), p=0.017. Table 1: tumour size fell 25.8 to 22.7 mm (median reduction 9.6%), SUVmax 6.42 to 4.04 (38.8%), MTV 14.66 to 5.37 (65.2%), TLG 48.04 to 14.72 (64.7%), all p<=0.002. AUC for survival: MTV 0.777, SUVmax 0.500, SULpeak 0.554, TLG 0.634. MTV reduction <50%: independent predictor of RFS (HR 3.92, p=0.044) and OS (HR 14.08, p=0.023).
DIAG-008.effect: Size reduction 9.6% vs metabolic-volume reduction 65.2%; PERCIST-pathology concordance 72.7% vs RECIST 36.4%.
DIAG-008.limitations: n=22; retrospective; single regimen mix; no vessel-interface-specific analysis.
DIAG-008.interpretation: Within-patient paired measurements isolate the measurement property (anatomic vs metabolic) from patient selection; supports the explanation that treated tumour retains its volume (fibrosis) while losing metabolic activity.

glosses.resectability-categories: A 22-patient study showing PET-based response matched pathology far better than size-based response after neoadjuvant therapy.
glosses.why-plans-change: A 22-patient study showing PET-based response matched pathology far better than size-based response after neoadjuvant therapy.
glosses.clear-scan: A 22-patient study showing PET-based response matched pathology in 73% against 36% for size-based criteria after neoadjuvant therapy.
glosses.pancreas-neck: Small Japanese series showing metabolic response on PET matched pathological response better than change in size.
glosses.smv-portal-vein: Small Japanese series showing metabolic response on PET matched pathological response better than change in size.
glosses.sma: Small Japanese series showing metabolic response on PET matched pathological response better than change in size.
glosses.celiac-hepatic-arteries: Small Japanese series showing metabolic response on PET matched pathological response better than change in size.
glosses.ct-scan: A 22-patient study showing PET-based response matched pathology in 73% against 36% for size-based criteria after preoperative therapy.
glosses.pet-scan: A 22-patient study in which metabolic volume fell 65% while diameter fell 10% after preoperative therapy, and PET criteria matched pathology far better than size.
glosses.restaging: A 22-patient study in which metabolic volume fell 65% while diameter fell 10% after preoperative therapy, and PET criteria matched pathology far better than size.

DIAG-009.citation: Yoo J, Lee JM, Joo I, et al. Post-neoadjuvant treatment pancreatic cancer resectability and outcome prediction using CT, 18F-FDG PET/MRI and CA 19-9. Cancer Imaging. 2023;23(1):49.
DIAG-009.clinical_status: PET/MRI restaging investigational; CT remains the guideline-preferred modality (NCCN cited in text)
DIAG-009.design: Retrospective multi-reader (3 radiologists) diagnostic accuracy study with three reading sessions (CT alone; CT plus PET/MRI; CT plus PET plus CA 19-9) scored on a 5-point resectability scale; jackknife free-response ROC; reference standard surgical/pathologic findings or multidisciplinary…
DIAG-009.population: 120 PDAC patients (65 women; mean age 66.7) at Seoul National University Hospital who had contrast CT, FDG-PET/MRI and CA 19-9 after neoadjuvant therapy, January 2013-June 2021; baseline CT category resectable 14.2%, borderline 59.2%, locally advanced 26.7%.
DIAG-009.finding: Pooled AUC 0.853 (CT) vs 0.873 (CT+PET/MRI) vs 0.874 (CT+PET+CA 19-9), p=0.026. Sensitivity for resectability 66.2% (137/207) vs 86.0% (178/207) vs 84.5% (175/207), p<0.001. Specificity 67.3% (103/153) vs 58.8% (90/153) vs 60.1% (92/153), p=0.048; CT+PET/MRI specificity lower than CT alone (adjusted p=0.042) whereas CT+PET+CA 19-9 not significantly different (p=0.081). RECIST after therapy: partial response 39.2%, stable 48.3%, progression 12.5%; CA 19-9 normalised in 31 (25.8%); mean CA 19-9 fell 1718.8 to 461.3 U/mL. 28/69 (40.6%) R0 patients recurred (mean follow-up 18.0 months); FDG avidity at tumour-vessel contact predicted RFS (HR 4.37, p=0.033) as did pathologic vascular invasion (HR 5.36, p=0.004).
DIAG-009.effect: CT-alone sensitivity 66.2% rises to 84.5-86.0% with PET and CA 19-9; specificity falls 67.3% to ~59-60%.
DIAG-009.limitations: Single centre; retrospective; reference standard partly non-pathologic; CA 19-9 rule required normalisation, excluding non-secretors.
DIAG-009.interpretation: Reader study with within-case design isolates the informational contribution of each modality; shows the CT failure is partly a bias (persistent contact read as unresectable) that other signals can override.

glosses.resectability-categories: A restaging study showing CT alone identifies a resectable tumor after chemotherapy only about two-thirds of the time.
glosses.why-plans-change: A restaging study showing CT alone identifies a resectable tumor after chemotherapy about two-thirds of the time, improving with PET and CA 19-9.
glosses.clear-scan: A restaging study showing CT alone identifies a resectable tumor after chemotherapy about two-thirds of the time.
glosses.ct-scan: A reader study showing CT alone identifies a resectable tumor after chemotherapy about two-thirds of the time.
glosses.mri: A three-reader study in which adding PET/MRI to CT raised sensitivity for a resectable tumor after chemotherapy from 66% to 86% while lowering specificity.
glosses.pet-scan: A reader study in which adding PET/MRI to CT raised sensitivity for resectability after chemotherapy but lowered specificity, and FDG uptake at the vessel contact predicted recurrence.
glosses.vessel-contact: A reader study in which FDG uptake at the tumor-vessel contact after chemotherapy predicted recurrence.
glosses.restaging: A three-reader study showing CT alone identifies a resectable tumor after chemotherapy about two-thirds of the time, improved by PET and CA 19-9 at a cost in specificity.
glosses.ca19-9: A reader study in which adding CA 19-9 to CT and PET improved identification of resectable tumors after chemotherapy.

DIAG-010.citation: Matsuda Y, Ohkubo S, Nakano-Narusawa Y, et al. Objective assessment of tumor regression in post-neoadjuvant therapy resections for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: comparison of multiple tumor regression grading systems. Sci Rep. 2020;10(1):18278.
DIAG-010.clinical_status: CAP grading is the US reporting standard (CAP protocol); checked 2026-10-08 via study text, protocol itself not retrieved
DIAG-010.design: Multicentre retrospective pathology study; two pathologists independently graded regression with five systems (Evans, CAP, MD Anderson, Japan Pancreas Society, area-of-residual-tumour ART); Cohen's kappa; final grades vs RFS/OS by Kaplan-Meier and Cox.
DIAG-010.population: 97 PDAC patients resected after gemcitabine plus S-1-based neoadjuvant therapy (55 chemotherapy only, 42 with radiation) at four Japanese hospitals; pre-treatment status borderline 53%, resectable 31%, metastatic 9%, locally advanced 7%.
DIAG-010.time_frame: Resections before 2020; survival follow-up not detailed in accessed text.
DIAG-010.finding: Interobserver kappa: Evans 0.34 (58.8% agreement), CAP 0.50 (72.2%), MD Anderson 0.65 (95.9%), JPS 0.33 (55.2%), ART 0.60 (Table 2). Agreement was lowest for intermediate grades (Evans IIa 41.9%, CAP 1 42.9%, MDA 1 42.9%, JPS 2 30%, ART 2 35.3%). Only ART grade was associated with OS (p=0.001) and RFS (p=0.005) in univariate analysis; Evans, CAP, MDA and JPS grades were not associated with outcome.
DIAG-010.limitations: Retrospective; the prognostic comparison is underpowered for rare complete responses; grading not blinded to clinical data in all cases per accessed text.
DIAG-010.interpretation: Measurement-reliability study; establishes an upper bound on how well any imaging method can agree with 'pathologic response' when the reference itself has kappa ~0.3-0.6.

glosses.clear-scan: A pathology study showing only moderate agreement between pathologists on how much tumor preoperative treatment had killed.
glosses.pet-scan: A pathology study showing only moderate agreement between pathologists on how much tumor preoperative treatment had killed.
glosses.restaging: A pathology study showing only moderate agreement between pathologists on how much tumor preoperative treatment had killed.
glosses.pathology-report: A pathology study showing only moderate agreement between pathologists on how much tumor preoperative treatment had killed.

DIAG-011.citation: Cohen JD, Javed AA, Thoburn C, et al. Combined circulating tumor DNA and protein biomarker-based liquid biopsy for the earlier detection of pancreatic cancers. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2017;114(38):10202-10207.
DIAG-011.clinical_status: research assay; the derived multi-cancer tests are not FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer (checked 2026-10-08 FDA CDx list)
DIAG-011.design: Case-control detection study; KRAS mutations in plasma by Safe-SeqS (one mutant template in up to 10,000), compared with tumour sequencing; thresholded protein markers (CA 19-9, CEA, HGF, OPN) combined; stage-specific sensitivity with 95% CI.
DIAG-011.population: 221 patients with resectable PDAC (stage IA 12, IB 17, IIA 22, IIB 170) and 182 controls without known cancer; multi-institutional plasma collection before surgery.
DIAG-011.finding: KRAS ctDNA detected in 66/221 (30%, 95% CI 24-36%); every plasma mutation matched the primary tumour (100% concordance). By stage (Table 1): IA 25% (5-57), IB 0% (0-20), IIA 18% (5-40), IIB 35% (28-42). CA 19-9 alone 49% (43-56). ctDNA + CA 19-9 60% (53-67); combination assay 141/221 (64%, 57-70%). One of 182 controls positive (specificity 99.5%). Mutations more frequent in stage II than stage I.
DIAG-011.effect: 30% ctDNA sensitivity in resectable disease at ~99.5% specificity; 0-35% by substage.
DIAG-011.limitations: Case-control design inflates specificity estimates relative to screening populations; no longitudinal data.
DIAG-011.interpretation: Defines the detection floor under near-ideal conditions (known hotspot, high-sensitivity assay); the stage gradient supports burden-driven shedding; cannot separate shedding rate from plasma volume limits.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A study detecting KRAS tumor DNA in 30% of resectable pancreatic cancers at 99.5% specificity.
glosses.clear-scan: A study detecting KRAS tumor DNA in 30% of resectable pancreatic cancers at 99.5% specificity.
glosses.ca19-9: A case-control study in which CA 19-9 alone detected 49% of resectable pancreatic cancers at a fixed threshold.
glosses.cea-ca125: A case-control study in which adding protein markers including CEA to tumor DNA raised detection of resectable cancers from 30% to 64%.
glosses.ctdna: A study detecting KRAS tumor DNA in 30% of resectable pancreatic cancers at 99.5% specificity, with 100% plasma-tissue concordance.

DIAG-012.citation: Botta GP, Abdelrahim M, Drengler RL, et al. Association of personalized and tumor-informed ctDNA with patient survival outcomes in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Oncologist. 2024;29(10):859-869.
DIAG-012.clinical_status: laboratory-developed test; not FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer (checked 2026-10-08: FDA companion-diagnostic list shows a ctDNA MRD CDx only for bladder cancer, approved 05/15/2026)
DIAG-012.design: Retrospective multi-institutional analysis of a whole-exome-designed, germline-controlled, 16-variant tumour-informed assay (positive if >=2 variants detected); DFS by ctDNA status (Kaplan-Meier, Cox); KRAS allele subgroups.
DIAG-012.population: 298 clinically validated US patients with PDAC (commercial testing, November 2019-March 2023), 1,329 plasma samples; survival analysis in 100 stage I-III patients with an MRD-window sample (2-12 weeks post-surgery, before adjuvant therapy) and 152 in surveillance.
DIAG-012.finding: ctDNA positive in 29/100 (29%) in the MRD window and 45/152 (29.6%) in surveillance. MRD-window positive: median DFS 6.37 vs 33.31 months (HR 5.45, 95% CI 2.94-10.1, p<0.0001), consistent across stage I (HR 18.64), II (7.92), III (8.61). Surveillance positive: median DFS 11.40 months vs not reached (HR 12.38, p<0.0001); multivariable HR 24.28 (p<0.001). KRAS G12V associated with worse DFS (HR 2.19, p=0.002) vs wild-type; G12R HR 0.99, G12D 1.42 (NS). 57% of MRD-window patients had neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Elevated CA 19-9 not associated with DFS (p=0.325).
DIAG-012.effect: MRD-window ctDNA positivity 29%; HR for recurrence 5.45 (MRD) and 12.38 (surveillance).
DIAG-012.limitations: Retrospective; no head-to-head with single-KRAS assay; median follow-up short relative to PDAC recurrence timing.
DIAG-012.interpretation: Prognostic association; tumour-informed design removes genotype blind spots, so residual negatives reflect shedding/sampling limits rather than assay target choice.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A 100-patient tumor-informed ctDNA study showing a positive postoperative test carried a hazard ratio of 5.45 for recurrence.
glosses.clear-scan: A 100-patient tumor-informed ctDNA study showing a positive postoperative test carried a hazard ratio of 5.45 for recurrence.
glosses.ca19-9: A tumor-informed ctDNA cohort in which elevated CA 19-9 did not predict disease-free survival.
glosses.ctdna: A tumor-informed ctDNA cohort in which a positive postoperative test carried a hazard ratio of 5.45 for recurrence, yet only 29% tested positive.

DIAG-013.citation: Sausen M, Phallen J, Adleff V, et al. Clinical implications of genomic alterations in the tumour and circulation of pancreatic cancer patients. Nat Commun. 2015;6:7686.
DIAG-013.design: Genomic cohort with digital-PCR ctDNA detection of tumour-identified mutations (mostly KRAS); ctDNA at diagnosis and after resection vs relapse and vs timing of CT-detected progression (paired t-test).
DIAG-013.population: 101 stage II PDAC patients with potentially curative resection (24 whole-exome, 77 targeted 116-gene sequencing); 51 with plasma at diagnosis; 20 with serial post-operative plasma.
DIAG-013.time_frame: Resections before 2015; serial sampling over post-operative follow-up.
DIAG-013.finding: ctDNA detectable at diagnosis in 22/51 (43%) with specificity >99.9%. Post-operative detectable ctDNA (n=10) vs undetectable (n=10): median time to CT recurrence 9.9 months vs not reached (p=0.0199, log-rank; Fig 3a). Progression detected by ctDNA at mean 3.1 months after surgery vs 9.6 months by CT (p=0.0004, paired t-test), i.e., 6.5 months earlier (Fig 3b). ctDNA at diagnosis predicted recurrence (p=0.015). Chromatin-regulator mutations (MLL, MLL2, MLL3, ARID1A) in 20% were associated with improved survival.
DIAG-013.effect: ctDNA lead time over CT 6.5 months (3.1 vs 9.6 months); diagnosis-time detection 43%.
DIAG-013.limitations: Very small post-operative cohort; targeted-gene detection; stage II only.
DIAG-013.interpretation: Small longitudinal series; establishes temporal precedence of the blood signal over imaging, consistent with growth from sub-resolution volumes to CT-visible volumes.

glosses.clear-scan: A small cohort in which postoperative tumor DNA detected recurrence a mean of 6.5 months before CT.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: A small cohort in which postoperative tumor DNA detected recurrence a mean of 6.5 months before CT.
glosses.ctdna: A small cohort in which postoperative tumor DNA detected recurrence a mean of 6.5 months before CT.

DIAG-014.citation: Humphris JL, Chang DK, Johns AL, et al. The prognostic and predictive value of serum CA19.9 in pancreatic cancer. Ann Oncol. 2012;23(7):1713-1722.
DIAG-014.design: Retrospective multi-centre cohort; non-expressors defined as persistently <5 U/mL (no red-cell Lewis phenotyping); corrected CA 19-9 for bilirubin >2 mg/dL; disease-specific survival by Kaplan-Meier and Cox; adjuvant benefit by pre-adjuvant CA 19-9 stratum.
DIAG-014.population: 260 patients resected for pancreatic cancer in the Australian Pancreatic Cancer Genome Initiative cohort; pre-resection CA 19-9 in 202, post-resection in 231 (131 within 3 months, 162 within 6 months).
DIAG-014.time_frame: Resections before 2011; survival follow-up to analysis.
DIAG-014.finding: 10/202 (5%) were non-expressors (<5 U/mL pre and post). Post-resection CA 19-9 <3 months: <37 vs 37-120 vs >120 U/mL median DSS 25.6 vs 20.7 vs 14.8 months (p=0.0052).
