Normalisation (<37 U/mL) within 6 months: 29.9 vs 14.8 months (p=0.0004; Fig 1B). Pre-resection, bilirubin <2 mg/dL: non-expressors 18.6, <120 U/mL 35.6, >120 U/mL 17.4 months (p=0.0444). Pre-adjuvant CA 19-9 <=90 U/mL: adjuvant chemotherapy 26.0 vs no adjuvant 16.7 months (p=0.0108); >90 U/mL: no adjuvant benefit (p=0.7194). Normal perioperative CA 19-9 (<37 pre and post): 5-year survival 42%. Of 122 with values within 3 months, 93% had bilirubin <2 mg/dL and needed no correction.
DIAG-014.effect: Normalisation within 6 months doubles median survival (29.9 vs 14.8 months); 5% non-expressors.
DIAG-014.limitations: Retrospective; incomplete sampling at each time point; adjuvant regimens heterogeneous.
DIAG-014.interpretation: Observational prognostic/predictive associations; the adjuvant-benefit stratification is hypothesis-generating, not randomised within strata.

glosses.why-plans-change: A 202-patient series finding 5% of patients make no CA 19-9 and that normalization after surgery doubles median survival.
glosses.clear-scan: A 202-patient series finding 5% of patients make no CA 19-9 and that normalization after surgery doubles median survival.
glosses.ca19-9: A 202-patient series finding 5% of patients make no CA 19-9 and that normalization after surgery doubles median survival.

DIAG-015.citation: Liu C, Deng S, Jin K, et al. Lewis antigen-negative pancreatic cancer: An aggressive subgroup. Int J Oncol. 2020;56(4):900-908.
DIAG-015.clinical_status: CA125 not guideline-endorsed as a pancreatic monitoring marker; used empirically
DIAG-015.design: Retrospective cohort plus in vitro/in vivo experiments; survival by Lewis status; serum CA 19-9 and CA125 by Lewis status; MUC16 immunohistochemistry; proteomics and morphology of Lewis-negative vs -positive cells.
DIAG-015.population: 853 pancreatic cancer patients at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (September 2004-November 2011) with Lewis antigen evaluation; six pancreatic cancer cell lines sequenced for Lewis (FUT3) status; orthotopic mouse model; immunohistochemistry on 20 Lewis-negative and 19 Lewis-positive…
DIAG-015.n: 853 patients; 39 tumours for IHC; 6 cell lines
DIAG-015.finding: 11.7% of 853 were Lewis negative. Median survival 7.4 vs 13.3 months (p<0.001); higher proportion metastatic (p=0.004). Serum CA 19-9 106.0 +/- 273.1 vs 499.7 +/- 635.0 U/mL (p<0.001); serum CA125 251.9 +/- 642.0 vs 135.8 +/- 401.6 U/mL (p<0.001). MUC16 IHC high in 16/20 Lewis-negative vs 9/19 Lewis-positive tumours (p=0.048). Lewis-negative cell lines showed higher MUC16 expression and altered morphology (accessed text).
DIAG-015.effect: Lewis-negative 11.7%; median survival 7.4 vs 13.3 months; CA125 roughly 1.9-fold higher, CA 19-9 roughly 5-fold lower.
DIAG-015.limitations: Lewis assay method and the 'low-secretor' Lewis-positive subgroup not separated in the accessed text; no longitudinal CA125 monitoring data.
DIAG-015.interpretation: Human observational plus experimental correlation; supports CA125 as a candidate monitoring marker in non-secretors but does not test monitoring performance.

glosses.why-plans-change: An 853-patient series finding 11.7% Lewis-negative patients, who make little or no CA 19-9 and had worse outcomes.
glosses.clear-scan: An 853-patient series finding 11.7% Lewis-negative patients, who make little or no CA 19-9.
glosses.ca19-9: An 853-patient series finding 11.7% Lewis-negative patients, with lower CA 19-9, higher CA-125 and shorter survival.
glosses.cea-ca125: An 853-patient series in which Lewis-negative patients had far lower CA 19-9, about twice the CA-125 and stronger tumor MUC16 staining.

DIAG-016.citation: Zhao B, Cheng Q, Cao H, et al. Dynamic change of serum CA19-9 levels in benign and malignant patients with obstructive jaundice after biliary drainage and new correction formulas. BMC Cancer. 2021;21(1):517.
DIAG-016.clinical_status: not applicable (interpretive rule; US guidelines advise measuring CA 19-9 after biliary decompression)
DIAG-016.design: Retrospective before/after cohort; CA 19-9 before and after drainage; comparison of percentage drop between benign and malignant; linear regression correction formula.
DIAG-016.population: 121 patients with obstructive jaundice undergoing biliary drainage at a single Chinese hospital, January 2014-January 2019: 102 malignant (pancreaticobiliary tumours) and 19 benign.
DIAG-016.time_frame: 2014-2019; CA 19-9 re-measured after drainage (interval per protocol in accessed text).
DIAG-016.finding: Baseline CA 19-9 higher in malignant than benign. Total bilirubin level not correlated with CA 19-9 (p=0.109). After drainage, mean CA 19-9 fell by 39.2% (IQR -18.4 to 78.6%) in malignant vs 75.7% (IQR 58.1-86.6%) in benign obstruction (p=0.014). Derived correction: CA 19-9_true = 0.63 x CA 19-9_measured - 20.3 (R2 0.693, p<0.001), with diagnostic value similar to the post-drainage value.
DIAG-016.effect: Benign obstruction: three-quarters of the CA 19-9 elevation disappears with drainage; malignant: 39% drop.
DIAG-016.limitations: Single centre; retrospective; the linear correction is derived and tested in the same cohort.
DIAG-016.interpretation: Before/after natural experiment (drainage as perturbation) establishing that obstruction itself raises CA 19-9 and that the increment is reversible within the drainage interval; benign group shows the obstruction-only component.

glosses.why-plans-change: A study of CA 19-9 before and after biliary drainage showing benign obstruction inflates the marker far more than cancer does.
glosses.clear-scan: A study of CA 19-9 before and after biliary drainage showing benign obstruction inflates the marker far more than cancer does.
glosses.jaundice: A study of CA 19-9 before and after biliary drainage showed the marker falls substantially once obstruction is relieved, more so in benign than malignant blockage.
glosses.bile-duct-ampulla: Study showing CA 19-9 falls after biliary drainage by about three-quarters in benign and 39% in malignant obstruction.
glosses.liver: Study showing CA 19-9 falls after biliary drainage by about three-quarters in benign and 39% in malignant obstruction.
glosses.ca19-9: A study of CA 19-9 before and after biliary drainage showing benign obstruction inflates the marker far more than cancer does.

DIAG-017.citation: van Roessel S, Kasumova GG, Verheij J, et al. International Validation of the Eighth Edition of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) TNM Staging System in Patients With Resected Pancreatic Cancer. JAMA Surg. 2018;153(12):e183617.
DIAG-017.design: International multicentre retrospective cohort; restaging by 7th and 8th editions; Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox, concordance statistics.
DIAG-017.population: 1,525 consecutive patients after pancreatoduodenectomy for non-metastatic PDAC at five tertiary centres in Europe and the United States, 2000-2015; median age 66; 52.6% male.
DIAG-017.finding: Stage distribution shifted from 7th (IA 2.7%, IB 2.8%, IIA 13.1%, IIB 80.6%, III 0.8%) to 8th (IA 7.7%, IB 9.4%, IIA 1.4%, IIB 42.2%, III 39.2%); 774 (50.8%) migrated (12.0% down, 38.8% up). 5-year survival by 8th edition: IA 39.2%, IB 33.9%, IIA 27.6%, IIB 21.0%, III 10.8% (p<0.001). N stage: N0 35.6%, N1 20.8%, N2 10.9% (p<0.001). In node-negative patients T stage was not associated with survival in either edition. C statistic 0.55 (95% CI 0.53-0.57) for 7th vs 0.57 (0.55-0.60) for 8th. Median OS 24.4 months (95% CI 23.4-26.2).
DIAG-017.effect: C statistic 0.55 to 0.57; N0/N1/N2 5-year survival 35.6/20.8/10.9%; T stage non-prognostic within N0.
DIAG-017.limitations: Retrospective; no neoadjuvant-era ypTNM analysis; modest discrimination overall.
DIAG-017.interpretation: Independent external validation; shows nodal burden, not primary size, carries most prognostic information after resection.

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: An international validation of the eighth-edition staging system in 1,525 resected patients showing nodal count separates survival while size does not within node-negative disease.
glosses.survival-statistics: An international validation of the eighth-edition staging system in 1,525 resected patients, giving five-year survival by stage and nodal status.
glosses.lymph-nodes: International validation of the AJCC 8th edition giving five-year survival of 35.6%, 20.8% and 10.9% for N0, N1 and N2.
glosses.pathology-report: A 1,525-patient international validation in which the number of positive nodes, not tumor size, carried most prognostic information.

DIAG-018.citation: Cacciato Insilla A, Vivaldi C, Giordano M, et al. Tumor Regression Grading Assessment in Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer After Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX: Interobserver Agreement and Prognostic Implications. Front Oncol. 2020;10:64.
DIAG-018.design: Retrospective pathology study; two expert pancreatic pathologists independently applied CAP, Evans, MD Anderson, Hartman and a Dworak-inspired score; Kendall coefficient of concordance; correlation of grades with OS, PFS, DFS.
DIAG-018.population: 29 patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer resected after modified FOLFIRINOX at Pisa (median age 58; ECOG 0 in 82.8%).
DIAG-018.finding: Concordance (Kendall K): CAP 0.644, MD Anderson 0.521, Evans 0.566, Hartman 0.830, Dworak-inspired 0.913 (all p<0.05; Table 3). Evans had total consensus in only 9/29. No complete pathologic response observed. None of the four established systems correlated with survival; the Dworak-inspired score correlated with OS in individual assessments.
DIAG-018.effect: Concordance 0.52-0.64 for the three systems in common US use.
DIAG-018.interpretation: Reliability study; converges with DIAG-010 across regimens, countries and statistics.

glosses.restaging: A FOLFIRINOX pathology series confirming moderate agreement between pathologists on regression grade and no link between grade and survival.
glosses.pathology-report: A FOLFIRINOX pathology series confirming moderate agreement on regression grade and no link between grade and survival.

DIAG-019.citation: Nakatsubo R, Yamamoto K, Itoi T, et al. Histopathological evaluation of needle tract seeding caused by EUS-fine-needle biopsy based on resected specimens from patients with solid pancreatic masses: An analysis of 73 consecutive cases. Endosc Ultrasound. 2021;10(3):207-213.
DIAG-019.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice (EUS-guided sampling before neoadjuvant therapy; transgastric route concern for body/tail tumours)
DIAG-019.design: Retrospective consecutive series; pathologic examination of the puncture route in the resected specimen with seeding defined as a continuum between tract and tumour; clinical adverse events recorded.
DIAG-019.population: 73 consecutive patients (67 PDAC, 5 neuroendocrine, 1 acinar) who had preoperative EUS-FNB and resection at Tokyo Medical University, April 2014-March 2016; needle 22G in 76.7%, 25G 19.2%, 20G 4.1%; median 3 passes; transgastric 46.5%, transduodenal 53.5%.
DIAG-019.finding: Diagnostic accuracy 98.6%; sampling adequate in 72/73. Clinical adverse events 3/73 (4.1%: bleeding 2, pancreatitis 1). Histologic needle-tract seeding in 2/73 (2.7%): case 1 a 60-mm head adenocarcinoma, transduodenal 22G, 2 passes, stage IIB, with later peritoneal recurrence; case 2 a 140-mm acinar carcinoma, transgastric, total pancreatectomy (Table 5). Median interval biopsy-to-surgery 35 days (6-304).
DIAG-019.limitations: Single centre; 73 cases; mostly head tumours where the tract is removed, so distal-tumour risk is extrapolated.
DIAG-019.interpretation: Direct histologic observation of the tract establishes that seeding occurs at a low but non-zero rate; cannot estimate clinical consequence because the tract was resected with the specimen in pancreatoduodenectomy.

glosses.duodenum: Japanese series of 73 resected tumors finding needle-track seeding after endoscopic biopsy in 2.7%.
glosses.stomach: Japanese series of 73 resected tumors finding needle-track seeding after endoscopic biopsy in 2.7%.
glosses.peritoneum: Japanese series of 73 resected tumors finding needle-track seeding after endoscopic biopsy in 2.7%.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A 73-patient resected series with 98.6% biopsy accuracy, 4.1% adverse events and needle-track seeding in 2.7%.

DIAG-020.citation: Bunduc S, Varzaru B, Iacob RA, et al. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration pancreatic adenocarcinoma samples yield adequate DNA for next-generation sequencing: A cohort analysis. World J Gastroenterol. 2023;29(18):2864-2874.
DIAG-020.clinical_status: practice-relevant; US guidelines (ASCO 2020) recommend somatic/germline testing for MSI/MMR, BRCA and NTRK in treatment-eligible patients
DIAG-020.design: Prospective single-centre cohort; spectrophotometric DNA yield and purity (A260/280, A260/230); adequacy thresholds >=10 ng (amplicon NGS), >=50 ng (exome), >=100 ng (genome); comparison by needle size and tumour characteristics.
DIAG-020.population: 105 patients with EUS-FNA-confirmed PDAC at a Romanian tertiary centre, November 2018-December 2021; 22G needle in 71%, 19G in 29%; one pass dedicated to DNA extraction.
DIAG-020.finding: Median DNA yield 1,289 ng (IQR 534.75-3,101); A260/280 1.85 (1.79-1.86); A260/230 2.2 (1.72-2.36). Yield >10 ng in all samples and >100 ng in 93% (one sample <50 ng). No difference in concentration or A260/280 by needle size; 22G had higher A260/230 (p=0.038). NGS adequacy 90% for 19G and 89-91% for 22G depending on NGS type. Tumour size and location did not correlate with DNA parameters.
DIAG-020.effect: ~90% of single FNA passes adequate for any NGS tier; 93% >100 ng.
DIAG-020.limitations: Single centre; no comparison with core biopsy; purity thresholds are surrogate endpoints.
DIAG-020.interpretation: Descriptive feasibility; shows DNA quantity is rarely the limit, so sequencing failures arise from tumour fraction/purity, not mass.

glosses.why-plans-change: A study showing a single endoscopic-ultrasound needle sample yields enough DNA for full gene sequencing in about 90% of cases.
glosses.molecular-testing: A study showing about 90 percent of single endoscopic-ultrasound needle passes yield adequate DNA for sequencing.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A 105-patient cohort in which a single EUS needle pass yielded enough DNA for sequencing in about 90%.

DIAG-021.citation: Alaref A, Siltamaki D, Cerasuolo JO, et al. Impact of pre-operative abdominal MRI on survival for patients with resected pancreatic carcinoma: a population-based study. Lancet Reg Health Am. 2024;35:100809.
DIAG-021.clinical_status: MRI for indeterminate liver lesions is guideline-endorsed; routine pre-operative MRI not mandated (US)
DIAG-021.design: Population-based retrospective cohort; all-cause mortality by receipt of pre-operative abdominal MRI with multivariable adjustment.
DIAG-021.population: 4,579 adults who underwent pancreatectomy for PDAC in Ontario, Canada, January 2011-December 2022 (ICES linked administrative data); 2,432 men; mean age 65.2.
DIAG-021.finding: 51.4% had pre-operative MRI. Median survival after pancreatectomy 25.9 months overall (95% CI 24.8-27.5); 33.1 months (30.7-37.2) with MRI vs 21.1 months (19.8-22.6) without. Adjusted HR 0.828 (95% CI 0.769-0.890), a 17.2% (11.0-23.1) reduction in mortality rate. Companion research letter in the same population (Cerasuolo 2026, World J Surg; not counted) reported futile laparotomy and/or diagnostic laparoscopy in 6.4% with MRI vs 9.7% without (propensity-weighted OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.60-0.96).
DIAG-021.effect: aHR 0.828 for all-cause mortality after resection; median survival 33.1 vs 21.1 months.
DIAG-021.limitations: Administrative data without imaging findings; cannot confirm that excluded patients had liver metastases.
DIAG-021.interpretation: Observational with confounding by indication (healthier patients, more neoadjuvant therapy, longer diagnosis-to-surgery interval in MRI group); supports but does not prove that MRI improves patient selection by detecting liver metastases.

glosses.survival-statistics: A Canadian population registry of 4,579 resected patients with a median survival of 25.9 months, higher among those who had preoperative MRI.
glosses.liver: Ontario population study associating pre-operative MRI with 17% lower mortality after pancreatectomy.
glosses.mri: A population study of 4,579 pancreatectomies in which preoperative MRI was associated with longer survival after adjustment.
glosses.staging-laparoscopy: A population study of 4,579 pancreatectomies in which preoperative MRI was associated with longer survival after adjustment.
glosses.liver-lesions: A population study of 4,579 pancreatectomies in which preoperative MRI was associated with longer survival after adjustment.

DIAG-022.citation: Psar R, Urban O, Cerna M, et al. Improvement of the Diagnosis of Isoattenuating Pancreatic Carcinomas by Defining their Characteristics on Contrast Enhanced Computed Tomography and Endosonography with Fine-Needle Aspiration (EUS-FNA). Diagnostics (Basel). 2021;11(5):776.
DIAG-022.clinical_status: guideline-recommended practice (EUS for suspected tumour not seen on CT)
DIAG-022.design: Retrospective diagnostic cohort; isoattenuating (no visible hypodense mass) vs hypoattenuating tumours on CT; secondary signs; EUS size; EUS-FNA sensitivity by group; ROC for size.
DIAG-022.population: 173 patients with pancreatic carcinoma (median age 68) who had multiphase contrast CT followed by EUS-FNA at diagnosis in two Czech centres.
DIAG-022.time_frame: Diagnosis period not specified in accessed text; cross-sectional.
DIAG-022.finding: Isoattenuating carcinomas 21/173 (12.1%). Secondary signs on CT in 20/21 (95.2%): duct and/or bile-duct dilatation 85.7%, pancreatic-duct interruption 76.2%, abnormal contour 33.3%, distal atrophy 9.5%. All isoattenuating tumours were in the head (100% vs 59.2%, p<0.001) and were resected with curative intent more often (85.7% vs 44.7%, p=0.001). EUS visualised the tumour in 100%; optimal EUS size cut-off for isoattenuation <=25 mm (AUC 0.898). EUS-FNA sensitivity 90.5% vs 92.8% (p=0.886); false-negative cytology in 2/21 isoattenuating (9.5%) and 11/152 hypoattenuating.
DIAG-022.effect: 12.1% of carcinomas isoattenuating; 95.2% have indirect CT signs; EUS-FNA sensitivity ~90% in both groups.
DIAG-022.limitations: Retrospective; no interval-cancer or missed-diagnosis follow-up; two-centre.
DIAG-022.interpretation: Descriptive; links small size (<=25 mm) and low cellularity/attenuation contrast to CT invisibility while ductal obstruction signs persist; EUS as rescue modality.

glosses.pancreas-head: Two-center study showing 12% of pancreatic cancers are invisible as a mass on CT and are revealed by duct changes and endoscopic ultrasound.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Two-center study showing 12% of pancreatic cancers are invisible as a mass on CT and are revealed by duct changes and endoscopic ultrasound.
glosses.duodenum: Two-center study showing 12% of pancreatic cancers are invisible as a mass on CT and are revealed by duct changes and endoscopic ultrasound.
glosses.stomach: Two-center study showing 12% of pancreatic cancers are invisible as a mass on CT and are revealed by duct changes and endoscopic ultrasound.
glosses.ct-scan: A two-center series in which 12% of pancreatic carcinomas were invisible as a mass on CT and were found by indirect duct signs and endoscopic ultrasound.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A two-center series in which EUS visualized every pancreatic carcinoma, including those invisible on CT, with needle sampling sensitivity of about 90%.

DIAG-023.citation: Yasuta S, Kobayashi T, Aizawa H, et al. Relationship between surgical R0 resectability and findings of peripancreatic vascular invasion on CT imaging after neoadjuvant S-1 and concurrent radiotherapy in patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. BMC Cancer. 2020;20(1):1184.
DIAG-023.clinical_status: S-1 chemoradiation not US standard; the imaging finding generalises
DIAG-023.design: Retrospective cohort; two blinded radiologists classified post-treatment MDCT as progression (PVI) or non-progression (NVI) of vascular invasion by tumour-vessel contact length; R0 rates compared with exact 95% CI of the difference; Evans pathologic grading.
DIAG-023.population: 29 borderline resectable (NCCN 2009 definition) PDAC patients who underwent laparotomy after neoadjuvant S-1 with concurrent radiotherapy at the National Cancer Center Hospital East, Japan, 2008-2017, including JASPAC 05 trial participants.
DIAG-023.finding: RECIST: partial response 3 (10%), stable 25 (86%), progression 1 (3%). PVI 9/29 (31%), NVI 20/29 (69%). R0 in 27/29 (93%): PVI 9/9 (100%), NVI 18/20 (90%); risk difference -10.0% (95% CI -31.7 to 20.4%).
DIAG-023.effect: R0 100% despite CT progression of vascular invasion (n=9).
DIAG-023.limitations: n=29; single centre; regimen not used in the US.
DIAG-023.interpretation: Small replication; strengthens the inference that post-radiation perivascular change on CT is not viable tumour.

glosses.resectability-categories: A 29-patient series in which margin-negative resection was achieved in all nine patients whose scans showed progression of vascular involvement after treatment.
glosses.pancreas-neck: Small Japanese series achieving clear margins despite apparent progression of vascular contact on CT after chemoradiation.
glosses.smv-portal-vein: Small Japanese series achieving clear margins despite apparent progression of vascular contact on CT after chemoradiation.
glosses.sma: Small Japanese series achieving clear margins despite apparent progression of vascular contact on CT after chemoradiation.
glosses.vessel-contact: A 29-patient chemoradiation series in which all nine patients whose CT showed progressing vascular contact had clear margins.
glosses.restaging: A 29-patient chemoradiation series in which all nine patients whose CT showed progressing vascular contact had clear margins.

DIAG-024.citation: Hadano N, Murakami Y, Uemura K, et al. Prognostic value of circulating tumour DNA in patients undergoing curative resection for pancreatic cancer. Br J Cancer. 2016;115(1):59-65.
DIAG-024.design: Retrospective; ddPCR for KRAS G12D/G12V/G12R in archived plasma cell-free DNA; analytic limit of detection 0.01-0.1% (1 mutant per 1,000-10,000 wild-type); OS by ctDNA status; multivariate Cox.
DIAG-024.population: 105 patients who underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy for PDAC at Hiroshima University; 82% received adjuvant gemcitabine; 50% borderline resectable (2014 NCCN); 17% para-aortic node positive (stage IV).
DIAG-024.finding: KRAS mutation in 86/105 (82%) tumours (G12D 42%, G12V 29%, G12R 11%; wild-type 18%). ctDNA detected in 33/105 (31%) at mean 10.1 copies/mL (0.05-9.5% mutant fraction). Median OS 13.6 (ctDNA+) vs 27.6 months (ctDNA-), p<0.0001. Multivariate independent predictors: ctDNA (HR 3.2, 95% CI 1.8-5.4, p<0.001), node metastasis (HR 2.2), UICC stage (HR 2.0); CA 19-9 >=90 U/mL not independent (HR 1.2, 0.7-2.0, p=0.57). In resectable subset (n=53) ctDNA detected in 14 (26%) and still prognostic (p<0.001). Among the 72 ctDNA-negative patients, 2-year OS was 53% - i.e., nearly half still died despite a negative test.
DIAG-024.effect: ctDNA detectable in 31% overall / 26% resectable; negative patients 2-year OS 53% (substantial residual mortality).
DIAG-024.limitations: Retrospective; three-allele assay; no serial post-operative sampling.
DIAG-024.interpretation: Independent prognostic replication; the gap between 31% detectability and ~70-80% eventual recurrence quantifies the false-negative space of a tumour-naive single-gene assay.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A 105-patient study showing two-year survival of only 53% even among patients with undetectable tumor DNA.
glosses.clear-scan: A 105-patient study showing two-year survival of only 53% even among patients with undetectable tumor DNA.
glosses.ca19-9: A 105-patient study in which CA 19-9 above 90 U/mL was not an independent predictor once tumor DNA was in the model.
glosses.ctdna: A 105-patient study showing two-year survival of only 53% even among patients with undetectable tumor DNA.

DIAG-025.citation: Maulat C, Canivet C, Cabarrou B, et al. Prognostic impact of circulating tumor DNA detection in portal and peripheral blood in resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients. Sci Rep. 2024;14(1):27296.
DIAG-025.design: Prospective single-centre cohort; tumour mutations by NGS, ctDNA by ddPCR (positive >=3 mutant droplets per >=10,000); portal vs peripheral and before- vs after-mobilisation comparison; RFS/OS associations.
DIAG-025.population: 34 patients undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy for resectable PDAC at Toulouse University Hospital, February 2018-June 2022; portal and peripheral blood drawn before and after tissue mobilisation and over 12 post-operative months.
DIAG-025.finding: 2-year RFS 47.6% (95% CI 29.5-63.6), OS 65.7% (46.5-79.4). Intraoperative ctDNA in portal or peripheral blood associated with worse RFS (HR 3.26, 95% CI 1.26-8.45, p=0.010) and OS (HR 5.46, 1.65-18.01, p=0.002). Portal-vein sampling did NOT improve detection over peripheral. Tissue mobilisation raised peripheral cfDNA 2.74-fold (2,864 to 7,866 copies/mL, p<0.0001) and ctDNA 2.5-fold (p=0.031); detection after mobilisation still prognostic (RFS HR 2.77; OS HR 4.24). 13/14 (92.9%) with positive intraoperative ctDNA had KRAS-mutant tumour; one KRAS-wild-type tumour became ctDNA-positive peripherally only after mobilisation.
DIAG-025.effect: Surgical manipulation raises measured ctDNA ~2.5-fold; sampling site/timing changes a negative to a positive.
DIAG-025.limitations: n=34; single centre; ddPCR limited to identified tumour mutations.
DIAG-025.interpretation: Within-patient perturbation (mechanical mobilisation) that causally raises shed fragments, demonstrating that measured ctDNA depends on physical release and sampling moment, not only on disease presence - directly supporting 'a negative test is not proof of absence'.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A 34-patient study showing surgical handling of the tumor raises measured tumor DNA about 2.5-fold, illustrating sampling limits.
glosses.clear-scan: A 34-patient study showing surgical handling of the tumor raises measured tumor DNA about 2.5-fold, illustrating sampling limits.
glosses.smv-portal-vein: French study showing portal-vein sampling did not improve tumor DNA detection and that handling the tumor raised it 2.5-fold.
glosses.ctdna: A 34-patient study showing surgical handling of the tumor raises measured tumor DNA about 2.5-fold, illustrating sampling limits.

DIAG-026.citation: Zill OA, Greene C, Sebisanovic D, et al. Cell-Free DNA Next-Generation Sequencing in Pancreatobiliary Carcinomas. Cancer Discov. 2015;5(10):1040-1048.
DIAG-026.clinical_status: not applicable (research/commercial assay); plasma NGS used clinically when tissue insufficient (ASCO 2020 permits plasma when tissue inadequate)
DIAG-026.design: Prospective concordance study; 54-gene cfDNA NGS panel vs commercial tissue gene-panel NGS; per-gene sensitivity/specificity with tissue as reference; serial cfDNA vs tumour-marker correlation.
DIAG-026.population: 26 patients with advanced pancreatic (n=18) or biliary (n=8) carcinoma with tumour material available; prospective blood draws.
DIAG-026.finding: Tumour sequencing failed in 9/26 (35%). In the 17 with paired results, 28/31 tissue-detected mutations were also found in cfDNA (90.3% overlap, 95% CI 73.1-97.5%). Diagnostic accuracy 97.7%; across KRAS, TP53, APC, FBXW7, SMAD4 average sensitivity 92.3% (range 50-100%), specificity 100%. cfDNA identified mutations in 7/9 (78%) of the quantity-not-sufficient tissue cases; the other 2 had none detected in plasma. Serial cfDNA correlated with tumour-marker dynamics (r=0.93). One plasma-only mutation (JAK2 V617F) came from a distinct haematopoietic compartment (clonal haematopoiesis); another tissue-only mutation was likely below the cfDNA limit of detection.
DIAG-026.effect: Plasma-tissue mutation concordance 90.3%; plasma recovered genotype in 78% of insufficient-tissue cases.
DIAG-026.limitations: 26 patients; advanced disease; concordance may fall in low-burden resectable disease where ctDNA is near the floor.
DIAG-026.interpretation: Prospective paired comparison; distinguishes assay-target and tissue-quantity limits from true biological absence, and flags clonal haematopoiesis as a source of plasma false positives.

glosses.molecular-testing: A concordance study in which plasma found 90 percent of tissue mutations and recovered a genotype in 78 percent of inadequate-tissue cases.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A small series in which plasma sequencing recovered the tumor genotype in 78% of cases whose tissue was insufficient.
glosses.ctdna: A paired tissue-plasma series with 90% concordance that recovered the genotype from plasma in 78% of insufficient-tissue cases and flagged clonal hematopoiesis as a false-positive source.

TX-001.citation: Von Hoff DD, Ervin T, Arena FP, et al. Increased survival in pancreatic cancer with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine. N Engl J Med. 2013;369(18):1691-1703.
TX-001.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine, first-line metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (Abraxane NDA 021660 s037, 2013-09-06; label 1.3 checked 2026-10-08)
TX-001.design: International open-label randomized phase 3 (MPACT), 1:1, stratified; primary endpoint OS in ITT
TX-001.population: Treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, Karnofsky PS >=70; 861 patients at 151 centers in 11 countries (North America 63%, eastern Europe 15%, Australia 14%, western Europe 9%)
TX-001.finding: Median OS 8.5 mo (95% CI 7.89-9.53) vs 6.7 mo (6.01-7.23); HR for death 0.72 (95% CI 0.62-0.83; P<0.001) based on 692 deaths (80%); 1-yr OS 35% vs 22%; 2-yr OS 9% vs 4%. Median PFS by independent review 5.5 vs 3.7 mo (HR 0.69, 0.58-0.82; P<0.001); response rate by independent review 23% vs 7% (P<0.001). Grade >=3: neutropenia 38% vs 27%, fatigue 17% vs 7%, neuropathy 17% vs 1%; febrile neutropenia 3% vs 1%; grade >=3 neuropathy improved to grade <=1 in a median of 29 days. Subsequent therapy 38% vs 42%; 6% of gemcitabine arm crossed to nab-paclitaxel; OS censored at subsequent therapy 9.4 vs 6.8 mo (HR 0.68). CA19-9 decrease >=90% in 31% vs 14% (P<0.001); >=90% decline associated with median OS 13.5 vs 8.2 mo (HR 0.53). Table 2 (efficacy), Fig 1 (KM OS).
TX-001.effect: HR death 0.72 (0.62-0.83); absolute median OS gain 1.8 months; 1-yr OS +13 percentage points
TX-001.limitations: Modest absolute gain; neuropathy; no quality-of-life primary data in accessed text; population excludes locally advanced disease
TX-001.interpretation: Randomized interventional evidence that the doublet causes longer survival than gemcitabine in this population; does not identify mechanism

glosses.fatigue: The phase 3 trial of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel reported severe fatigue in 17% versus 7% with gemcitabine alone.
glosses.neuropathy: The phase 3 trial of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel reported severe neuropathy in 17% versus 1% with gemcitabine alone.
glosses.fever-infection: The phase 3 trial of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel reported severe neutropenia in 38% versus 27% with gemcitabine alone.
glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: MPACT: 861 previously untreated patients with metastatic disease; gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel gave median survival of 8.5 versus 6.7 months with more neutropenia, fatigue and neuropathy.
glosses.gemcitabine: MPACT: gemcitabine alone was the control arm in 861 patients with metastatic disease, with median survival of 6.7 months and grade 3 or worse neutropenia in 27%.

TX-002.citation: Wainberg ZA, Melisi D, Macarulla T, et al. NALIRIFOX versus nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine in treatment-naive patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (NAPOLI 3): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2023;402(10409):1272-1281.
TX-002.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): Onivyde with oxaliplatin, fluorouracil and leucovorin, first-line metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (NDA 207793 s016, 2024-02-13; label checked 2026-10-08)
TX-002.design: Randomized open-label phase 3, 1:1, stratified by region, ECOG PS, liver metastases; primary endpoint OS in ITT; 543 events for 90% power for HR 0.75
TX-002.population: Treatment-naive metastatic PDAC, ECOG PS 0-1, no upper age limit; 187 community and academic sites in 18 countries
TX-002.finding: 544 deaths at median follow-up 16.1 mo (data cutoff July 23, 2022). Median OS 11.1 mo (95% CI 10.0-12.1) vs 9.2 mo (8.3-10.6); HR 0.83 (0.70-0.99); p=0.036. OS at 12 mo 45.6% vs 39.5%; at 18 mo 26.2% vs 19.3%. Median PFS 7.4 (6.0-7.7) vs 5.6 (5.3-5.8) mo; HR 0.69 (0.58-0.83); p<0.0001; PFS at 12 mo 27.4% vs 13.9%. ORR 42% (160/383) vs 36% (140/387), p=0.11; median duration of response 7.3 vs 5.0 mo. Subsequent systemic therapy 51% vs 54%. Grade 3-4 TEAEs (safety pop): diarrhoea 20% vs 5%, hypokalaemia 15% vs 4%, nausea 12% vs 3%, neutropenia 14% vs 25%, anaemia 11% vs 17%, peripheral neuropathy 3% vs 6%; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 2%. Table 2 (efficacy), Table 3 (safety), Fig 2 (KM).
TX-002.effect: HR death 0.83 (0.70-0.99); absolute median OS gain 1.9 months; PFS HR 0.69
TX-002.limitations: Modest absolute benefit; different toxicity profiles (GI vs haematologic/neuropathy) complicate the choice; no quality-of-life results in accessed text
TX-002.interpretation: Randomized interventional; establishes superiority of the irinotecan/oxaliplatin/fluoropyrimidine triplet over the gemcitabine doublet in ITT

glosses.nausea-bowel: The phase 3 NALIRIFOX trial in metastatic pancreatic cancer found more diarrhea but less neuropathy and neutropenia than gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel.
glosses.neuropathy: The phase 3 NALIRIFOX trial found less neuropathy and neutropenia but more diarrhea than gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel.
glosses.fever-infection: The phase 3 NALIRIFOX trial found less neutropenia than gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: NAPOLI-3: 770 previously untreated patients with metastatic disease; NALIRIFOX gave median survival of 11.1 versus 9.2 months with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel.
glosses.folfirinox: NAPOLI-3: NALIRIFOX versus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in 770 patients; it did not test classic FOLFIRINOX.
glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: NAPOLI-3: gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel was the comparator and gave median survival of 9.2 months versus 11.1 with NALIRIFOX, with more neutropenia and neuropathy but less diarrhea.
glosses.nalirifox: NAPOLI-3: 770 previously untreated patients with metastatic disease randomized to NALIRIFOX or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel; median survival 11.1 versus 9.2 months, with more diarrhea but less neutropenia and neuropathy.
glosses.second-line: NAPOLI-3: about half of patients in each first-line arm went on to further treatment, without a trial of what that treatment should be.
glosses.oxaliplatin: The randomized NAPOLI 3 trial in which NALIRIFOX beat gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel first line, with less neuropathy and more diarrhea.
glosses.irinotecan: The NAPOLI 3 trial in which first-line NALIRIFOX beat gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel with more diarrhea and less neutropenia.

TX-003.citation: Conroy T, Castan F, Lopez A, et al. Five-Year Outcomes of FOLFIRINOX vs Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Oncol. 2022;8(11):1571-1578.
TX-003.clinical_status: Guideline-recommended practice; FOLFIRINOX components not FDA-labeled as a regimen for pancreatic cancer (oxaliplatin and irinotecan labels list colorectal indications only; checked 2026-10-08)
TX-003.design: Open-label randomized phase 3; primary endpoint DFS; ITT analyses; final analysis at median follow-up 69.7 months (cutoff June 28, 2021)
TX-003.population: Resected PDAC (R0/R1 macroscopically complete) within 3-12 weeks of surgery, age 18-79, WHO PS 0-1, postoperative CA19-9 <180 U/mL; 77 hospitals in France and Canada
TX-003.finding: 367 DFS events; median DFS 21.4 (95% CI 17.5-26.7) vs 12.8 (11.6-15.2) mo; HR 0.66 (0.54-0.82; P<.001); 5-yr DFS 26.1% vs 19.0%. 304 deaths; median OS 53.5 (43.5-58.4) vs 35.5 (30.1-40.3) mo; HR 0.68 (0.54-0.85; P=.001); 5-yr OS 43.2% (36.5-49.7) vs 31.4% (25.5-37.5). Metastasis-free survival 29.4 vs 17.7 mo (HR 0.64); cancer-specific survival 54.7 vs 36.3 mo in abstract (36.6 in results text; HR 0.65). All planned cycles completed by 67.2% vs 79.0%; relative dose intensity >=0.80 in 33.6% vs 79.0%; 55.0% discontinued oxaliplatin early. First relapse metastatic in 54.3% vs 46.9%; single-site lung metastases more frequent with mFOLFIRINOX (39.4% vs 24.6%). Chemotherapy at relapse 66.9% vs 83.0% (74.2% of gemcitabine-arm relapses received FOLFIRINOX). Completing all cycles predicted OS (HR 0.64, 0.49-0.84; landmark). Figure 1A-B, Figure 2 (subgroups), Table 2.
TX-003.effect: OS HR 0.68 (0.54-0.85); absolute 5-yr OS +11.8 points; median OS +18 months
TX-003.limitations: Not generalizable to frail or elderly patients; mFOLFIRINOX delivered at reduced dose intensity in most patients; no quality-of-life data in this report
TX-003.interpretation: Randomized interventional; durable OS effect in a selected fit population

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: The five-year report of the randomized adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial in fit patients under 80, showing median survival of 53.5 versus 35.5 months.
glosses.microscopic-disease: The five-year report of the randomized adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial showing median survival of 53.5 versus 35.5 months.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: The five-year report of the randomized adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial showing longer disease-free and overall survival than gemcitabine.
glosses.survival-statistics: The five-year report of the randomized adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial in fit patients under 80, showing median survival of 53.5 versus 35.5 months.
glosses.neuropathy: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial showed a large survival benefit although most patients received reduced dose intensity.
glosses.fever-infection: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial showed a large survival benefit although most patients received reduced dose intensity.
glosses.life-after-whipple: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial showed a large survival benefit although most patients received reduced dose intensity.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: PRODIGE 24 five-year report: adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 493 resected patients gave median survival of 53.5 versus 35.5 months.
glosses.folfirinox: PRODIGE 24 five-year report: adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 493 resected patients; median survival 53.5 versus 35.5 months, with most patients receiving reduced doses.
glosses.second-line: PRODIGE 24: at relapse, most patients from the gemcitabine arm received FOLFIRINOX, illustrating the switch-class logic of later lines.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: PRODIGE 24 five-year report: adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX, built on infusional fluorouracil without a bolus, lengthened median survival to 53.5 months versus 35.5 with gemcitabine.
glosses.oxaliplatin: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial, in which most patients received reduced dose intensity and over half stopped oxaliplatin early yet survival improved.
glosses.irinotecan: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial, in which the irinotecan dose was lowered early for safety and survival still improved.
glosses.gemcitabine: PRODIGE 24 five-year report: adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 493 resected patients gave median survival of 53.5 versus 35.5 months.
glosses.whipple: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial: five-year survival 43.2% versus 31.4% with gemcitabine in fit patients.
glosses.surgical-complications: Five-year results of the adjuvant FOLFIRINOX trial, which enrolled patients recovered enough to start chemotherapy within 3 to 12 weeks of surgery.
glosses.growth-factor-support: The five-year report of the PRODIGE 24 trial of adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 493 resected patients, which also recorded how often doses were reduced or cycles missed.

TX-004.citation: Versteijne E, Suker M, Groothuis K, et al. Preoperative Chemoradiotherapy Versus Immediate Surgery for Resectable and Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Cancer: Results of the Dutch Randomized Phase III PREOPANC Trial. J Clin Oncol. 2020;38(16):1763-1773.
TX-004.trial_id: NTR3709 (Netherlands Trial Register; from protocol paper, not stated in accessed text)
TX-004.clinical_status: Guideline-recommended option (neoadjuvant therapy for borderline resectable disease); gemcitabine-based CRT regimen itself superseded by FOLFIRINOX-based approaches in practice
TX-004.design: Multicenter randomized phase 3, 1:1; primary endpoint OS by ITT; powered for 6-month median OS difference (17 vs 11 mo, 176 events)
TX-004.population: Pathologically confirmed resectable or borderline resectable PDAC (DPCG CT criteria), WHO PS 0-1, 16 Dutch centers
TX-004.n: 246 ITT (119 preoperative CRT, 127 immediate surgery) of 248 randomized
TX-004.time_frame: Enrollment April 2013-July 2017; median follow-up 27 months (primary) and 59 months (long-term report)
TX-004.finding: Median OS ITT 16.0 (95% CI 13.0-20.9) vs 14.3 (12.7-17.9) mo; HR 0.78 (0.58-1.05); P=.096 (180 deaths; median follow-up 27 mo). Resection rate 61% vs 72% (P=.058). R0 rate among resected 71-72% (51/72) vs 40% (37/92), P<.001; pathologic N+ 33% vs 78%; perineural invasion 39% vs 73%; venous invasion 19% vs 36%. DFS HR 0.73 (0.55-0.96; P=.032); locoregional failure-free interval improved. Predefined subgroups: resectable - no significant OS/DFS difference; borderline resectable - significantly improved OS, DFS, LFFI; interaction P=.14 (Table 3). Resected patients who started adjuvant therapy: median OS 35.2 vs 19.8 mo (HR 0.58, 0.35-0.95; P=.029) (Fig 3). Compliance: 76% started preoperative CRT (ITT), 89% of starters completed; postoperative chemotherapy started by 51% of immediate-surgery arm; 24% dropout before surgery in CRT arm. Serious adverse events 52% vs 41% (P=.096).
TX-004.effect: OS HR 0.78 (0.58-1.05), not significant at primary analysis; R0 +32 points; long-term update (TX-L10) HR 0.73 (0.56-0.96), 5-yr OS 20.5% vs 6.5%
TX-004.limitations: Subgroup interaction test not significant; primary endpoint not met at first analysis; resected-cohort comparisons are conditional on surviving to surgery
TX-004.interpretation: Randomized ITT evidence for the whole strategy (CRT + selection + surgery + adjuvant) rather than for radiation per se

glosses.resectability-categories: The randomized PREOPANC trial showing preoperative chemoradiation raised margin-negative resection from 40% to 72% in resectable and borderline disease.
glosses.why-chemo-first: The randomized PREOPANC trial of preoperative chemoradiation versus immediate surgery in resectable and borderline disease.
glosses.vessel-contact: The randomized PREOPANC trial in which preoperative chemoradiation improved margins and node status, with survival benefit clearest in borderline resectable disease.
glosses.pathology-report: The randomized PREOPANC trial in which preoperative chemoradiation lowered node positivity, perineural and venous invasion in the specimen.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: PREOPANC: 246 patients with resectable or borderline resectable tumors randomized to preoperative gemcitabine-based chemoradiation or immediate surgery; clear margins rose from 40% to 72% among those resected, and borderline patients gained survival.
glosses.gemcitabine: PREOPANC: gemcitabine was given with radiation before surgery and alone after it in a randomized trial of 246 patients.
glosses.vascular-resection: The PREOPANC randomized trial of preoperative chemoradiation versus immediate surgery, which raised clear-margin rates from 40% to 72%.
glosses.radiation: The PREOPANC randomized trial of preoperative gemcitabine-based chemoradiation versus immediate surgery, which raised margin-negative resection from 40 to 72 percent.

TX-005.citation: Golan T, Hammel P, Reni M, et al. Maintenance Olaparib for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2019;381(4):317-327.
TX-005.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): olaparib maintenance for gBRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma without progression on >=16 weeks first-line platinum (Lynparza NDA 208558 s010, 2019-12-27; label checked 2026-10-08)
TX-005.design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3, 3:2; primary endpoint PFS by blinded independent central review (modified RECIST 1.1); 87 events for 80% power at HR 0.54
TX-005.population: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation (central BRACAnalysis CDx) and no progression after >=16 weeks of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy; 3315 screened, 7.5% gBRCA-positive; 119 sites, 12 countries
TX-005.finding: Primary analysis at 104 PFS events (68% maturity, cutoff Jan 15, 2019): median PFS 7.4 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.35-0.82); P=0.004; curves separate from ~5 months. Interim OS at 46% maturity: median 18.9 vs 18.1 mo; HR 0.91 (0.56-1.46); P=0.68. Second PFS 13.2 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.76, 0.46-1.23). Response rate in measurable disease 23% (18/78) vs 12% (6/52), OR 2.30 (0.89-6.76); two complete responses in olaparib arm. Grade >=3 anaemia 11% vs 3%. No clinically meaningful change in EORTC QLQ-C30 global HRQoL. 15% of placebo patients received a PARP inhibitor after progression (Table 2, Fig 1A-B).
TX-005.effect: PFS HR 0.53 (0.35-0.82); absolute median PFS gain 3.6 months; OS HR 0.91 (interim) and 0.83 (final, TX-L24)
TX-005.limitations: Small trial; OS underpowered; no comparison with continued FOLFIRINOX or fluoropyrimidine maintenance
TX-005.interpretation: Placebo-controlled randomized evidence that olaparib delays progression in platinum-sensitive gBRCA disease; OS inference confounded by subsequent therapy and small size

glosses.reading-trial-results: The randomized POLO trial of maintenance olaparib in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic cancer, which doubled progression-free survival.
glosses.dna-repair-checkpoints: The POLO randomized trial of maintenance olaparib in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer.
glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: The POLO randomized trial in which maintenance olaparib doubled progression-free survival in germline BRCA carriers.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: POLO: maintenance olaparib in 154 patients with germline BRCA mutations and metastatic disease doubled progression-free survival (7.4 versus 3.8 months) without a significant survival difference.
glosses.second-line: POLO: maintenance olaparib after platinum chemotherapy in germline BRCA carriers doubled progression-free survival without a significant survival difference.
glosses.olaparib: The POLO randomized trial, in which maintenance olaparib doubled progression-free survival in germline BRCA carriers after platinum chemotherapy.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: The randomized POLO trial in which maintenance olaparib roughly doubled progression-free survival in inherited BRCA-mutated disease.

TX-006.citation: Tempero MA, Pelzer U, O'Reilly EM, et al. Adjuvant nab-Paclitaxel + Gemcitabine in Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Results From a Randomized, Open-Label, Phase III Trial. J Clin Oncol. 2023;41(11):2007-2019.
TX-006.clinical_status: Not FDA-approved for adjuvant use (Abraxane label covers metastatic disease only, checked 2026-10-08); negative phase 3 for primary endpoint
TX-006.design: Open-label randomized phase 3 (APACT), 1:1, stratified by resection and nodal status; primary endpoint independently assessed DFS (blinded radiologists); secondary OS, investigator-assessed DFS
TX-006.population: Treatment-naive resected PDAC (R0 76%, node-positive 72%), ECOG 0-1; 160 sites in 21 countries (Europe 47%, North America 35%, Asia 12%, Australia 6%)
TX-006.n: 866 randomized (432 nab-paclitaxel+gemcitabine, 434 gemcitabine); 287/432 vs 310/434 completed six cycles
TX-006.finding: Primary cutoff Dec 31, 2018 (median follow-up 38.5 mo): independently assessed median DFS 19.4 (95% CI 16.62-21.91) vs 18.8 (13.83-20.30) mo; HR 0.88 (0.729-1.063); P=.18 - not met. Investigator-assessed DFS 16.6 vs 13.7 mo; HR 0.82 (0.694-0.965); P=.02; concordance between reviews 77%; independent review censored 48%/51% vs investigator 35%/33%. OS at primary cutoff 40.5 vs 36.2 mo (HR 0.82, 0.680-0.996; P=.045); 16-month follow-up 41.8 vs 37.7 mo (HR 0.82, 0.687-0.973; P=.023); 5-year follow-up (cutoff April 9, 2021; 88% mature) 41.8 vs 37.7 mo (HR 0.80, 0.678-0.947; P=.0091); >=5-yr OS 38% vs 31%. Grade >=3: neutropenia 49% vs 43%, anemia 15% vs 8%, fatigue 10% vs 3%, peripheral neuropathy 15% vs 0% (median improvement >=1 grade in 195 days). Fig 2A-E, Table 2.
TX-006.effect: Primary DFS HR 0.88 (0.73-1.06), not significant; OS HR 0.80 (0.68-0.95) descriptive only
TX-006.limitations: Open-label; superseded by mFOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine-capecitabine as preferred regimens during the trial
TX-006.interpretation: Randomized; demonstrates that an OS signal can coexist with a failed primary endpoint when the endpoint depends on radiologic adjudication rules

glosses.reading-trial-results: The randomized APACT adjuvant trial in which independently reviewed disease-free survival was not significant while investigator-assessed recurrence and overall survival favored the experimental arm.
glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: APACT: adjuvant gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in 866 resected patients missed its primary endpoint of independently assessed disease-free survival despite a later survival difference.
glosses.gemcitabine: APACT: gemcitabine alone was the adjuvant control arm in 866 resected patients, with grade 3 or worse neutropenia in 43% and anemia in 8%.

TX-007.citation: Le DT, Durham JN, Smith KN, et al. Mismatch repair deficiency predicts response of solid tumors to PD-1 blockade. Science. 2017;357(6349):409-413.
TX-007.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): pembrolizumab for MSI-H/dMMR solid tumors after prior therapy (accelerated 2017-05-23; regular approval 2023-03-28/29; label checked 2026-10-08)
TX-007.design: Prospective single-arm phase 2 of pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg every 14 days with exome and T-cell receptor analyses
TX-007.population: 86 patients with treatment-refractory dMMR advanced cancers across 12 tumor types (pancreatic cases included; per-type numbers in Fig 1A not in accessed text)
TX-007.finding: Objective radiographic response 53% (46/86; 95% CI 42-64%), complete response 21% (18); disease control 77%. Median PFS and OS not reached at median follow-up 12.5 months; 1- and 2-yr PFS 64% and 53%; 1- and 2-yr OS 76% and 64%. 11 complete responders stopped therapy after 2 years with no recurrence at median 8.3 months off therapy. 12/20 post-treatment biopsies showed no tumor cells. Primary resistance 14% (12 patients). Functional expansion of mutation-associated neoantigen-specific T-cell clones in blood after treatment (TCRseq). Table 1, Fig 1-3.
TX-007.effect: ORR 53% across histologies; 2-yr OS 64% in a refractory population
TX-007.limitations: Small per-tumor cohorts; the pancreatic MSI-H subset (~1-2% of PDAC per GENE-006) behaves worse in later data (KEYNOTE-158 pancreatic ORR 18%)
TX-007.interpretation: Prospective biomarker-selected intervention with mechanistic correlates (neoantigen-specific T-cell expansion); supports causal role of dMMR-driven mutation load in response

glosses.clinical-trials: A study of pembrolizumab in mismatch-repair-deficient cancers showing a 53% response rate across tumor types.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: The 86-patient trial across 12 cancer types that showed mismatch-repair deficiency predicts response to PD-1 blockade, with a 53 percent response rate.

TX-008.citation: Frese KK, Neesse A, Cook N, et al. nab-Paclitaxel potentiates gemcitabine activity by reducing cytidine deaminase levels in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer. Cancer Discov. 2012;2(3):260-269.
TX-008.clinical_status: preclinical only (mechanism); the regimen is FDA-approved
TX-008.design: Randomized preclinical intervention (vehicle, gemcitabine, nab-paclitaxel, combination for 8 days) with tumor growth, histology, LC-MS/MS intratumoral drug metabolite measurement, siRNA knockdown
TX-008.population: KPC mice (LSL-KrasG12D; LSL-Trp53R172H; Pdx-1-Cre) with established ultrasound-measured tumors; KPC-derived cell lines
TX-008.n: Cohort sizes per arm not stated in accessed text (figure legends not captured)
TX-008.finding: Tumor growth over 8 days: combination 140% +/- 15 of baseline vs gemcitabine 234% +/- 32 (p<0.01) vs vehicle 278% +/- 33; nab-paclitaxel alone 170% +/- 15 (NS vs gemcitabine, p=0.12); two combination tumors regressed; liver metastatic burden reduced in nab-paclitaxel-containing arms. Apoptosis increased only with combination and was in E-cadherin+ neoplastic cells, not alpha-SMA+ stromal cells; no change in stromal content, alpha-SMA, collagen density, SPARC level, or vascular density/lumen area. Combination raised intratumoral dFdC:dFdU ratio and dFdCTP; paclitaxel levels unchanged by gemcitabine. Free paclitaxel raised dFdCTP in cultured cells. Cda protein (primary gemcitabine catabolic enzyme) was lower in nab-paclitaxel-treated tumors; Cda knockdown sensitized cells to gemcitabine; Ent1 knockdown desensitized. Fig 1-4.
TX-008.effect: Tumor growth 140% vs 234% (combination vs gemcitabine); dFdCTP increased (fold change in figure, not in accessed text)
TX-008.limitations: Preparation-level evidence; the CDA mechanism has not been shown in patients
TX-008.interpretation: Perturbation experiment with rescue/knockdown; establishes a sufficient pharmacologic mechanism in mice; does not exclude other mechanisms in humans

glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: In genetically engineered mice, nab-paclitaxel raised active gemcitabine in tumors by lowering cytidine deaminase and killed tumor cells without changing the stroma.
glosses.gemcitabine: In genetically engineered mice, gemcitabine's active metabolite rose when nab-paclitaxel lowered cytidine deaminase, and lowering the uptake transporter Ent1 made cells resistant.

TX-009.citation: Neesse A, Frese KK, Chan DS, et al. SPARC independent drug delivery and antitumour effects of nab-paclitaxel in genetically engineered mice. Gut. 2014;63(6):974-983.
TX-009.design: Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study (LC-MS/MS) of cremophor-paclitaxel, human nab-paclitaxel and a novel mouse-albumin nab-paclitaxel; genetic SPARC ablation; extended 15-day intervention
TX-009.population: KPC and KPfC (KrasG12D; p53flox; p48-Cre) mice; KPfC crossed to SPARC-/-; wild-type and SPARC-/- C57BL/6 mice
TX-009.n: Single-dose PK: cremophor-paclitaxel n=12, nab-paclitaxel 30 mg/kg n=5, 120 mg/kg n=10; SPARC+/+ n=30 and SPARC-/- n=31 mice across 7 time points; KPfC cohorts SPARC+/+ n=10, +/- n=18, -/- n=10
TX-009.finding: nab-paclitaxel and cremophor-paclitaxel had comparable tumor PK/PD at equimolar dose but nab-paclitaxel could be dosed >=4x higher (improved tolerability; 5/12 cremophor mice had toxicity). SPARC-null KPfC mice developed desmoplastic tumours with impaired collagen maturation but identical latency (mean onset 154 vs 153 vs 156 days). At low dose (30 mg/kg), paclitaxel concentrations were significantly lower in SPARC-null plasma and tissues (p<0.02); at MTD, SPARC deficiency did not affect intratumoral paclitaxel, stromal deposition or immediate therapeutic response. Prolonged m-nab-paclitaxel at MTD increased phospho-histone H3 mitotic figures and cleaved caspase-3 (p<0.001) without stromal depletion in KPC mice. Fig 1-5.
TX-009.effect: SPARC effect on drug exposure present only at low dose and saturated at therapeutic dose
TX-009.limitations: Preclinical; no survival endpoint in accessed text
TX-009.interpretation: Genetic perturbation (SPARC knockout) in an autochthonous model; defines a dose boundary condition for the SPARC-sequestration hypothesis

glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: In mice lacking SPARC, nab-paclitaxel delivery and effect at therapeutic doses were unchanged, and the albumin formulation allowed fourfold higher dosing than solvent-based paclitaxel.

TX-010.citation: Babiker HM, Picozzi V, Chandana SR, et al. Tumor Treating Fields With Gemcitabine and Nab-Paclitaxel for Locally Advanced Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: Randomized, Open-Label, Pivotal Phase 3 PANOVA-3 Study. J Clin Oncol. 2025 (online).
TX-010.clinical_status: FDA premarket approval (US): Optune Pax for adult locally advanced pancreatic cancer with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, announced 2026-02-12 (FDA bulletin; PMA P250034 per accessdata listing, not fetched)
TX-010.design: Global randomized open-label phase 3, 1:1, stratified by ECOG and region; primary endpoint OS (ITT); 80% power for HR <0.75 with 556 patients; OS and PFS tested hierarchically
TX-010.population: Newly diagnosed unresectable locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-2; 196 sites in 20 countries
TX-010.time_frame: Enrollment May 2018-March 2023; analysis after prespecified events (date not in accessed text)
TX-010.finding: Median OS 16.2 (95% CI 15.0-18.0) vs 14.2 (12.8-15.4) months; HR 0.82 (0.68-0.99); log-rank p=0.039; 1-yr OS 68.1% vs 60.2% (p=0.029); mITT (>=1 cycle) median OS 18.3 vs 15.1 mo, HR 0.73. PFS not different: median 10.6 vs 9.3 mo; HR 0.85 (0.68-1.05); p=0.137; 1-yr PFS 43.9% vs 34.1% (p=0.026). Local PFS not different; ORR not improved. Pain-free survival 15.2 vs 9.1 mo; HR 0.74 (0.56-0.97); p=0.027. Distant PFS improved (post hoc). Resectability 7.0% vs 10.1% (NS). Device-related AEs: skin reactions in 76.3%; grade >=3 device-related AEs 7.7%; no additive systemic toxicity. Salvage therapy 51.2% vs 46.9%. Enrollment May 2018-March 2023. Table 2, Fig 2-3.
TX-010.effect: OS HR 0.82 (0.68-0.99), absolute median gain 2.0 months; PFS HR 0.85 (NS)
TX-010.limitations: PFS, local PFS and ORR not improved - mismatch with a local-control rationale; pain-free survival is partly subjective in an open-label trial
TX-010.interpretation: Randomized ITT evidence for an OS effect of a local physical therapy; mechanism of the OS gain without PFS/local control gain is unexplained

glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: PANOVA-3: adding Tumor Treating Fields to gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in locally advanced disease improved median survival from 14.2 to 16.2 months without improving progression-free survival.
glosses.ttfields: The PANOVA-3 randomized trial of 571 people with locally advanced pancreatic cancer, in which adding Tumor Treating Fields to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel improved median survival by two months without improving progression-free survival.

TX-011.citation: Murphy JE, Wo JY, Ryan DP, et al. Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With FOLFIRINOX Followed by Individualized Chemoradiotherapy for Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Phase 2 Clinical Trial. JAMA Oncol. 2018;4(7):963-969.
TX-011.clinical_status: Phase 2; total neoadjuvant therapy is a guideline-listed option for borderline disease
TX-011.design: Single-arm phase 2; primary endpoint R0 resection rate (design: >=16/50 R0 to exclude 20% historical baseline; 90% power for 40%)
TX-011.population: Biopsy-proven borderline resectable PDAC by multidisciplinary review at a single high-volume academic center (Massachusetts General Hospital)
TX-011.n: 50 enrolled, 48 eligible; 43 post-amendment patients planned for 8 preoperative cycles
TX-011.finding: 34/43 (79%) completed 8 cycles; RECIST partial response 44% (19/43), stable 30%, progression 5%. Short-course CRT in 27 (56%), long-course in 17 (35%). R0 resection 31/48 eligible (65%; 95% CI 49-78%) and 31/32 resected (97%). ITT: median PFS 14.7 mo (95% CI 10.5-NR), 2-yr PFS 43%; median OS 37.7 mo (19.4-NR), 2-yr OS 56%. Resected subgroup: median PFS 48.6 mo, median OS not reached, 2-yr PFS 55%, 2-yr OS 72%. Grade >=3 preoperative toxicity 9/48 (19%): diarrhea 5, neutropenia 2, neuropathy 2. Fig 2A-B, Table 2.
TX-011.effect: R0 65% ITT vs 20% historical; resected vs ITT 2-yr OS 72% vs 56%
TX-011.limitations: No control arm; small; radiotherapy contribution untestable
TX-011.interpretation: Single-arm prospective; shows the sequence can convert borderline tumors to R0 and quantifies the gap between resected-cohort and ITT survival within one cohort

glosses.why-chemo-first: A single-arm trial of eight cycles of FOLFIRINOX then chemoradiation for borderline resectable cancer achieving 65% margin-negative resection in everyone enrolled.
glosses.reading-trial-results: A single-arm trial of preoperative FOLFIRINOX for borderline resectable cancer reporting both resected-cohort and intention-to-treat survival.
glosses.survival-statistics: A single-arm trial of preoperative FOLFIRINOX for borderline resectable cancer reporting both resected-cohort and intention-to-treat survival.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: Single-arm phase 2 of FOLFIRINOX then chemoradiation in 48 borderline resectable patients: 65% had clear margins, and two-year survival was 56% for all who started versus 72% for those resected.

TX-012.citation: Katz MHG, Shi Q, Meyers J, et al. Efficacy of Preoperative mFOLFIRINOX vs mFOLFIRINOX Plus Hypofractionated Radiotherapy for Borderline Resectable Adenocarcinoma of the Pancreas: The A021501 Phase 2 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Oncol. 2022;8(9):1263-1270.
TX-012.clinical_status: Phase 2; neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX is guideline-listed for borderline disease; role of RT undefined
TX-012.design: Randomized phase 2 with each arm compared with a historical 18-month OS of 50% (not a head-to-head comparison); interim futility rule: close an arm if <=11 of first 30 had R0 resection
TX-012.population: Borderline resectable PDAC (Alliance/Intergroup criteria, central review), NCTN institutions
TX-012.n: 126 registered (70 arm 1 including 16 non-randomized after arm 2 closure; 56 arm 2); 120 evaluable
TX-012.finding: Interim (first 30 per arm): R0 resection 17 (57%) arm 1 vs 10 (33%) arm 2 → arm 2 closed. Pancreatectomy 32/65 (49%) arm 1 vs 19/55 (35%) arm 2; R0 among resected 88% vs 74%; pCR 0 vs 2. Arm 1: 41/62 first evaluable (66.1%) alive at 18 mo (>36 required) → efficacious; median OS 29.8 mo (95% CI 21.1-36.6); KM 18-mo OS 66.7% (56.1-79.4); median EFS 15.0 mo. Arm 2: median OS 17.1 mo (12.8-24.4); 18-mo OS 47.3% (35.8-62.5); median EFS 10.2 mo. 18-mo OS among resected: 87.5% (arm 1) vs 78.9% (arm 2). Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 57% vs 64% (mostly during chemotherapy: diarrhea 18%, hypokalemia 14%, neutropenia 12%). Median follow-up 42.9 mo. Fig 2, Tables 2-3.
TX-012.effect: 18-mo OS 66.7% (chemo alone) vs 47.3% (chemo + RT) vs 50% historical; R0 at interim 57% vs 33%
TX-012.limitations: Not powered for between-arm comparison; 16 non-randomized patients in arm 1
TX-012.interpretation: Randomized allocation but arms judged against historical control; supports 'RT adds nothing (or harms) on this backbone' as a boundary finding rather than a definitive comparison

glosses.why-plans-change: The randomized A021501 trial in borderline resectable cancer in which the radiation arm was closed early for a low margin-negative rate.
glosses.why-chemo-first: The randomized A021501 trial showing preoperative modified FOLFIRINOX gave 18-month survival of 67% in borderline disease while adding radiation did not help.
glosses.reading-trial-results: The randomized A021501 trial reporting 18-month survival among all patients and among the resected subgroup.
glosses.survival-statistics: The randomized A021501 trial reporting 18-month survival among all patients and among the resected subgroup.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: A021501: 126 patients with borderline resectable tumors; eight cycles of mFOLFIRINOX before surgery gave median survival of 29.8 months, and adding short-course radiation did not help.
glosses.folfirinox: A021501: eight cycles of mFOLFIRINOX before surgery in borderline resectable disease gave median survival of 29.8 months; adding radiation did not help.
glosses.radiation: The A021501 randomized phase 2 trial in borderline resectable disease, which closed its SBRT arm early for fewer margin-negative resections than mFOLFIRINOX alone.

TX-013.citation: Sohal DPS, Duong M, Ahmad SA, et al. Efficacy of Perioperative Chemotherapy for Resectable Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Phase 2 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Oncol. 2021;7(3):421-427.
TX-013.clinical_status: Phase 2; perioperative chemotherapy for resectable disease under phase 3 testing (Alliance A021806 NCT04340141, PREOPANC-3 NCT04927780; no results posted as of 2026-10-08)
TX-013.design: Randomized phase 2 pick-the-winner (SWOG S1505); each arm's 2-yr OS compared with null 40% (alternative 58%, 88% power, 1-sided); not designed for between-arm comparison
TX-013.population: Resectable PDAC by Intergroup criteria with central radiology review, Zubrod PS 0-1; NCTN academic and community centers across the US
TX-013.n: 147 enrolled; 43 (29%) ineligible at central review (venous interface >=180 degrees 35%, any arterial interface 51%, suspected metastases 65% of the ineligible); 102 eligible and evaluable (55…
TX-013.finding: Started neoadjuvant chemotherapy 96% in both arms; completed 84% and 85%; resection 40/55 (73%) and 33/47 (70%); R0 among resected 85% (34/40) and 85% (28/33); node-negative 40% and 45%; started adjuvant 78%/79% of resected (56%/55% overall); completed all treatment 49% and 40% of eligible. Overall response rate 9% vs 21% (P=.15). 2-yr OS 47% (95% CI 31-61; P=.15 vs 40%) and 48% (31-63; P=.14); median OS 23.2 (17.6-45.9) and 23.6 (17.8-31.7) months. Neoadjuvant grade 3-4 neutropenia 27% (GnP) vs 19% (mFOLFIRINOX). Fig 1-2, Table 2.
TX-013.effect: 2-yr OS 47-48% vs 40% null (not significant); median OS ~23 months in ITT
TX-013.limitations: Small; no upfront-surgery control; adjuvant completion <50%
TX-013.interpretation: Prospective randomized allocation but single-arm inference against historical control; useful as a boundary condition and for deliverability data

glosses.why-chemo-first: The randomized SWOG S1505 trial of perioperative chemotherapy for resectable cancer, in which two-year survival of 47-48% did not beat the historical bar.
glosses.clinical-trials: The randomized SWOG S1505 'pick-the-winner' phase 2 trial, illustrating a design that cannot prove benefit.
glosses.ct-scan: A US randomized phase 2 trial in which central review reclassified 29% of patients enrolled as resectable, mostly for vessel contact.
glosses.vessel-contact: A US randomized phase 2 trial in which central review reclassified 29% of patients enrolled as resectable, mostly for vessel contact.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: SWOG S1505: 102 patients with resectable tumors given chemotherapy before and after surgery; two-year survival was 47-48%, not above the historical bar of 40%.

TX-014.citation: Wang-Gillam A, Li CP, Bodoky G, et al. Nanoliposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil and folinic acid in metastatic pancreatic cancer after previous gemcitabine-based therapy (NAPOLI-1): a global, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2016;387(10018):545-557.
TX-014.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): Onivyde + 5-FU/LV after gemcitabine-based therapy (NDA 207793, 2015-10-22; label checked 2026-10-08)
TX-014.design: Global open-label randomized phase 3; initially 1:1 (liposomal irinotecan monotherapy vs 5-FU/LV), third combination arm added by amendment (1:1:1); stratified by albumin, KPS, ethnic origin; primary endpoint OS in ITT after 305 events
TX-014.population: Metastatic PDAC previously treated with gemcitabine-based therapy; 76 sites in 14 countries
TX-014.finding: Registry (cutoff 14 Feb 2014) and abstract: median OS combination 6.1 mo (95% CI 4.76-8.87) vs 5-FU/LV 4.2 (3.29-5.32); HR 0.67 (0.49-0.92); p=0.012. Monotherapy 4.9 (4.23-5.62) vs 4.2 (3.58-4.86); HR 0.99 (0.77-1.28); p=0.94. PFS combination 3.1 vs 1.5 mo, HR 0.56 (0.41-0.75), p<0.001; monotherapy 2.7 vs 1.6, HR 0.81 (NS). ORR 7.69% vs 0.84% (p=0.010). Time to treatment failure 2.3 vs 1.4 mo (HR 0.60). CA19-9 response 28.9% vs 8.6%. Clinical benefit response 14% vs 12% (NS). Grade 3-4 (combination, n=117): neutropenia 27%, diarrhoea 13%, vomiting 11%, fatigue 14% (abstract). Enrollment Jan 11, 2012-Sept 11, 2013.
TX-014.effect: OS HR 0.67 (0.49-0.92), absolute median gain 1.9 months; monotherapy ineffective
TX-014.limitations: Full text not accessed (Lancet paywall); numbers from registry and abstract; small absolute benefit
TX-014.interpretation: Randomized; shows the fluoropyrimidine backbone is required for the liposomal irinotecan benefit

glosses.treatment-sequencing: NAPOLI-1 (abstract and registry): after gemcitabine-based therapy, liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil/leucovorin gave median survival of 6.1 versus 4.2 months.
glosses.second-line: NAPOLI-1 (abstract and registry): after gemcitabine-based therapy, liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil/leucovorin gave median survival of 6.1 versus 4.2 months, while liposomal irinotecan alone gave no benefit.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: NAPOLI-1 (abstract and registry): fluorouracil/leucovorin alone gave median survival of 4.2 months after gemcitabine, versus 6.1 months with liposomal irinotecan added.
glosses.irinotecan: The NAPOLI-1 trial: liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil extended survival after gemcitabine, while liposomal irinotecan alone did not.

TX-015.citation: Yoo C, Hwang JY, Kim JE, et al. A randomised phase II study of modified FOLFIRI.3 vs modified FOLFOX as second-line therapy in patients with gemcitabine-refractory advanced pancreatic cancer. Br J Cancer. 2009;101(10):1658-1663.
TX-015.clinical_status: Phase 2; neither regimen FDA-labeled for pancreatic cancer
TX-015.design: Open-label randomized phase 2 selection design (1:1), stratified by age, PS, prior gemcitabine response; primary endpoint 6-month OS rate
TX-015.population: Gemcitabine-refractory locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-2; single center (Asan Medical Center, Seoul)
TX-015.finding: Median 3 cycles per arm; 50/61 (82%) died at median follow-up 24.4 weeks. 6-month OS 27% (95% CI 13-46%) vs 30% (15-49%). Median OS 16.6 (12.5-20.6) vs 14.9 (8.0-21.8) weeks; median PFS 8.3 (6.9-9.6) vs 6.0 (5.1-6.9) weeks. Disease control 23% vs (reported in Table 2). Severe toxicity 38% in each arm; grade 3/4 asthenia 3% vs 14%; grade 3/4 diarrhoea 7% vs 0%; one treatment-related death per arm. Enrollment Jan 2007-Dec 2008. Fig 1, Tables 2-3.
TX-015.effect: No meaningful difference; both regimens ~4 months median OS
TX-015.limitations: No non-oxaliplatin/irinotecan control; 2-week infusional 5-FU at 2000 mg/m2 differs from Western doses
TX-015.interpretation: Randomized selection design; not powered to compare arms; documents baseline second-line expectations

glosses.second-line: Korean randomized phase 2 of 61 gemcitabine-refractory patients: irinotecan- and oxaliplatin-based doublets both gave about four months median survival.

TX-016.citation: Marabelle A, Le DT, Ascierto PA, et al. Efficacy of Pembrolizumab in Patients With Noncolorectal High Microsatellite Instability/Mismatch Repair-Deficient Cancer: Results From the Phase II KEYNOTE-158 Study. J Clin Oncol. 2020;38(1):1-10.
TX-016.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): pembrolizumab for MSI-H/dMMR solid tumors (regular approval 2023-03-28/29 per Drugs@FDA s132) and TMB-H >=10 mut/Mb solid tumors (2020-06-16, s071/s090); label checked 2026-10-08
TX-016.design: Nonrandomized open-label phase 2 basket (cohort K prospective plus retrospectively identified MSI-H in cohorts A-J); primary endpoint ORR by independent central review (RECIST 1.1)
TX-016.population: Previously treated advanced MSI-H/dMMR non-colorectal cancers, 27 tumor types (endometrial, gastric, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic most common); 55 sites, 18 countries
TX-016.n: 233 patients (pancreatic n=22 in the FDA-label analysis of the expanded 373-patient dataset)
TX-016.finding: Data cutoff Dec 6, 2018; median follow-up 13.4 mo. ORR 34.3% (95% CI 28.3-40.8): CR 9.9% (23), PR 24.5% (57); median time to response 2.1 mo; median duration of response not reached (2.9-31.3+ mo); 86.9% of responses >=12 mo and 77.6% >=24 mo (KM). Median PFS 4.1 mo (2.4-4.9); 12- and 24-mo PFS 33.9% and 29.3%. Median OS 23.5 mo (13.5-NR). Immune-mediated AEs/infusion reactions 23.2%; grade 3-4 6.0%. Pancreatic cohort (per Keytruda label Table, expanded dataset): n=22, ORR 18% (4/22; 95% CI 5-40%), DoR range 8.1 to 24.3+ months; per-tumor table not rendered in the accessed PMC text (Table 2 image).
TX-016.limitations: Single arm; heterogeneous prior therapy; pancreatic-specific survival not in accessed text
TX-016.interpretation: Prospective biomarker-selected single-arm registrational cohort; supports tissue-agnostic activity with histology-dependent magnitude

glosses.clinical-trials: The KEYNOTE-158 study of pembrolizumab in non-colorectal mismatch-repair-deficient cancers, with an 18% response in the pancreatic cohort.
glosses.msi-mmr: A tissue-agnostic pembrolizumab basket trial with an 18 percent response rate in 22 pancreatic patients.
glosses.second-line: KEYNOTE-158: pembrolizumab in mismatch-repair-deficient cancers after prior therapy; overall response 34%, with the pancreatic cohort at 18%.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: The KEYNOTE-158 basket trial of pembrolizumab in non-colorectal MSI-high cancers, with a 34 percent overall response rate and 18 percent in the pancreatic cohort.

TX-017.citation: Reiss KA, Mick R, O'Hara MH, et al. Phase II Study of Maintenance Rucaparib in Patients With Platinum-Sensitive Advanced Pancreatic Cancer and a Pathogenic Germline or Somatic Variant in BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2. J Clin Oncol. 2021;39(22):2497-2505.
TX-017.clinical_status: Rucaparib not FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer; olaparib label restricted to germline BRCA (checked 2026-10-08)
TX-017.design: Single-arm phase 2; primary endpoint PFS rate at 6 months (PFS6)
TX-017.population: Advanced pancreatic cancer with germline or somatic pathogenic variant in BRCA1, BRCA2 or PALB2 and >=16 weeks platinum-based chemotherapy without platinum resistance; single-center investigator-initiated (University of Pennsylvania)
TX-017.n: 46 enrolled, 42 evaluable (27 gBRCA2, 7 gBRCA1, 6 gPALB2, 2 sBRCA2); 36 with measurable disease
TX-017.finding: Registry: PFS6 59.5% (95% CI 44.6-74.4); median OS 23.5 mo (20-27); ORR 41.7% (25.5-59.2; 3 CR, 12 PR of 36 measurable); disease control 66.7% (49.0-81.4); duration of response 17.3 mo (8.8-25.8). Abstract: median PFS 13.1 mo (4.4-21.8); 12-month PFS 54.8%; responses in gBRCA2 41% (11/27), gPALB2 50% (3/6), sBRCA2 50% (1/2). Related AEs (registry, any grade): anemia 74%, nausea 48%, ALT increase 47%, fatigue 45%, thrombocytopenia 39%. Trial status TERMINATED (registry; reason not stated in accessed data); results first posted 2023-09-28.
TX-017.effect: PFS6 59.5%; ORR 41.7% in a maintenance setting
TX-017.limitations: No control arm; full text not accessed
TX-017.interpretation: Single-arm prospective; supports (not proves) PARP inhibitor activity in PALB2/somatic BRCA; selection for platinum sensitivity is built in

glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: A phase 2 trial of maintenance rucaparib with responses in germline PALB2 and somatic BRCA2 carriers.
glosses.olaparib: A single-arm phase 2 trial of maintenance rucaparib in 42 people with germline or tumor BRCA or PALB2 variants, with responses in PALB2 and tumor-acquired BRCA2 carriers.

TX-018.citation: Drilon A, Laetsch TW, Kummar S, et al. Efficacy of Larotrectinib in TRK Fusion-Positive Cancers in Adults and Children. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(8):731-739.
TX-018.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): larotrectinib for NTRK fusion solid tumors (NDA 210861, 2018-11-26; label checked 2026-10-08); entrectinib similarly approved 2019-08-15 (accelerated; label checked)
TX-018.design: Pooled analysis of three single-arm studies (adult phase 1, pediatric phase 1-2, adolescent/adult phase 2); primary endpoint ORR by independent review; 55 patients for 80% power to exclude 30% lower bound
TX-018.population: TRK fusion-positive cancers (17 tumor types) in adults and children, identified by routine molecular profiling
TX-018.finding: Cutoff July 17, 2017: ORR 75% (95% CI 61-85) by independent review (CR 13%, PR 62%, SD 13%, PD 9%); investigator ORR 80% (67-90). Median time to response 1.8 mo. Median duration of response and PFS not reached (median follow-up 8.3 and 9.9 mo); at 1 year 71% of responses ongoing and 55% progression-free. Dose reductions in 15%; AEs mostly grade 1; no treatment discontinuation for drug-related AEs. Tumor types: salivary MASC 12, infantile fibrosarcoma 7, thyroid 5, colon 4, lung 4, melanoma 4, GIST 3, other 16 (pancreatic cases not enumerated in accessed text). Table 1, Fig 1-2.
TX-018.limitations: No pancreatic-specific data in accessed text; small
TX-018.interpretation: Biomarker-selected single-arm; the magnitude and histology-independence support a driver-dependency causal model

glosses.fusions-rare-targets: A larotrectinib trial in NTRK-fusion cancers with a 75 percent response and no pancreatic cases enumerated.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: The pooled analysis of larotrectinib in 55 TRK-fusion cancers across 17 types, with a 75 percent response rate and pancreatic cases not enumerated.

TX-019.citation: Subbiah V, Wolf J, Konda B, et al. Tumour-agnostic efficacy and safety of selpercatinib in patients with RET fusion-positive solid tumours other than lung or thyroid tumours (LIBRETTO-001): a phase 1/2, open-label, basket trial. Lancet Oncol. 2022;23(10):1261-1273.
TX-019.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): selpercatinib for RET fusion-positive solid tumors (Retevmo NDA 213246 s007/s008, 2022-09-21, accelerated; label indication 1.4 revised 07/2026 and no longer carries accelerated-approval language in DailyMed version checked 2026-10-08 - conversion not independently verified)
TX-019.design: Prespecified interim analysis of a phase 1/2 single-group basket trial; primary endpoint ORR by independent review committee; ~40 patients planned by agreement with FDA
TX-019.population: RET fusion-positive advanced solid tumours other than NSCLC/thyroid, progressed on or without satisfactory prior therapy; 45 enrolled of 806 in LIBRETTO-001; 14 tumour types; pancreatic n=12 enrolled (27%), 11 efficacy-evaluable
TX-019.finding: Cutoff Sept 24, 2021. ORR 43.9% (95% CI 28.5-60.3; 18/41) by IRC; median duration of response 24.5 mo (IQR 9.2-NR); median PFS 13.2 mo (7.4-26.2); 1-yr progression-free 53.1%. Pancreatic cancer (n=11): ORR 54.5% (23.4-83.3) by IRC and 55.5% by investigator; median DoR not reached (Table 3). Colorectal ORR 20.0%. Grade >=3 TEAEs: hypertension 22%, ALT 16%, AST 13%; serious TEAEs 40%; no treatment-related deaths. Enrollment Dec 4, 2017-Aug 4, 2021.
TX-019.limitations: No pancreatic OS data; interim analysis
TX-019.interpretation: Biomarker-selected single-arm; pancreatic-specific signal is from 11 patients

glosses.fusions-rare-targets: A tissue-agnostic selpercatinib trial with 6 of 11 RET-fusion pancreatic patients responding.
glosses.second-line: Selpercatinib in RET fusion-positive cancers: 6 of 11 pancreatic patients responded.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: The LIBRETTO-001 basket cohort of selpercatinib in RET-fusion cancers, in which 6 of 11 pancreatic cancers responded.

TX-020.citation: Schram AM, Goto K, Kim DW, et al. Efficacy of Zenocutuzumab in NRG1 Fusion-Positive Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2025;392(6):566-576.
TX-020.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US, accelerated): zenocutuzumab-zbco for NRG1 fusion-positive advanced NSCLC and pancreatic adenocarcinoma after prior systemic therapy (BLA 761352, 2024-12-04); label (checked 2026-10-08) also lists cholangiocarcinoma (supplement s010 approved 2026-05-08)
