TX-020.design: Tumor-agnostic registrational phase 2 (eNRGy), single arm; primary endpoint investigator-assessed ORR (RECIST 1.1); primary efficacy set = measurable disease and enrolled >=24 weeks before cutoff
TX-020.population: Advanced NRG1 fusion-positive solid tumors (12 types); 204 treated; pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma 36 (22%), all KRAS wild-type; 35/36 pancreatic patients had prior systemic therapy (FOLFIRINOX and/or gemcitabine/taxane)
TX-020.finding: Cutoff Jan 31, 2024. Overall ORR 30% (95% CI 23-37; 47/158, 1 CR); median DoR 11.1 mo (7.4-12.9); 19% of responses ongoing. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma: ORR 42% (15/36; 95% CI 25-59) by investigator, 44% (16/36) by BICR; median DoR 7.4 mo (95% CI 4.0-11.2; range 2.1+ to 20.7) investigator / 9.1 mo BICR (Table 2). NSCLC ORR 29%. Most common NRG1 partner in pancreatic cancer ATP1B1 (44%). Grade 3-4 AEs regardless of attribution: anemia 5%, GGT increase 4%, pneumonia 3%; mainly low-grade AEs. Median exposure 5.5 mo; treatment ongoing in 25%.
TX-020.effect: Pancreatic ORR 42% in previously treated patients; DoR 7.4 months
TX-020.limitations: Rare target (<1% of solid tumors; enriched in KRAS-WT PDAC); durability modest in pancreatic cohort
TX-020.interpretation: Biomarker-selected single-arm; supports NRG1 fusion as a ligand-type driver in KRAS-wild-type PDAC

glosses.clinical-trials: A single-arm study of zenocutuzumab in NRG1-fusion cancers with a 42% response rate in 36 pancreatic patients.
glosses.fusions-rare-targets: A trial of zenocutuzumab with a 42 percent response in 36 NRG1-fusion pancreatic patients.
glosses.second-line: Zenocutuzumab in NRG1 fusion-positive cancers: 15 of 36 previously treated pancreatic patients responded, with responses lasting a median of 7.4 months.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: The eNRGy registrational trial of zenocutuzumab in NRG1-fusion cancers, with 15 of 36 pancreatic adenocarcinomas responding for a median of 7.4 months.

TX-021.citation: Subbiah V, Kreitman RJ, Wainberg ZA, et al. Dabrafenib plus trametinib in BRAFV600E-mutated rare cancers: the phase 2 ROAR trial. Nat Med. 2023;29(5):1103-1112.
TX-021.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US, accelerated): dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E unresectable/metastatic solid tumors after prior treatment, patients >=1 year (Tafinlar NDA 202806 s022, 2022-06-22; label checked 2026-10-08, still accelerated)
TX-021.design: Open-label phase 2 basket with Bayesian hierarchical adaptive design; primary endpoint investigator-assessed ORR (RECIST 1.1 for solid tumors; RANO for gliomas)
TX-021.population: BRAF V600E-mutated advanced rare cancers without satisfactory options: anaplastic thyroid (36), biliary tract (43), GIST (1), low-grade glioma (13), high-grade glioma (45), small-intestine adenocarcinoma (3), hairy cell leukemia (55), multiple myeloma (10); no pancreatic cohort
TX-021.finding: Per-cohort ORRs reported in Table/Fig (not captured as text in accessed version); treatment-related AEs in 87.9%; most frequent pyrexia 40.8%, fatigue 25.7%, chills 25.7%, nausea 23.8%, rash 20.4%; fatal SAEs 4.4% (9 patients, one listed as pancreatic adenocarcinoma in the HCL cohort). Authors note consistency with NCI-MATCH EAY131-H (GI tract BRAF V600E cancers n=11) and case reports in pancreatic cancer.
TX-021.effect: Not extractable per cohort from accessed text; approval based on ORR/DoR across cohorts
TX-021.limitations: No pancreatic patients; the ORR values were not retrievable from the text version used (tables rendered as images)
TX-021.interpretation: Biomarker-selected basket; supports BRAF V600E dependency across histologies; pancreatic activity rests on case reports and NCI-MATCH, not this trial

glosses.fusions-rare-targets: The ROAR trial of dabrafenib plus trametinib in BRAF V600E rare cancers, with no pancreatic cohort.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: The ROAR basket trial of dabrafenib plus trametinib in BRAF V600E rare cancers, which included no pancreatic cohort.

TX-022.citation: Pachman DR, Qin R, Seisler DK, et al. Clinical Course of Oxaliplatin-Induced Neuropathy: Results From the Randomized Phase III Trial N08CB (Alliance). J Clin Oncol. 2015;33(30):3416-3422.
TX-022.clinical_status: Not applicable (toxicity natural history); oxaliplatin FDA-labeled for colorectal indications only (checked 2026-10-08)
TX-022.design: Prospective longitudinal patient-reported outcomes nested in a randomized phase 3: daily 0-10 acute-symptom questionnaires for 5 days each cycle; EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 before each cycle and up to 18 months after chemotherapy
TX-022.population: Patients with colon cancer receiving adjuvant FOLFOX (12 cycles) on the N08CB calcium/magnesium neuroprotection trial (CaMg was ineffective, so arms pooled)
TX-022.finding: Acute neuropathy with cycle 1 in 308/346 (89%): sensitivity to touching cold 71%, swallowing cold 71%, throat discomfort 63%, muscle cramps 42%; symptoms peaked day 3 and were about twice as severe in cycles 2-12 as in cycle 1; 11% had no acute symptoms in cycle 1 but 74% of those developed cold sensitivity by cycle 2. Chronic CIPN20: sensory score fell 21 points, motor 8, autonomic 5 during treatment; tingling > numbness > pain; hands worse than feet during treatment, feet worse than hands by 18 months. Numbness/tingling worsened most during the first 3 months after completion; at 18 months 50% had <10% reduction from baseline sensory score, 31% a 10-30% reduction, and 19% severe persistent symptoms. Acute severity in cycle 1 predicted chronic neurotoxicity (P<.0001). Fig 1-4, Appendix Table A2.
TX-022.effect: 19% severe sensory neuropathy at 18 months; acute symptoms in 89% at first cycle
TX-022.interpretation: Prospective within-subject exposure-response time course in a colorectal population; transfer to PDAC assumes drug-specific toxicity independent of tumor type

glosses.neuropathy: A 346-patient study within a colorectal cancer trial charted the acute and chronic course of oxaliplatin neuropathy over 18 months.
glosses.folfirinox: Prospective symptom study of 346 colorectal patients on oxaliplatin: 89% had cold-triggered neuropathy with the first cycle, and 19% had severe sensory symptoms 18 months after finishing.
glosses.nalirifox: Prospective symptom study of 346 colorectal patients on oxaliplatin showing neuropathy rising with cumulative dose and persisting severely in 19% at 18 months.
glosses.second-line: Prospective study of oxaliplatin neuropathy in 346 colorectal patients: acute cold-triggered symptoms in 89% and severe persistent symptoms in 19% at 18 months.
glosses.oxaliplatin: A prospective study of 346 people on FOLFOX for colon cancer charting acute and chronic oxaliplatin neuropathy for 18 months after treatment.

TX-023.citation: Philip PA, Lacy J, Portales F, et al. Nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine in patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPACT): a multicentre, open-label phase 2 study. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2020;5(3):285-294.
TX-023.clinical_status: Phase 2; GnP in LAPC is guideline-listed practice (off-label relative to the metastatic-only FDA indication)
TX-023.design: Single-arm international phase 2; six induction cycles then investigator's choice (continue GnP, chemoradiation, or surgery); primary endpoint time to treatment failure; ITT efficacy
TX-023.population: Previously untreated unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer, ECOG 0-1; 35 sites in USA, France, Spain, Canada, Italy
TX-023.finding: Registry/abstract: median TTF 9.0 mo (90% CI 7.3-10.1; registry 95% CI 7.26-10.05); median PFS 10.9 mo (9.3-11.6); median OS 18.8 mo (15.0-24.0). Disease control 77.6%; ORR 33.6% (abstract) / 39.3% (registry, broader window). 62/107 (58%) completed induction; 44 (41%) discontinued induction (AEs 21%). After induction 47 (44%) received continued therapy: 12 continued GnP, 18 chemoradiation, 17 (16%) surgery (7 R0, 9 R1). Grade >=3 during induction: neutropenia 33%, anaemia 11%, fatigue 10%; no treatment-related deaths. Global QoL maintained in most patients (registry: improved 43, stable 34, worsened 18).
TX-023.effect: Conversion to resection 16% (7% R0 of all enrolled); median OS 18.8 months ITT
TX-023.limitations: Full text not accessed; no control arm; small number resected
TX-023.interpretation: Single-arm prospective; benchmarks induction GnP; no inference about surgery's causal contribution

glosses.treatment-sequencing: LAPACT (abstract and registry): 107 patients with unresectable locally advanced disease given gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel had median survival of 18.8 months, and 16% went to surgery.
glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: LAPACT (abstract and registry): single-arm study of 107 patients with locally advanced disease; median survival 18.8 months and 16% proceeded to surgery.

TX-024.citation: Krishnan S, Chadha AS, Suh Y, et al. Focal Radiation Therapy Dose Escalation Improves Overall Survival in Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer Patients Receiving Induction Chemotherapy and Consolidative Chemoradiation. Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys. 2016;94(4):755-765.
TX-024.clinical_status: Dose-escalated RT is investigational (no FDA device/drug label applies); SBRT/ablative RT are guideline-listed options for selected LAPC
TX-024.design: Retrospective single-institution cohort; exposure BED >70 Gy (simultaneous integrated boost IMRT, e.g., 57.25 Gy/25 = BED 70.36) vs <=70 Gy (50.4 Gy/28 = BED 59.47); inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting on propensity score; multivariable Cox
TX-024.population: 200 LAPC patients treated with induction chemotherapy (FOLFIRINOX 21%, gemcitabine-based 79%; median 3.5 months) then chemoradiation at MD Anderson, 2006-2014; 47 (24%) with tumors >1 cm from luminal organs selected for dose escalation
TX-024.finding: Median OS from start of CRT 15.3 mo overall (151 deaths). BED >70 vs <=70 Gy: median OS 17.8 vs 15.0 mo (P=.03); 2-yr OS 36% vs 19%; 3-yr OS 31% vs 9%; local-regional recurrence-free survival 10.2 vs 6.2 mo (P=.05). After IPTW adjustment medians converged (14.4 vs 14.4 mo) but BED remained significantly associated with OS in adjusted Cox models (P=.01) and with recurrence-free, local-regional and distant recurrence-free survival; dose escalation not associated with smaller tumors (3.2 vs 3.6 cm, P=.16). Toxicity in the high-dose group: grade 3 diarrhea 1 patient (2%); 13% required transfusion. Figs 2-3, Tables 2-3.
TX-024.effect: 3-yr OS 31% vs 9% (unadjusted); adjusted HR not extracted (significant, P=.01)
TX-024.limitations: Retrospective, single center, heterogeneous induction; adjusted medians identical
TX-024.interpretation: Observational dose-response with anatomic selection; hypothesis-generating for a BED threshold; cannot exclude confounding by anatomy and fitness

glosses.radiation: A 200-patient single-center retrospective series in which higher radiation doses after induction chemotherapy were associated with longer survival before adjustment but identical medians after propensity weighting.

TX-025.citation: Reyngold M, O'Reilly EM, Varghese AM, et al. Association of Ablative Radiation Therapy With Survival Among Patients With Inoperable Pancreatic Cancer. JAMA Oncol. 2021;7(5):735-738.
TX-025.clinical_status: Investigational/guideline-listed option; randomized trials of ablative RT pending
TX-025.design: Cohort study from a prospectively maintained database; standardized ablative RT (75 Gy/25 fractions, BED 97.5 Gy, for tumors <1 cm from stomach/intestine [n=96]; 67.5 Gy/15 fractions [n=23]) with respiratory gating, soft-tissue image guidance, selective adaptive planning, concurrent…
TX-025.population: 119 consecutive patients with localized unresectable or medically inoperable PDAC (T3/T4 83%, node-positive 49%; median CA19-9 >167 U/mL) treated June 2016-Feb 2019 at Memorial Sloan Kettering network; 97.5% received induction chemotherapy (mFOLFIRINOX 66, GnP 37, other 13; median 4 months)
TX-025.finding: Median follow-up 18.4 mo from RT; 55 deaths. Median OS from RT 18.2 mo (95% CI 16.3-26.8) and from diagnosis 26.8 mo (21.7-35.7); 12- and 24-mo OS from RT 74% and 38%. Median PFS from RT 6.3 mo; from diagnosis 13.2 mo. Cumulative incidence of locoregional progression 17.6% at 12 mo and 32.8% at 24 mo. Post-induction CA19-9 reduction associated with better PFS and lower local progression. Grade 3 RT-attributable AEs in 16 patients, no grade 4; 10 upper GI bleeds (8 on anticoagulation; 2 needed endoscopic intervention). Fig 1-2, eTables 2-3.
TX-025.limitations: Retrospective, single network, heterogeneous induction; 'local control' without randomized comparison
TX-025.interpretation: Observational single-arm; supports feasibility and local control of ablative dosing; survival effect cannot be separated from induction-chemotherapy selection

glosses.radiation: A 119-patient single-network cohort treated with ablative-dose radiation after induction chemotherapy, with 2-year survival of 38 percent from radiation and 2-year local progression of 33 percent.

TX-026.citation: Herman JM, Chang DT, Goodman KA, et al. Phase 2 multi-institutional trial evaluating gemcitabine and stereotactic body radiotherapy for patients with locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Cancer. 2015;121(7):1128-1137.
TX-026.clinical_status: Phase 2; SBRT is a guideline-listed option for LAPC
TX-026.design: Single-arm phase 2; primary endpoint late grade >=2 gastritis/fistula/enteritis/ulcer toxicity (target <20% vs 47% historical with 25 Gy single fraction; 40% used as conservative comparator); secondary 1-yr freedom from local progression (FFLP), OS, QoL
TX-026.population: Locally advanced unresectable PDAC (84% head), median age 67; 3 institutions (Johns Hopkins, Stanford, Memorial Sloan Kettering)
TX-026.finding: Median follow-up 13.9 mo. Acute grade >=2 GI toxicity 2% (one grade 4 duodenal ulcer, patient not on prescribed PPI); late grade >=2 GI toxicity 11% (5/47); serious late GI 6%; one death from GI bleed. Median OS 13.9 mo (95% CI 10.2-16.7); 1- and 2-yr OS 59% and 18%; 1-yr FFLP 78% (60-89%); median PFS 7.8 mo (5.8-10.2). QLQ-C30 global QoL maintained; pancreatic pain scores improved after SBRT. 5 patients (10%) became resectable; 4 (8%) had margin- and node-negative resection (1 pathologic complete response); resected median OS 22.2 vs 13.8 mo (HR 0.45, 0.13-1.49; P=.182). Table 3, Fig 2.
TX-026.effect: Median OS 13.9 months; 1-yr local control 78%; late GI toxicity 11%
TX-026.limitations: Small; gemcitabine-era systemic therapy; FFLP below target 80%
TX-026.interpretation: Prospective multi-institutional single-arm; establishes toxicity/feasibility and a local-control benchmark at a modest dose; no survival inference vs chemotherapy alone

glosses.radiation: A 49-patient multicenter phase 2 trial of five-fraction SBRT with gemcitabine in locally advanced disease, reporting 11 percent late bowel toxicity, 78 percent 1-year local control and median survival of 13.9 months.

TX-L01.citation: Conroy T, Hammel P, Hebbar M, et al. FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(25):2395-2406.
TX-L01.finding: Abstract: median follow-up 33.6 mo; median DFS 21.6 vs 12.8 mo (stratified HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.46-0.73; P<0.001); 3-yr DFS 39.7% vs 21.4%; median OS 54.4 vs 35.0 mo (HR 0.64, 0.48-0.86; P=0.003); 3-yr OS 63.4% vs 48.6%; grade 3-4 AEs 75.9% vs 52.9%; one toxic death (gemcitabine, interstitial pneumonitis).

glosses.treatment-sequencing: PRODIGE 24 primary report (abstract): adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine; disease-free survival 21.6 versus 12.8 months at first analysis.
glosses.folfirinox: PRODIGE 24 primary report (abstract): grade 3-4 adverse events in 75.9% with mFOLFIRINOX versus 52.9% with gemcitabine.
glosses.gemcitabine: PRODIGE 24 primary report (abstract): the one toxic death occurred in the gemcitabine arm from interstitial pneumonitis.

TX-L02.citation: Conroy T, Desseigne F, Ychou M, et al. FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine for metastatic pancreatic cancer. N Engl J Med. 2011;364(19):1817-1825.
TX-L02.clinical_status: Guideline-recommended; regimen components not FDA-labeled for pancreatic cancer (checked 2026-10-08)
TX-L02.population: Metastatic pancreatic cancer, ECOG PS 0-1, age <=75 (per NAPOLI-3 discussion), France
TX-L02.time_frame: Enrollment dates not in abstract; registry start 2004-11, primary completion 2010-06
TX-L02.finding: Abstract: median OS 11.1 vs 6.8 mo (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.45-0.73; P<0.001); median PFS 6.4 vs 3.3 mo (HR 0.47, 0.37-0.59); ORR 31.6% vs 9.4%; febrile neutropenia 5.4% (FOLFIRINOX); definitive QoL degradation at 6 months 31% vs 66% (HR 0.47, 0.30-0.70).

glosses.neuropathy: The 2011 phase 3 trial of FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in metastatic pancreatic cancer found median survival 11.1 versus 6.8 months (abstract only).
glosses.fever-infection: The 2011 phase 3 trial of FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in metastatic pancreatic cancer reported febrile neutropenia in 5.4% (abstract only).
glosses.activity-function: The 2011 phase 3 FOLFIRINOX trial enrolled only patients with performance status 0-1 (abstract only).
glosses.treatment-sequencing: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (abstract): FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 342 fit patients with metastatic disease gave median survival of 11.1 versus 6.8 months.
glosses.folfirinox: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (abstract): original FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 342 fit patients with metastatic disease; median survival 11.1 versus 6.8 months.
glosses.nalirifox: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (abstract): original FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 342 fit patients aged 75 or under; median survival 11.1 versus 6.8 months.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (abstract): the original FOLFIRINOX used a 400 mg/m² fluorouracil bolus followed by a 46-hour infusion.
glosses.oxaliplatin: The randomized trial that established FOLFIRINOX over gemcitabine in fit patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer (abstract only).
glosses.gemcitabine: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (abstract): FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 342 fit patients with metastatic disease gave median survival of 11.1 versus 6.8 months.
glosses.growth-factor-support: The 2011 randomized trial of FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine in 342 people with metastatic pancreatic cancer, known here from its abstract, which reported febrile neutropenia in 5.4 percent.

TX-L03.citation: Burris HA 3rd, Moore MJ, Andersen J, et al. Improvements in survival and clinical benefit with gemcitabine as first-line therapy for patients with advanced pancreas cancer: a randomized trial. J Clin Oncol. 1997;15(6):2403-2413.
TX-L03.clinical_status: FDA-approved (US): gemcitabine single agent for pancreatic cancer (NDA 020509, 1996-05-15; generic label 1.4 checked 2026-10-08)
TX-L03.design: Randomized trial; primary endpoint clinical benefit response (pain, KPS, weight composite sustained >=4 weeks)
TX-L03.population: 126 patients with advanced symptomatic pancreas cancer after a pain-stabilization lead-in
TX-L03.finding: Abstract: clinical benefit response 23.8% vs 4.8% (P=.0022); median survival 5.65 vs 4.41 mo (P=.0025); 12-month survival 18% vs 2%; treatment well tolerated.

glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: Burris 1997 (abstract): gemcitabine versus weekly bolus fluorouracil in 126 patients; median survival 5.65 versus 4.41 months and clinical benefit 23.8% versus 4.8%.
glosses.gemcitabine: Burris 1997 (abstract): gemcitabine versus weekly bolus fluorouracil in 126 patients; clinical benefit 23.8% versus 4.8% and median survival 5.65 versus 4.41 months.

TX-L04.citation: Oettle H, Riess H, Stieler JM, et al. Second-line oxaliplatin, folinic acid, and fluorouracil versus folinic acid and fluorouracil alone for gemcitabine-refractory pancreatic cancer: outcomes from the CONKO-003 trial. J Clin Oncol. 2014;32(23):2423-2429.
TX-L04.clinical_status: Oxaliplatin not FDA-labeled for pancreatic cancer; OFF is guideline-listed
TX-L04.design: Randomized open-label phase 3; stratified by metastases, duration of first-line, KPS
TX-L04.population: 168 patients progressing on first-line gemcitabine monotherapy, 16 German institutions
TX-L04.finding: Abstract: median OS 5.9 (95% CI 4.1-7.4) vs 3.3 (2.7-4.0) mo; HR 0.66 (0.48-0.91); P=.010; time to progression 2.9 vs 2.0 mo (HR 0.68); grade 1-2 neurotoxicity 38.2% vs 7.1%; enrollment Jan 2004-May 2007; median follow-up 54.1 mo.

glosses.second-line: CONKO-003 (abstract): OFF versus fluorouracil/folinic acid after gemcitabine in 168 patients; median survival 5.9 versus 3.3 months.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: CONKO-003 (abstract): fluorouracil with folinic acid gave median survival of 3.3 months after gemcitabine, versus 5.9 months with oxaliplatin added.
glosses.oxaliplatin: The CONKO-003 trial in which second-line oxaliplatin with fluorouracil improved survival after gemcitabine (abstract only).

TX-L05.citation: Gill S, Ko YJ, Cripps C, et al. PANCREOX: A Randomized Phase III Study of Fluorouracil/Leucovorin With or Without Oxaliplatin for Second-Line Advanced Pancreatic Cancer in Patients Who Have Received Gemcitabine-Based Chemotherapy. J Clin Oncol. 2016;34(32):3914-3920.
TX-L05.population: 108 patients with advanced pancreatic cancer after gemcitabine-based therapy, ECOG 0-2
TX-L05.finding: Abstract: PFS 3.1 vs 2.9 mo (P=.99); OS inferior with mFOLFOX6, 6.1 vs 9.9 mo (P=.02); grade 3/4 AEs 63% vs 11%; withdrawals for AEs 20% vs 2%; post-progression therapy 7% vs 25% (P=.015); no QoL difference.
TX-L05.effect: No PFS benefit; OS worse with oxaliplatin

glosses.second-line: PANCREOX (abstract): mFOLFOX6 versus infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin after gemcitabine-based therapy in 108 patients; no progression-free benefit and shorter survival with oxaliplatin.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: PANCREOX (abstract): infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin gave median survival of 9.9 months after gemcitabine-based therapy, longer than with oxaliplatin added.
glosses.oxaliplatin: The PANCREOX trial in which second-line FOLFOX gave worse survival than fluorouracil alone (abstract only).

TX-L06.citation: Neoptolemos JP, Palmer DH, Ghaneh P, et al. Comparison of adjuvant gemcitabine and capecitabine with gemcitabine monotherapy in patients with resected pancreatic cancer (ESPAC-4): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2017;389(10073):1011-1024.
TX-L06.clinical_status: Guideline-listed adjuvant option; capecitabine FDA-labeled for colorectal/breast/gastric indications (GENE SEC-02)
TX-L06.design: Randomized open-label phase 3; primary endpoint OS (ITT)
TX-L06.population: 730 patients with R0/R1 resected PDAC randomized within 12 weeks of surgery, 92 hospitals in UK, Germany, France, Sweden
TX-L06.time_frame: Enrollment dates not in abstract; reported at 458 of 480 target deaths

glosses.treatment-sequencing: ESPAC-4 (abstract): adding capecitabine to adjuvant gemcitabine in 730 patients gave median survival of 28.0 versus 25.5 months.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: ESPAC-4 (abstract): adding capecitabine to adjuvant gemcitabine in 730 patients gave median survival of 28.0 versus 25.5 months; capecitabine is not labeled for pancreatic cancer.
glosses.gemcitabine: ESPAC-4 (abstract): adding capecitabine to adjuvant gemcitabine in 730 patients gave median survival of 28.0 versus 25.5 months.

TX-L07.citation: Oettle H, Post S, Neuhaus P, et al. Adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine vs observation in patients undergoing curative-intent resection of pancreatic cancer: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA. 2007;297(3):267-277.
TX-L07.design: Open randomized phase 3; primary endpoint DFS
TX-L07.population: 368 patients with R0/R1 resected pancreatic cancer, 88 centers in Germany and Austria, July 1998-Dec 2004
TX-L07.finding: Abstract: median DFS 13.4 (95% CI 11.4-15.3) vs 6.9 (6.1-7.8) mo (P<.001); 5-yr DFS 16.5% vs 5.5%; median OS 22.1 vs 20.2 mo (P=.06); recurrence 74% vs 92% at median follow-up 53 mo; no QoL difference.
TX-L07.effect: DFS doubled; OS not significant at first analysis

glosses.treatment-sequencing: CONKO-001 (abstract): six months of adjuvant gemcitabine versus observation in 368 resected patients doubled disease-free survival (13.4 versus 6.9 months).
glosses.gemcitabine: CONKO-001 (abstract): six months of adjuvant gemcitabine versus observation in 368 resected patients doubled disease-free survival (13.4 versus 6.9 months).

TX-L08.citation: Oettle H, Neuhaus P, Hochhaus A, et al. Adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and long-term outcomes among patients with resected pancreatic cancer: the CONKO-001 randomized trial. JAMA. 2013;310(14):1473-1481.
TX-L08.design: Long-term follow-up of randomized trial (median follow-up 136 months)

glosses.treatment-sequencing: CONKO-001 long-term follow-up (abstract): adjuvant gemcitabine improved overall survival (hazard ratio 0.76), with 20.7% versus 10.4% alive at five years.
glosses.gemcitabine: CONKO-001 long-term follow-up (abstract): adjuvant gemcitabine improved overall survival (hazard ratio 0.76), with 20.7% versus 10.4% alive at five years.

TX-L09.citation: Uesaka K, Boku N, Fukutomi A, et al. Adjuvant chemotherapy of S-1 versus gemcitabine for resected pancreatic cancer: a phase 3, open-label, randomised, non-inferiority trial (JASPAC 01). Lancet. 2016;388(10041):248-257.
TX-L09.design: Randomized open-label non-inferiority phase 3 (margin HR 1.25) with prespecified superiority test; per-protocol primary analysis
TX-L09.population: 385 patients with resected stage I-III PDAC without residual tumour, 33 hospitals in Japan
TX-L09.finding: Abstract: stopped early for efficacy at interim (Sept 2012); HR for death 0.57 (95% CI 0.44-0.72; p non-inferiority <0.0001; p superiority <0.0001); 5-yr OS 44.1% (36.9-51.1) vs 24.4% (18.6-30.8); more leucopenia/neutropenia/transaminase rises with gemcitabine, more stomatitis/diarrhoea with S-1. Enrollment April 2007-June 2010.

glosses.gemcitabine: JASPAC 01 (abstract): in Japanese patients, adjuvant S-1 beat gemcitabine, which caused more low white cells and liver-enzyme rises; S-1 is not approved in the US.

TX-L10.citation: Versteijne E, van Dam JL, Suker M, et al. Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy Versus Upfront Surgery for Resectable and Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Cancer: Long-Term Results of the Dutch Randomized PREOPANC Trial. J Clin Oncol. 2022;40(11):1220-1230.
TX-L10.design: Long-term follow-up (median 59 months) of randomized phase 3; OS by ITT
TX-L10.finding: Abstract: OS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.96; P=.025); median 15.7 vs 14.3 mo; 5-yr OS 20.5% (14.2-29.8) vs 6.5% (3.1-13.7); effect consistent across prespecified subgroups including resectable and borderline resectable.
TX-L10.limitations: Abstract only; subgroup-level numbers not accessible

glosses.why-chemo-first: The long-term PREOPANC report, recorded from its abstract, showing a survival benefit for preoperative treatment with five-year survival of 20.5% versus 6.5%.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: PREOPANC long-term update (abstract): with 59 months of follow-up, preoperative chemoradiation improved survival (hazard ratio 0.73; five-year survival 20.5% versus 6.5%).
glosses.vascular-resection: Long-term PREOPANC results showing a survival benefit for preoperative treatment with longer follow-up (abstract only).
glosses.radiation: The long-term PREOPANC report, with 5-year survival 20.5 versus 6.5 percent favoring preoperative chemoradiation.

TX-L11.citation: Labori KJ, Bratlie SO, Andersson B, et al. Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX versus upfront surgery for resectable pancreatic head cancer (NORPACT-1): a multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2024;9(3):205-217.
TX-L11.design: Randomized phase 2 (3:2 then 1:1); primary endpoint 18-month OS; ITT and per-protocol
TX-L11.population: 140 patients with resectable pancreatic head tumours radiologically suspected to be PDAC (histology not required), WHO PS 0-1, 12 hospitals in Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden
TX-L11.finding: Abstract: 18-month OS ITT 60% (95% CI 49-71) vs 73% (62-84) (p=0.032); median OS ITT 25.1 vs 38.5 mo (HR 1.52, 1.00-2.33; p=0.050); per-protocol 23.0 vs 34.4 mo (HR 1.46). Only 61/77 (79%) received neoadjuvant therapy; 4 neoadjuvant and 7 upfront patients did not have PDAC; resection 82% vs 89% (p=0.24); adjuvant started in 86% vs 90% of resected PDAC; adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX in 25% vs 43%; grade >=3 AEs 58% vs 40%. Enrollment Feb 2017-April 2021.

glosses.why-chemo-first: The randomized NORPACT-1 trial, recorded from its abstract, in which neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX for resectable head cancer gave worse 18-month survival than up-front surgery.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: NORPACT-1 (abstract): in 140 patients with resectable pancreatic head tumors, neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX gave 18-month survival of 60% versus 73% with upfront surgery.

TX-L12.citation: Ghaneh P, Palmer D, Cicconi S, et al. Immediate surgery compared with short-course neoadjuvant gemcitabine plus capecitabine, FOLFIRINOX, or chemoradiotherapy in patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer (ESPAC5): a four-arm, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2023;8(2):157-168.
TX-L12.clinical_status: Phase 2; supports neoadjuvant chemotherapy in borderline disease
TX-L12.design: Four-arm randomized phase 2 feasibility; primary endpoints recruitment and resection rate; ITT
TX-L12.population: 90 patients with biopsy-proven borderline resectable pancreatic head PDAC by central CT review, 16 centres UK and Germany
TX-L12.n: 90 (33 immediate surgery, 20 gem/cap, 20 FOLFIRINOX, 17 CRT); 86 analysed
TX-L12.finding: Abstract: resection 21/31 (68%) immediate vs 30/55 (55%) neoadjuvant (p=0.33); R0 3/21 (14%) vs 7/30 (23%) (p=0.49); 1-yr OS 39% (24-61) immediate, 78% gem/cap, 84% FOLFIRINOX, 60% CRT (p=0.0028); 1-yr DFS from surgery 33% vs 59% (HR 0.53, 0.28-0.98; p=0.016); grade >=3 AEs 7% vs 34%; partial response 6/46 (13%). Enrollment Sept 2014-Dec 2018; median follow-up 12.2 months.

glosses.treatment-sequencing: ESPAC-5 (abstract): 90 borderline resectable patients; one-year survival was 39% with immediate surgery versus 78-84% with short-course chemotherapy first.

TX-L13.citation: Janssen QP, van Dam JL, van Bekkum ML, et al. Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX versus neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy in resectable and borderline resectable pancreatic cancer (PREOPANC-2): a multicentre, open-label, phase 3 randomised trial. Lancet Oncol. 2025.
TX-L13.design: Open-label randomized phase 3; primary endpoint OS in modified ITT; stratified by resectability
TX-L13.population: 375 patients with resectable or borderline resectable PDAC, WHO PS 0-1, 19 Dutch centres
TX-L13.finding: Abstract: median follow-up 42.3 mo; median OS 21.9 (95% CI 17.7-27.0) vs 21.3 (16.8-25.5) mo; HR 0.88 (0.69-1.13); p=0.32. Grade 3-4: neutropenia 25% vs 22%, diarrhoea 23% vs 1%, leukopenia 8% vs 15%; serious AEs 49% vs 43%; treatment-related deaths 2 vs 1. Enrollment June 5, 2018-Jan 28, 2021.

glosses.nausea-bowel: A Dutch randomized trial of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX versus gemcitabine-based chemoradiation reported grade 3-4 diarrhea in 23% versus 1% (abstract only).
glosses.gemcitabine: PREOPANC-2 (abstract): gemcitabine-based chemoradiation and FOLFIRINOX before surgery gave similar survival (21.3 versus 21.9 months) in 375 patients.
glosses.radiation: The PREOPANC-2 randomized trial, in which neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine-based chemoradiation gave similar survival (hazard ratio 0.88).

TX-L14.citation: Schwarz L, Bachet JB, Meurisse A, et al. Neoadjuvant FOLF(IRIN)OX Chemotherapy for Resectable Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Multicenter Randomized Noncomparative Phase II Trial (PANACHE01 FRENCH08 PRODIGE48 study). J Clin Oncol. 2025.
TX-L14.design: Randomized noncomparative phase 2 (2:2:1); co-primary endpoints 1-yr OS and completion of full therapeutic sequence
TX-L14.population: 153 patients with resectable PDAC, 28 French centers, Feb 2017-July 2020
TX-L14.finding: Abstract: completion of therapeutic sequence 70.8% (arm 1) and 68% (arm 2); 1-yr OS 84.3% (90% CI 75.3-90.9) and 71.4% (59.0-81.8); arm 2 stopped for lack of efficacy; 1-yr EFS 51.4%, 43.1%, 38.7% (control). Primary objective met for mFOLFIRINOX only.

TX-L15.citation: Hammel P, Huguet F, van Laethem JL, et al. Effect of Chemoradiotherapy vs Chemotherapy on Survival in Patients With Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer Controlled After 4 Months of Gemcitabine With or Without Erlotinib: The LAP07 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. 2016;315(17):1844-1853.
TX-L15.clinical_status: Negative phase 3; CRT remains a guideline option for selected LAPC
TX-L15.design: Two-step randomized phase 3 (gemcitabine +/- erlotinib; then chemotherapy x2 months vs CRT 54 Gy + capecitabine); primary endpoint OS from first randomization
TX-L15.population: 449 LAPC patients enrolled 2008-2011 (international); 442 first randomization; 269 second randomization after 4 months without progression
TX-L15.finding: Abstract: stopped for futility at interim (221 deaths); median OS 15.2 (95% CI 13.9-17.3) CRT vs 16.5 (14.5-18.5) chemotherapy; HR 1.03 (0.79-1.34); P=.83; gemcitabine vs gemcitabine+erlotinib 13.6 vs 11.9 mo (HR 1.19, P=.09); CRT reduced local progression 32% vs 46% (P=.03) with no increase in grade 3-4 toxicity except nausea; median follow-up 36.7 months.
TX-L15.effect: OS HR 1.03 (no benefit); local progression -14 points

glosses.radiation: The LAP07 randomized trial, in which chemoradiation after four months of gemcitabine reduced local progression but did not improve survival (hazard ratio 1.03).

TX-L16.citation: Fietkau R, Ghadimi M, Grutzmann R, et al. Benefit of Chemoradiotherapy Versus Chemotherapy After Induction Therapy for Conversion of Unresectable Into Resectable Pancreatic Cancer: The Randomized CONKO-007 Trial. J Clin Oncol. 2025.
TX-L16.design: Open-label randomized phase 3; primary endpoint changed from OS to overall R0 resection rate after interim (slow recruitment); central surgical panel reassessed resectability
TX-L16.population: 525 enrolled with unresectable (locally advanced) PDAC; 495 received induction (FOLFIRINOX 402, gemcitabine 93); 336 without progression at 3 months randomized
TX-L16.finding: Abstract: overall R0 rate 25% (43/169) vs 18% (30/167), P=.113 (not significant); surgery performed equally often (P=.91); R0 among operated 69.4% (43/62) vs 50.0% (30/60), P=.04; OS HR 0.937 (95% CI 0.747-1.174; P=.57); surgery associated with longer OS (HR 0.525, 0.408-0.676; P<.001); median follow-up 76 months.
TX-L16.limitations: Abstract only; primary endpoint changed mid-trial

glosses.radiation: The CONKO-007 randomized trial, in which chemoradiation after induction raised the margin-negative rate among those operated but not overall, with no survival difference.

TX-L17.citation: Hidalgo M, Plaza C, Musteanu M, et al. SPARC Expression Did Not Predict Efficacy of nab-Paclitaxel plus Gemcitabine or Gemcitabine Alone for Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer in an Exploratory Analysis of the Phase III MPACT Trial. Clin Cancer Res. 2015;21(21):4811-4818.
TX-L17.design: Exploratory biomarker analysis of randomized trial + SPARC-knockout mouse experiments
TX-L17.population: MPACT patients with evaluable SPARC: stroma 256 (30%), epithelium 301 (35%), plasma 343 (40%); 71% of stromal samples from metastases
TX-L17.finding: Abstract: stromal SPARC high (n=71) vs low (n=185) not associated with OS (HR 1.019; P=0.903), confirmed in multivariate analysis and within each arm; epithelial and plasma SPARC not associated with OS; SPARC-knockout mouse model showed no correlation between SPARC and tumor progression or treatment efficacy.
TX-L17.interpretation: Prespecified exploratory biomarker analysis in a randomized trial; null result

glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: Analysis of MPACT tumors (abstract): SPARC levels in stroma, tumor cells or plasma did not predict survival or benefit.

TX-L18.citation: Petrelli N, Douglass HO Jr, Herrera L, et al. The modulation of fluorouracil with leucovorin in metastatic colorectal carcinoma: a prospective randomized phase III trial. Gastrointestinal Tumor Study Group. J Clin Oncol. 1989;7(10):1419-1426.
TX-L18.clinical_status: Leucovorin FDA-labeled for use with 5-FU in colorectal cancer (label not examined in detail)
TX-L18.finding: Abstract: response 30.3% (33/109) high-dose LV (P<.01 vs control) vs 12.1% (13/107) 5-FU alone vs 18.8% (21/112) low-dose LV; dose-limiting toxicity diarrhea; treatment-related deaths 11 (5%); trend to longer survival with high-dose LV.
TX-L18.interpretation: Randomized clinical confirmation of the biochemical modulation hypothesis

glosses.folfirinox: Colorectal trial (abstract) in which adding high-dose leucovorin to fluorouracil raised response from 12.1% to 30.3%.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: Colorectal trial (abstract) of 343 patients in which adding high-dose leucovorin to fluorouracil raised response from 12.1% to 30.3%.

TX-L19.citation: de Gramont A, Bosset JF, Milan C, et al. Randomized trial comparing monthly low-dose leucovorin and fluorouracil bolus with bimonthly high-dose leucovorin and fluorouracil bolus plus continuous infusion for advanced colorectal cancer: a French intergroup study. J Clin Oncol. 1997;15(2):808-815.
TX-L19.clinical_status: Infusional 5-FU schedule is FDA-labeled (fluorouracil label lists 400 mg/m2 bolus then 2400-3000 mg/m2 over 46 h with leucovorin; pancreatic adenocarcinoma is a labeled indication - checked 2026-10-08)
TX-L19.finding: Abstract: response 32.6% vs 14.4% (P=.0004); median PFS 27.6 vs 22 weeks (P=.0012); median survival 62 vs 56.8 weeks (P=.067); grade 3-4 toxicity 11.1% vs 23.9% (P=.0004); granulocytopenia 1.9% vs 7.3%, diarrhea 2.9% vs 7.3%, mucositis 1.9% vs 7.3%.
TX-L19.effect: Response doubled; severe toxicity halved; survival NS

glosses.folfirinox: Colorectal trial (abstract) in which a 46-hour infusional fluorouracil schedule doubled response and halved severe toxicity compared with bolus dosing.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: Colorectal trial (abstract) of 448 patients in which a 46-hour infusional fluorouracil schedule doubled response and halved severe toxicity compared with monthly bolus dosing.

TX-L20.citation: de Gramont A, Figer A, Seymour M, et al. Leucovorin and fluorouracil with or without oxaliplatin as first-line treatment in advanced colorectal cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2000;18(16):2938-2947.
TX-L20.clinical_status: Oxaliplatin FDA-labeled for colorectal cancer only (checked 2026-10-08)
TX-L20.finding: Abstract: median PFS 9.0 vs 6.2 mo (P=.0003); response 50.7% vs 22.3% (P=.0001); median OS 16.2 vs 14.7 mo (P=.12); grade 3/4 neutropenia 41.7% vs 5.3%; grade 3/4 diarrhea 11.9% vs 5.3%; grade 3 neurosensory toxicity 18.2% vs 0%; QoL not impaired.
TX-L20.interpretation: Randomized add-on design isolates oxaliplatin's contribution

glosses.folfirinox: Colorectal trial (abstract) in which adding oxaliplatin to infusional fluorouracil/leucovorin lengthened progression-free survival at the cost of grade 3 neuropathy in 18.2%.
glosses.oxaliplatin: A randomized colorectal cancer trial that added oxaliplatin to fluorouracil and leucovorin, more than doubling response at the cost of neuropathy and neutropenia (abstract only).

TX-L21.citation: Hsiang YH, Hertzberg R, Hecht S, Liu LF. Camptothecin induces protein-linked DNA breaks via mammalian DNA topoisomerase I. J Biol Chem. 1985;260(27):14873-14878.
TX-L21.clinical_status: Irinotecan FDA-labeled for colorectal cancer (GENE SEC-01); liposomal irinotecan labeled for pancreatic cancer
TX-L21.population: Purified mammalian DNA topoisomerase I and DNA; mammalian cells
TX-L21.finding: Abstract: camptothecin does not bind purified DNA but induces extensive, immediate and reversible single-strand DNA breaks in reactions with purified topoisomerase I; the enzyme is covalently linked to the 3' end of broken DNA; camptothecin inhibits catalytic activity; proposed blockade of the rejoining step with accumulation of a 'cleavable complex'.
TX-L21.interpretation: Biochemical mechanism in a purified system

glosses.folfirinox: Biochemical study (abstract) showing that camptothecin, the parent of irinotecan, traps topoisomerase I on broken DNA rather than binding DNA itself.
glosses.nalirifox: Biochemical study (abstract) showing that camptothecin, the parent of irinotecan, traps topoisomerase I on broken DNA rather than binding DNA itself.
glosses.irinotecan: The 1985 biochemical study showing that camptothecin drugs break DNA only by trapping topoisomerase I on it (abstract only).

TX-L22.citation: Ullman B, Lee M, Martin DW Jr, Santi DV. Cytotoxicity of 5-fluoro-2'-deoxyuridine: requirement for reduced folate cofactors and antagonism by methotrexate. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 1978;75(2):980-983.
TX-L22.population: L1210 mouse leukemia cells; purified thymidylate synthase
TX-L22.finding: Abstract: inhibition of thymidylate synthase by FdUMP requires 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate; FdUrd cytotoxicity is reduced when intracellular reduced folates are depleted by medium limitation or methotrexate; covalently bound FdUMP-thymidylate synthase complex is greatly diminished under folate depletion; folate requirement for maximal cytotoxicity exceeds that for growth.

glosses.folfirinox: Cell-culture study (abstract) showing fluorouracil's metabolite blocks thymidylate synthase only when a reduced folate is present, the basis for giving leucovorin.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: Cell-culture study (abstract) showing fluorouracil's metabolite blocks thymidylate synthase only when a reduced folate is present, the basis for giving leucovorin.

TX-L23.citation: Von Hoff DD, Ramanathan RK, Borad MJ, et al. Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel is an active regimen in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: a phase I/II trial. J Clin Oncol. 2011;29(34):4548-4554.
TX-L23.design: Phase I/II dose escalation + preclinical xenograft study
TX-L23.population: 67 patients with previously untreated advanced pancreatic cancer; human pancreatic cancer xenografts in mice
TX-L23.finding: Abstract: MTD nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2; DLTs sepsis and neutropenia; at MTD response rate 48%, median OS 12.2 months, 1-yr survival 48%; stromal (not tumor) SPARC correlated with survival; in xenografts nab-paclitaxel depleted desmoplastic stroma and intratumoral gemcitabine rose 2.8-fold.

glosses.gem-nabpaclitaxel: Phase 1/2 study (abstract) that set the nab-paclitaxel dose at 125 mg/m² with gemcitabine and reported stromal depletion in mouse xenografts, the origin of the stroma hypothesis.

TX-L24.citation: Kindler HL, Reni M, Van Cutsem E, et al. Overall Survival Results From the POLO Trial: A Phase III Study of Active Maintenance Olaparib Versus Placebo for Germline BRCA-Mutated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2022;40(34):3929-3939.
TX-L24.design: Preplanned final OS analysis at 70.1% maturity (DCO2, July 21, 2020)
TX-L24.finding: Median OS 19.0 vs 19.2 mo; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.56-1.22); P=.3487; curves cross at ~12 months and separate from ~24 months; 3-yr OS 33.9% vs 17.8%. Investigator PFS 6.7 vs 3.7 mo (HR 0.49, 0.33-0.73; P=.0004); 3-yr progression-free 23.1% vs 5.4%. PFS2 HR not significant. Time to first subsequent therapy HR 0.44 (significant); time to second subsequent therapy and time to discontinuation significantly longer. Subsequent therapy 62.0% vs 87.1%; subsequent PARP inhibitor 7.8% vs 27.1% of discontinuers; most common second-line therapy platinum-based (FOLFIRINOX). No MDS/AML. Fig 1-4, Appendix Tables A2-A3.

glosses.reading-trial-results: The final overall-survival report of the POLO trial, showing no significant survival difference despite a three-year tail.
glosses.survival-statistics: The final overall-survival report of the POLO trial, showing near-identical medians but a three-year survival difference of 34% against 18%.
glosses.brca-palb2-hrd: The overall-survival report of POLO, 19.0 versus 19.2 months, not significant, with a better three-year survival tail.
glosses.olaparib: The final overall-survival report of POLO, 19.0 versus 19.2 months, not significant, with a better 3-year survival tail.

TX-L25.citation: Truty MJ, Kendrick ML, Nagorney DM, et al. Factors Predicting Response, Perioperative Outcomes, and Survival Following Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Borderline/Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer. Ann Surg. 2021;273(2):341-349.
TX-L25.population: 194 patients (123 borderline, 71 locally advanced) resected after total neoadjuvant therapy at Mayo Clinic, 2010-2017
TX-L25.finding: Abstract: radiologic downstaging in only 28%; R0 94%; 90-day major morbidity 36%, mortality 6.7%; median OS 58.8 months (excluding operative deaths), 3-yr OS 62%; survival independently predicted by >=6 cycles chemotherapy, optimal CA19-9 response and major pathologic response; all three present → superior survival; downstaging, vascular resection and regimen not associated with survival; complete metabolic response on interval PET correlated with major pathologic response.
TX-L25.interpretation: Observational resected cohort; prognostic, not causal

glosses.why-chemo-first: A single-center report, recorded from its abstract, of resected patients after total neoadjuvant therapy with a selected-cohort median survival of 58.8 months.
glosses.survival-statistics: A single-center report, recorded from its abstract, of resected patients after total neoadjuvant therapy with a selected-cohort median survival of 58.8 months.
glosses.pet-scan: An abstract-only resected cohort after total neoadjuvant therapy in which complete metabolic response on PET tracked major pathologic response.
glosses.restaging: An abstract-only resected cohort after total neoadjuvant therapy with downstaging in only 28% but 94% clear margins.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: Mayo Clinic series (abstract) of 194 patients resected after total neoadjuvant therapy, with median survival of 58.8 months in this selected resected group.
glosses.vascular-resection: A Mayo Clinic cohort of 194 patients resected after total neoadjuvant therapy, 65% with vascular resection, reporting 90-day morbidity and mortality (abstract only).

SURG-001.citation: Rhim AD, Mirek ET, Aiello NM, Maitra A, Bailey JM, McAllister F, et al. EMT and dissemination precede pancreatic tumor formation. Cell. 2012;148(1-2):349-61.
SURG-001.design: Genetic lineage-tracing / flow cytometry for circulating pancreatic cells (CPCs); perturbation with pancreatitis and dexamethasone.
SURG-001.population: Pdx1-Cre;LSL-Kras G12D;p53;Rosa-YFP (PKCY) and inflammation (IKCY) autochthonous mouse PDAC with lineage labeling (>95%).
SURG-001.n: Mouse cohorts (per-figure n); CPC flow across PanIN vs PDAC mice.
SURG-001.finding: 42% of YFP+ cells in PKCY tumors had undergone EMT (68% in IKCY). EMT present in 2.7% of PanIN2 and 6.8% of PanIN3 lesions, never in PanIN1; 15.8% of inflamed acinar-to-ductal metaplasia foci. YFP+ circulating pancreatic cells abundant in 8-10 wk PanIN mice BEFORE histologic cancer; cells were mesenchymal, stem-like, seeded liver. Pancreatitis increased CPCs; dexamethasone abolished dissemination.
SURG-001.effect: Dissemination detectable at premalignant (PanIN) stage; dexamethasone -> ~abolished CPCs.
SURG-001.limitations: Mouse model; relevance of pre-tumor CPCs to clinically meaningful metastasis not shown; later work (Zheng) challenges EMT necessity.
SURG-001.interpretation: Lineage tracing + perturbation in vivo supports causal claim that EMT/inflammation enable early dissemination (in mouse preparation).

glosses.microscopic-disease: A mouse lineage-tracing study showing pancreatic cells can enter the circulation and reach the liver before a tumor is histologically visible.
glosses.liver-niche: A lineage-tracing mouse study showing pancreatic cells enter the circulation and seed the liver at the precursor stage, before an invasive cancer exists.

SURG-002.citation: Yachida S, Jones S, Bozic I, Antal T, Leary R, Fu B, et al. Distant metastasis occurs late during the genetic evolution of pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2010;467(7319):1114-7.
SURG-002.design: Whole-exome/copy-number clonal reconstruction + mathematical timing model (Ki67-anchored).
SURG-002.population: 7 patients with end-stage PDAC; index metastasis + anatomically distinct autopsy metastases + primary; microdissected.
SURG-002.n: 7 index metastases (426 somatic mutations; avg 61/lesion) across multi-region autopsy samples.
SURG-002.finding: Founder mutations mean 64% (48-83%) shared across all samples; progressor 36%. Parental clone already carried all driver mutations (KRAS, TP53, SMAD4). Timing: ~11.7 yr from initiation to parental (founder) clone; +6.8 yr to the index metastatic subclone; +2.7 yr to death (~17 yr total). Metastatic subclones carried many additional progressor mutations arising within the primary.
SURG-002.effect: ~5+ year window between a resectable-stage founder clone and metastatic competence.
SURG-002.limitations: n=7; model assumptions; no direct measure of when cells physically disseminate (cf. Rhim shows early physical dissemination).
SURG-002.interpretation: Human genomic phylogeny supports temporal ordering (parental->metastatic clone) but is correlational for mechanism.

glosses.what-is-pdac: Genetic reconstruction of seven autopsy cases estimating that metastatic subclones arise years before death.
glosses.why-chemo-first: Genetic reconstruction of seven autopsy cases estimating that metastatic subclones arise years before death.
glosses.microscopic-disease: Genetic reconstruction of seven autopsy cases estimating that metastatic subclones arise years before death.
glosses.liver-niche: A human multi-region sequencing and timing study placing the acquisition of full metastatic capacity late in the tumor's genetic evolution.
glosses.smad4: A genetic reconstruction of seven metastatic cases showing all major driver genes present in the founding clone years before spread.
glosses.genome-evolution: A genetic reconstruction of seven metastatic cases estimating about 17 years from initiation to death, with metastatic ability acquired late.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: Genetic reconstruction of tumors and metastases from seven autopsies showed metastatic clones arise years after the founding clone, implying a window in which spread may already have begun by diagnosis.
glosses.whipple: Genomic reconstruction in seven autopsied patients timing the metastasis-capable clone years before the cancer became lethal.
glosses.total-pancreatectomy: Genomic reconstruction in seven autopsied patients timing the metastasis-capable clone years before the cancer became lethal.

SURG-003.citation: Reames BN, Ghaferi AA, Birkmeyer JD, Dimick JB. Hospital volume and operative mortality in the modern era. Ann Surg. 2014;260(2):244-51.
SURG-003.design: Retrospective national claims cohort; multivariable + hierarchical logistic regression; hospitals in volume quintiles.
SURG-003.population: US Medicare patients, 8 cardiovascular/GI operations incl. pancreatectomy, 2000-2009.
SURG-003.finding: Pancreatectomy adjusted OR of mortality (very-low vs very-high volume) 5.83 (95%CI 3.64-9.36) in 2000-01, decreasing to 3.08 (2.07-4.57) in 2008-09 (only procedure whose volume effect weakened). Inverse volume-mortality relationship significant for all 8 procedures throughout; strengthened over time for 5/8.
SURG-003.effect: 3-6x higher operative mortality at very-low vs very-high volume hospitals for pancreatectomy.
SURG-003.limitations: Medicare >=65y; administrative coding; no granular complication data.
SURG-003.interpretation: Large risk-adjusted observational cohort; supports volume as a strong marker (not proof of causation) for perioperative mortality.

glosses.why-plans-change: A US Medicare analysis showing operative mortality after pancreatectomy is three to six times higher at very-low-volume hospitals.
glosses.survival-statistics: A US Medicare analysis showing operative mortality after pancreatectomy is three to six times higher at very-low-volume hospitals.
glosses.whipple: A US Medicare analysis of 3.3 million operations showing pancreatectomy mortality three to six times higher at the lowest-volume hospitals.
glosses.distal-pancreatectomy: A US Medicare analysis showing pancreatectomy mortality three to six times higher at the lowest-volume hospitals.
glosses.surgical-complications: A US Medicare analysis showing pancreatectomy mortality three to six times higher at the lowest-volume hospitals.

SURG-004.citation: Bruna CL, van Hilst J, Korrel M, Jones LR, Abu Hilal M, Besselink MG, et al. Minimally Invasive vs Open Left Pancreatectomy for Resectable Pancreatic Cancer: Long-Term Results of the DIPLOMA Randomized Trial. JAMA Surg. 2025;160(12):1299-1307.
SURG-004.clinical_status: guideline-accepted for distal pancreatectomy in experienced centers (US/intl)
SURG-004.design: Randomized, patient- and pathologist-blinded noninferiority RCT (DIPLOMA); >=36 mo follow-up.
SURG-004.population: Patients with upfront-resectable PDAC of pancreatic body/tail; 35 centers, 12 countries.
SURG-004.n: 258 randomized (minimally invasive [laparoscopic+robotic] vs open left pancreatectomy).
SURG-004.finding: No significant difference in median overall survival or disease-free survival between MILP and OLP at long-term follow-up; comparable radical (R0) resection rates reported in the primary trial. Supports long-term oncologic safety of MILP.
SURG-004.effect: OS/DFS: no significant between-arm difference (noninferiority supported).
SURG-004.limitations: Left-sided/distal only (not pancreatoduodenectomy); experienced centers; selected resectable disease.
SURG-004.interpretation: Blinded RCT -> strongest design for approach equivalence on oncologic endpoints.

glosses.pancreas-body-tail: DIPLOMA randomized trial of 258 patients showing similar long-term survival after minimally invasive and open left pancreatectomy for cancer.
glosses.spleen: DIPLOMA randomized trial of 258 patients showing similar long-term survival after minimally invasive and open left pancreatectomy for cancer.
glosses.splenic-vessels: DIPLOMA randomized trial of 258 patients showing similar long-term survival after minimally invasive and open left pancreatectomy for cancer.
glosses.distal-pancreatectomy: The DIPLOMA randomized trial of 258 patients showing minimally invasive and open distal pancreatectomy give similar long-term survival.

SURG-005.citation: Taherian M, Katz MHG, Prakash LR, Wei D, Tang Z, Sun X, et al. The Association between Sampling and Survival in Patients with Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Who Received Neoadjuvant Therapy and Pancreaticoduodenectomy. Cancers (Basel). 2024;16(19):3312.
SURG-005.design: Retrospective pathology cohort; entire submission of tumor (ESOT) / pancreas (ESOP) vs partial sampling; multivariable survival.
SURG-005.population: 627 PDAC patients after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) + pancreaticoduodenectomy (MD Anderson).
SURG-005.finding: ESOP associated with more lymph nodes (p<0.001), lower ypN (p<0.001), smaller size, better differentiation, less lymphovascular invasion (p=0.009); ESOT/ESOP associated with lower ypT, less perineural invasion, better tumor response. Both independently associated with less recurrence and better DFS/OS (multivariable). (Bias: complete submission done preferentially for minimal residual tumor.)
SURG-005.effect: ESOT and ESOP independent prognostic factors for OS.
SURG-005.limitations: Single center; selection/indication bias explicitly acknowledged.
SURG-005.interpretation: Observational; demonstrates that pathologic assessment method changes stage assignment (measurement effect), confounded by indication.

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: A 627-patient pathology study showing that more thorough specimen sampling changes stage and response assignments after neoadjuvant therapy.
glosses.microscopic-disease: A pathology study showing that how thoroughly a specimen is sampled changes stage and response assignments.
glosses.lymph-nodes: Single-center study showing that more thorough pathological sampling of the specimen finds more lymph nodes and changes the stage assigned.
glosses.pathology-report: A 627-patient series showing that how completely the specimen is examined changes the stage assigned after preoperative therapy.

SURG-006.citation: Ahuja M, Pande R, Chugtai S, Brown RM, Cuesta Martin de Vidales V, Bartlett DC, et al. Vein Wall Invasion Is a More Reliable Predictor of Oncological Outcomes than Vein-Related Margins after Pancreaticoduodenectomy for Early Stages of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma. Diagnostics (Basel). 2023;13(22):3465.
SURG-006.design: Retrospective analysis of prospective data; multivariable Cox for OS/DFS/local recurrence (LR).
SURG-006.population: 372 PD patients (resectable / borderline venous-only PDAC) over 10 yr, prospectively collected.
SURG-006.n: 372 patients; 105 (28%) vein resection; vein-wall involvement in 37% of resected veins.
SURG-006.finding: Vein-related margins NOT independent predictors of OS/DFS/LR. Vein-wall invasion independently predicted OS (HR ~1.7-2.0) and DFS (~1.9-2.2) across models, and replaced overall margin positivity as the only parameter independently predicting local recurrence (HR ~2.4).
SURG-006.effect: Vein-wall invasion HR ~1.7-2.4 across endpoints; margin distance not independent.
SURG-006.limitations: Single centre; venous-only involvement subset; margin protocol/standardization not detailed.
SURG-006.interpretation: Observational multivariable; distinguishes two competing pathology predictors (invasion depth vs margin distance).

glosses.pancreas-neck: Series of 372 Whipple patients showing invasion of the vein wall, not margin distance, predicted recurrence and survival.
glosses.smv-portal-vein: Series of 372 Whipple patients showing invasion of the vein wall, not margin distance, predicted recurrence and survival.
glosses.vessel-contact: A 372-patient series in which invasion of the vein wall, not the distance to the vein margin, predicted survival and local recurrence.
glosses.pathology-report: A 372-patient series in which invasion of the vein wall, not the distance to the vein margin, predicted survival and local recurrence.
glosses.vascular-resection: A series of 372 Whipples in which microscopic vein-wall invasion, not margin distance, predicted recurrence and survival.

SURG-007.citation: Groot VP, Gemenetzis G, Blair AB, Rivero-Soto RJ, Yu J, Javed AA, et al. Defining and Predicting Early Recurrence in 957 Patients With Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma. Ann Surg. 2019;269(6):1154-1162.
SURG-007.design: Retrospective cohort; minimum-P-value cutoff for recurrence-free survival; logistic regression for predictors.
SURG-007.population: 957 resected PDAC (2000-2013, Johns Hopkins), neoadjuvant excluded.
SURG-007.n: 957 (753 with recurrence analyzed; 204 (21.3%) recurrence-free at last follow-up).
SURG-007.finding: Optimal early/late cutoff = 12 mo (p<0.001); early 51.5%, late 48.5%. Post-recurrence survival worse for early (1-yr 20%, 2-yr 6%) vs late (45%, 22%). Preop predictors: CA19-9>210 U/mL (OR 2.30), CT size>3 cm (OR 1.53), Charlson age-comorbidity>=4 (OR 1.65). Postop predictors: poor differentiation (OR 1.66), lymphovascular invasion (OR 1.70), lymph-node ratio>0.2 (OR 2.49), CA19-9>37 (OR 3.38). Adjuvant chemo (OR 0.28) / chemoradiation (OR 0.29) protective.
SURG-007.effect: CA19-9 and nodal burden are the strongest early-recurrence predictors (OR 2.3-3.4).
SURG-007.limitations: Single centre; no neoadjuvant patients; CA19-9 confounded by biliary obstruction/Lewis status.
SURG-007.interpretation: Large observational cohort; identifies predictors (association), not mechanism.

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: A 957-patient resected series defining early recurrence as within 12 months and identifying its preoperative and pathological predictors.
glosses.why-plans-change: A 957-patient resected series identifying lymph-node ratio, CA 19-9 and differentiation as predictors of early recurrence.
glosses.microscopic-disease: A 957-patient resected series defining early recurrence and its predictors.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: A 957-patient resected series defining early recurrence as within 12 months and identifying its predictors.
glosses.liver: Johns Hopkins study of 957 resected patients defining early recurrence and its predictors, including a high lymph node ratio.
glosses.lymph-nodes: Johns Hopkins study of 957 resected patients defining early recurrence and its predictors, including a high lymph node ratio.
glosses.liver-niche: A 957-patient cohort defining recurrence within 12 months as early and identifying the clinical and pathological features that predict it.
glosses.ca19-9: A 957-patient series in which CA 19-9 above 210 U/mL before surgery raised the odds of recurrence within a year 2.3-fold.
glosses.pathology-report: A 957-patient series identifying lymph node ratio, poor differentiation and lymphovascular invasion as predictors of recurrence within a year.
glosses.whipple: A Johns Hopkins series of 957 resected patients in which about half of recurrences came within 12 months of surgery.

SURG-008.citation: Crippa S, Malleo G, Mazzaferro V, Langella S, Ricci C, Casciani F, et al. Futility of Up-Front Resection for Anatomically Resectable Pancreatic Cancer. JAMA Surg. 2024;159(10):1139-1147.
SURG-008.clinical_status: supports neoadjuvant selection; not yet guideline-mandated for resectable disease (US)
SURG-008.design: Retrospective multi-institutional cohort; derivation (885) + validation (541); futility risk model (MetroPancreas).
SURG-008.population: 1426 patients, up-front pancreatectomy for anatomically resectable PDAC, 5 high-volume Italian centres (2010-2021).
SURG-008.finding: Futile pancreatectomy (death or recurrence <=6 mo) = 18.9% (dev 19.2%, val 18.6%). Independent preop predictors: ASA class, CA19-9, tumour size. Four CA19-9-adjusted-to-size criteria keep futility <20% (e.g., <2 cm with CA19-9<1000; <3 cm with <500; <4 cm with <150; <5 cm with <50 U/mL). DFS and OS significantly longer in patients meeting criteria.
SURG-008.effect: ~1 in 5 'curative' resections for resectable PDAC is futile at 6 months.
SURG-008.limitations: Retrospective; European high-volume centres; model not yet prospectively validated.
SURG-008.interpretation: Large multi-institutional observational; supports selection by biology over anatomy; model needs prospective validation.

glosses.resectability-categories: A 1,426-patient study finding that about one in five up-front operations for resectable cancer is futile and that CA 19-9 adjusted for size predicts futility.
glosses.ca19-9: A European series in which about one in five up-front resections was futile, predicted by CA 19-9 read against tumor size.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: In 1,426 upfront operations for anatomically resectable tumors at five Italian centers, 18.9% were futile, meaning death or recurrence within six months.
glosses.whipple: A study of 1,426 up-front resections for resectable pancreatic cancer in which 18.9% ended in death or recurrence within six months.
glosses.total-pancreatectomy: A study of 1,426 up-front resections in which 18.9% ended in death or recurrence within six months despite clear-looking anatomy.
glosses.vascular-resection: A study of 1,426 up-front resections in which 18.9% ended in death or recurrence within six months despite clear-looking anatomy.

SURG-009.citation: Haeno H, Gonen M, Davis MB, Herman JM, Iacobuzio-Donahue CA, Michor F. Computational modeling of pancreatic cancer reveals kinetics of metastasis suggesting optimum treatment strategies. Cell. 2012;148(1-2):362-75.
SURG-009.design: Mathematical/branching-process modeling of growth and dissemination; validated in independent database.
SURG-009.population: 228 patients (101 with autopsy) with primary + metastatic burden data.
SURG-009.finding: Pancreatic cancer growth initially exponential; model infers patients likely already harbor metastases at diagnosis; predicts number/size distribution of metastases and survival. Therapies reducing cell growth rate early appear superior to up-front resection.
SURG-009.effect: Predicted near-universal subclinical metastatic burden at diagnosis.
SURG-009.limitations: In silico; parameter uncertainty; treatment predictions untested prospectively.
SURG-009.interpretation: Model-based inference anchored to human autopsy data; hypothesis-generating, not experimental proof.

glosses.stage-vs-resectability: A mathematical model fitted to 228 patients inferring that most harbor subclinical metastases at diagnosis.
glosses.why-chemo-first: A mathematical model fitted to 228 patients inferring that most harbor subclinical metastases at diagnosis.
glosses.microscopic-disease: A mathematical model fitted to 228 patients inferring that most harbor subclinical metastases at diagnosis.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: A mathematical model fitted to 228 patients inferring that most harbor subclinical metastases at diagnosis.
glosses.staging-laparoscopy: A mathematical model anchored to autopsy data predicting that most patients already carry microscopic metastases at diagnosis.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: A mathematical model fitted to 228 patients inferred that most people already harbor microscopic metastases at diagnosis, favoring early systemic treatment.
glosses.whipple: A mathematical model of pancreatic cancer growth inferring that most patients already harbor metastases at diagnosis.

SURG-010.citation: Costa-Silva B, Aiello NM, Ocean AJ, Singh S, Zhang H, Thakur BK, et al. Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver. Nat Cell Biol. 2015;17(6):816-26.
SURG-010.design: Exosome education experiments + mechanistic blockade (MIF knockdown/blockade) + patient exosome proteomics/correlation.
SURG-010.population: Naive mice injected with PDAC-derived exosomes; human PDAC patient exosomes (incl. stage I).
SURG-010.n: Mouse cohorts; human exosome samples (stage I progressors vs non-progressors).
SURG-010.finding: PDAC exosomes taken up by Kupffer cells -> TGF-beta secretion -> hepatic stellate cell fibronectin -> recruitment of bone-marrow-derived macrophages = liver pre-metastatic niche, increasing metastatic burden. MIF highly expressed in PDAC exosomes; MIF blockade prevented niche formation and metastasis. Exosomal MIF markedly higher in stage I patients who later developed liver metastasis vs non-progressors.
SURG-010.effect: MIF blockade -> prevented niche and reduced liver metastasis (categorical).
SURG-010.limitations: Mouse mechanism; patient data observational; MIF not yet a validated clinical biomarker/target.
SURG-010.interpretation: Perturbation (MIF blockade) + rescue/prevention supports causal niche mechanism in mice; human correlation adds translational weight.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A mouse study showing tumor-derived exosomes prepare the liver to receive metastases.
glosses.liver: Mouse study showing tumor exosomes carrying the protein MIF prepare a pre-metastatic niche in the liver.
glosses.liver-niche: A mouse and human study showing pancreatic cancer exosomes carrying MIF prime the liver through Kupffer cells, with blockade preventing metastasis.
glosses.liver-lesions: A mouse study in which pancreatic cancer vesicles prepared a fibrotic, macrophage-rich niche in the liver before metastases arrived.

SURG-011.citation: Zheng X, Carstens JL, Kim J, Scheible M, Kaye J, Sugimoto H, et al. Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition is dispensable for metastasis but induces chemoresistance in pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2015;527(7579):525-530.
SURG-011.design: Genetic loss-of-function (Snai1cKO, Twist1cKO) in autochthonous PDAC; CTC quantification; metastasis + gemcitabine response.
SURG-011.population: KPC (Pdx1-Cre;Kras G12D;p53 R172H) mice with conditional Snai1 or Twist1 deletion; lineage traced.
SURG-011.n: Mouse cohorts (KPC vs KPC;TwistcKO vs KPC;SnailcKO).
SURG-011.finding: Snai1/Twist1 deletion did NOT delay tumorigenesis, alter histology, change YFP+ CTC numbers or circulating KrasG12D mRNA, or reduce liver/lung/spleen metastasis. EMT suppression increased proliferation and upregulated nucleoside transporters ENT1/CNT3 -> increased gemcitabine sensitivity (i.e., EMT drives chemoresistance).
SURG-011.effect: No change in dissemination/metastasis; EMT suppression -> enhanced gemcitabine response.
SURG-011.limitations: Tests only two EMT-TFs; later work shows alternative (non-transcriptional) EMT programs.
SURG-011.interpretation: Genetic perturbation directly tests necessity of specific EMT-TFs for metastasis.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A mouse study showing the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition is not required for metastasis but drives chemotherapy resistance.

SURG-012.citation: Pommier A, Anaparthy N, Memos N, Kelley ZL, Gouronnec A, Yan R, et al. Unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress engenders immune-resistant, latent pancreatic cancer metastases. Science. 2018;360(6394):eaao4908.
SURG-012.design: DCC phenotyping (CK19/MHC-I); inducible XBP1s + T-cell depletion to trigger outgrowth.
SURG-012.population: Patient and mouse PDAC livers; engineered mouse model with intra-portal injection into pre-immunized hosts.
SURG-012.time_frame: Latency period after dissemination (dormancy to outgrowth).
SURG-012.finding: Livers from PDAC patients and mice harbor single disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) lacking CK19 and MHC-I. Immunogenic PDAC cells injected into pre-immunized mice seeded only single, non-replicating CK19-/MHC-I- DCCs with an ER-stress response but WITHOUT IRE1-alpha/XBP1s activation. Inducing XBP1s plus T-cell depletion drove outgrowth of CK19+/MHC-I+ macro-metastases. Unresolved ER stress enables immune escape and latency.
SURG-012.effect: Dormancy vs outgrowth switch controlled by XBP1s + immune pressure (categorical).
SURG-012.limitations: Model-specific induction; human data descriptive; no therapeutic reversal shown clinically.
SURG-012.interpretation: Engineered induction/rescue supports a causal dormancy mechanism in mice; human DCC detection corroborative.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A study finding single dormant, immune-invisible cancer cells in the livers of patients and mice, with outgrowth controlled by cell stress and immune pressure.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: A study finding single dormant, immune-invisible cancer cells in the livers of patients and mice, with outgrowth controlled by cell stress and immune pressure.
glosses.liver: Study finding single dormant, immune-invisible cancer cells in the livers of pancreatic cancer patients and mice.
glosses.liver-niche: A study finding single dormant cancer cells lacking CK19 and MHC class I in patient and mouse livers, with outgrowth requiring a stress switch plus loss of T cells.
glosses.staging-laparoscopy: A study finding single dormant cancer cells lacking recognition markers in the livers of patients and mice.
glosses.ctdna: A study finding single dormant cancer cells lacking recognition markers in the livers of patients and mice.
glosses.liver-lesions: A study finding single dormant cancer cells lacking recognition markers in the livers of patients and mice.

SURG-013.citation: Campbell PJ, Yachida S, Mudie LJ, Stephens PJ, Pleasance ED, Stebbings LA, et al. The patterns and dynamics of genomic instability in metastatic pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2010;467(7319):1109-13.
SURG-013.design: Paired-end sequencing of genomic rearrangements; clonal phylogeny across metastatic sites.
SURG-013.population: 13 patients with PDAC; primary + multiple metastases; genomic rearrangement mapping.
SURG-013.time_frame: Across tumour lifetime (early instability -> late parallel evolution).
SURG-013.finding: Rearrangements indicating telomere dysfunction and dysregulated G1-S (intact G2-M) initiate oncogene amplification predominantly EARLY. Genomic instability persists after dissemination -> ongoing parallel and convergent evolution among metastases; genetic heterogeneity among metastasis-initiating cells; seeding may require driver mutations BEYOND those for the primary; phylogenetic trees show organ-specific branches.
SURG-013.effect: Metastasis-initiating clones genetically distinct and organ-branched.
SURG-013.interpretation: Human genomic phylogeny; correlational for mechanism, strong for clonal ordering.

glosses.recurrence-meaning: An autopsy genomics study showing metastasis-initiating clones are genetically distinct and keep evolving separately in each organ.
glosses.liver-niche: A 13-patient sequencing study showing continuing genomic change after dissemination and organ-specific branches in the tumor's family tree.
glosses.genome-evolution: Rearrangement analysis of 13 metastatic cases showing genomic instability continues after spread with organ-specific evolution.

SURG-014.citation: Jones RP, Psarelli EE, Jackson R, Ghaneh P, Halloran CM, Palmer DH, et al. Patterns of Recurrence After Resection of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Secondary Analysis of the ESPAC-4 Randomized Adjuvant Chemotherapy Trial. JAMA Surg. 2019;154(11):1038-1048.
SURG-014.design: Prospective secondary analysis of a multicentre RCT; recurrence site + survival.
SURG-014.population: 730 resected PDAC patients with adjuvant chemotherapy (ESPAC-4 phase 3).
SURG-014.finding: Recurrence in 479 (65.6%); 78 (10.7%) died without recurrence. Local recurrence median 11.63 mo vs distant 9.49 mo (distant earlier; HR 1.21, p=.04). Post-recurrence survival similar: local 9.36 vs distant 8.94 mo (HR 0.89, p=.27). OS from surgery 27.9 (gem) vs 30.2 mo (gem+cap) (HR 0.81). Gem+cap reduced local recurrence. Conclusion: PDAC behaves as systemic disease irrespective of recurrence site.
SURG-014.effect: Recurrence site does not change post-recurrence survival (HR 0.89, NS).
SURG-014.limitations: Secondary analysis; recurrence detection per protocol, not autopsy.
SURG-014.interpretation: RCT-derived cohort with standardized adjuvant therapy; strong for pattern description.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A secondary analysis of the ESPAC-4 trial showing recurrence in 66% of resected patients, with distant recurrence appearing earlier than local.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: A secondary analysis of the ESPAC-4 trial showing recurrence in 66% of resected patients with similar survival after local or distant recurrence.
glosses.peritoneum: Secondary analysis of a randomized adjuvant trial showing survival after recurrence was similar whether the first site was local or distant.
glosses.fluorouracil-leucovorin: Secondary analysis of ESPAC-4 showing gemcitabine plus capecitabine reduced local recurrence and that recurrence site did not change survival after recurrence.
glosses.distal-pancreatectomy: A secondary analysis of the ESPAC-4 trial showing that recurrence after resection is usually distant and behaves as systemic disease.

SURG-015.citation: D'Souza M, Andree M, Feili A, Sadr-Azodi O, Ghorbani P, Sparrelid E, et al. Pulmonary Metastases After Surgical Resection of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Impact on Long-Term Survival and Perspectives on Targeted Treatments. Ann Surg Oncol. 2026;33(8):7112-7122.
SURG-015.clinical_status: supports selected pulmonary metastasectomy (US practice, case-selected)
SURG-015.design: Retrospective cohort; flexible parametric + Kaplan-Meier survival by recurrence pattern within 3 yr.
SURG-015.finding: Recurrence sites: liver 145 (49%), lung 61 (21%), other 87 (30%). Median OS: liver 13 mo (95%CI 12-16), lung 30 mo (27-35), other 20 mo (19-26) (p<=0.001). Recurrence-specific mortality vs no recurrence: lung 7x, other 12x, liver 23x -> clear prognostic hierarchy; pulmonary metastases favorable even when combined with other distant spread.
SURG-015.effect: Lung recurrence OS ~2.3x longer than liver (30 vs 13 mo).
SURG-015.limitations: Single centre; site assignment by imaging; no autopsy confirmation.
SURG-015.interpretation: Observational; establishes organ-specific prognosis (association), raising a mechanistic/biology question.

glosses.recurrence-meaning: A Swedish series of 343 resected patients showing median survival of 30 months after lung recurrence against 13 months after liver recurrence.
glosses.liver: Karolinska series of 343 resected patients showing liver recurrence was the commonest site and carried the shortest survival.
glosses.peritoneum: Karolinska series of 343 resected patients showing liver recurrence was the commonest site and carried the shortest survival.
glosses.liver-niche: A 343-patient resected cohort in which median survival after recurrence was 13 months for liver, 30 for isolated lung and 20 for other sites.
glosses.mri: A resected cohort in which the liver was the first site of recurrence in 49% and carried the shortest survival.
glosses.liver-lesions: A resected cohort in which the liver was the first site of recurrence in 49% and carried a median survival of 13 months.

SURG-016.citation: Theijse RT, Stoop TF, Hendriks TE, Suurmeijer JA, Smits FJ, Bonsing BA, et al. Nationwide Outcome after Pancreatoduodenectomy in Patients at Very High Risk (ISGPS-D) for Postoperative Pancreatic Fistula. Ann Surg. 2023;281(2):322-328.
SURG-016.population: 1402 patients undergoing ISGPS-D pancreatoduodenectomy (soft gland + duct <=3 mm); Dutch Pancreatic Cancer Audit 2014-2021.
SURG-016.finding: In-hospital mortality 4.1% (57; falling to 3.7% most recent 2 yr). Major morbidity (Clavien-Dindo >=IIIa) 45.9%; clinically relevant POPF (ISGPS grade B/C) 30.0%; failure-to-rescue 8.9%. POPF patients had much higher major morbidity (88.0% vs 28.3%, p<0.001) and mortality (6.3% vs 3.5%, p=0.016). Prophylactic total pancreatectomy to avoid POPF performed in only 4/190 TPs (2.1%).
SURG-016.effect: POPF triples-to-quadruples major morbidity; ~4% mortality even in worst-risk glands.
SURG-016.limitations: Dutch system (high-volume, centralized); may not generalize to low-volume settings.
SURG-016.interpretation: Population-level observational; defines real-world complication burden and definitions.

glosses.life-after-whipple: A Dutch nationwide series of Whipple operations in the highest-risk glands found major complications in 46%, fistula in 30% and mortality around 4%.
glosses.pancreas-head: Dutch national audit of 1,402 high-risk Whipple operations showing 30% clinically relevant pancreatic fistula and 4% in-hospital mortality.
glosses.pancreas-neck: Dutch national audit of 1,402 high-risk Whipple operations showing 30% clinically relevant pancreatic fistula and 4% in-hospital mortality.
glosses.pancreatic-duct: Dutch national audit of 1,402 high-risk Whipple operations showing 30% clinically relevant pancreatic fistula and 4% in-hospital mortality.
glosses.whipple: A Dutch nationwide series of 1,402 Whipple operations in the highest-risk glands: fistula 30%, major complications 46%, in-hospital mortality 4.1%.
glosses.distal-pancreatectomy: A Dutch nationwide Whipple series providing the only nationwide complication rates among the sources gathered for this atlas, which do not cover distal resection.
glosses.total-pancreatectomy: A Dutch nationwide Whipple audit that also records how rarely total pancreatectomy is done just to avoid a fistula (2.1%).
glosses.surgical-complications: A Dutch nationwide series of 1,402 Whipples in the highest-risk glands: fistula 30%, major complications 46%, mortality 4.1%, failure to rescue 8.9%.

SURG-017.citation: Zhang J, Ren L, Jager C, Dogruoz A, Friess H, Demir IE, et al. Prognostic implications of superior mesenteric vein/portal vein resection and histologic venous invasion in borderline resectable or locally advanced PDAC after neoadjuvant therapy. Langenbecks Arch Surg. 2026;411(1).
SURG-017.clinical_status: venous resection standard in experienced centres when it achieves R0 (US/intl)
SURG-017.design: Retrospective cohort; resection vs venous preservation; subgroup by histologic venous invasion; Cox regression.
