RAS-018.finding: All patients experienced adverse events. Three monotherapy patients developed interstitial lung disease during the first treatment cycle leading to death, considered drug-related by the investigator. In the monotherapy group, 1 patient (1.8%) had a partial response and 12 patients (21.8%) had stable disease. In the combination group there were no objective responses and 4 patients (33.3%) had stable disease, across different KRAS alleles. The maximum tolerated dose was 800 mg for monotherapy (NCT04111458) and 100 mg BI 1701963 / 1 mg trametinib for the combination. The authors conclude that BI 1701963 demonstrated limited efficacy as monotherapy.
RAS-018.effect: Monotherapy ORR 1.8% (1/55 evaluable); combination ORR 0%; 3 fatal drug-related interstitial lung disease events
RAS-018.limitations: No randomisation; pancreatic subgroup of 13 and 6 patients; efficacy secondary and not centrally reviewed; pooling across three trials in different regions.
RAS-018.interpretation: First-in-human dose-finding with efficacy as a secondary endpoint: sufficient to exclude a large single-agent effect and to show that the tolerated combination dose of trametinib (1 mg) is far below its own active dose, i.e. a pharmacological ceiling rather than a biology failure.

glosses.clinical-trials: A phase 1 program of a SOS1 inhibitor with almost no responses and fatal lung toxicity.
glosses.ras-resistance: Phase 1 trials of a SOS1 inhibitor alone and with trametinib, with a 1.8% response rate alone, none in combination, and three fatal drug-related lung injuries.
glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: Phase 1 trials of a SOS1 inhibitor alone and with trametinib, with almost no responses and three fatal drug-related lung injuries.

RAS-019.citation: Tapia Contreras C, Falke JD, Seifert DM, Schneider C, Krauss L, Fang X, et al. KRAS(G12C)-inhibitor-based combination therapies for pancreatic cancer: insights from drug screening. Mol Oncol. 2025;19(2):295-310.
RAS-019.clinical_status: Preclinical; the two nominated classes (SOS1, SHP2) have since failed to show clinical activity in KRAS-mutant PDAC in phase I. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-019.design: Unbiased drug-combination screening with a KRAS G12C inhibitor backbone, followed by validation of top hits in the patient-derived organoid
RAS-019.population: KRAS G12C-mutant pancreatic cancer cell lines and a newly established KRAS G12C-mutant patient-derived organoid model
RAS-019.n: Screening library across KRAS G12C PDAC cell models; one novel KRAS G12C patient-derived organoid for validation
RAS-019.time_frame: In vitro viability assays over days
RAS-019.finding: Screening revealed synergistic effects with SOS1 inhibitors, PTPN11/SHP2 inhibitors and broad-spectrum multi-kinase inhibitors. The hits identified in the screen were confirmed in a novel and unique KRAS G12C-mutated patient-derived organoid model. The authors frame these as strategies to enhance KRAS G12C inhibitor efficacy and to guide clinical trial design and molecular tumour board decisions.
RAS-019.effect: Synergy (not quantified as a single index in the accessed abstract/text) for SOS1, SHP2 and multi-kinase inhibitor classes
RAS-019.limitations: No in vivo arm; KRAS G12C is a rare PDAC allele so the models are atypical of the disease; quantitative synergy metrics not extracted from the accessed text.
RAS-019.interpretation: Unbiased screening reduces the risk of confirmation bias in combination selection; organoid validation adds patient-derived material but remains an in vitro inference.

RAS-020.citation: Ko AH, Bekaii-Saab T, Van Ziffle J, Mirzoeva OM, Joseph NM, Talasaz A, et al. A Multicenter, Open-Label Phase II Clinical Trial of Combined MEK plus EGFR Inhibition for Chemotherapy-Refractory Advanced Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma. Clin Cancer Res. 2016;22(1):61-68.
RAS-020.clinical_status: Negative phase II; neither selumetinib nor the combination is approved for pancreatic cancer. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-020.design: Single-arm multicentre phase II trial with a minimax design; primary endpoint overall survival (median and 24-week survival proportion); correlative immunohistochemistry and next-generation digital cell-free DNA sequencing
RAS-020.population: Adults with inoperable (locally advanced or metastatic) histologically confirmed PDAC after exactly one prior line of systemic therapy; two US academic centres
RAS-020.n: 46 evaluable patients (design required 46 for 80% power to detect a 24-week survival rate >=51%); 34 with elevated baseline CA19-9
RAS-020.time_frame: Median 2 treatment cycles (6 weeks); survival follow-up
RAS-020.finding: Patients received a median of 2 cycles (range 1-7). No objective responses were observed. Nineteen patients (41%) had stable disease for >=6 weeks and 13/34 (38%) had a CA19-9 decline >=50%. Median progression-free survival was 1.9 months (95% CI 1.4-3.3) and median overall survival 7.3 months (95% CI 5.2-8.0). Common adverse events were rash, diarrhoea and nausea/vomiting. Patients whose tumours showed an epithelial phenotype (high E-cadherin expression by immunohistochemistry) were more likely to be sensitive to study treatment. Tumour-derived DNA was detectable in plasma in the majority of patients by next-generation digital sequencing.
RAS-020.effect: Objective response rate 0/46; median PFS 1.9 months; median OS 7.3 months
RAS-020.limitations: n=46, no control arm; biomarker analyses exploratory and unadjusted; second-line population heterogeneous.
RAS-020.interpretation: Prospective hypothesis test with a prespecified survival threshold: excludes clinically meaningful activity for this specific vertical/horizontal combination, and the E-cadherin association generates (not tests) a cell-state hypothesis.

glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: A single-arm phase 2 trial of MEK plus EGFR inhibition in 46 patients after one prior line, with no tumor responses.

RAS-021.citation: Pant S, Wainberg ZA, Weekes CD, Furqan M, Kasi PM, Devoe CE, et al. Lymph-node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic and colorectal cancer: the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. Nat Med. 2024;30(2):531-542.
RAS-021.clinical_status: Investigational. The successor randomised study AMPLIFY-7P (ELI-002 7P, NCT05726864, phase 1/2, n=158) is listed ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING with no posted results (registry checked 2026-10-08). No KRAS vaccine is approved in the US.
RAS-021.design: Phase 1 multi-cohort dose-escalation study: fixed-dose amphiphile-modified mutant KRAS peptides (G12D and G12R) with ascending-dose amphiphile CpG-7909 adjuvant; primary endpoints safety and recommended phase 2 dose; secondary endpoint tumour biomarker response; exploratory immunogenicity and…
RAS-021.population: 25 patients (20 pancreatic, 5 colorectal) positive for minimal residual disease by ctDNA and/or serum tumour antigen after definitive locoregional treatment, at high risk of radiographic relapse
RAS-021.n: 25 patients across 5 dose cohorts (0.1, 0.5, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0 mg of Amph-CpG-7909; n=3, 6, 5, 5, 6)
RAS-021.time_frame: Phase 1 with follow-up ongoing at publication; trial listed as COMPLETED on ClinicalTrials.gov (registry checked 2026-10-08)
RAS-021.finding: No dose-limiting toxicities occurred and the recommended phase 2 dose was 10.0 mg of Amph-CpG-7909. Direct ex vivo mutant-KRAS-specific T-cell responses were seen in 21/25 patients (84%), with 59% having both CD4+ and CD8+ responses. Tumour biomarker responses occurred in 21/25 (84%) and biomarker clearance in 6/25 (24%; 3 pancreatic and 3 colorectal). Median relapse-free survival was 16.33 months. Comparing patients above versus below the median fold increase in T cells over baseline (12.75-fold): median tumour biomarker reduction was -76.0% versus -10.2% (P<0.0014) and median relapse-free survival was not reached versus 4.01 months (hazard ratio 0.14, P=0.0167). The rationale cites loss of class I HLA expression in 43% of KRAS-mutated pancreatic metastases versus 6% of primary tumours.
RAS-021.effect: 84% T-cell response rate; 24% biomarker clearance; RFS not reached versus 4.01 months by T-cell response (HR 0.14, P=0.0167)
RAS-021.limitations: Phase 1, no control arm, n=25 with only 20 pancreatic patients; immunogenicity assays are the primary positive readout; relapse-free survival exploratory.
RAS-021.interpretation: Dose-escalation study with within-patient biomarker change and an immunological exposure-response relationship: supports immunogenicity and an association between immune magnitude and biomarker/relapse outcome, but the T-cell-response split is a post hoc, non-randomised comparison.

RAS-022.citation: Choi Y, Diehl MC, Schutzman JL, Nutescu Chiroiu CP, Zhang X, Pant S, et al. Circulating Tumor DNA Dynamics Reveal KRAS G12C Mutation Heterogeneity and Response to Treatment with the KRAS G12C Inhibitor Divarasib in Solid Tumors. Clin Cancer Res. 2024;30(17):3788-3797.
RAS-022.clinical_status: Divarasib remains investigational (not FDA-approved) as of 2026-10-08; this analysis bears on companion-diagnostic strategy for KRAS-directed therapy generally.
RAS-022.design: Prespecified exploratory serial ctDNA profiling (PredicineWES+ at baseline; PredicineBEACON tumour-informed MRD assay on treatment) within a phase 1 dose-escalation/expansion trial; limit of detection 0.05%
RAS-022.population: 134 patients with KRAS G12C-mutant advanced/metastatic solid tumours treated with single-agent divarasib in a phase 1 study: 59 NSCLC, 54 colorectal, 21 other solid tumours
RAS-022.n: 134 evaluable baseline plasma samples; 95 patients with >=1 on-treatment sample (74 with both cycle 1 day 15 and cycle 3 day 1)
RAS-022.time_frame: Baseline (cycle 1 day 1), cycle 1 day 15 and cycle 3 day 1
RAS-022.finding: Trial eligibility had been established by local tissue testing in 106/137 (77.4%) patients, by local or central blood testing in 26 (19.0%) and by a local test of unknown type in 5 (3.6%). At cycle 1 day 1, the KRAS G12C mutation was detected in plasma in 72.9% (43/59) of NSCLC patients, 92.6% (50/54) of colorectal cancer patients and 81.0% (17/21) of patients with other solid tumours (median ctDNA tumour fraction 3.7% in the latter group). Baseline ctDNA tumour fraction tended to be higher where KRAS G12C was plasma-detectable than where it was not (P=0.08, 0.08 and 0.05 for NSCLC, colorectal and other solid tumours; Fig 2B). Early on-treatment ctDNA dynamics were associated with patient outcomes and tumour response.
RAS-022.effect: Plasma false-negative rate for a tissue-confirmed targetable allele: 27.1% in NSCLC, 7.4% in colorectal, 19.0% in other solid tumours
RAS-022.limitations: Exploratory; pancreatic cancer is pooled into 'other solid tumours' (n=21) with no separate figure; one assay platform; no comparison with same-timepoint tissue re-biopsy.
RAS-022.interpretation: Within-patient paired tissue-versus-plasma comparison in a population where the allele is known to be present: gives a direct, interpretable false-negative rate for blood-based allele assignment, which is a measurement-validity inference rather than a causal one.

glosses.kras-alleles-wildtype: A trial analysis in which blood testing found a tissue-confirmed KRAS G12C mutation in only 73 to 81 percent of patients.
glosses.molecular-testing: A trial analysis in which blood testing found a tissue-confirmed KRAS G12C mutation in only 73 to 81 percent of patients.
glosses.ctdna: A serial ctDNA analysis in a KRAS G12C inhibitor trial in which plasma missed a tissue-confirmed allele in 7-27% of patients by tumor type.
glosses.ras-resistance: An analysis of blood versus tissue genotyping showing that blood testing misses a tissue-confirmed KRAS G12C mutation in a sizeable minority of patients.

RAS-023.citation: Leidner R, Sanjuan Silva N, Huang H, Sprott D, Zheng C, Shih YP, et al. Neoantigen T-Cell Receptor Gene Therapy in Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2022;386(22):2112-2119.
RAS-023.clinical_status: Investigational cell therapy; no KRAS-directed TCR product is FDA-approved. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-023.design: Single-patient (N-of-1) adoptive cell therapy report with RECIST imaging and longitudinal peripheral-blood persistence measurement
RAS-023.population: One patient with progressive metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma whose tumour expressed KRAS G12D and who carried HLA-C*08:02
RAS-023.time_frame: Response ongoing at 6 months after a single infusion
RAS-023.finding: The patient had regression of visceral metastases with an overall partial response of 72% by RECIST version 1.1, ongoing at 6 months. The engineered T cells constituted more than 2% of all circulating peripheral-blood T cells 6 months after the cell transfer.
RAS-023.effect: 72% partial response; >2% engineered T cells in circulation at 6 months
RAS-023.limitations: n=1; restricted to patients with HLA-C*08:02 (a minority) and KRAS G12D; manufacturing-intensive; durability beyond 6 months not reported here.
RAS-023.interpretation: N-of-1 with a defined, measurable intervention and a tightly linked pharmacodynamic marker (engineered T-cell persistence): strong within-patient temporal inference, no population inference.

RAS-024.citation: McAndrews KM, Mahadevan KK, Sugimoto H, Kirtley ML, Yang S, Kim J, et al. CDK8 remodels the tumor microenvironment and promotes resistance to KRAS(G12D) inhibitors and daraxonrasib in PDAC. EMBO J. 2026;45(16):5727-5758.
RAS-024.clinical_status: Preclinical. No CDK8 inhibitor and no KRAS-inhibitor-plus-checkpoint regimen is approved for PDAC in the US. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-024.design: Longitudinal profiling of the tumour microenvironment under short- versus long-term KRAS G12D inhibition, with genetic/pharmacological CDK8 targeting and CTLA-4 blockade as intervention arms; mechanistic dissection of CXCL2 and FAS
RAS-024.population: Immunocompetent mouse PDAC models treated long-term with KRAS G12D inhibition; patient-derived xenograft tumours rendered resistant to daraxonrasib (RAS(ON) multi-selective) and zoldonrasib (RAS G12D(ON)-selective)
RAS-024.n: Multiple mouse PDAC model cohorts plus PDX tumours resistant to daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib (exact per-arm n not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-024.time_frame: Short-term (days) versus long-term (weeks) KRAS inhibition to resistance
RAS-024.finding: KRAS G12D inhibition by MRTX1133 initially increased CD11c+ cells and T-cell infiltration proximal to cancer cells, but long-term treatment reversed these immune responses, leading to resistance promoted by the Mediator-complex-associated kinase CDK8. CDK8 conferred resistance via induction of CXCL2 chemokine secretion, inhibition of FAS expression, and remodelling of the tumour microenvironment to promote immune evasion. Targeting CDK8 alone or in combination with anti-CTLA-4 immunotherapy overcame resistance to KRAS G12D inhibition. CDK8 was also upregulated in patient-derived xenograft tumours resistant to daraxonrasib and to zoldonrasib, identifying a shared microenvironmental resistance node across RAS(ON)- and RAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitors. The authors' synopsis states that priming with oncogenic KRAS inhibitors followed by combination with checkpoint immunotherapy…
RAS-024.effect: Reversal of early immune activation with long-term dosing; resistance overcome by CDK8 targeting with or without anti-CTLA-4 (quantitative effect sizes not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-024.limitations: Mouse models; exact group sizes and effect magnitudes not extracted; no human data on CDK8 in KRAS-inhibitor-treated PDAC; CDK8 inhibitors are early-stage clinically.
RAS-024.interpretation: Time-resolved perturbation with a rescue arm in immunocompetent hosts: supports a causal, reversible microenvironmental mechanism rather than a cell-intrinsic genetic one, and the cross-drug PDX finding argues the node is not inhibitor-specific.

glosses.kras-g12d-inhibitors: A mouse study showing that long-term G12D inhibition reverses the early immune activation through CDK8, and that blocking CDK8 or adding anti-CTLA-4 prevents the reversal.
glosses.ras-resistance: A mouse and xenograft study showing that the immune response to KRAS blockade is reversed over weeks through the kinase CDK8, and that blocking CDK8 restores control.

RAS-025.citation: Bulle A, Chen Y, Li H, Chen TH, Khawar IA, Li L, et al. Prolonged KRAS-MAPK Inhibition Induces Interferon Signaling That Promotes Cell State Transition and Confers Therapeutic Vulnerability in Pancreatic Cancer. Cancer Res. 2026;86(13):3270-3286.
RAS-025.clinical_status: Preclinical. Sacituzumab govitecan has no US pancreatic indication; no KRAS-inhibitor-plus-ADC regimen is approved. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-025.design: Mechanistic perturbation study: transcriptional network analysis of sustained pathway inhibition, loss/gain-of-function on the nominated regulator, pathway reconstruction (IRF1/IRF9, TRIM22, IkBalpha, NF-kB), then a targeted combination test in vivo
RAS-025.population: Human PDAC cell models under sustained KRAS-MAPK inhibition; xenograft models for the combination test
RAS-025.n: Multiple PDAC cell models and xenograft cohorts (per-arm n not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-025.time_frame: Prolonged (weeks) pathway inhibition in vitro; xenograft treatment courses
RAS-025.finding: Sustained KRAS-MAPK inhibition induced interferon and NF-kB signalling and promoted a cell-state change mimicking an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition state associated with drug resistance. Network analysis identified the interferon-inducible E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM22 as a central regulator. Mechanistically, TRIM22 promoted proteasomal degradation of IkBalpha, producing sustained NF-kB and EMT programme activation coinciding with a basal-like transcriptional cell state. TRIM22 expression was driven by IRF1 and IRF9 following relief of ERK-mediated transcriptional repression during pathway inhibition. EMT induction was accompanied by marked upregulation of TROP2 (TACSTD2), an NF-kB target gene enriched in basal-like PDAC cell states. Combining the TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate sacituzumab govitecan with KRAS or ERK inhibitors significantly suppressed PDAC tumour growth in…
RAS-025.effect: Significant xenograft growth suppression with sacituzumab govitecan plus KRAS or ERK inhibition versus single agents (magnitude not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-025.limitations: No autochthonous or immunocompetent model; human tissue validation under KRAS inhibitor therapy not shown in the accessed text; sacituzumab govitecan is not approved for PDAC.
RAS-025.interpretation: Mechanistic chain with each link perturbed (ERK repression relieved to IRF to TRIM22 to IkBalpha to NF-kB to TROP2) and a downstream therapeutic test: supports a drug-induced, reversible cell-state route to resistance distinct from mutation.

glosses.ras-resistance: Laboratory work showing that prolonged pathway blockade pushes pancreatic cells into a mesenchymal state displaying TROP2, which an existing antibody-drug conjugate attacked in mice.

RAS-026.citation: Chen Y, Hu Y, Liu S, Wang X, Huang C, Zheng L, et al. Targeting WFS1 overcomes KRAS(G12D) dependency and adaptive resistance to KRAS inhibition in pancreatic cancer. NPJ Precis Oncol. 2026;10(1).
RAS-026.clinical_status: Preclinical; no WFS1-directed agent exists clinically. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-026.design: Target-identification and perturbation study: expression profiling after KRAS G12D activation and after acquired MRTX1133 resistance, WFS1 loss-of-function with sensitivity restoration, and mechanistic work on unfolded-protein-response activation and Smurf1-dependent WFS1 protein stability
RAS-026.population: KRAS G12D-driven pancreatic cancer cell and tumour models, including MRTX1133-resistant tumours
RAS-026.n: Multiple KRAS G12D cell and tumour models, sensitive and MRTX1133-resistant (per-arm n not extracted)
RAS-026.time_frame: Acquired resistance established over prolonged culture/dosing
RAS-026.finding: WFS1 (Wolfram syndrome 1) expression was upregulated following KRAS G12D activation and promoted tumorigenesis and metastasis. WFS1 expression was further elevated in tumours resistant to MRTX1133, and this elevation was independent of KRAS activation status. Inhibition of WFS1 partially restored sensitivity to MRTX1133 in resistant tumours by inducing excessive and sustained activation of the unfolded protein response, which triggered apoptosis. While WFS1 is regulated by the MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways in MRTX1133-sensitive cells, acquired resistance was associated with downregulation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase Smurf1, leading to increased WFS1 protein stability.
RAS-026.effect: Partial restoration of MRTX1133 sensitivity on WFS1 inhibition (magnitude not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-026.limitations: Preclinical; relies on MRTX1133, whose human trial was terminated; no patient-sample validation; quantitative effect sizes not extracted.
RAS-026.interpretation: Loss-of-function rescue in matched resistant models with a post-transcriptional mechanism (Smurf1-dependent stability): supports a resistance route that does not require RAS-MAPK reactivation, which discriminates between the 'always pathway reactivation' and 'multiple independent routes' models.

RAS-027.citation: Ge X, Singh J, Li W, Markham CS, Ruiz CF, Stites EC, et al. PI3K Regulates Wild-type RAS Signaling to Confer Resistance to KRAS Inhibition. Cancer Res. 2026;86(15):3819-3837.
RAS-027.clinical_status: Preclinical; no PI3K-inhibitor-plus-KRAS-inhibitor regimen is approved. Relevant to the observation that daraxonrasib's label and trial included RAS wild-type patients. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-027.design: Mechanistic study combining proximity-labelling proteomics, CRISPR screening, live-cell imaging (ERK-KTR reporter), immunoprecipitation and functional viability assays, with pharmacological PI3K inhibition as the intervention
RAS-027.population: Human PDAC cell models, including KRAS-knockout lines and cells carrying clinically identified PIK3CA mutations (E542K, E545K, G118D context)
RAS-027.n: Multiple PDAC cell lines including isogenic KRAS-knockout derivatives (per-arm n not extracted)
RAS-027.time_frame: Acute signalling (30 minutes for drug treatments before lysis) to multi-day viability
RAS-027.finding: PI3K activity broadly governed RAS-MAPK signalling in both basal and KRAS-inhibited states: PI3K activation enhanced wild-type - but not mutant - RAS activity and MAPK phosphorylation, while PI3K inhibition reduced them. Proximity labelling, CRISPR screening, live-cell imaging and functional assays showed that PI3K, through its catalytic lipid-kinase function, orchestrates phosphoinositide-mediated recruitment of the scaffold protein GAB1 to the plasma membrane, nucleating assembly of RAS signalling complexes that activate MAPK in an EGFR/SHP2/SOS1-dependent manner. Inhibiting PI3K enhanced sensitivity to mutant-specific KRAS inhibitors in PDAC cells, including cells with clinically identified PIK3CA mutations. The authors note that a subset of PDAC cells survive CRISPR/Cas9-mediated complete KRAS ablation.
RAS-027.effect: Enhanced sensitivity to mutant-selective KRAS inhibitors on PI3K inhibition (magnitude not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-027.limitations: In vitro only in the accessed text; no in vivo or patient validation; PI3K inhibitors have narrow therapeutic windows clinically.
RAS-027.interpretation: Multi-modal mechanism with orthogonal methods converging on one node, plus a rescue/sensitisation arm: supports a specific upstream route by which wild-type RAS sustains MAPK under allele-selective blockade.

glosses.growth-control: A cell study showing PI3K sustains wild-type RAS signaling and limits the effect of mutant-selective KRAS inhibitors.
glosses.kras: A cell study showing PI3K sustains wild-type RAS signaling and limits mutant-selective KRAS inhibition.
glosses.daraxonrasib: A preclinical study showing that PI3K-driven recruitment of GAB1 assembles signaling complexes around normal RAS that sustain growth signals during KRAS inhibition.
glosses.ras-on-inhibitors: A cell and mouse study showing that PI3K and GAB1 assemble normal RAS signaling complexes that reactivate the pathway while mutant KRAS is blocked.
glosses.ras-resistance: Laboratory work showing that PI3K activity recruits scaffolding to the membrane and reactivates the pathway through normal, non-mutant RAS while mutant KRAS is blocked.
glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: Laboratory work showing that PI3K recruits scaffolding to the membrane and reactivates the pathway through normal RAS while mutant KRAS is blocked.

RAS-028.citation: Liaki V, Rosas-Alonso R, Fernandez-Garcia F, Guerra C, Barbacid M, Drosten M, et al. A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2025;122(49):e2523039122.
RAS-028.clinical_status: Preclinical. Daraxonrasib is US-approved as monotherapy for mPDAC; no triple combination of this kind is in approved use, and no corresponding registered pancreatic trial was identified in the 2026-10-08 registry searches. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-028.design: Paired genetic and pharmacological perturbation: conditional ablation of three signalling nodes (downstream RAF1, upstream EGFR, orthogonal STAT3) versus a matched three-drug combination, with long-term follow-up for relapse
RAS-028.population: Orthotopic mouse PDAC induced by KRAS/TP53 mutations, genetically engineered mouse model (GEMM) tumours, and patient-derived xenografts
RAS-028.n: Orthotopic, GEMM and PDX cohorts (per-arm n not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-028.finding: Genetic ablation of three independent nodes involved in downstream (RAF1), upstream (EGFR) and orthogonal (STAT3) KRAS signalling led to complete and permanent regression of orthotopic PDAC induced by KRAS/TP53 mutations. The pharmacological equivalent - daraxonrasib plus afatinib plus SD36 - induced complete regression of orthotopic PDAC tumours with no evidence of tumour resistance for over 200 days after treatment. The combination also produced significant regression of genetically engineered mouse tumours and of patient-derived xenografts without tumour relapse, and was well tolerated in mice.
RAS-028.effect: Complete regression with no relapse for >200 days post-treatment in orthotopic tumours
RAS-028.limitations: Preclinical only; no human data for the triple combination; group sizes not extracted; single laboratory.
RAS-028.interpretation: Genetic ablation establishes necessity/sufficiency of the three-node combination, and the drug arm shows the same outcome is pharmacologically reachable in mice: a strong discriminating test of 'prevent rather than treat' resistance.

RAS-029.citation: Hafner P, Mayer-Wrangowski S, Schneider C, Krauss L, Falke JD, Ammer-Beck M, et al. Vertical RAS pathway inhibition in pancreatic cancer drives therapeutically exploitable mitochondrial alterations. Signal Transduct Target Ther. 2026;11(1):33.
RAS-029.clinical_status: Preclinical. The authors cite an ongoing clinical trial of vertical RAS pathway inhibition (NCT04916236). No ferroptosis-inducing combination is approved. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-029.design: Perturbation and metabolic-phenotyping study: dual SHP2 plus MEK1/2 inhibition with mitochondrial mass/function, reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation readouts, then a ferroptosis-induction combination tested in vitro and in an endogenous in vivo model
RAS-029.population: Human and murine PDAC cell lines, endogenous (autochthonous) mouse tumour models, and patient-derived organoids spanning the recognised PDAC molecular subtypes
RAS-029.n: Panels of human and murine PDAC lines, patient-derived organoids across subtypes, and an endogenous in vivo PDAC model (per-arm n not extracted)
RAS-029.time_frame: Days in vitro; weeks in vivo; resistant state assessed after prolonged exposure
RAS-029.finding: Dual SHP2/MEK1/2 inhibition induced major alterations in mitochondrial mass and function, altered reactive oxygen species homeostasis and triggered lipid peroxidase dependency; anabolic pathways, autophagy and glycolysis were also profoundly altered. Most strikingly, mitochondrial remodelling persisted into a therapy-resistant state. The resulting vulnerability to ferroptotic cell death induced by combining vertical SHP2/MEK1/2 inhibition with GPX4 inhibition was largely independent of PDAC molecular subtype and was confirmed when RAS was targeted directly. The triple combination of SHP2/MEK1/2 inhibition plus withaferin A suppressed tumour progression in an endogenous PDAC tumour model in vivo.
RAS-029.effect: Subtype-independent ferroptotic vulnerability; tumour progression suppressed in an endogenous model (magnitudes not extracted from the accessed text)
RAS-029.limitations: Preclinical; the SHP2+MEK backbone has not shown clinical activity in PDAC; no selective GPX4 inhibitor is clinically available; quantitative results not extracted.
RAS-029.interpretation: Phenotype-persistence design: because the mitochondrial state persists into resistance, targeting it is a test of whether the induced state rather than the pathway is the durable vulnerability - and the direct-RAS confirmation arm generalises beyond the SHP2/MEK combination.

glosses.ras-resistance: Laboratory work showing that blocking the pathway above and below RAS leaves pancreatic cells with remodeled mitochondria and a vulnerability to ferroptosis.

RAS-030.citation: Yamazaki S, Hondo N, Yasukawa K, Kitazawa M, Nakamura S, Yamamoto Y, et al. Targeting adaptive EGFR feedback enhances the therapeutic efficacy of RMC-6236 in cholangiocarcinoma. Exp Hematol Oncol. 2026;15(1).
RAS-030.clinical_status: Preclinical. Daraxonrasib is not approved for cholangiocarcinoma; a phase 2 trial of daraxonrasib in recurrent KRAS-mutant biliary tract cancer (NCT07793253) is listed NOT_YET_RECRUITING (registry checked 2026-10-08).
RAS-030.design: Preclinical combination study: RMC-6236 monotherapy versus combination with gemcitabine or the anti-EGFR antibody cetuximab, with signalling readouts (pERK, pEGFR) in vitro and xenograft efficacy in vivo
RAS-030.population: KRAS-mutant (G12D and G12V) cholangiocarcinoma cell lines and xenograft models; approximately 20% of cholangiocarcinomas carry KRAS mutations, mostly codon 12
RAS-030.n: KRAS G12D and G12V cholangiocarcinoma cell lines plus xenograft cohorts (per-arm n not extracted)
RAS-030.time_frame: Days in vitro; weeks in xenografts
RAS-030.finding: RMC-6236 potently inhibited proliferation of KRAS-mutant (G12D and G12V) cholangiocarcinoma cell lines at nanomolar concentrations (10-30 nM) and effectively suppressed pERK signalling. RMC-6236 treatment was accompanied by increased pEGFR expression, indicating adaptive EGFR feedback activation as a potential resistance mechanism. In vitro, combination treatments significantly enhanced growth inhibition compared with monotherapy, and the combinations were also assessed in xenograft models.
RAS-030.effect: Nanomolar (10-30 nM) antiproliferative potency; combination superior to monotherapy in vitro
RAS-030.limitations: Preclinical; single-centre; not pancreatic; no in vivo resistance-emergence time course; quantitative in vivo results not extracted.
RAS-030.interpretation: Same-drug, different-tissue replication of an adaptive feedback mechanism: supports that EGFR re-activation under RAS(ON) inhibition is a property of the drug class rather than of pancreatic tissue.

RAS-031.citation: Liu Y, Nanjo S, Murase Y, Arai S, Watanabe S, Tsuda T, et al. Amphiregulin-mediated EGFR activation drives both intrinsic and acquired resistance to KRAS G12C inhibitors in KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. Oncogene. 2026;45(31):3244-3257.
RAS-031.clinical_status: Preclinical with exploratory human tissue; no AREG-selected KRAS inhibitor combination is approved or in a registered selection-based pancreatic trial identified on 2026-10-08.
RAS-031.design: Resistance-model establishment with ligand identification (ELISA, siRNA knockdown of KRAS, EGFR and AREG), RNAscope in situ hybridisation on patient tissue, and combination testing in vivo
RAS-031.population: KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC: patient-derived xenograft and mouse models engineered or selected for intrinsic and acquired KRAS G12C inhibitor resistance, including a leptomeningeal carcinomatosis model; plus nine patient tumour samples
RAS-031.n: Multiple PDX/mouse resistance models; 9 patient tumour samples with KRAS G12C mutation
RAS-031.time_frame: Weeks of in vivo dosing; patient samples cross-sectional
RAS-031.finding: Tumour-cell-autocrine amphiregulin (AREG)-mediated EGFR phosphorylation was identified as pivotal in both intrinsic and acquired resistance to KRAS inhibitors. The same resistance mechanism was observed in central nervous system metastatic recurrence in a leptomeningeal carcinomatosis mouse model. RNAscope in situ hybridisation detected AREG mRNA in tumour tissues and may serve as a diagnostic tool for assessing AREG expression. Combining KRAS inhibitors with EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors suppressed tumour growth and overcame resistance. High AREG mRNA expression was observed in 3 of 9 tumour samples from patients harbouring the KRAS G12C mutation, including two patients who had a poor response to sotorasib and one who achieved a partial response.
RAS-031.effect: High AREG in 3/9 patient samples; 2 of those 3 had poor sotorasib response; combination overcame resistance in models
RAS-031.limitations: NSCLC not PDAC (species/tissue transfer assumption); 9 patient samples; no prospective biomarker validation; combination with EGFR TKIs has its own toxicity.
RAS-031.interpretation: Ligand-level identification with knockdown and pharmacological rescue plus a candidate tissue assay: supports a measurable, selectable mechanism, though the patient component (3/9 with a discordant case) is far too small to be predictive.

RAS-032.citation: Wolpin BM, Park W, Garrido-Laguna I, Spira A, Starodub A, Sommerhalder D, et al. Daraxonrasib in Previously Treated Advanced RAS-Mutated Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2026;394(18):1790-1802.
RAS-032.clinical_status: Supported the dose and population for RASolute 302; daraxonrasib (RASONQUE) is now FDA-approved for mPDAC. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-032.design: Phase 1-2 dose-escalation and expansion study; primary endpoint safety; pharmacokinetics and antitumour activity secondary
RAS-032.population: Patients with advanced solid tumours bearing activating RAS mutations; this report focuses on 168 patients with previously treated RAS-mutated PDAC
RAS-032.n: 168 PDAC patients dosed at <=300 mg; prespecified subgroups of 26 (RAS G12, second line, 300 mg) and 38 (RAS G12/G13/Q61)
RAS-032.time_frame: Ongoing phase 1/2 (NCT05379985, started 2022-05-31, RECRUITING, estimated enrolment 754, no posted results; registry checked 2026-10-08)
RAS-032.finding: From the published abstract: among the 168 PDAC patients receiving <=300 mg, treatment-related adverse events of any grade occurred in 96% and grade >=3 in 30%; events in >=10% included rash, diarrhoea, nausea, stomatitis/mucositis, vomiting and fatigue. In the 26 patients with RAS G12 mutations treated with second-line daraxonrasib 300 mg, objective response was 35% (95% CI 17-56), median duration of response 8.2 months (95% CI 3.8-NE), median PFS 8.5 months and median OS 13.1 months. Among the 38 patients with RAS G12, G13 or Q61 mutations, objective response was 29% (95% CI 15-46), median duration of response 8.2 months (95% CI 3.8-8.8), median PFS 8.1 months and median OS 15.6 months. (RAS-012 independently reports median PFS 8.1 months, 95% CI 5.9-10.1, and median OS 15.6 months for the 38-patient second-line RAS-mutant group.)
RAS-032.effect: ORR 35% (26 patients, RAS G12, second line, 300 mg); median DoR 8.2 months; median PFS 8.5 months; median OS 13.1 months
RAS-032.limitations: Full text not retrieved (paywalled, no PMC version, no registry results), so only abstract-level numbers are recorded and the record is marked non-counting; figure/table locations unverified.
RAS-032.interpretation: Single-arm early-phase activity estimate in small prespecified subgroups; supports feasibility and a response signal, not comparative benefit.

glosses.clinical-trials: The phase 1/2 daraxonrasib study, recorded from its abstract, with a 35% response rate in second-line RAS G12 patients.
glosses.daraxonrasib: The phase 1-2 study of daraxonrasib in 168 previously treated pancreatic patients, giving the adverse-event profile and a 35 percent response rate in the 26-patient RAS G12 second-line group, read from the abstract only.
glosses.ras-on-inhibitors: The phase 1/2 pancreatic report for daraxonrasib in 168 previously treated patients; abstract only, giving a 35 percent response rate in 26 second-line RAS G12 patients and the side-effect profile.

RAS-033.citation: O'Reilly EM, Wainberg ZA, Hendifar AE, Borad MJ, Pietrantonio F, Pant S, et al. Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2026;395(4):325-337.
RAS-033.clinical_status: Basis of FDA approval of RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) on 26 August 2026 for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after >=1 prior systemic therapy or in patients who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-033.design: Phase 3 international open-label randomised trial (1:1) with dual primary endpoints of overall survival and progression-free survival in the RAS G12 subpopulation; key secondary endpoints OS and PFS in the overall population, objective response and patient-reported quality of life
RAS-033.population: Adults with histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic PDAC, ECOG 0-1, measurable disease, previously treated, with documented RAS mutation status (mutant or wild-type); 91.8% had RAS G12 mutations
RAS-033.n: 500 patients randomised (248 daraxonrasib, 252 chemotherapy); actual enrolment 500 per registry
RAS-033.time_frame: Trial started 2024-10-16; estimated primary completion 2026-06; registry status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, last update posted 2026-06-02; no posted results (checked 2026-10-08)
RAS-033.finding: From the published abstract: median OS in the RAS G12 population 13.2 months with daraxonrasib versus 6.6 months with chemotherapy, and in the overall population 13.2 versus 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.40 in both populations (P<0.001). Median PFS in the RAS G12 population 7.3 versus 3.5 months and in the overall population 7.2 versus 3.6 months, hazard ratios 0.45 and 0.49 respectively (P<0.001 for both). Adverse events after treatment start occurred in all daraxonrasib patients and 97.7% of chemotherapy patients; grade >=3 adverse events 61.8% versus 69.6%. Treatment-related adverse events leading to discontinuation occurred in 1.2% versus 11.2%. The FDA approval page independently reports, for the overall population: median OS 13.2 months (95% CI 10.0-not estimable) versus 6.7 months (95% CI 5.8-8.0), HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53), P<0.0001; median PFS 7.2 months (95% CI 5.7-7.5) versus…
RAS-033.effect: OS HR 0.40; PFS HR 0.45 (RAS G12) and 0.49 (overall); ORR 30% versus 11%
RAS-033.limitations: Full text not retrieved, so trial conduct, stratification, subgroup forest plots, crossover handling and limitations as stated by the authors were not examined; marked non-counting for that reason. The dual primary endpoints were defined in the RAS G12 population whereas the US indication carries no mutation requirement.
RAS-033.interpretation: Randomised comparison against active chemotherapy: supports drug-attributable survival benefit, the strongest causal claim available in this domain.

glosses.reading-trial-results: The randomized phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, recorded from its abstract, in which daraxonrasib doubled median survival against chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic cancer.
glosses.clinical-trials: The randomized phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, recorded from its abstract, in which daraxonrasib doubled median survival against chemotherapy.
glosses.kras: The RASolute 302 phase 3 trial (abstract only) in which daraxonrasib roughly doubled median survival versus chemotherapy in 500 previously treated patients.
glosses.second-line: RASolute 302 (abstract plus FDA page): daraxonrasib versus chemotherapy in 500 previously treated patients with metastatic disease; median survival 13.2 versus 6.7 months.
glosses.daraxonrasib: The RASolute 302 randomized phase 3 trial of 500 previously treated patients, in which daraxonrasib doubled median survival versus chemotherapy, read from the abstract only.
glosses.ras-on-inhibitors: The RASolute 302 randomized phase 3 trial of 500 previously treated patients, median survival 13.2 versus 6.7 months; abstract only, corroborated by the FDA approval page.
glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: The randomized phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, recorded from its abstract, in which daraxonrasib roughly doubled median survival against chemotherapy.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: The randomized phase 3 RASolute 302 trial, recorded from its abstract, in which response, progression-free survival and overall survival all improved together.

RAS-034.citation: Weller C, Burnett GL, Jiang L, Chakraborty S, Zhang D, Vita NA, et al. A neomorphic protein interface catalyzes covalent inhibition of RAS(G12D) aspartic acid in tumors. Science. 2025;389(6758):eads0239.
RAS-034.clinical_status: Zoldonrasib is investigational. Phase 1/1b NCT06040541 is RECRUITING (estimated enrolment 604, no posted results). Phase 3 pancreatic trials RASolute 305 (NCT07621718, zoldonrasib + chemotherapy versus placebo + chemotherapy, n=670 estimated, RECRUITING) and RASolute 309 (NCT07805954, zoldonrasib…
RAS-034.design: Chemical biology and preclinical pharmacology: engineering a neomorphic cyclophilin A / active-RAS protein-protein interface that catalyses covalent reaction with aspartate 12
RAS-034.population: Biochemical systems and multiple preclinical models of KRAS G12D cancers
RAS-034.finding: From the abstract: compounds that bind cyclophilin A create a neomorphic protein-protein interface between cyclophilin A and active RAS, enabling selective enzyme-like rate enhancement of the covalent reaction between aspartate 12 and electrophilic warheads of exceptionally low intrinsic reactivity. This yielded orally bioavailable compounds with marked antitumour activity in multiple preclinical models of KRAS G12D cancers, including the investigational agent zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), which is in clinical evaluation (NCT06040541). No numeric efficacy data were available in the accessed abstract.
RAS-034.limitations: Abstract only; no methods, denominators, model identities or figure references examined. Does not count toward the minimum.
RAS-034.interpretation: Chemical-mechanism paper: establishes feasibility of covalently targeting an aspartate, which is the enabling step for G12D-selective drugs.

glosses.kras-g12d-inhibitors: The chemistry paper describing how zoldonrasib uses cyclophilin A to form a covalent bond with the G12D aspartic acid; abstract only, with no efficacy numbers.

RAS-035.citation: Hallin J, Bowcut V, Calinisan A, Briere DM, Hargis L, Engstrom LD, et al. Anti-tumor efficacy of a potent and selective non-covalent KRAS(G12D) inhibitor. Nat Med. 2022;28(10):2171-2182.
RAS-035.clinical_status: MRTX1133's first-in-human phase 1 (NCT05737706) is TERMINATED with 63 patients enrolled; the registry reason given is 'Formulation challenges' (checked 2026-10-08).
RAS-035.design: Preclinical pharmacology with co-crystal structure, cell-line panel potency/selectivity, in vivo efficacy, and pharmacological plus CRISPR combination screens
RAS-035.population: Biochemistry, KRAS G12D-mutant and wild-type cell lines, cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts including pancreatic models
RAS-035.n: 11 PDAC models among the xenograft panel; cell-line panels (full denominators not in accessed abstract)
RAS-035.finding: From the abstract: MRTX1133 bound GDP-loaded KRAS G12D with KD approximately 0.2 pM and IC50 <2 nM, with approximately 700-fold selectivity for KRAS G12D over KRAS wild-type binding. It inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation and cell viability in KRAS G12D-mutant lines with median IC50 approximately 5 nM and >1,000-fold selectivity versus KRAS wild-type lines. It produced dose-dependent inhibition of KRAS-mediated signal transduction and marked tumour regression (>=30%) in a subset of KRAS G12D-mutant cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenograft models, including 8 of 11 (73%) pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma models. Pharmacological and CRISPR screens showed that co-targeting KRAS G12D together with putative feedback or bypass pathways including EGFR or PI3K-alpha enhanced antitumour activity.
RAS-035.effect: KD ~0.2 pM; ~700-fold binding selectivity; regression >=30% in 8/11 (73%) PDAC xenograft models
RAS-035.limitations: Abstract only; figure/table locations and in vivo dosing details not examined. Non-counting.
RAS-035.interpretation: Dose-response and selectivity data establish on-target action; the xenograft panel supports breadth of KRAS G12D dependence in PDAC.

glosses.kras-g12d-inhibitors: The discovery paper for MRTX1133, reporting 700-fold selectivity for G12D over normal KRAS and regressions in 8 of 11 pancreatic xenograft models; abstract only.

RAS-036.citation: Van Cutsem E, van de Velde H, Karasek P, Oettle H, Vervenne WL, Szawlowski A, et al. Phase III trial of gemcitabine plus tipifarnib compared with gemcitabine plus placebo in advanced pancreatic cancer. J Clin Oncol. 2004;22(8):1430-1438.
RAS-036.clinical_status: Negative phase 3; tipifarnib is not approved for pancreatic cancer in the US. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-036.design: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial; primary endpoint overall survival
RAS-036.population: Patients with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma previously untreated with systemic therapy
RAS-036.finding: From the abstract: no statistically significant differences in survival parameters were observed. Median overall survival was 193 days in the experimental arm versus 182 days in the control arm (P=0.75). Six-month and one-year survival rates were 53% and 27% versus 49% and 24%. Median progression-free survival was 112 versus 109 days. Ten drug-related deaths occurred in the experimental arm versus seven in the control arm. Grade >=3 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia occurred in 40% and 15% versus 30% and 12%.
RAS-036.effect: Median OS 193 versus 182 days, P=0.75 (no benefit)
RAS-036.limitations: Abstract only; CIs and hazard ratios not reported in the abstract; no biomarker selection.
RAS-036.interpretation: Large double-blind randomised trial: excludes a clinically meaningful survival benefit from farnesyltransferase inhibition added to gemcitabine.

glosses.clinical-trials: A negative phase 3 trial of the farnesyltransferase inhibitor tipifarnib with gemcitabine, recorded from its abstract.
glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: The 688-patient phase 3 trial of tipifarnib with gemcitabine, recorded from its abstract, which showed no survival difference (193 against 182 days).

RAS-037.citation: Moore MJ, Goldstein D, Hamm J, Figer A, Hecht JR, Gallinger S, et al. Erlotinib plus gemcitabine compared with gemcitabine alone in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: a phase III trial of the National Cancer Institute of Canada Clinical Trials Group. J Clin Oncol. 2007;25(15):1960-1966.
RAS-037.clinical_status: Erlotinib plus gemcitabine was FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer on the basis of this trial but is rarely used; it remains the only EGFR-directed regimen with a positive randomised result in this disease. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-037.design: Double-blind international randomised (1:1) phase 3 trial; primary endpoint overall survival
RAS-037.population: Patients with unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer
RAS-037.finding: From the abstract: overall survival in the intention-to-treat analysis was significantly prolonged with erlotinib/gemcitabine, hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.69-0.99; P=0.038 adjusted for stratification factors), with median survival 6.24 versus 5.91 months. One-year survival was 23% versus 17% (P=0.023). Progression-free survival was significantly longer with erlotinib plus gemcitabine, estimated hazard ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.64-0.92; P=0.004). Objective response rates did not differ significantly between arms although more erlotinib patients had disease stabilisation. Some adverse events were more frequent with erlotinib but most were grade 1 or 2. The recommended erlotinib dose with gemcitabine for this indication is 100 mg/day.
RAS-037.effect: OS HR 0.82 (0.69-0.99), median 6.24 versus 5.91 months - an absolute median gain of about 10 days
RAS-037.limitations: Abstract only; no biomarker selection; the 1-year survival difference is the more meaningful figure than the median.
RAS-037.interpretation: Large double-blind randomised trial: establishes a real but very small survival effect of EGFR inhibition, setting the magnitude against which direct RAS inhibition must be judged.

glosses.reading-trial-results: The randomized trial, recorded from its abstract, in which erlotinib plus gemcitabine gave a hazard ratio of 0.82 with a median survival gain of about ten days.
glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: The 569-patient phase 3 trial of erlotinib with gemcitabine, recorded from its abstract, with a hazard ratio of 0.82 and a median survival gain of about ten days.

RAS-038.citation: Infante JR, Somer BG, Park JO, Li CP, Scheulen ME, Kasubhai SM, et al. A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of trametinib, an oral MEK inhibitor, in combination with gemcitabine for patients with untreated metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. Eur J Cancer. 2014;50(12):2072-2081.
RAS-038.clinical_status: Negative randomised phase 2; trametinib is not approved for pancreatic cancer. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-038.design: Randomised (1:1) double-blind placebo-controlled phase 2 trial; primary endpoint overall survival; prespecified analysis in KRAS-mutant and KRAS wild-type subgroups
RAS-038.population: Adults with untreated metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas; RAS mutation determined in circulating free DNA and archival tumour tissue
RAS-038.finding: From the abstract: there was no significant difference in overall survival (hazard ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.67-1.44; P=0.453); median OS was 8.4 months with gemcitabine plus trametinib versus 6.7 months with gemcitabine plus placebo. Median PFS (16 versus 15 weeks), objective response rate (22% versus 18%) and median duration of response (23.9 versus 16.1 weeks) were also similar. In the 103 KRAS mutation-positive patients there was no difference in overall survival between arms. Thrombocytopenia, diarrhoea, rash and stomatitis were more frequent with trametinib, as was grade 3 anaemia. Outcomes were independent of KRAS mutations determined by cell-free DNA.
RAS-038.effect: OS HR 0.98 (0.67-1.44), P=0.453; no benefit overall or in the KRAS-mutant subgroup
RAS-038.limitations: Abstract only; phase 2 size; no pharmacodynamic tumour sampling reported in the abstract.
RAS-038.interpretation: Double-blind randomised design with prospective genotyping in two compartments: excludes benefit and specifically excludes KRAS mutation status as a predictive biomarker for MEK inhibition here.

glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: The 160-patient randomized trial of trametinib with gemcitabine, recorded from its abstract, with a hazard ratio of 0.98 and no benefit in KRAS-mutant patients.

RAS-039.citation: Kanhailal AC, Knikman JE, Zielhuis SWJ, Kodach LL, Bernards R, Huitema ADR, et al. The SHERPA trial: A phase I study combining SHP2 inhibitor RMC-4630 and ERK inhibitor LY3214996 in patients with KRAS-mutant solid tumours. Eur J Cancer. 2026;241:116782.
RAS-039.clinical_status: Negative/terminated phase I; neither RMC-4630 nor LY3214996 is approved. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-039.design: Phase I 3+3 dose-escalation trial with recommended phase 2 dose as the primary aim; pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics explored
RAS-039.population: Patients with KRAS-mutant PDAC, NSCLC or colorectal cancer
RAS-039.n: 24 patients treated; 19 evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity; four dose levels explored
RAS-039.finding: From the abstract: dose-limiting toxicities occurred at three of the four explored dose levels, preventing further escalation. Three DLTs were grade 3 thrombocytopenia; the other three were grade 2 decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, grade 3 acute kidney injury and grade 3 diarrhoea. At dose level 1b (100 mg RMC-4630; 200 mg LY3214996) no DLTs were reported. Pharmacokinetics showed high interpatient variability with intrapatient correlation of exposure to both agents; no exposure-toxicity relationship was established. Pharmacodynamic analysis showed a significant decrease in phosphorylated S6 ribosomal protein (P=0.034), but no radiological responses were observed. Sufficient exposure was not reached because of the combination's toxicity profile, dose escalation was discontinued and the recommended phase 2 dose was not determined.
RAS-039.effect: Objective responses: none in 24 treated patients; pS6 reduction P=0.034
RAS-039.limitations: Abstract only; mixed tumour types with no pancreatic-specific breakdown in the accessed abstract; n=24.
RAS-039.interpretation: Dose-escalation with pharmacodynamic sampling: demonstrates partial target engagement (pS6 fall) without tumour response, i.e. pathway modulation without clinical effect, and identifies toxicity rather than biology as the proximate barrier.

glosses.ras-resistance: The SHERPA phase 1 trial of a SHP2 inhibitor with an ERK inhibitor, recorded from its abstract, with no responses in 24 patients and dose escalation stopped for toxicity.
glosses.earlier-pathway-failures: The SHERPA phase 1 trial of a SHP2 inhibitor with an ERK inhibitor, recorded from its abstract, with no responses in 24 patients.

RAS-040.citation: Sacher A, LoRusso P, Patel MR, Miller WH Jr, Garralda E, Forster MD, et al. Single-Agent Divarasib (GDC-6036) in Solid Tumors with a KRAS G12C Mutation. N Engl J Med. 2023;389(8):710-721.
RAS-040.clinical_status: Divarasib is investigational; not FDA-approved. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-040.design: Phase 1 dose-escalation study (50-400 mg once daily); primary objective safety; pharmacokinetics, investigator-assessed antitumour activity and response/resistance biomarkers also assessed
RAS-040.population: 137 patients with advanced or metastatic KRAS G12C-mutant solid tumours: 60 NSCLC, 55 colorectal, 22 other solid tumours
RAS-040.finding: From the abstract: no dose-limiting toxic effects or treatment-related deaths were reported. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 127/137 (93%), grade 3 in 15 (11%) and grade 4 in 1 (1%); they caused dose reduction in 19 (14%) and discontinuation in 4 (3%). Among NSCLC patients a confirmed response occurred in 53.4% (95% CI 39.9-66.7) with median PFS 13.1 months (95% CI 8.8-not estimable). Among colorectal cancer patients a confirmed response occurred in 29.1% (95% CI 17.6-42.9) with median PFS 5.6 months (95% CI 4.1-8.2). Responses were also observed in patients with other solid tumours (not individually quantified in the abstract). Serial ctDNA showed declines in KRAS G12C variant allele frequency associated with response and identified genomic alterations that may confer resistance.
RAS-040.effect: NSCLC ORR 53.4%, median PFS 13.1 months; colorectal ORR 29.1%, median PFS 5.6 months
RAS-040.limitations: Abstract only; the pancreatic contribution is inside a 22-patient 'other solid tumours' group with no reported subgroup result.
RAS-040.interpretation: Single-arm dose escalation; the NSCLC-versus-colorectal contrast at identical target and dose supports tissue context as a determinant of durability.

RAS-041.citation: Wainberg ZA, Pant S, Weekes CD, Furqan M, Kasi PM, Devoe CE, et al. Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic and colorectal cancer: phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial final results. Nat Med. 2025;31(11):3648-3653.
RAS-041.design: Final analysis of the phase 1 dose-escalation study with extended follow-up
RAS-041.population: The same 25 MRD-positive patients (20 pancreatic, 5 colorectal) as the primary AMPLIFY-201 report
RAS-041.time_frame: Extended follow-up of the phase 1 cohort; ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT04853017 as COMPLETED (checked 2026-10-08)
RAS-041.finding: Not extracted: the PMC record retrieved for this article did not contain the abstract or results passages, so no numeric outcomes are recorded here. Recorded as a family member of RAS-021 for completeness only.
RAS-041.limitations: Numeric results not retrieved; same participants as RAS-021 so it could not count toward the minimum in any case.
RAS-041.interpretation: Same design as RAS-021 with longer follow-up; no new causal leverage.

RAS-042.citation: Cregg J, Pota K, Tomlinson ACA, Yano J, Marquez A, Liu Y, et al. Discovery of Elironrasib (RMC-6291), a Potent and Orally Bioavailable, RAS(ON) G12C-Selective, Covalent Tricomplex Inhibitor for the Treatment of Patients with RAS G12C-Addicted Cancers. J Med Chem. 2025;68(6):6041-6063.
RAS-042.clinical_status: Elironrasib is investigational. NCT06128551 (elironrasib and daraxonrasib as monotherapies and in combination) is RECRUITING with estimated enrolment 534 and no posted results (checked 2026-10-08).
RAS-042.design: Structure-guided medicinal chemistry campaign with preclinical pharmacology
RAS-042.population: Biochemical and cellular systems plus preclinical models of KRAS G12C mutant human cancers
RAS-042.finding: From the abstract: the tri-complex modality inhibits oncogenic signalling and induces tumour regressions across various preclinical models of KRAS G12C mutant human cancers. Elironrasib is in phase 1 clinical trials (NCT05462717, NCT06128551, NCT06162221), with preliminary data indicating clinical activity in patients who had progressed on first-generation inactive-state-selective KRAS G12C inhibitors. No numeric efficacy data were available in the accessed abstract.
RAS-042.interpretation: Chemistry/pharmacology paper; the statement about activity after first-generation failure is a forward reference, not data presented here.

glosses.kras-g12c-inhibitors: The discovery paper for elironrasib, an ON-state G12C-selective inhibitor, available only as an abstract reporting preliminary activity after first-generation G12C drugs fail.
glosses.ras-on-inhibitors: The discovery paper for elironrasib, an ON-state G12C-selective inhibitor, available only as an abstract reporting preliminary activity after first-generation G12C drugs fail.

RAS-043.citation: Sianoya AC, Zuo Y, Pagba CV, Jakubec JL, Planque SA, Frost JA, et al. MRTX1133 Suppresses ERK Signaling but Elicits Context-Dependent Antiproliferative Responses in KRAS(G12C) Cancer Cells. Mol Cancer Ther. 2026;OF1-OF10.
RAS-043.clinical_status: Preclinical. Corroborates the registry finding that the MRTX1133 phase 1 (NCT05737706) is TERMINATED. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-043.design: Biophysical binding and nucleotide-exchange assays, MAPK signalling readouts, proliferation assays across tissue contexts, and a xenograft arm
RAS-043.population: KRAS G12C-mutant cancer cell lines from pancreas (MIA PaCa-2), lung and colorectal origin; MIA PaCa-2 mouse xenografts
RAS-043.n: Multiple KRAS G12C cell lines plus MIA PaCa-2 xenografts (denominators not in accessed abstract)
RAS-043.finding: From the abstract: MRTX1133, developed as a KRAS G12D-selective non-covalent inhibitor, also binds G12C mutant KRAS with high affinity and suppresses nucleotide exchange and MAPK signalling in KRAS G12C cancer cell lines. However, its effect on proliferation is context-dependent: it robustly inhibited proliferation of the pancreatic line MIA PaCa-2 and the growth of MIA PaCa-2 mouse xenografts, whereas it had minimal effect in lung and colorectal cells. This appears to be due to a lack of effect on downstream KRAS effectors such as ribosomal protein S6. The authors also note the failure of sotorasib as monotherapy and the recent termination of an early-phase clinical trial for MRTX1133.
RAS-043.effect: Not quantified in accessed abstract; qualitative dissociation between MAPK suppression and antiproliferative effect outside pancreatic cells
RAS-043.limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative values; cell lines only plus one xenograft model.
RAS-043.interpretation: Cross-tissue comparison at a fixed target: separates proximal signalling inhibition from growth inhibition, which is the central discordance of this domain.

RAS-044.citation: Wang X, Allen S, Blake JF, Bowcut V, Briere DM, Calinisan A, et al. Identification of MRTX1133, a Noncovalent, Potent, and Selective KRAS(G12D) Inhibitor. J Med Chem. 2022;65(4):3123-3133.
RAS-044.clinical_status: MRTX1133 phase 1 (NCT05737706) TERMINATED for formulation challenges; no G12D-selective inhibitor approved. Checked 2026-10-08.
RAS-044.design: Structure-based medicinal chemistry optimisation campaign with in vivo efficacy confirmation
RAS-044.population: Biochemical and cellular assays; a KRAS G12D mutant xenograft mouse tumour model
RAS-044.finding: From the abstract: selective inhibition of KRAS G12D is a greater challenge than KRAS G12C because inhibitors must bind with sufficiently high affinity to obviate covalent interaction. The authors report the discovery and characterisation of the first non-covalent, potent and selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, MRTX1133, found through extensive structure-based activity improvement and shown to be efficacious in a KRAS G12D mutant xenograft mouse tumour model. No numeric potency or efficacy values were available in the accessed abstract.
RAS-044.interpretation: Chemical feasibility demonstration; no biological inference beyond on-target efficacy in one model.

IMM-001.citation: Rojas LA, Sethna Z, Soares KC, Olcese C, Pang N, Patterson E, et al. Personalized RNA neoantigen vaccines stimulate T cells in pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2023;618(7963):144-150.
IMM-001.clinical_status: Phase 1 completed; autogene cevumeran is investigational and NOT FDA-approved for any indication (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-001.design: Single-arm, open-label phase 1 trial; sequential immunotherapy to allow attribution of each agent. Primary endpoint safety; secondary endpoints 18-month RFS and OS; immune response and feasibility prespecified as EXPLORATORY. Responder/non-responder comparison of RFS is a post hoc within-trial…
IMM-001.population: Adults with single, radiographically resectable PDAC, ECOG 0-1, treated and followed at Memorial Sloan Kettering (single centre, USA).
IMM-001.n: 34 enrolled -> 28 resected -> 19 received atezolizumab (safety-evaluable) -> 16 received autogene cevumeran (biomarker-evaluable n=16; 15 also received mFOLFIRINOX). 1/19 (5%) had insufficient…
IMM-001.time_frame: Enrolment December 2019 - August 2021; data cut-off 1 April 2022; median follow-up 18 months.
IMM-001.finding: SAFETY: 0/19 grade >=3 AEs attributable to atezolizumab; 1/16 (6%) grade 3 AE attributable to vaccine (fever, hypertension); 16/16 (100%) grade 1-2 AEs (Fig 1c, Ext Data Fig 1c; Ext Data Table 1). FEASIBILITY: median time to atezolizumab 6.1 wk (range 4.3-7.9), to vaccine 9.4 wk (range 7.4-11.0), both within 1-3 days of benchmark; 3/16 (19%) did not receive all 9 doses (progression, death or mFOLFIRINOX toxicity) (Fig 1d). IMMUNOGENICITY: 8/16 (50%) were ex vivo IFN-gamma ELISpot responders; only 25/230 (11%) administered neoantigens were immunogenic; median 2 immunogenic neoantigens per responder (range 1-8); half of responses polytopic; responses ranged ~100 to >2000 spots per million PBMCs; no pre-vaccination responses detectable (Fig 1e-g, Ext Data Fig 2). CloneTrack TCR-Vbeta: vaccine-induced clonal expansion in 8/8 responders vs 1/8 non-responders; median 7.5 clones per responder…
IMM-001.effect: Immunogenicity 50% (8/16) of vaccinated patients; 11% (25/230) of targeted neoantigens. RFS by vaccine response HR 0.08 (95% CI 0.01-0.4), P=0.003 - an exploratory, non-randomized, post hoc stratification in 16 patients.
IMM-001.limitations: n=16 biomarker-evaluable; single centre; no control arm; immune response and RFS-by-response were exploratory; ex vivo ELISpot detects only high-magnitude responses and does not separate CD4 from CD8; responder/non-responder cut-point is dichotomous and data-derived.
IMM-001.interpretation: Supports causal attribution of the T-cell response to the vaccine (de novo responses absent pre-vaccination, clones non-overlapping with atezolizumab-expanded clones, in vitro neopeptide validation). Does NOT support a causal claim that the vaccine prolongs RFS: the RFS contrast is between two subgroups of one treated arm defined by an…

glosses.clinical-trials: The phase 1 trial of a personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccine that generated T cells in half of 16 patients.
glosses.mrna-vaccines: The phase 1 trial of an individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccine in 16 patients with resected pancreatic cancer, in which half developed vaccine-specific T cells and 11 percent of targeted mutations provoked a response.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: The 16-patient phase 1 trial of a personalized mRNA vaccine, in which the responder comparison was exploratory and the threshold drawn from the same patients.

IMM-002.citation: Sethna Z, Guasp P, Reiche C, Milighetti M, Ceglia N, Patterson E, et al. RNA neoantigen vaccines prime long-lived CD8+ T cells in pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2025;639(8056):1042-1051.
IMM-002.clinical_status: Investigational; same trial as IMM-001 (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-002.design: Prespecified-as-exploratory extended clinical and immunological follow-up of the phase 1 cohort; TCR clonal tracing (CloneTrack), scRNA-seq phenotyping, exponential decay modelling of clone half-life/lifespan, in vitro neoantigen recall and TCR-avidity mapping.
IMM-002.population: Same cohort as IMM-001 (resected PDAC, MSK).
IMM-002.n: Biomarker-evaluable n=16 (8 responders, 8 non-responders); safety-evaluable n=19; 7 patients received the boost; median immunological follow-up 2.95 years post-vaccination.
IMM-002.time_frame: Median clinical follow-up 3.2 years; median immunological follow-up 2.95 years post-vaccination; functional recall tested to 3.6 years.
IMM-002.finding: At median follow-up 3.2 years (range 2.3-4.0): responders median RFS not reached vs non-responders 13.4 months (P=0.007; HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.03-0.59; Fig 1a). Median OS not reached in either group. Safety-evaluable cohort median RFS 18.0 months, median OS not reached (Fig 1b). CLONE KINETICS: after priming alone, estimated median clone lifespan 1.1 years (range 0.3 to ~100 years), median half-life ~40 days. A single boost extended estimated median lifespan ~7-fold to 7.7 years (range 1.5 to >=100 years; median half-life 297 days); in 5/7 boosted patients median estimated clone lifespan exceeded the 3-year post-surgery window in which ~80% of PDAC recurrences historically occur; in 4/7 boosted patients some clones had estimated lifespans >10 years (20/65 clones, 30%) (Fig 2c,d). PERSISTENCE: 86% (median) of CloneTrack clones persisted >=2 years, occupying a median 0.07% (up to 1.1% at…
IMM-002.effect: RFS by vaccine response HR 0.14 (95% CI 0.03-0.59) at 3.2 years; boost extended estimated clone lifespan ~7-fold (median 1.1 -> 7.7 years).
IMM-002.limitations: Same 16 patients; lifespan estimates depend on the decay model; no tumour tissue at recurrence in most patients; OS not reached so no OS inference.
IMM-002.interpretation: Strong support that a uridine mRNA-lipoplex vaccine can install durable, functional CD8 memory in PDAC, and that boosting is causally responsible for extended persistence (within-patient pre/post-boost comparison). Clinical benefit remains uninferable from this design.

glosses.mrna-vaccines: Extended follow-up of the same 16 patients, showing vaccine-induced T cells persisting beyond two years and a single booster dose lengthening their estimated lifespan about sevenfold.

IMM-003.citation: Wainberg ZA, Weekes CD, Furqan M, Kasi PM, Devoe CE, Leal AD, et al. Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic and colorectal cancer: phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial final results. Nat Med. 2025;31(11):3648-3653.
IMM-003.clinical_status: Phase 1 complete; ELI-002 is investigational and NOT FDA-approved (US, checked 2026-10-08). Randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P (NCT05726864) ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING with 158 actual enrolment, no results posted (checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-003.design: Multi-cohort, open-label, dose-escalation phase 1 (final analysis). Primary endpoints safety, tolerability, RP2D. Radiographic RFS and OS were EXPLORATORY. Responder threshold re-derived post hoc by ROC analysis on the trial's own outcome data.
IMM-003.population: Adults with surgically resected stage I-IV PDAC (n=20) or colorectal cancer (n=5) expressing KRAS G12D or G12R, with no evidence of disease on imaging but minimal residual disease (MRD+) by ctDNA and/or CA19-9/CEA.
IMM-003.n: n=25 (20 PDAC, 5 CRC). MRD basis: ctDNA+ only 13/25, CA19-9/CEA only 7/25, both 5/25.
IMM-003.time_frame: Initial cut-off 6 September 2023 (median follow-up 8.5 months); final cut-off 24 September 2024 (median follow-up 19.7 months).
IMM-003.finding: IMMUNOGENICITY: 21/25 (84%) generated mKRAS-specific T-cell responses; 100% responders at the two highest adjuvant dose levels (5.0 and 10.0 mg); median response 13.38-fold over baseline; both CD4 and CD8 responses in 59%; sustained central-memory CD4 phenotype shift from baseline (Fig 2h). ANTIGEN SPREADING: T-cell responses to non-vaccine personal tumour neoantigens were detected; 5/6 (83%) patients with positive antigen spreading had mKRAS T-cell counts above the ROC threshold. OUTCOMES at median follow-up 19.7 months (cut-off 24 September 2024): whole-cohort median OS 28.94 months, median RFS 16.33 months; PDAC subset median RFS 15.31 and median OS 28.94 months (Ext Data Fig 2). STRATIFIED BY POST HOC ROC THRESHOLD (9.17-fold; 17 patients above, 8 below): all above-threshold patients had tumour biomarker reductions, including 6/6 (100%) complete ctDNA clearance; 11/17 (65%) above…
IMM-003.effect: Immunogenicity 84% (21/25). RFS HR 0.12 and OS HR 0.23 across a threshold selected by ROC on these same outcomes - an upper bound on the apparent effect, not an unbiased estimate.
IMM-003.limitations: n=25, no control, mixed tumour types, MRD defined inconsistently (ctDNA vs serum markers), threshold post hoc, RFS censored at subsequent therapy, no tumour tissue at progression.
IMM-003.interpretation: Dose-response in immunogenicity (100% response at the top two adjuvant doses) supports a causal vaccine effect on T cells. The outcome separation is non-randomized and the cut-point is data-derived, so it cannot estimate clinical benefit; it can only generate the hypothesis that AMPLIFY-7P was designed to test.

glosses.clinical-trials: The phase 1 trial of a lymph-node-targeted KRAS vaccine in which the responder threshold was chosen from the same patients' outcomes.
glosses.cea-ca125: A 25-patient phase 1 vaccine trial that defined residual disease by tumor DNA or by CA 19-9 or CEA in patients with clear scans.
glosses.ctdna: A 25-patient phase 1 vaccine trial that enrolled patients with clear scans but residual disease by ctDNA or serum markers.
glosses.kras-vaccines: The final report of the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial of a lymph-node-targeted mutant-KRAS vaccine in 25 patients with no visible disease but detectable tumor markers, with T-cell responses in 84 percent.

IMM-004.citation: Pant S, Wainberg ZA, Weekes CD, Furqan M, Kasi PM, Devoe CE, et al. Lymph-node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic and colorectal cancer: the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. Nat Med. 2024;30(2):531-542.
IMM-004.time_frame: Median follow-up 8.5 months at primary analysis.
IMM-004.finding: SAFETY (primary): 12/25 (48%) had an ELI-002-related AE, ALL grade 1-2; no grade >=3 related events, no cytokine release syndrome, no dose-limiting toxicity, no MTD reached. Most frequent related AEs: fatigue 6/25 (24%), injection-site reaction 4/25 (16%). RP2D 10 mg Amph-CpG-7909. ctDNA monitoring: tumour-informed assay in 21/25, serum-based in 4/25. Immunogenicity 21/25 (84%) responders, median 12.75-fold increase. Above- vs below-median T-cell response was associated with better biomarker response and RFS; in the 22 patients recurrence-free at completion of priming (landmark analysis to address time-to-response bias) RFS HR 0.22 (95% CI 0.038-1.27, P=0.076) - i.e. NOT statistically significant once the landmark correction was applied.
IMM-004.limitations: Short follow-up; wide confidence intervals; n=25.
IMM-004.interpretation: Establishes safety and a dose-responsive immunogenicity signal; the landmark analysis is the honest bound on the outcome association.

glosses.kras-vaccines: The primary report of the same trial, giving the safety results and the landmark-corrected recurrence hazard ratio of 0.22 that was not statistically significant.

IMM-005.citation: Le DT, Picozzi VJ, Ko AH, Wainberg ZA, Kindler H, Wang-Gillam A, et al. Results from a Phase IIb, Randomized, Multicenter Study of GVAX Pancreas and CRS-207 Compared with Chemotherapy in Adults with Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (ECLIPSE Study). Clin Cancer Res. 2019;25(18):5493-5502.
IMM-005.clinical_status: Negative randomized phase 2b. GVAX and CRS-207 are NOT FDA-approved for any indication (US, checked 2026-10-08); the programme was discontinued in this setting.
IMM-005.design: Multicentre, randomized (1:1:1), open-label phase 2b with two cohorts (primary cohort = >=2 prior lines including a gemcitabine-based regimen in the metastatic setting; exploratory second-line cohort). Primary endpoint: OS, arm A vs arm C in the primary cohort, ITT. Two-stage group-sequential…
IMM-005.population: Adults with histologically proven, previously treated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0-1, 21 centres in the USA and Canada.
IMM-005.n: 513 assessed for eligibility; 303 enrolled (213 primary cohort, 90 second-line cohort). Primary cohort ITT: arm A n=73, arm B n=68, arm C n=72. 44/213 (20.7%) in the primary cohort never started…
IMM-005.time_frame: Enrolment from February 2014; last patient visit August 2016; final analysis reported 2019.
IMM-005.finding: The study DID NOT MEET its primary endpoint. Primary cohort final analysis, ITT: median OS 3.7 months (95% CI 2.9-5.3) in arm A vs 4.6 months (95% CI 4.2-5.7) in arm C; HR 1.17 (95% CI 0.84-1.64), not significant - i.e. the point estimate FAVOURED chemotherapy (Fig 3). Arm B (CRS-207 alone) median OS 5.4 months (95% CI 4.2-...), similar to chemotherapy. 91.1% of primary-cohort and 87.9% of second-line-cohort patients had progressive disease at enrolment. Median time on protocol treatment in the second-line cohort 58 / 43 / 36 days (arms A/B/C). The regimen was well tolerated. First randomization February 2014; last patient visit August 2016.
IMM-005.effect: OS HR 1.17 (95% CI 0.84-1.64) for Cy/GVAX+CRS-207 vs single-agent chemotherapy; absolute median OS difference -0.9 months.
IMM-005.limitations: Open-label; heterogeneous physician's-choice comparator; no standard of care existed for third-line+ PDAC at the time; the trial population was selected on the basis of a subset analysis of a prior phase 2a, which the authors identify as a design error.
IMM-005.interpretation: Randomized, multicentre, ITT: supports a causal conclusion of NO OS benefit for this vaccine/Listeria regimen over single-agent chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic PDAC. The strongest available evidence that mesothelin-directed vaccine immunity does not translate into survival in this setting.

glosses.clinical-trials: The randomized phase 2b trial in which the GVAX plus CRS-207 vaccine gave shorter median survival than chemotherapy.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: The randomized ECLIPSE trial, in which a vaccine regimen did no better than single-agent chemotherapy in previously treated pancreatic cancer.
glosses.kras-vaccines: The randomized ECLIPSE phase 2b trial, in which the GVAX and CRS-207 vaccine regimen gave median survival of 3.7 months against 4.6 months for single-agent chemotherapy.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: The randomized 303-patient ECLIPSE trial in which a vaccine combination gave shorter median survival than single-agent chemotherapy.

IMM-006.citation: Leidner R, Sanjuan Silva N, Huang H, Sprott D, Zheng C, Shih YP, et al. Neoantigen T-Cell Receptor Gene Therapy in Pancreatic Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2022;386(22):2112-2119.
IMM-006.trial_id: NCT03935893 (prior TIL therapy); treatment given under single-patient investigational new drug applications
IMM-006.clinical_status: Single-patient IND experience; KRAS G12D TCR gene therapy is investigational and NOT FDA-approved (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-006.design: Single-patient (n=1) report with a second single-patient case; detailed correlative immunology (TCR specificity, serum cytokines, TCR-transgene persistence, phenotype). No control, no cohort.
IMM-006.population: Patient CRI-4483: 71-year-old woman, HLA-C*08:02-positive, KRAS G12D metastatic PDAC confined to both lungs after Whipple resection, adjuvant FOLFIRINOX and chemoradiation, then progression on autologous TIL therapy with high-dose IL-2. PD-L1 tumour proportion score <1%. Plus a second patient…
IMM-006.n: n=1 primary case; n=1 additional case.
IMM-006.time_frame: Patient 1 followed 6 months post-infusion at publication; patient 2 died 6 months post-infusion.
IMM-006.finding: PATIENT 1: regression of lung metastases at first follow-up 1 month post-infusion; RECIST v1.1 overall partial response of 62%, deepening to 72% at 6 months, still ongoing at last follow-up (Fig 1C). Serum IFN-gamma, TNF, GM-CSF and CCL4/MIP-1beta rose from low baseline to picogram levels, peaking 1 day post-infusion; IFN-gamma still elevated at discharge day 11. Transduced cells were 13% of all circulating T cells at ~1 month, 3.3% at 3 months, 2.4% at 6 months; at 6 months 34% were 9mer and 66% 10mer, overwhelmingly CD8+, with a tissue-resident-memory-like phenotype (CD103+, CD69+, CD49a+; Fig S3A). Toxicity limited to orthostatic hypotension during prolonged filgrastim, managed with fluids and 10 days of fludrocortisone. TCRs recognised peptide at 1-10 nM and recognised allogeneic pancreatic cancer lines ONLY when both KRAS G12D and HLA-C*08:02 were expressed (Fig 2B,C). PATIENT 2…
IMM-006.effect: Patient 1: 72% RECIST tumour reduction at 6 months with 2.4% of circulating T cells transduced. Patient 2: progression and death at 6 months despite high persistence; no detectable escape mechanism.
IMM-006.limitations: n=1 plus n=1; requires HLA-C*08:02 (~8-13% of people of European ancestry) AND KRAS G12D, so the eligible fraction of PDAC is small; no cohort response rate; 6-month follow-up; mechanism of failure in patient 2 undetermined.
IMM-006.interpretation: n=1 proof of principle that a shared driver neoantigen is a sufficient target for T-cell-mediated regression of established metastatic PDAC; HLA/antigen co-dependence in vitro supports on-target specificity. Cannot estimate response rate or durability. The paired discordant case is a within-report natural experiment separating 'T cells present…

glosses.engineered-t-cells: The single-patient report of KRAS G12D-directed receptor gene therapy in pancreatic cancer, with a 72 percent tumor reduction at six months in one patient and unexplained progression in a second.
