IMM-007.citation: Renouf DJ, Loree JM, Knox JJ, Topham JT, Kavan P, Jonker D, et al. The CCTG PA.7 phase II trial of gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel with or without durvalumab and tremelimumab as initial therapy in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Nat Commun. 2022;13(1):5020.
IMM-007.clinical_status: Negative randomized phase 2. No checkpoint inhibitor is FDA-approved for biomarker-unselected PDAC (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-007.design: Multicentre randomized (2:1) open-label phase 2; randomization dynamically balanced by ECOG (0 vs 1) and prior adjuvant therapy, by minimization, centrally. Primary endpoint OS. Secondary: PFS, safety, ORR, EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life. Exploratory: baseline ctDNA sequencing (PredicineATLAS, 600…
IMM-007.population: Treatment-naive adults with metastatic PDAC, unselected for any immune biomarker; multicentre Canadian Cancer Trials Group.
IMM-007.n: n=180 randomized (chemo+ICI n=119, chemo n=61); 11 safety run-in patients preceded the randomized component. Treatment initiated in 119/119 and 58/61 (95.1%). ctDNA sequencing succeeded in 173/174…
IMM-007.time_frame: Randomized component opened 10 April 2017, closed 28 July 2018 (accrual began 22 August 2016); median follow-up 28.5 months.
IMM-007.finding: PRIMARY ENDPOINT NOT MET. At median follow-up 28.5 months: median OS 9.8 months (chemo+ICI) vs 8.8 months (chemo); HR 0.94 (90% CI 0.71-1.25), P=0.72 (Fig 1A). Median PFS 5.5 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.98 (90% CI 0.75-1.29), P=0.91 (Fig 1B). No significant OS difference in subgroups defined by performance status, age, sex, race or number of metastatic organ sites (Fig 1C). Disease control rate showed a non-significant trend favouring chemo+ICI (70.6% vs 57.4%). Two grade 5 events at least possibly related to immunotherapy in the chemo+ICI arm (colonic perforation; enterocolitis) plus grade 5 hypertension, sepsis and pneumonitis; two possibly treatment-related grade 5 events in the chemo arm. No significant excess deterioration in physical function or global health status at 8 or 16 weeks. BIOMARKERS: 172/173 patients were microsatellite STABLE; only 1 patient was MSI-high (bTMB 52.9 mut/Mb).…
IMM-007.effect: OS HR 0.94 (90% CI 0.71-1.25); PFS HR 0.98 (90% CI 0.75-1.29). MSI-high prevalence 1/173 (0.6%); median bTMB 3.7 mut/Mb with maximum 11.2.
IMM-007.limitations: Phase 2 size; open-label; no PD-L1 selection; bTMB from a 2.4 Mb panel is not identical to tissue whole-exome TMB.
IMM-007.interpretation: Randomized: supports a causal conclusion of no OS or PFS benefit from adding durvalumab+tremelimumab to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in unselected metastatic PDAC. The paired ctDNA data give the quantitative reason - essentially no patient in a 173-patient metastatic PDAC cohort met the TMB or MSI thresholds that predict checkpoint benefit elsewhere.

glosses.t-cells: The randomized phase 2 PA.7 trial in 180 patients with untreated metastatic pancreatic cancer, which found no survival benefit from adding dual checkpoint blockade and showed 172 of 173 tumors were microsatellite stable.
glosses.antigen-presentation: The randomized phase 2 PA.7 trial in 180 patients with untreated metastatic pancreatic cancer, which found no survival benefit from adding dual checkpoint blockade and showed 172 of 173 tumors were microsatellite stable.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: The randomized PA.7 trial, in which adding durvalumab and tremelimumab to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel did not improve survival in unselected metastatic pancreatic cancer.
glosses.fusion-directed-drugs: The randomized PA.7 trial, in which KRAS-wild-type tumors had better survival in both arms, showing that KRAS status is prognostic independent of immunotherapy.
glosses.kras-vaccines: The randomized PA.7 trial, whose circulating-tumor-DNA analysis found KRAS mutations in 77 percent of 173 metastatic pancreatic cancers.
glosses.immune-combinations: The randomized PA.7 trial of chemotherapy with or without durvalumab and tremelimumab in 180 patients, which found no survival difference and showed that essentially no tumor reached the mutation-load threshold that predicts checkpoint benefit.

IMM-008.citation: Qi C, Gong J, Li J, Liu D, Qin Y, Ge S, et al. Claudin18.2-specific CAR T cells in gastrointestinal cancers: phase 1 trial interim results. Nat Med. 2022;28(6):1189-1198.
IMM-008.clinical_status: Satricabtagene autoleucel (satri-cel) was approved by China's NMPA in June 2026 for CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after failure of >=2 prior lines - the first CAR-T approved for a solid tumour. It is NOT approved for pancreatic cancer in any jurisdiction and…
IMM-008.design: Open-label, multicentre, single-arm, dose-escalation/de-escalation and dose-expansion phase 1; non-prespecified interim analysis. Primary objective: safety and tolerability through 28 days after first infusion. Preliminary efficacy by RECIST 1.1 (investigator-assessed).
IMM-008.population: Adults with metastatic, heavily pretreated CLDN18.2-positive digestive-system cancers: 28 gastric/gastro-oesophageal junction (GC/GEJ), 5 pancreatic cancer (PC), 4 other. Median age 53 (25-74); 64.9% men; all metastatic; 50% with >=3 organ sites. Among GC patients, 25/28 (89.3%) had >=2 prior…
IMM-008.n: 74 consented, 59 apheresed, 49 infused; first 37 infused patients with >=12 weeks follow-up analysed; 36/37 had measurable target lesions.
IMM-008.time_frame: Enrolment 26 March 2019 to 8 April 2021; data cut-off 8 April 2021; median follow-up 8.5 months since apheresis (range 2.9-19.4).
IMM-008.finding: EFFICACY by tumour type (Table 3): ALL (n=37) ORR 48.6% (95% CI 31.9-65.6), DCR 73.0% (55.9-86.2), median PFS 3.7 months (2.6-5.4), 6-month OS 80.1% (62.5-90.0); no complete responses. GASTRIC (n=28) ORR 57.1% (37.2-75.5), DCR 75.0%, median PFS 4.2 months (3.7-9.2), 6-month OS 81.2%. 'OTHER' (n=9; 5 PC + 4 other) ORR 22.2% (95% CI 2.8-60.0) = 2/9 partial responses, DCR 66.7%, median PFS 2.6 months (1.8-3.5), 6-month OS 77.8%, 6-month duration-of-response rate not applicable. 30/36 (83.3%) patients with target lesions showed some tumour regression. SAFETY: no predefined dose-limiting toxicity within 28 days, but one patient (Pt02) at 5.0x10^8 had GRADE 4 gastrointestinal haemorrhage from rapid tumour regression after a second infusion, prompting dose reduction. Grade 3-4 AEs were dominated by preconditioning-related haematological toxicity in 37/37 (100%): lymphopenia 37/37 (100%),…
IMM-008.effect: ORR 57.1% in gastric vs 22.2% in the pooled pancreatic/other group; median PFS 4.2 vs 2.6 months. Pancreatic cancer (n=5) was not reported separately.
IMM-008.limitations: Non-prespecified interim analysis; no pancreatic-specific efficacy readout; no control arm; 100% grade 3-4 haematologic toxicity from preconditioning; short follow-up.
IMM-008.interpretation: Single-arm phase 1 with deep, rapid responses in a chemorefractory population: supports a causal antitumour effect of CLDN18.2 CAR-T in gastric cancer. The within-trial tumour-type contrast supports a boundary condition rather than a general solid-tumour claim; with n=5 pancreatic patients it cannot estimate PDAC activity.

glosses.engineered-t-cells: The phase 1 interim report of claudin-18.2 CAR-T in 37 patients with digestive cancers, with a 57 percent response rate in gastric cancer and 22 percent in a nine-patient group containing all five pancreatic patients.

IMM-009.citation: Yamamoto K, Venida A, Yano J, Biancur DE, Kakiuchi M, Gupta S, et al. Autophagy promotes immune evasion of pancreatic cancer by degrading MHC-I. Nature. 2020;581(7806):100-105.
IMM-009.clinical_status: Preclinical only. Chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine are not approved for PDAC; no autophagy-inhibitor plus checkpoint combination is approved (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-009.design: Multi-level perturbation study: subcellular localisation (immunofluorescence, lysosome fractionation), genetic knockdown/knockout of autophagy genes, proximity biotinylation (HLA-A-TurboID) to find the cargo receptor, OVA/SIINFEKL model-neoantigen presentation assays, OT-I co-culture killing…
IMM-009.population: Human PDAC cell lines, non-transformed human pancreatic ductal epithelial (HPDE) cells, human PDAC tumour tissue, KPC genetically engineered mouse model-derived PDAC cells, syngeneic orthotopic and liver-metastasis mouse models in C57BL/6 and Batf3-/- mice; NSCLC lines as a cross-tissue comparison.
IMM-009.n: Multiple human and mouse PDAC lines; 'all human PDAC tumours analysed' contained regions of intracellular MHC-I (Fig 1g, Ext Data Fig 1f); mouse cohorts per figure.
IMM-009.time_frame: Not applicable (preclinical); in vivo experiments over days to weeks.
IMM-009.finding: MHC-I in PDAC lines is punctate and cytoplasmic, co-localising with lysosomes and LC3B+ autophagosomes, whereas HPDE cells display it on the plasma membrane (Fig 1a-f); MHC-I is enriched in PDAC lysosomes vs HPDE lysosomes (Fig 1c); lysosomal inhibition causes MHC-I to accumulate inside lysosomes, proving active routing for degradation (Fig 1d). All human PDAC tumours analysed contained regions of intracellular MHC-I (Fig 1g). Surface MHC-I was lower in KPC-derived mouse PDAC cells than normal pancreas cells (Ext Data Fig 1e). ATG3/ATG7 knockdown, bafilomycin A1, Atg5-/-, FIP200, ATG14, Atg13 or Ulk1 knockdown all INCREASED total and surface MHC-I, while Rubicon knockdown (required for LAP/LANDO but not autophagy) did not - specifying macroautophagy (Fig 2a,b; Ext Data Figs 2-3). Lysosomal inhibition did not change antigen-processing/presentation machinery proteins (Ext Data Fig 2k,l).…
IMM-009.effect: Not expressed as a single effect size; the decisive results are the direction-specific rescues: CD8 depletion, Batf3 loss and B2m knockdown each abolish the benefit of autophagy inhibition, and checkpoint sensitisation requires dual (not single-agent) blockade.
IMM-009.limitations: Mouse and cell-line based; OVA is a surrogate neoantigen; no human interventional data; hydroxychloroquine trials in PDAC were not combined with checkpoint blockade at the time.
IMM-009.interpretation: Loss-of-function, gain-of-function and epistasis in matched isogenic systems, with three independent necessity tests (CD8, cDC1, B2m). This is causation established in a preparation: it identifies the presentation step as rate-limiting and shows the step is reversible. It does not establish that reversing it benefits patients.

glosses.antigen-presentation: A study showing pancreatic cancer cells route MHC class I to the lysosome through NBR1-dependent autophagy, with genetic and drug reversal and dependency tests on CD8 cells, cDC1 and beta-2-microglobulin.

IMM-010.citation: Bockorny B, Semenisty V, Macarulla T, Borazanci E, Wolpin BM, Stemmer SM, et al. BL-8040, a CXCR4 antagonist, in combination with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy for pancreatic cancer: the COMBAT trial. Nat Med. 2020;26(6):878-885.
IMM-010.clinical_status: No CXCR4 antagonist is FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer. Motixafortide is FDA-approved only for haematopoietic stem-cell mobilisation in multiple myeloma, a different indication (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-010.design: Phase 2a, open-label, two-cohort, non-randomized. Primary outcome objective response rate (RECIST 1.1); secondary OS, disease control rate, safety. Final results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (hasResults true; study COMPLETED, primary completion 6 September 2022, record last updated 28 August 2024).
IMM-010.population: Adults with histologically confirmed metastatic unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma, including with intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm. Cohort 1 chemotherapy-resistant; cohort 2 received the combination with chemotherapy.
IMM-010.n: Registry actual enrolment 80; posted participant flow cohort 1 n=37, cohort 2 n=43 (0 completed, 80 not completed). The 2020 publication reported cohort 1 n=37 (modified ITT n=29 evaluable) and an…
IMM-010.time_frame: Study start September 2016; primary completion and completion 6 September 2022; results record last updated 28 August 2024 (verified 2024-08); checked 2026-10-08.
IMM-010.finding: POSTED REGISTRY RESULTS (final): PRIMARY ORR - cohort 1 (BL-8040 + pembrolizumab) 1/37 participants with an objective response; cohort 2 (BL-8040 + pembrolizumab + chemotherapy) 8/43. SECONDARY median OS - cohort 1 3.3 months (95% CI 2.8-7.5); cohort 2 6.6 months (95% CI 4.5-8.7). Median PFS - cohort 1 1.5 months (95% CI 1.5-1.8); cohort 2 3.8 months (95% CI 1.6-5.1). Disease control - cohort 1 10/37; cohort 2 25/43. PUBLISHED 2020 ABSTRACT: cohort 1 disease control rate 34.5% in the evaluable mITT population (n=29), comprising 9/29 (31%) stable disease and 1/29 (3.4%) partial response; median OS 3.3 months ITT, and 7.5 months in the subgroup receiving study drugs as second-line therapy. BL-8040 increased CD8+ effector T-cell tumour infiltration, decreased myeloid-derived suppressor cells and further decreased circulating regulatory T cells. Interim cohort 2 (n=22) was reported as ORR…
IMM-010.effect: CXCR4 antagonist + anti-PD-1 WITHOUT chemotherapy: 1/37 objective responses (2.7%), median OS 3.3 months, median PFS 1.5 months. Adding chemotherapy: 8/43 (18.6%), median OS 6.6 months - within the range expected from the chemotherapy alone.
IMM-010.limitations: Non-randomized; two non-comparable cohorts; mITT denominators in the publication differ from the registry's randomized denominators; no confirmatory randomized trial was conducted in PDAC.
IMM-010.interpretation: Single-arm: supports a causal claim about pharmacodynamics (BL-8040 increased intratumoural CD8 T cells and reduced MDSCs - this part was measured in paired biopsies) but NOT about efficacy. The chemotherapy-free cohort is the informative arm: it isolates CXCR4 blockade plus PD-1 blockade from cytotoxic activity and shows near-absent activity.

glosses.clinical-trials: Registry results of a CXCR4-antagonist plus pembrolizumab study whose interim response rate fell at full accrual.
glosses.t-cells: The COMBAT trial of a CXCR4 antagonist with pembrolizumab in metastatic pancreatic cancer, in which the chemotherapy-free cohort produced one objective response in 37 patients.
glosses.immune-combinations: The COMBAT trial of the CXCR4 antagonist motixafortide with pembrolizumab, which increased CD8 infiltration in biopsies while producing 1 objective response in 37 patients without chemotherapy.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: A non-randomized trial of a CXCR4 antagonist with pembrolizumab whose interim response rate of 32% fell to 8 of 43 once the cohort was fully enrolled.

IMM-011.citation: Hegde S, Krisnawan VE, Herzog BH, Zuo C, Breden MA, Knolhoff BL, et al. Dendritic Cell Paucity Leads to Dysfunctional Immune Surveillance in Pancreatic Cancer. Cancer Cell. 2020;37(3):289-307.e9.
IMM-011.clinical_status: Preclinical only; no Flt3L-based therapy is FDA-approved for PDAC (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-011.design: Genetic gain-of-function (neoantigen knock-in) in autochthonous tumour models, cross-organ comparison (pancreas vs lung) of innate immune composition, RNA-seq of matched tissues, adoptive OT-I transfer, checkpoint blockade, Flt3L-mediated cDC mobilisation with CD8 and IFN-gamma depletion as…
IMM-011.population: Autochthonous mouse PDAC: KPC (Kras-LSL-G12D; Trp53) and KPPC models engineered to express a model neoantigen (ovalbumin-GFP, 'OG'), including an inducible mosaic model (iKPC-OG) and a lung counterpart (KPL-OG) for cross-organ comparison; plus immune profiling of early- and late-stage mouse lung…
IMM-011.n: Multiple genetically engineered mouse cohorts (KPC-OG vs KPC, iKPC-OG vs iKPC, KPL-OG vs OG-negative lung); group sizes per figure panel.
IMM-011.time_frame: Preclinical, weeks; early (6-week) through end-stage disease.
IMM-011.finding: PARADOXICAL ANTIGEN EFFECT: OG (neoantigen) expression ACCELERATED tumour progression at every stage. At 6 weeks, KPC-OG mice had increased PanIN area, higher-grade PanIN lesions and increased tumour-cell proliferation (Fig 2A-B), with increased collagen deposition and alpha-SMA+ fibroblast density (Fig 2C-D) and increased neutrophil, eosinophil and macrophage infiltration but no change in NK, NKT or gamma-delta T cells (Fig 2E). KPC-OG mice had REDUCED overall survival, higher-grade tumours and markedly more liver metastases (Fig 2F-H); the inducible mosaic iKPC-OG model reproduced this (Fig 2I). This contrasts with analogous KP LUNG models in which neoantigen recognition restrains progression. THERAPY: despite neoantigen expression, anti-PD-1 + anti-CTLA-4 did NOT affect survival of KPPC-OG tumours (Fig S2L); OT-I adoptive transfer with IL-2 gave only a MODEST survival benefit,…
IMM-011.effect: cDC1s 10-fold fewer in premalignant pancreas than lung; Flt3L produced a 10-fold cDC1 increase; tumour control by Flt3L was entirely CD8- and IFN-gamma-dependent.
IMM-011.limitations: Mouse models; model neoantigen; human data limited to transcriptional comparison; Flt3L was given at early stages, not in established tumours.
IMM-011.interpretation: A genuine natural-experiment design: it holds antigen constant and varies organ and dendritic-cell availability. The gain-of-function (antigen), rescue (Flt3L) and necessity (CD8/IFN-gamma depletion) arms together establish that in PDAC the rate-limiting step for productive antineoplastic immunity is cDC1-dependent PRIMING, not antigen supply -…

glosses.antigen-presentation: A mouse study in which forcing a strong antigen into pancreatic tumors accelerated disease, and in which cDC1 dendritic cells were tenfold scarcer in pancreas than lung, with mobilization reversing the effect.

IMM-012.citation: Bever KM, Huff AL, Danilova L, Wetzel M, Tandurella JA, Durham JN, et al. A Randomized Phase II Study: CRS207/GVAX plus Anti-PD-1 and Anti-CTLA4 Recruits Mesothelin- and mKRAS-Specific T Cells into PDAC. Cancer Immunol Res. 2026;14(3):411-422.
IMM-012.clinical_status: Negative randomized phase 2 (primary endpoint not met). GVAX, CRS-207 and this combination are NOT FDA-approved (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-012.design: Randomized, open-label phase 2, two arms, random block randomization. Primary endpoint objective response rate per RECIST 1.1, testing an ORR of 22% against a null of <=6%, 30 patients per arm; NOT powered for inter-arm comparison. PFS and OS exploratory. Correlatives: 30+ marker CyTOF of…
IMM-012.population: Adults with previously treated metastatic PDAC at Johns Hopkins; heavily pretreated (majority >=2 prior systemic lines), 79% with liver metastases; mean age 63; 56% male; 9 patients with germline or somatic BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations; one patient with a germline MSH6 mutation.
IMM-012.n: 61 eligible patients enrolled and randomized (arm A n=31, arm B n=30); 57 received >=1 dose (arm A n=30, arm B n=27). Enrolment closed before planned accrual was complete due to loss of drug…
IMM-012.time_frame: Enrolment December 2017 to August 2021; survival follow-up through study completion.
IMM-012.finding: PRIMARY ENDPOINT NOT MET IN EITHER ARM (Table 2). Arm A (n=30): ORR 0% (95% CI 0-12); 0 partial responses, 7 stable disease (23%), 23 progressive disease (77%); disease control 7/30 (23%). Arm B (n=27): ORR 7% (95% CI 1-24); 2 partial responses (7%), 2 stable disease (7%), 23 progressive disease (85%); disease control 4/27 (14%). P=0.43 between arms. Median OS 4.3 months (95% CI 3-9) arm A vs 3.9 months (95% CI 2.6-6) arm B; median PFS 2.2 months (95% CI 1.8-2.8) vs 1.9 months (95% CI 1.7-2.3). 8/46 (17%) had at least some CA19-9 decline. The patient with the germline MSH6 mutation had stable disease and remained on study 131 days. IMMUNOLOGY DESPITE THAT: the authors report significant T-cell expansion AND infiltration within the tumour microenvironment, and for the first time identify the specific TCR clonotypes reactive to mesothelin and to mutant KRAS arising in response to…
IMM-012.effect: ORR 0/30 vs 2/27; median OS 4.3 vs 3.9 months - against documented antigen-specific CD8 memory T-cell expansion and tumour infiltration in the same patients.
IMM-012.limitations: Underpowered single-centre randomized phase 2 closed early; no chemotherapy control arm; 68% grade >=3 treatment-related AEs; immunological correlatives were exploratory and not prespecified for hypothesis testing.
IMM-012.interpretation: Randomized and biopsy-controlled. Because the immunological endpoint (antigen-specific T cells in the tumour) was MET while the clinical endpoint was not, this trial localises the failure DOWNSTREAM of priming and trafficking - the two steps most vaccine strategies are designed to fix. It is the strongest available dissociation of immunogenicity…

glosses.clinical-trials: A randomized phase 2 trial of vaccine plus dual checkpoint blockade with response rates of 0% and 7%.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: A randomized phase 2 trial of nivolumab and ipilimumab with vaccines in previously treated pancreatic cancer, with response rates of 0 and 7 percent.
glosses.kras-vaccines: A randomized phase 2 adding nivolumab and ipilimumab to GVAX and CRS-207, which missed its response endpoint at 0 and 7 percent while documenting mutant-KRAS- and mesothelin-reactive T cells inside the tumors.
glosses.immune-combinations: A randomized phase 2 of vaccines plus nivolumab and ipilimumab, which documented antigen-specific T cells inside tumors while response rates were 0 and 7 percent.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: A randomized phase 2 trial of a vaccine with dual checkpoint blockade, with response rates of 0% and 7% despite documented tumor infiltration by antigen-specific T cells.

IMM-013.citation: Lutz E, Yeo CJ, Lillemoe KD, Biedrzycki B, Kobrin B, Herman J, et al. A lethally irradiated allogeneic granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor-secreting tumor vaccine for pancreatic adenocarcinoma. A Phase II trial of safety, efficacy, and immune activation. Ann Surg. 2011;253(2):328-335.
IMM-013.clinical_status: Phase 2 complete; GVAX is NOT FDA-approved (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-013.design: Single-institution, single-arm phase 2. Primary endpoint disease-free survival (time from surgery to clinical evidence of disease or death from any cause). Powered (91%) to detect a rise in 1-year survival from 20.2% to 34.3% (two-sided alpha 0.10). Immune endpoint: prevalence of…
IMM-013.population: 60 patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma who underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy at the Johns Hopkins Hospital between December 2001 and November 2004.
IMM-013.n: n=60 resected patients at the highest immunotherapy dose (5x10^8 vaccine cells).
IMM-013.finding: Median disease-free survival 17.3 months (95% CI 14.6-22.8); median overall survival 24.8 months (95% CI 21.2-31.6). Disease-free at 1 year 67.4% (95% CI 56.4-80.6%); alive at 1 year 85.0% (95% CI 76.3-94.5%). In univariate models positive lymph nodes and other standard pathological factors behaved as expected. Post-immunotherapy induction of mesothelin-specific CD8+ T cells CORRELATED with disease-free survival in HLA-A*0101 and HLA-A*0201 patients. CRITICALLY: the comparison with a Johns Hopkins subset matched on tumour size, nodal status and margin status 'produced nearly identical results... and DID NOT FAVOR the immunotherapy group'. The authors' earlier phase 1 experience had identified delayed-type hypersensitivity responders among patients disease-free at 10+ years, and all 3 of those DTH responders had post-immunotherapy T-cell responses to mesothelin.
IMM-013.effect: Median DFS 17.3 months and median OS 24.8 months in vaccinated resected patients, with no advantage over a matched unvaccinated surgical cohort. The within-trial immune-response/DFS correlation reproduces, 12 years earlier, the pattern later seen with mRNA neoantigen vaccination.
IMM-013.limitations: Single arm; non-randomized external comparison; HLA-restricted immune analysis available only in A0101/A0201 patients; vaccine given together with chemoradiotherapy so immunological and cytotoxic effects are entangled.
IMM-013.interpretation: Single-arm with external matched comparison: supports a causal claim about immunogenicity (mesothelin-specific CD8 responses arise after vaccination) and refutes nothing about benefit, because the matched comparison showed no survival advantage. Its main inferential value is historical control on the 'responder correlation' design itself: the…

glosses.clinical-trials: A single-arm trial of the GVAX vaccine after surgery showing no advantage over a matched unvaccinated cohort despite a within-trial responder correlation.

IMM-014.citation: Tran E, Robbins PF, Lu YC, Prickett TD, Gartner JJ, Jia L, et al. T-Cell Transfer Therapy Targeting Mutant KRAS in Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2016;375(23):2255-2262.
IMM-014.clinical_status: Investigational; no KRAS-directed TCR or TIL product is FDA-approved for pancreatic or colorectal cancer (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-014.design: Single patient (n=1) within a phase 2 TIL trial, with whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing of three resected lung lesions (median depth 128/131/163), 24 individual TIL cultures screened for neoepitope reactivity, TCR identification and retroviral re-expression for specificity testing, serial…
IMM-014.population: Patient 4095: 50-year-old woman with metastatic colorectal cancer, lung-only progression, HLA-C*08:02-positive, KRAS G12D-mutant, enrolled in an ongoing phase 2 trial of adoptive transfer of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes targeting personalised neoepitopes.
IMM-014.n: n=1; 10 lung lesions at baseline, 3 resected for TIL generation and sequencing; 24 TIL cultures.
IMM-014.time_frame: Follow-up to ~9 months post-infusion; progressing lesion resected at ~9 months.
IMM-014.finding: At first follow-up 40 days after cell therapy ALL SEVEN remaining lung metastases had regressed; six had completely regressed or were still regressing at 9 months (Fig 1B). No adverse effects beyond recovery from interleukin-2. PERSISTENCE: the most dominant infused clonotype (~7.3x10^10 cells) was undetectable in blood at 40 days, while the other KRAS G12D-reactive clones persisted at 10.4%, 4.5% and 0.005% of all peripheral-blood T cells at ~9 months; the dominant blood clone at 9 months was the TRBV10-02 mutant-KRAS-G12D-reactive TCR (Fig 2A). There was NO enrichment of KRAS G12D-reactive clones in the progressing tumour relative to blood. SPECIFICITY: re-expressed TCRs recognised peptide at 1-10 nM on autologous PBMCs and recognised allogeneic pancreatic cancer lines ONLY when both KRAS G12D and HLA-C*08:02 were present (Fig 2B,C). ESCAPE: one lesion progressed and was resected at…
IMM-014.effect: 7/7 lung metastases regressed; 6/7 complete or continuing regression at 9 months; a single lesion escaped by HLA-C*08:02 loss of heterozygosity with the target antigen intact.
IMM-014.limitations: Single patient; colorectal cancer, not PDAC; 9-month follow-up; HLA-LOH detected in only one lesion and not systematically surveyed.
IMM-014.interpretation: n=1, but an exceptionally strong causal chain: specificity shown in vitro to require both antigen and the restricting allele; escape shown in vivo to occur precisely by loss of that allele with antigen retained. This is a natural knockout experiment that confirms the presentation step, not the antigen, is the single point of failure for this…

glosses.engineered-t-cells: A single colorectal case of KRAS G12D-directed cell therapy in which seven of seven lung metastases regressed and the one escaping lesion had deleted the chromosome copy carrying the restricting HLA allele.

IMM-015.citation: Beatty GL, O'Hara MH, Lacey SF, Torigian DA, Nazimuddin F, Chen F, et al. Activity of Mesothelin-Specific Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cells Against Pancreatic Carcinoma Metastases in a Phase 1 Trial. Gastroenterology. 2018;155(1):29-32.
IMM-015.clinical_status: Phase 1; no mesothelin CAR-T product is FDA-approved for any indication (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-015.design: Phase 1, single-arm, no lymphodepletion; mRNA electroporation chosen deliberately to make CAR expression TRANSIENT and limit toxicity. Response by RECIST v1.1 with FDG-PET/CT metabolically active volume (MAV) and SUVmax as additional lesion-level readouts.
IMM-015.population: Six patients with chemotherapy-refractory metastatic PDAC.
IMM-015.time_frame: PFS 3.8 and 5.4 months in the two patients with prolonged stable disease.
IMM-015.finding: SAFETY: none of the 6 patients experienced cytokine release syndrome or neurologic symptoms; there were no dose-limiting toxicities. EFFICACY: the BEST OVERALL RESPONSE was STABLE DISEASE by RECIST v1.1 - no objective responses. Two patients (08212-100 and 08212-108) had progression-free survival of 3.8 and 5.4 months respectively (Fig 1B). FDG-PET: total metabolically active volume remained stable in three patients and decreased by 69.2% in one patient (08212-113), in whom SUVmax decreased across lesions with complete loss of FDG uptake in ALL LIVER LESIONS (Fig 1C,D) - evidence of heterogeneous, organ-dependent antitumour activity without a RECIST response.
IMM-015.effect: 0/6 objective responses; best response stable disease; one patient with a 69.2% reduction in metabolically active tumour volume and complete resolution of FDG uptake in liver lesions.
IMM-015.limitations: n=6; transient CAR expression by design; no lymphodepletion; no on-treatment tumour biopsies reported in the accessed text; FDG-PET changes are exploratory.
IMM-015.interpretation: Single-arm n=6: cannot estimate efficacy, but the lesion-level FDG-PET data provide within-patient evidence that mesothelin CAR-T cells can act on some metastatic sites (notably liver) while the overall tumour burden does not meet response criteria. Combined with the TCR anchor, it shows that bypassing MHC presentation does NOT by itself rescue…

glosses.engineered-t-cells: A phase 1 trial of mesothelin CAR-T in six patients with pancreatic cancer, with no objective responses but a 69 percent fall in metabolically active tumor volume in one patient.

IMM-016.citation: Drakes DJ, Abbas AM, Shields J, Steinbuck MP, Jakubowski A, Seenappa LM, et al. Lymph Node-Targeted Vaccine Boosting of TCR T-cell Therapy Enhances Antitumor Function and Eradicates Solid Tumors. Cancer Immunol Res. 2024;12(2):214-231.
IMM-016.clinical_status: Preclinical. No lymph-node-targeted vaccine plus TCR-T combination is FDA-approved (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-016.design: Preclinical comparative-intervention study. The key specificity contrast is amphiphile (AMP, albumin-binding, lymph-node-targeted) peptide plus AMP-CpG versus the SAME peptide and adjuvant in soluble (SOL) form, plus TCR-T alone and PBS controls; outcomes include tumour growth, TCR-T…
IMM-016.population: Multiple mouse TCR-T models: Pmel-1 (gp100-specific) T cells in B16F10 melanoma-bearing C57BL/6 mice; HLA-A*11:01-transgenic (CB6F1-Tg A11.01) mice with mutant KRAS G12V- and G12D-specific TCR-T cells; and human HLA-A*11:01 T cells transduced with a mutant KRAS G12D-specific TCR against Panc-1…
IMM-016.n: Multiple mouse cohorts per model (group sizes per figure); human TCR-T xenograft arm used NSG mice implanted with 1x10^6 Panc-1 cells 10 days before transfer.
IMM-016.time_frame: Preclinical; immune analyses on days 7, 14 (B16F10) and day 15 (murine HLA-A*11:01 mKRAS models).
IMM-016.finding: Lymph-node-targeted AMP vaccination, but not soluble vaccination, enabled TCR-T cells to colocalise in the lymph node with a population of highly costimulatory, cognate-peptide-presenting antigen-presenting cells, delivering TCR stimulus together with endogenous costimulation and cytokine support. This produced enhanced TCR-T activation and expansion, enhanced tumour infiltration, and ERADICATION OF ESTABLISHED SOLID TUMOURS without any preconditioning or exogenous cytokines. The authors additionally report that AMP boosting establishes a supportive lymphatic niche with potential for ANTIGEN SPREADING, diversifying tumour-specific recognition for longer-term protection. The approach extended to HUMAN TCR-T cells specific for clinically relevant targets, including a mutant KRAS G12D-specific human TCR against Panc-1 pancreatic cancer in NSG mice, activated in vitro by AMP-peptide-pulsed…
IMM-016.effect: Eradication of established tumours with AMP (lymph-node-targeted) boosting versus failure of the identical soluble construct - the effect is attributable to lymphatic targeting, not to the peptide or adjuvant themselves.
IMM-016.limitations: Preclinical; no human clinical outcome; melanoma model carries the strongest efficacy data; antigen spreading described as potential rather than demonstrated in the pancreatic arm.
IMM-016.interpretation: Controlled comparative perturbation in which the only difference between the effective and ineffective arms is lymph-node targeting of the same antigen and adjuvant. This isolates antigen delivery to the draining lymph node as the causal variable and provides a mechanism (APC-mediated restimulation with costimulation and cytokine support) that…

glosses.kras-vaccines: A mouse study showing that lymph-node-targeted vaccine boosting eradicated established tumors while the identical soluble peptide and adjuvant did not.
glosses.engineered-t-cells: A mouse study showing that re-stimulating transferred receptor-engineered T cells with a lymph-node-targeted vaccine eradicated established tumors without chemotherapy preconditioning or high-dose cytokines.

IMM-017.citation: Nywening TM, Wang-Gillam A, Sanford DE, Belt BA, Panni RZ, Cusworth BM, et al. Targeting tumour-associated macrophages with CCR2 inhibition in combination with FOLFIRINOX in patients with borderline resectable and locally advanced pancreatic cancer: a single-centre, open-label, dose-finding, non-randomised, phase 1b trial. Lancet Oncol. 2016;17(5):651-662.
IMM-017.clinical_status: Phase 1b only. PF-04136309 is investigational and NOT FDA-approved; it was not advanced in PDAC, and no CCR2 inhibitor is approved for any cancer indication (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-017.design: Phase 1b, open-label, non-randomised, dose-finding (3+3 dose de-escalation). Primary endpoint: safety, tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose. Secondary: partial response rate and tumour control rate (CR+PR+SD) by RECIST 1.1, tested by a PRE-SPECIFIED two-sided hypothesis against a null PR rate…
IMM-017.population: Treatment-naive adults (>=18 years) with biopsy-proven borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma with measurable disease, ECOG <=1, single centre (Washington University). Mostly locally advanced (75-79%) with head/neck lesions (75-77%); biliary stent needed in 25% vs…
IMM-017.n: 71 screened, 47 enrolled (FOLFIRINOX alone n=8, FOLFIRINOX + PF-04136309 n=39); 45 assessed for toxicity; 33 evaluable for RECIST response in the combination group and 5 in the FOLFIRINOX-alone…
IMM-017.time_frame: Enrolment 19 April 2012 to 12 November 2014; median duration of toxicity evaluation 72.0 days (IQR 49.5-89.0) in the FOLFIRINOX-alone group.
IMM-017.finding: RESPONSE: 16/33 (48.5%, 95% CI 30.80-66.54) achieved a partial response with FOLFIRINOX + PF-04136309, significantly above the pre-specified 25% null (P=0.006; Fig 2). Tumour control (CR+PR+SD) 32/33 (97.0%, 95% CI 84.24-99.92), with only 1/33 progressing and NO distant metastases reported during the study. In the FOLFIRINOX-alone group, NO objective responses were seen among 5 evaluable patients and 1 patient developed distant metastasis (tumour control 80%). PHARMACODYNAMICS: after therapy the mean bone-marrow-to-peripheral-blood inflammatory monocyte ratio fell in the PF-04136309 group (n=23) versus a mean ratio of 6.46 (95% CI 3.97-8.95) in the FOLFIRINOX-only group (P=0.0006; Fig 3C). Bone-marrow inflammatory monocytes increased by a mean of 69.8% (95% CI -2.71 to 142.3%) from baseline in the 10 patients achieving a RECIST partial response versus 30.31% (95% CI -16.11 to 76.73) in…
IMM-017.effect: PR 48.5% (16/33) versus a pre-specified 25% benchmark (P=0.006) and 0/5 in the concurrent FOLFIRINOX-alone group; target engagement confirmed by a significant shift in the bone-marrow-to-blood inflammatory monocyte ratio (P=0.0006).
IMM-017.limitations: Phase 1b, non-randomised, n=33 evaluable, single centre, asymmetric group sizes (39 vs 8), historical benchmark, exploratory immune endpoints, no survival endpoint powered.
IMM-017.interpretation: Supports a causal pharmacodynamic claim (CCR2 blockade retains inflammatory monocytes in the bone marrow) because the comparison is to a concurrent FOLFIRINOX-only group with paired samples. Does NOT support a causal efficacy claim: n=33, non-randomised, single centre, FOLFIRINOX itself produces high response rates in…

glosses.myeloid-cells: A 47-patient phase 1b study of a CCR2 inhibitor with FOLFIRINOX in pancreatic cancer that had not spread beyond the pancreas and nearby vessels, with partial responses in 16 of 33 and confirmed target engagement.
glosses.immune-combinations: A phase 1b of the CCR2 inhibitor PF-04136309 with FOLFIRINOX, which confirmed target engagement in bone marrow and reported a 48.5 percent partial response rate in 33 non-randomized patients.

IMM-018.citation: Urman A, Ding Y, Durham J, Wang H, Qi H, Narang A, et al. Safety and immunologic impact of neoadjuvant/adjuvant GVAX, cyclophosphamide, pembrolizumab, and anti-CSF1R agent IMC-CS4 in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Front Immunol. 2026;17:1715761.
IMM-018.clinical_status: Pilot phase 1/2. IMC-CS4 is investigational; no CSF1R-targeted agent is FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-018.design: Single-centre, open-label pilot study with a safety run-in and Bayesian stopping rule (combination considered safe if grade 3-4 toxicity rate <30%). PRIMARY IMMUNOLOGIC ENDPOINT, prespecified at design: change in intratumoural CD8+ T-cell density between pretreatment biopsy and post-treatment…
IMM-018.population: Adults with resectable or borderline resectable PDAC (NCCN/surgical criteria, Johns Hopkins pancreas tumour board), ECOG 0-1, after completion of standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy; 9/9 had prior standard chemotherapy, 78% FOLFIRINOX. Single centre (Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center, Johns…
IMM-018.n: 11 enrolled, 9 treated (2 withdrew consent before first dose), 8 with evaluable paired pre/post specimens.
IMM-018.time_frame: Treatment September 2018 to January 2021; survival follow-up to August 2023.
IMM-018.finding: PRIMARY IMMUNOLOGIC ENDPOINT MET: 5/8 evaluable patients (63%) had a >80% increase in intratumoural CD8+ T cells meeting the >=1.8x MAD criterion. Of those 5, FOUR also had a >80% and >=1.8x MAD increase in granzyme B+ CD8+ T cells, indicating cytotoxic effector activation. Statistically significant pre-to-post increases were seen for CD8+ T cells, CD8+granzymeB+ T cells, CD4+ T cells, CD4+PD1+ T cells, REGULATORY T CELLS and B cells (p<0.05 each); other cell types did not change significantly - i.e. the regimen expanded effector AND suppressive compartments together. CLINICAL: all 9 patients (100%) had STABLE DISEASE by irRECIST on the CT preceding surgery - no objective responses; all 9 (100%) underwent surgery within two weeks of completing neoadjuvant immunotherapy; pathologic response rate 78% (7/9) including ONE complete pathologic response (in a patient with stage III disease);…
IMM-018.effect: Intratumoural CD8 increase meeting the prespecified threshold in 5/8 (63%); objective response rate 0/9; median OS 20.4 months - within the range expected for resected PDAC after neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX.
IMM-018.limitations: n=9 treated, n=8 evaluable; single arm; single centre; pre/post comparison confounded by prior chemotherapy and by biopsy-versus-resection sampling; 0/9 objective responses; OS from a 9-patient pilot is uninterpretable.
IMM-018.interpretation: Paired within-patient tissue sampling with a prespecified quantitative threshold supports a causal claim that this combination raises intratumoural CD8 and granzyme B+ CD8 density in human PDAC. Because the trial has no control arm, 9 patients and a median OS indistinguishable from standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus surgery, it cannot speak…

glosses.immune-combinations: A nine-patient pilot of an anti-CSF1R antibody with a vaccine and pembrolizumab, which met its prespecified endpoint of raising CD8 T cells inside the tumor while also raising regulatory T cells and producing no objective responses.

IMM-019.citation: Mahalingam D, Wilkinson GA, Eng KH, Fields P, Raber P, Moseley JL, et al. Pembrolizumab in Combination with the Oncolytic Virus Pelareorep and Chemotherapy in Patients with Advanced Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Phase Ib Study. Clin Cancer Res. 2020;26(1):71-81.
IMM-019.clinical_status: Phase 1b. Pelareorep is investigational; no oncolytic virus is FDA-approved for pancreatic cancer (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-019.design: Phase 1b, single-arm, 3+8 expansion (3 patients then 8 added after no dose-limiting toxicity). Primary objective: safety and dose-limiting toxicities. Secondary: overall response rate and PFS by IMMUNE-RELATED response criteria, plus OS; and paired pre-/on-treatment tumour biopsies and peripheral…
IMM-019.population: Adults with advanced/metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after prior therapy; median age 64 (range 50-84), 45% >=65 years, 73% female, 100% Caucasian, 64% non-Hispanic, ECOG 0 (55%) or 1 (45%).
IMM-019.n: n=11 enrolled; 10/11 evaluable for efficacy; 5 patients treated for fewer than 3 cycles (4 for clinical progression, 1 toxicity/withdrawal) and not evaluable for radiographic response.
IMM-019.time_frame: Enrolment January to August 2016; the single responder's response lasted 17.4 months and began 6.5 months after treatment start.
IMM-019.finding: EFFICACY: overall response rate 9% and disease control rate 27%. ONE patient achieved a partial response beginning 6.5 months after the start of therapy that LASTED 17.4 MONTHS; two patients achieved stable disease from 2 months lasting 9.1 and 4.1 months; three had progressive disease as best response. No complete responses. Median PFS 2.0 months (95% CI 0-6.8); median OS 3.1 months (95% CI 0-8.7), with 1-year and 2-year survival of 35% and 23%. ALL PATIENTS DIED OF THEIR DISEASE. SAFETY: grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs in 2/11 (18%) - one neutropenia/leukopenia and one myalgias/fever/chills; one patient had transient grade 2 transaminase elevation twice. MECHANISM: pelareorep given intravenously replicated in tumour tissue on on-treatment biopsy; known biology is that double-stranded-RNA sensing drives interferon secretion and upregulates PD-L1 and antigen-processing genes (TAP1/2,…
IMM-019.effect: ORR 9% (1/11), DCR 27%; median OS 3.1 months with 1-year survival 35% and 2-year survival 23% - a flat-tail pattern driven by a small number of long survivors rather than by a shift in the median.
IMM-019.limitations: n=11; single-arm; immune-related response criteria rather than RECIST for the primary efficacy readout; 5/11 not response-evaluable; trends in TCR metrics not statistically established; unadjusted p-values for differential abundance.
IMM-019.interpretation: Single-arm n=11: supports a causal claim that intravenously administered pelareorep reaches and replicates in pancreatic tumour tissue (direct on-treatment biopsy evidence). It cannot establish efficacy. The dissociation between a 3.1-month median OS and 23% two-year survival is the informative pattern: a small subgroup may derive durable benefit…

glosses.immune-combinations: A phase 1b of the oncolytic virus pelareorep with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in 11 patients, which confirmed the virus replicating in tumor tissue and recorded one response lasting 17.4 months.

IMM-020.citation: Hu ZI, Shia J, Stadler ZK, Varghese AM, Capanu M, Salo-Mullen E, et al. Evaluating Mismatch Repair Deficiency in Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: Challenges and Recommendations. Clin Cancer Res. 2018;24(6):1326-1336.
IMM-020.clinical_status: Observational. Pembrolizumab has an FDA tissue-agnostic approval for unresectable or metastatic MSI-high/dMMR solid tumours after prior treatment, which includes PDAC; the approval itself and its pivotal data are recorded by the TX domain. Real-world availability therefore depends entirely on…
IMM-020.design: Single-institution retrospective consecutive-cohort review with multimodal MMR ascertainment: immunohistochemistry, germline testing, and tumour plus germline next-generation sequencing (MSK-IMPACT), with MSIsensor scores and mutational load, and Spearman correlation between mutational load and…
IMM-020.population: 833 consecutive patients with PDAC treated at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center between 2006 and 2017 (institutional tumour registry and ICD billing database query), with all MMR-deficient tumours characterised.
IMM-020.n: 833 consecutive PDAC patients; 7 with confirmed MMR deficiency.
IMM-020.time_frame: Patients treated 2006-2017; MMR-deficiency query covering 1 January 2006 to 30 July 2017.
IMM-020.finding: PREVALENCE: 7 of 833 consecutive PDAC patients (0.8%) had confirmed MMR deficiency by immunohistochemistry, germline testing or germline next-generation sequencing (Table 1). ALL 7 had Lynch syndrome. 5 of 7 (71%) had an extensive personal or family cancer history. The paper documents at least one MMR-deficient patient who, after being taken off a checkpoint-blockade trial, continued to progress despite multiple subsequent lines of chemotherapy and died of her disease in December 2016 - MMR deficiency is therefore NOT a guarantee of benefit. The authors note that previously reported rates of MMR deficiency in PDAC, adjudicated by immunohistochemistry and microsatellite-instability testing, have ranged absurdly widely from 0% to 75% across studies because of different and evolving detection methods and sample sizes, and that existing literature is 'generally discordant' on prevalence,…
IMM-020.effect: MMR-deficiency prevalence 7/833 (0.8%) in consecutive PDAC; 7/7 associated with Lynch syndrome. Prior literature estimates span 0-75%, i.e. a ~90-fold disagreement, attributable to assay and sampling differences.
IMM-020.limitations: Retrospective; n=7 MMR-deficient patients; non-uniform testing; no systematic outcome analysis of the 7; single centre. Cross-domain note: this study is the GENE domain's counted record (GENE-006); it is retained here only for the immunotherapy-eligibility denominator and the assay-discordance point.
IMM-020.interpretation: Observational consecutive-cohort design: establishes prevalence with low selection bias within one institution and establishes a measurement-validity problem (assay discordance). It cannot estimate treatment effect; the individual clinical courses are descriptive.

glosses.antigen-presentation: A review of 833 consecutive pancreatic cancer patients at one center finding mismatch-repair deficiency in 7, all with Lynch syndrome, and documenting how widely published prevalence estimates disagree.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: The same consecutive series read for the immunotherapy denominator, documenting that reported MSI prevalence in pancreatic cancer ranged from 0 to 75 percent across assays.
glosses.immune-combinations: A consecutive series of 833 pancreatic cancers in which 7, or 0.8 percent, were mismatch-repair deficient, all associated with Lynch syndrome.

IMM-021.citation: Chakrabarti S, Bucheit L, Starr JS, Innis-Shelton R, Shergill A, Dada H, et al. Detection of microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) by liquid biopsy predicts robust and durable response to immunotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer. J Immunother Cancer. 2022;10(6):e004485.
IMM-021.clinical_status: Retrospective real-world cohort supporting the existing FDA tissue-agnostic MSI-high/dMMR pembrolizumab indication (approval recorded by TX). Guardant360 is an FDA-approved companion/comprehensive genomic profiling test; its MSI-high result is used in routine US practice (checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-021.design: Retrospective multi-institutional cohort using a commercial liquid-biopsy database, with chart-derived treatment and RECIST outcomes; concordance analysis against tissue immunohistochemistry where available.
IMM-021.population: Patients with PDAC in the Guardant central database whose tumours were found MSI-high by a validated plasma circulating-tumour-DNA assay (Guardant360) performed as part of routine clinical care between 1 October 2018 and April 2021 (multi-institution, real-world US practice).
IMM-021.n: 10 PDAC patients identified as MSI-high by plasma ctDNA; 9 evaluable for outcome (1 died before receiving immunotherapy). Tissue MMR immunohistochemistry was available in 6/10 (60%).
IMM-021.time_frame: Liquid biopsies performed 1 October 2018 to April 2021; median follow-up 21 months (range 11-33).
IMM-021.finding: RESPONSE: overall response rate by RECIST 77% (7/9), and 6 of the 7 responders were STILL RESPONDING at data cut-off after a median follow-up of 21 months (range 11-33) (Fig 1). Median progression-free survival and median overall survival were NOT REACHED. Median duration of immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy 8 months (range 1-24). 7/9 (78%) were alive at data cut-off. ASSAY CONCORDANCE: of the 6 cases with tissue immunohistochemistry, all but one were concordant; in the DISCORDANT case, immunohistochemistry on a pancreatic body mass biopsy FAILED to identify mismatch-repair deficiency, while Guardant360 obtained two weeks before starting immunotherapy identified MSI-high - that patient received neoadjuvant ipilimumab plus nivolumab. Several patients also had homologous-recombination-repair alterations detected alongside MSI-high. The authors note the prevalence of an MSI-high…
IMM-021.effect: ORR 77% (7/9) with 6/7 responses ongoing at a median 21 months - an order of magnitude above the <5% response rate of checkpoint blockade in unselected PDAC. Tissue immunohistochemistry was falsely negative in 1 of 6 cases tested.
IMM-021.limitations: n=9 evaluable; retrospective commercial database; no central radiology review; tissue immunohistochemistry available in only 6/10; no comparison of liquid-biopsy-detected versus tissue-detected patients' outcomes.
IMM-021.interpretation: Single-group cohort with a biologically specified biomarker and an effect size far outside the range achievable by selection alone in this disease: this supports a strong causal inference that MSI-high status identifies PDAC in which PD-1 blockade produces durable responses. The discordant case supports a causal claim about assay sensitivity (a…

glosses.antigen-presentation: A retrospective series of 10 pancreatic cancers found microsatellite-instability-high by plasma testing, 7 of 9 evaluable patients responding to checkpoint blockade with most responses ongoing at 21 months.
glosses.msi-mmr: A real-world cohort in which a blood test found a mismatch-repair-deficient pancreatic cancer that tissue staining had missed.
glosses.molecular-testing: A cohort in which a blood test found a mismatch-repair-deficient cancer that tissue staining had missed.
glosses.eus-biopsy: A real-world series in which a blood assay detected mismatch-repair deficiency that a tissue stain had missed in one of six cases.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: A real-world series of 9 pancreatic cancers identified as MSI-high by blood testing, 7 of which responded to checkpoint blockade, including one that tissue staining had missed.
glosses.immune-combinations: A real-world series of nine pancreatic cancers identified as MSI-high by blood testing, seven of which responded to checkpoint blockade with six responses ongoing at a median 21 months.

IMM-022.citation: Nair N, Chen SY, Lemmens E, Chang S, Le DT, Jaffee EM, et al. Single-Cell Immune Competency Signatures Associate with Survival in Phase II GVAX and CRS-207 Randomized Studies in Patients with Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer. Cancer Immunol Res. 2020;8(5):609-617.
IMM-022.clinical_status: Biomarker research; no immune-competency assay is FDA-cleared for selecting PDAC immunotherapy (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-022.design: Biomarker discovery and verification across two randomized trials. Discovery: 38-antibody mass cytometry (CyTOF) of PBMCs at baseline and 7 and 10 weeks, with CITRUS (cluster identification, characterization and regression) unsupervised cluster discovery, verified by manual biaxial gating.…
IMM-022.population: Previously treated patients with stage IV metastatic PDAC, ECOG 0-1, no radiographic ascites or clinically significant pleural effusion, enrolled in two randomized vaccine trials: a phase 2a of Cy/GVAX plus CRS-207 versus Cy/GVAX alone (discovery subcohort), and the phase 2b ECLIPSE study of…
IMM-022.n: Discovery subcohort n=38 (phase 2a); verification subcohort n=200 (phase 2b, NCT02004262).
IMM-022.time_frame: Baseline, 7-week and 10-week sampling within the parent trials; OS followed within those trials.
IMM-022.finding: At baseline, the abundance of EIGHT cell clusters in the CD8+ T-cell and myeloid lineages was associated with overall survival (Fig 1B). The phenotypes correlating with OS ACROSS BOTH TREATMENT ARMS were CD8+CD45RO-CCR7-CD57+ (also CD45RA+CD127-, HLA-DR low/negative, CD38 low/negative, PD-1+) and CD14+CD33+CD85j+ (also HLA-DR+CD11b+CD15-PD-L1+) (Fig 1C). Manual gating verification: baseline median frequency of CD8+CD45RO-CCR7-CD57+ cells was HIGHER in best responders than in poor/worst responders (P=0.0100); CD14+CD33+CD85j+ cells were higher in poor/worst responders, not significantly (P=0.0785) (Fig 1D, Table 2). Unsupervised hierarchical clustering split the 38 patients into Group 1 (n=11; high CD8+CD45RO-CCR7-CD57+, low CD14+CD33+CD85j+) and Group 2 (n=27; the inverse) (Fig 1E). Group 1 had LONGER OS than Group 2: median OS 271 days (range 43-1,247) versus 77 days (range 24-1,247),…
IMM-022.effect: Baseline immune-competency group: median OS 271 versus 77 days (P=0.0442), i.e. roughly a 3.5-fold difference in median survival explained by pretreatment peripheral immune composition alone, present in every treatment arm.
IMM-022.limitations: Discovery n=38 with multiplicity; functional role of the identified subsets not established; verification cohort analysis was prospective-retrospective; the parent trials were themselves negative, so the signature identifies survivors rather than beneficiaries.
IMM-022.interpretation: Because the signature was measured BEFORE treatment and tracked survival equally in all randomized arms, this design cleanly separates host immune competence (prognostic) from vaccine effect (predictive). It is the strongest available argument that on-treatment responder/non-responder survival splits in single-arm vaccine trials can be generated…

glosses.clinical-trials: A study showing a pre-treatment blood immune profile predicted survival equally in control and vaccine arms of randomized trials.
glosses.mrna-vaccines: A biomarker study across two randomized vaccine trials in metastatic pancreatic cancer, in which an immune profile measured before treatment split median survival 271 versus 77 days equally in every arm.
glosses.what-counts-as-progress: An analysis across two randomized vaccine trials showing that a pre-treatment blood immune profile predicted survival equally in every arm.

IMM-023.citation: Plesset J, Stone ML, McVey JC, Coho H, Markowitz K, Coho K, et al. TLR2 signaling regulates T cell exclusion in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. JCI Insight. 2026;11(10):e195329.
IMM-023.clinical_status: Preclinical only; no TLR2-directed agent is FDA-approved or in registered PDAC trials known to this review (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-023.design: Comparative-model plus perturbation design. Step 1: compare infiltration of adoptively transferred tumour-specific T cells between T-cell-high and T-cell-low tumours. Step 2: cross-species transcriptional profiling to nominate candidates correlated with T-cell infiltration. Step 3: flow-cytometric…
IMM-023.population: Mouse PDAC tumour models stratified a priori into T-cell-high and T-cell-low tumours, with adoptive transfer of tumour-specific T cells; transcriptional profiling performed in BOTH mice and humans; T-cell-specific TLR2 deletion.
IMM-023.n: Mouse cohorts per figure panel; human data from transcriptional profiling of PDAC.
IMM-023.time_frame: Preclinical; not stated in the accessed text.
IMM-023.finding: PDAC infiltration by adoptively transferred tumour-specific T cells was ENHANCED in tumour models that already had high endogenous T-cell infiltration - i.e. the capacity to admit transferred cells is a property of the tumour, not of the product. Transcriptional profiling in mice AND humans identified TLR2 as increased in the tumour microenvironment and POSITIVELY correlated with T-cell infiltration. Flow cytometry showed significantly increased TLR2+CD8+ T cells and TLR2+F4/80+ macrophages in T-cell-high versus T-cell-low tumours, with no difference in TLR2+CD11c+F4/80- dendritic cells (Fig 2D-G). Candidate endogenous TLR2 ligands expressed in tumours included Hmgb1. Functionally, and in the opposite direction from the correlation, TLR2 signalling INHIBITS T-cell infiltration into tumours, and T-cell-specific deletion of TLR2 implicates the T cell itself as a site of action.
IMM-023.effect: Not expressed as a single effect size in the accessed text; the decisive results are directional: TLR2 is higher where T cells are more abundant, yet TLR2 signalling restrains T-cell entry, and the restraint is at least partly T-cell-intrinsic.
IMM-023.limitations: Preclinical; human contribution limited to transcriptional correlation; quantitative effect sizes and group sizes not captured in the accessed sections; no therapeutic TLR2 antagonist tested clinically in PDAC.
IMM-023.interpretation: Cell-type-specific genetic deletion establishes causation in a preparation and localises the mechanism to the T cell rather than only to the stroma. Combined with the human transcriptional correlation it is a cross-scale link. It does not establish that TLR2 blockade would help patients.

glosses.t-cells: A mouse study, supported by human transcriptional profiling, showing TLR2 signaling on T cells themselves restrains their entry into pancreatic tumors.

IMM-024.citation: Tsujikawa T, Crocenzi T, Durham JN, Sugar EA, Wu AA, Onners B, et al. Evaluation of Cyclophosphamide/GVAX Pancreas Followed by Listeria-Mesothelin (CRS-207) with or without Nivolumab in Patients with Pancreatic Cancer. Clin Cancer Res. 2020;26(14):3578-3588.
IMM-024.clinical_status: Negative randomized phase 2. Neither GVAX, CRS-207 nor this combination is FDA-approved (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-024.design: Open-label randomized phase 2. Primary efficacy endpoint: OS comparison of arm A versus arm B by log-rank, in all randomized subjects who received at least one dose. Original sample size 88 (44/arm) for 80% power to detect HR 1.66 (median OS 6 to 9.96 months) at two-sided alpha 0.15; revised to…
IMM-024.population: Adults with previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer at 5 US sites. A substantial minority had undergone prior resection with curative intent, unevenly distributed between arms (24% arm A vs 52% arm B).
IMM-024.n: 96 patients enrolled and randomized across 5 US sites; 3 (all arm B) never treated and excluded; 93 analysed (arm A n=51, arm B n=42). Median duration on treatment 64 and 61 days.
IMM-024.time_frame: Sample size revised October 2015; analysis at 87% of expected events.
IMM-024.finding: PRIMARY ENDPOINT NOT MET. Median OS 5.9 months (95% CI 4.7-8.6) in arm A versus 6.1 months (95% CI 3.5-7.0) in arm B; HAZARD RATIO 0.86 (95% CI 0.55-1.34), with 87% of expected events having occurred. 12- and 18-month OS rates 25% and 18% (arm A) versus 19% and 12% (arm B). The design was permissive (two-sided alpha 0.15, powered for an implausibly large HR of 1.66), so the failure is not attributable to a stringent threshold. The authors state the study 'did not meet the ambitious goal of showing a survival advantage to the addition of a PD-1 inhibitor to a prime-boost vaccination strategy', while noting 'signs of clinical activity coupled with evidence of immunologic changes in the peripheral blood and tumor microenvironment'. Historical context given in the paper: in an earlier GVAX-plus-ipilimumab experience (n=15), 7 patients had CA19-9 responses and 3 had prolonged stable disease…
IMM-024.effect: OS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.55-1.34) for adding nivolumab to Cy/GVAX -> CRS-207; absolute median OS difference -0.2 months. Documented immunologic changes in blood and tumour in the same patients.
IMM-024.limitations: Open-label; both arms received the same investigational vaccine so there is no chemotherapy or standard-of-care control; baseline imbalance in prior resection; heavily pretreated metastatic population; alpha 0.15.
IMM-024.interpretation: Randomized with the vaccine backbone held constant in both arms: this is a clean causal test of adding PD-1 blockade on top of a vaccine, and it is negative. Because immunologic changes were documented in both blood and tumour while OS was unchanged, it independently replicates the trigger dissociation in a second, larger randomized cohort than…

IMM-025.citation: Seki T, Araki K, Yokobori T, Ikota H, Kubo N, Igarashi T, et al. CD86-Positive Mature Tertiary Lymphoid Structures Are Associated With CD8+ T-Cell Infiltration and Favorable Clinical Outcomes in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma. Ann Gastroenterol Surg. 2026. doi:10.1002/ags3.70275.
IMM-025.clinical_status: Observational pathology; TLS assessment is not a validated or approved biomarker for therapy selection in PDAC (US, checked 2026-10-08).
IMM-025.design: Retrospective two-centre cohort with prespecified histological scoring. Tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) evaluation area defined as a 1-mm-wide band centred on the tumour margin spanning intratumoural and extratumoural sides. Serial sections stained by immunohistochemistry for CD20 (B cells),…
IMM-025.population: 128 patients with PDAC who underwent radical surgical resection at Gunma University Hospital or Saiseikai Maebashi Hospital between 2007 and 2022. NONE received neoadjuvant therapy - so the immune architecture is treatment-naive.
IMM-025.finding: DISTRIBUTION: median maximum TLS diameter 0.53 mm (range 0.10-1.16); median TLS density 0.17 counts/mm (range 0.02-1.39). TLSs were ABSENT in only 4/128 (3.1%). Of the 124 TLS-positive cases, 13 (10.2%) were immature, 21 (16.4%) intermediate and 90 (70.3%) mature (Fig 1D) - i.e. TLSs are near-universal in resected PDAC and most are histologically mature, which by itself argues that TLS presence cannot explain why PDAC is immunologically inert. OUTCOME: the TLS-positive groups had significantly better OS and RFS than the TLS-absent group (P=0.010 and P=0.014; Fig 3D). The CD86-positive mature TLS group showed a TREND toward more favourable OS and RFS than the CD86-negative mature TLS group. In UNIVARIATE Cox regression, absence of CD86-positive mature TLS was significantly associated with poor OS: hazard ratio 1.79 (95% CI 1.11-2.87), P=0.017 (Table 2). In MULTIVARIATE analysis, absence…
IMM-025.effect: CD86-positive mature TLS absence: univariate OS HR 1.79 (95% CI 1.11-2.87), P=0.017, LOST on multivariable adjustment. TLS present in 124/128 (96.9%) and mature in 90/128 (70.3%).
IMM-025.limitations: Retrospective; two centres; only 4 TLS-absent cases, so the TLS-positive-versus-absent comparison rests on a tiny reference group; one scoring task had poor inter-observer agreement (kappa 0.35); no treatment interaction tested because the cohort received no immunotherapy; neoadjuvant-naive only, so not generalisable to the neoadjuvant/MRD settings where vaccines are now tested.
IMM-025.interpretation: Observational with prespecified scoring and formal multivariable adjustment. Its value is as a boundary condition: it shows that local lymphoid organisation correlates with CD8 infiltration and crude survival but is confounded by stage, so the 'build better local priming structures' hypothesis is not supported as an independent causal driver by…

IMM-026.citation: Luksza M, Sethna ZM, Rojas LA, Lihm J, Bravi B, Elhanati Y, et al. Neoantigen quality predicts immunoediting in survivors of pancreatic cancer. Nature. 2022;606(7913):389-395.
IMM-026.design: Longitudinal multi-sample tumour evolution study with joint multisample phylogenetic reconstruction, neoantigen quality scoring (amplitude C and cross-reactivity D terms) and a fitness model used to predict which clones are immunoedited.
IMM-026.population: 70 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas from 15 patients, comprising long-term survivors (LTSs) and short-term survivors (STSs), followed longitudinally over 10 years from primary tumour to recurrence.
IMM-026.finding: Design rationale quantified: human PDACs harbour on average 35 neoantigens, versus ~112 in non-small-cell lung cancer and ~370 in melanoma, and PDAC T-cell infiltrates span a nearly 1,000-fold range, so PDAC contains both immune-deficient and immune-proficient extremes. LTS primary tumours had around 12-fold more activated CD8+ T cells than STS primary tumours, predicted to target immunogenic neoantigens. Neoantigens with both higher amplitude (C) and higher cross-reactivity (D) were strikingly more DEPLETED in LTS than STS tumours over time (Fig 3i) - tumours in long-term survivors selectively lose high-quality neoantigens. Importantly, genes in the HLA class-I pathway were NOT differentially mutated, deleted, expressed or mislocalised in STS versus LTS PDACs (Ext Data Fig 8a-c), so the neoantigen depletion in LTSs occurred WITHOUT acquired HLA class-I resistance. Incorporating…
IMM-026.effect: ~12-fold higher activated CD8+ T-cell density in long-term-survivor primary tumours; selective depletion of high-quality (high C, high D) neoantigens in long-term survivors, without HLA class-I pathway alteration.
IMM-026.limitations: Small cohort; model-dependent; same cohort as the TME-owned landmark; no interventional component.
IMM-026.interpretation: Longitudinal natural experiment: because the same patients are followed from primary tumour to recurrence and the predicted-high-quality neoantigens are the ones that disappear, it supports the inference that human T-cell pressure genuinely edits PDAC clones - the positive control proving the machinery CAN work in this disease without any therapy.

glosses.antigen-presentation: A ten-year longitudinal study of 70 tumors from 15 patients showing human T-cell pressure selectively removes high-quality neoantigens in long-term survivors without any change to the HLA class I pathway.
glosses.mrna-vaccines: An analysis of long-term survivors showing pancreatic cancers carry around 35 predicted neoantigens on average, far fewer than lung cancer or melanoma, and that high-quality neoantigens are selectively lost in survivors.

IMM-027.citation: O'Connor CA, Harrold E, Lin D, Walch H, Gazzo A, Ranganathan M, et al. Lynch Syndrome and Somatic Mismatch Repair Variants in Pancreas Cancer. JAMA Oncol. 2024;10(11):1511-1518.
IMM-027.clinical_status: Retrospective cohort supporting the existing FDA tissue-agnostic MSI-high/dMMR pembrolizumab pathway (the approval itself is recorded by the TX domain). Practical consequence for US availability: because roughly half of MMR-variant pancreatic cancers are microsatellite stable, roughly half the…
IMM-027.design: Single-institution retrospective cross-sectional analysis, March 2012 to July 2023. Microsatellite status was determined as a COMPOSITE across orthogonal methods (immunohistochemistry, PCR, next-generation sequencing) with an artificial-intelligence microsatellite classifier applied to account for…
IMM-027.population: 55 patients with pancreatic cancer and a mismatch-repair (MMR) gene variant, identified from 4626 pancreatic cancer cases queried at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. Two cohorts: Lynch syndrome with a germline pathogenic variant (n=32; 29 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, 2 pancreatic…
IMM-027.n: 55 patients with an MMR variant out of 4626 pancreatic cancer cases queried (1.2%); Lynch cohort n=32, somatic MMR cohort n=23; 20 patients received immune checkpoint blockade, of whom 17 were…
IMM-027.time_frame: Cases accrued March 2012 to July 2023; checkpoint-therapy duration followed to a median of 27.7 months.
IMM-027.finding: PREVALENCE AND ORIGIN: 55/4626 (1.2%) of queried pancreatic cancer cases carried an MMR variant. Lynch cohort germline genes: MSH2 10/32 (31%), MSH6 9/32 (28%), PMS2 8/32 (25%), MLH1 4/32 (13%, one an epimutation), EPCAM 1/32 (3%). Somatic MMR cohort genes: MSH6 11/23 (48%), MLH1 7/23 (30%), MSH2 3/23 (13%), PMS2 2/23 (9%). COMPOSITE MICROSATELLITE STATUS: Lynch cohort 17 (59%) MSI-high, 12 (41%) microsatellite stable, 3 unknown; somatic cohort 10 (43%) MSI-high, 11 (48%) stable, 2 (9%) indeterminate. Overall, an MMR variant conferred MSI-high in roughly 50% of patients - carrying the variant is NOT the same as having an immunotherapy-responsive tumour. MISCLASSIFICATION: the artificial-intelligence classifier RECLASSIFIED cases as MSI-high that initial testing had not - 5 cases in the Lynch cohort and 6 in the somatic cohort, approximately 20% of cases overall, most of them…
IMM-027.effect: MMR variants in 1.2% of 4626 pancreatic cancers; MSI-high in ~50% of variant carriers; ~20% of cases reclassified as MSI-high only after orthogonal/AI testing; median checkpoint-therapy duration 27.7 months with an 80% disease control rate in 20 treated patients. Published MSI-high pancreatic objective response rates span 18.2% to 83%.
IMM-027.limitations: Single-centre, retrospective, no external validation, small cohort, relative lack of racial and ethnic diversity (stated by the authors); 20 treated patients with heterogeneous checkpoint regimens and lines of therapy; objective response rate for this cohort is reported as disease control rate rather than a centrally reviewed RECIST response rate; two responders carried variants of unknown significance.
IMM-027.interpretation: Retrospective cross-sectional design: it cannot estimate a treatment effect, but it establishes three things the branch needed. First, the ORIGIN question is answered descriptively - somatic MMR variants account for a substantial share of MSI-high pancreatic cancer, so germline testing alone under-ascertains the eligible population. Second, the…

glosses.msi-mmr: A cohort showing an MMR variant conferred high microsatellite instability in only about half of carriers.
glosses.pembrolizumab-msi: A series of 55 pancreatic cancers with mismatch-repair gene variants, about half MSI-high, a fifth recognized only after orthogonal testing, with an 80 percent disease-control rate on checkpoint blockade.

INF-ANAT-01.phenomenon: New-onset diabetes resolves after resection of a head tumour, whereas healthy donors who lose the same or more parenchyma by hemipancreatectomy become dysglycemic.
INF-ANAT-01.missing: What makes tumour-associated beta-cell dysfunction reversible while surgical mass loss is not.
INF-ANAT-01.mechanism: The tumour imposes a functional, mediator-driven suppression of insulin secretion and/or insulin resistance on a numerically preserved beta-cell mass; removing the tumour withdraws the mediator and function recovers, whereas surgery removes beta-cell mass irreversibly.
assumptions: Mediator effects in rodent islets/cell lines transfer to human islets
Residual beta-cell mass in PDAC patients is near-normal at diagnosis
supporting: ANAT-015
ANAT-016
ANAT-014
ANAT-025
conflicting: ANAT-026
ANAT-006
INF-ANAT-01.competing: Structural beta-cell loss (TGF-beta-driven apoptosis) rather than reversible dysfunction; apparent resolution could be post-operative weight loss and altered nutrition.
INF-ANAT-01.prediction: If functional, C-peptide/insulin response should recover after resection despite unchanged beta-cell mass on imaging/autopsy; if structural, beta-cell mass should be measurably reduced at diagnosis and not recover.
INF-ANAT-01.test: Serial mixed-meal C-peptide before and after resection in new-onset PDAC-diabetes versus matched type 2 diabetes, with islet autoantibody and (where available) autopsy/biopsy beta-cell quantification.
INF-ANAT-01.implication: Supports using new-onset diabetes as an early-detection sieve and suggests the mediator itself could be a biomarker; does not by itself recommend any therapy.

premises.statement: PDAC-diabetes is independent of tumour size/location and resolves in 57% of new-onset cases after pancreaticoduodenectomy.
Hyperglycemia tracks tumour volume above ~1 cc and reverses after resection regardless of location.
Tumour-secreted/exosomal adrenomedullin and TGF-beta impair or deplete beta-cells in preparations.
~50% surgical parenchymal loss causes persistent dysglycemia in healthy donors.
