glosses.diabetes-after-surgery: This atlas's proposed explanation for why cancer-associated diabetes can resolve after resection: a reversible, mediator-driven suppression of insulin function rather than islet loss.

INF-ANAT-02.phenomenon: Pancreatic cancer is painless early (and so diagnosed late) but severely painful when advanced, and the Schwann cell appears on both sides of this.
INF-ANAT-02.missing: The signal that switches peripheral glia from a pain-suppressing to a pain-promoting state as the tumour grows.
INF-ANAT-02.mechanism: As hypoxia and tumour burden rise, tumour secretion shifts (e.g., toward GDF15) and reprograms recruited Schwann cells from an analgesic, CXCL12-responsive state to an algesic, CCN3+/neurotrophin-secreting state that sensitises TRPV1/CGRP afferents.
assumptions: Mouse orthotopic kinetics reflect human time course
The same Schwann-cell pool transitions rather than two independent populations
supporting: ANAT-012
ANAT-029
ANAT-002
INF-ANAT-02.competing: Early and late pain states involve distinct, independently recruited glial populations; or late pain is mainly non-neural (capsular distension, obstruction, metastasis).
INF-ANAT-02.test: Lineage-tracing of CXCL12-responsive Schwann cells in an autochthonous model across time to test whether the same cells acquire the CCN3+/GDF15-responsive phenotype as pain emerges, with staged plasma GDF15/CXCL12 in patients.
INF-ANAT-02.implication: Explains the clinically important painless early window and identifies GDF15 as a candidate pain biomarker/target; does not itself prescribe an analgesic strategy (owned by SUPP).

premises.statement: Early PanIN lesions recruit Schwann cells via CXCL12/CXCR4-7 and suppress nociception, with lower neural CXCR7 in painful human tumours.
Established tumours induce a GDF15/GFRAL-driven CCN3+ Schwann-cell subset that promotes sensory-fibre growth and pain, with plasma GDF15 tracking patient pain.
Mast-cell enrichment and neurotrophin excess accompany pain in resected (advanced) tumours.

glosses.pain: An inference record proposing that Schwann cells switch from a pain-suppressing to a pain-promoting state as the tumor grows.
glosses.nerve-plexus: Published hypothesis, recorded by the atlas, that Schwann cells switch from suppressing to promoting pain as the tumor advances.

INF-ANAT-03.phenomenon: Blunted pancreatic-polypeptide response in cancer-associated diabetes appears to be strongest for head tumours, yet the diabetes/hyperglycemia itself is location-independent.
INF-ANAT-03.missing: Whether the PP signal reflects destruction of the anatomically localised ventral PP-cell compartment or a general islet effect shared with the glycemic change.
INF-ANAT-03.mechanism: A blunted PP response marks functional loss of the ventral PP-cell field by a head tumour (a local, location-specific readout), whereas the hyperglycemia is a separate, mediator-driven whole-islet effect - so PP and glucose report different lesions.
assumptions: Mixed-meal PP reflects ventral-field integrity rather than vagal tone or cachexia
Body/tail tumours spare enough PP cells to preserve the response
supporting: ANAT-017
ANAT-005
ANAT-042
conflicting: ANAT-015
INF-ANAT-03.competing: PP blunting is a general feature of pancreatogenic diabetes (it is also seen in chronic pancreatitis) driven by vagal/enteric dysfunction rather than ventral-field anatomy.
INF-ANAT-03.test: Adequately powered mixed-meal PP testing stratified by head/uncinate versus body/tail tumour location with imaging of the ventral field, in PDAC-diabetes versus chronic-pancreatitis-diabetes versus type 2 diabetes.
INF-ANAT-03.implication: If location-specific, a blunted PP response could help localise and distinguish pancreatogenic diabetes for early detection; remains a diagnostic inference, not a treatment claim.

premises.statement: PP cells are concentrated in the ventral head/uncinate process.
PP meal-response is blunted in PDAC-associated new-onset diabetes versus type 2 diabetes (78% proximal tumours), without a powered location subgroup.
A pilot found PP blunting only in head tumours, not body/tail.
Hyperglycemia is independent of head-versus-tail location.

glosses.pancreas-head: Published hypothesis, recorded by the atlas, that a blunted pancreatic polypeptide response marks local damage to the head while hyperglycemia is a whole-gland effect.
glosses.islets: Published hypothesis, recorded by the atlas, that a blunted pancreatic polypeptide response marks local damage to the head while hyperglycemia is a whole-gland effect.

INF-ORIG-01.phenomenon: Only a tiny minority of the hundreds of KRAS-mutant PanINs in a normal pancreas ever progress, and the progressing minority is marked by chromosomal loss of CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 rather than by any distinctive initiating mutation.
INF-ORIG-01.missing: What determines WHICH lesion acquires those losses. The baseline has no variable standing between a stalled KRAS-mutant lesion and one that becomes genomically unstable.
INF-ORIG-01.mechanism: Local, focal inflammation is the variable that converts a senescent KRAS-mutant PanIN into a proliferating one. Senescence escape permits continued division, and continued division in a lesion that has already lost normal checkpoint restraint is what allows chromosomal missegregation and the copy-number losses at CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 to accumulate and be selected. On this account the immune hotspot is not merely a consequence of higher grade but part of the permissive machinery, and the extreme spatial patchiness of inflammation (50% decay within 40 um) is exactly why only a few lesions in a field of many progress.
assumptions: Mouse caerulein pancreatitis models the focal, subclinical inflammation seen around human PanINs
The senescence barrier demonstrated for Kras-G12V-expressing mouse acinar cells also operates in human PanIN, supported only by P16INK4a staining in nine chronic pancreatitis patients
Immune hotspots identified in surgical resection specimens behave as they would in an otherwise healthy pancreas, which the authors of ORIG-024 explicitly flag as unverified
Copy-number instability is a consequence of proliferation rather than an independent initiating event
supporting: Pancreatitis is both a strong human risk factor and the experimental variable that unlocks progression in mice (ORIG-014)
Sulindac reduced mPanIN/mPDAC development, a pharmacological perturbation in the predicted direction (ORIG-014)
Hotspots co-localise with the specific features the model predicts — high-grade dysplasia, reactive stroma and ADM (ORIG-024)
Larger PanINs, i.e. those that have proliferated more, carry higher Treg fractions (ORIG-024)
conflicting: Adult acinar Kras-G12D produced the full mPanIN spectrum with no imposed inflammation, so inflammation is not strictly necessary (ORIG-021)

Bulk pancreatic inflammation correlated as strongly with acinar atrophy and stromal density as with PanIN burden, so inflammation may be driven by ductal obstruction rather than by neoplasia (ORIG-024)
Duct-derived tumours in mice reach invasion faster and apparently without engaging a low-grade senescent stage at all, so at least one route bypasses this mechanism entirely (ORIG-003, ORIG-013)
INF-ORIG-01.competing: Progression is cell-intrinsic and stochastic: copy-number instability arises from replication errors at a fixed low rate per cell division, so the progressing lesion is simply the one that got unlucky, and the immune hotspot is a downstream reaction to the resulting higher-grade, more antigenic, more obstructive lesion. This explanation accounts for all the same cross-sectional observations…
INF-ORIG-01.prediction: If focal inflammation drives the transition, then in a mouse model where PanINs can be mapped in 3D and immune hotspots scored, hotspot status at an early time point should predict which individual lesions later show copy-number instability and high-grade morphology — and an anti-inflammatory or Treg-depleting intervention applied AFTER lesions are established should reduce the fraction…
INF-ORIG-01.test: A longitudinal mouse study combining serial-section 3D immune mapping (the CODA approach of ORIG-024 applied to a Kras-driven model) with lesion-level single-cell copy-number sequencing at staggered time points, plus a randomised post-initiation intervention arm (COX inhibition or Treg depletion) and lesion-number versus lesion-grade as separate endpoints. In humans the nearest feasible design…
INF-ORIG-01.implication: If supported, the rate-limiting step for human pancreatic cancer is focal inflammation acting on lesions that already exist in nearly everyone, which would make the relevant target the inflammatory niche rather than the precursor lesion, and would make lesion COUNT an almost useless risk marker while making lesion-level inflammatory state a candidate one. This is a statement about where to look,…

premises.statement: PanINs are ubiquitous and 92-95% carry KRAS codon-12 mutations at every grade, with mutant cells a minority of the lesion at low grade.
CDKN2A point mutation is rare in low-grade PanIN (11.5%), but somatic copy-number loss at 9p21, 17p and 18q was present in all 11 high-grade PanINs examined (mean 2.7 gains, 4.3 losses per lesion).

Low-grade PanINs in mice are held in oncogene-induced senescence, and episodic pancreatitis abrogates that barrier; human chronic pancreatitis specimens from patients given anti-inflammatory drugs contained…

PanINs are the most inflamed structures in grossly normal pancreas, and discrete immunosuppressive hotspots enriched for FOXP3+ cells localise to higher-grade dysplasia, reactive stroma and ADM, with FOXP3+ rising from…

glosses.acinar-cells: Published hypothesis, recorded by the atlas, that focal inflammation is the rate-limiting step converting a senescent KRAS-mutant lesion into a progressing one.
glosses.genome-evolution: A published hypothesis that focal inflammation gates the progression of precursor lesions by releasing senescence.
glosses.panin: A published hypothesis that focal inflammation gates the progression of precursor lesions by releasing senescence.
glosses.cell-of-origin: A published hypothesis that focal inflammation gates the progression of precursor lesions by releasing senescence.
glosses.risk-factors: A published hypothesis that focal inflammation gates the progression of precursor lesions by releasing senescence.

INF-ORIG-02.phenomenon: Histologically identical pancreatic tissue differs by hundreds of proteins depending on whether the organ contains a cancer — 192 proteins in normal-appearing ducts and 301 in low-grade PanIN — and separately, a pancreas containing a watched IPMN develops cancer elsewhere in the gland more often than the watched lesion becomes cancer.
INF-ORIG-02.missing: Whether the organ-wide molecular difference is a precondition that makes the whole gland cancer-prone, or a reaction to a cancer that is already present. The baseline has no organ-level state variable at all, so it cannot represent either reading.
INF-ORIG-02.mechanism: A field state — most plausibly chronic low-grade injury with ductal obstruction, acinar atrophy and stromal remodeling — raises the transformation probability of every independent clone across the gland simultaneously. Because PanINs arise as hundreds of independent clones, a modest organ-wide shift in transformation probability translates into a materially higher chance that SOME clone progresses, anywhere, without any individual lesion being distinguishable in advance. The IPMN would then be a visible marker of the field rather than the main hazard within it, which is why concomitant cancer exceeds cyst-derived cancer and why no cyst morphology predicts it.
assumptions: Protein-level differences in FFPE tissue reflect a durable tissue state rather than acute perianalytical or ischaemic differences between organ-donor and surgical specimens
The multiclonal architecture of PanIN means organ-level risk scales with clone number, which has not been modelled against observed incidence

INF-TME-01.phenomenon: Interventions on the pancreatic tumour stroma produce opposite effects on survival depending on the tool used, even within the same species and similar models.
INF-TME-01.missing: No study links a single measured stromal composition variable to the sign of the treatment effect. The connection between 'how much stroma' and 'what happens to the animal' is missing a term for 'which fibroblast'.
INF-TME-01.mechanism: The net effect of a stromal intervention is set by the resulting ratio of immune-suppressive fibroblast states (LRRC15+/CD105+/myCAF-like, which suppress CD8 function and support growth) to tumour-restraining states (CD105-negative and collagen-producing myofibroblasts, which maintain differentiation, limit angiogenesis and sustain cDC1-dependent adaptive immunity). Tools that act on the restraining population - hedgehog inhibition, aSMA-driven ablation, collagen deletion - shift the ratio towards suppression and shorten survival; tools that act on the suppressive population, or that convert cells to a quiescent non-suppressive state, shift it the other way.

INF-TME-02.phenomenon: Two independent interventions - hyaluronidase and hydroxychloroquine - each significantly increased the proportion of patients whose tumours shrank on imaging while leaving survival unchanged or numerically worse.
INF-TME-02.missing: The baseline has no step connecting shrinkage of the measured lesion to length of life. What determines survival in metastatic PDAC is not captured by any link in the current baseline.
INF-TME-02.mechanism: Both agents improve control of the index lesions - more drug reaching cells, or cells less able to survive stress - but survival in metastatic PDAC is governed by disease outside those lesions (micrometastatic burden present at diagnosis, and host factors such as performance status, nutrition and treatment tolerance). Added toxicity then reduces delivered chemotherapy dose intensity and functional reserve, offsetting the local gain. Net effect: measurable shrinkage, unchanged or slightly worse survival.
assumptions: That radiographic response in PDAC largely reflects the stromal and index-lesion compartment rather than total body tumour burden
That the toxicity-driven dose-intensity reduction is large enough to matter, which neither trial reported in a form that allows this to be checked
supporting: Identical direction and similar magnitude of the dissociation in two mechanistically unrelated randomised trials (TME-004, TME-027)
Substantially higher toxicity in the hyaluronidase arm, with all patients also receiving prophylactic enoxaparin (TME-004)
Early widespread dissemination is a documented feature of PDAC biology (ORIG and GENE domains), consistent with survival being set outside the index lesion
conflicting: In TME-027 hydroxychloroquine toxicity was not reported as markedly higher, so the toxicity arm of the explanation is weakly supported there

TME-016 reports long survival (31.4 months) in locally advanced disease treated with a matrix-directed agent plus intensive chemotherapy, which would be unexpected if local control never translated - though that trial…
The HALO-301 placebo arm outperformed its historical assumption (11.5 versus 8.5 months), so reduced power rather than a true null is a live alternative
INF-TME-02.competing: Simple statistical and design explanation: both trials were powered for larger effects than exist, HALO-301 used 2:1 allocation and an optimistic historical assumption, and the response-rate gains are real but too small to move survival detectably. On this account there is no biological dissociation to explain, only an underpowered test of a modest effect.
INF-TME-02.prediction: If the dissociation is driven by extra-lesional disease plus toxicity-mediated dose reduction, then in these datasets the response-rate benefit should be largest in patients with the lowest metastatic burden, delivered chemotherapy dose intensity should be measurably lower in the experimental arms, and the survival hazard ratio should approach the response benefit in a subgroup with low burden…
INF-TME-02.test: A secondary analysis of the HALO-301 and hydroxychloroquine trial datasets reporting delivered chemotherapy dose intensity by arm, response and survival stratified by baseline metastatic burden and by circulating tumour DNA at baseline and at first restaging. Prospectively, any future stroma- or metabolism-directed trial should prespecify dose intensity and a molecular residual-disease measure…
INF-TME-02.implication: For the atlas this supports a specific caution to give visitors: in pancreatic cancer, a report that a tumour shrank is not by itself evidence that a treatment is extending life, and the two randomised examples here are the reason. It also implies that trials of local-control mechanisms should be judged on survival with dose intensity reported, not on response rate. It is not a recommendation…

premises.statement: Hyaluronidase added to chemotherapy raised objective response from 36% to 47% (ORR ratio 1.29, 95% CI 1.03-1.63) with a hazard ratio for death of 1.00 (95% CI 0.80-1.27).
Hydroxychloroquine added to chemotherapy raised objective response from 21.1% to 38.2% (P=.047) with 12-month survival of 41% versus 49%.
In mice, both mechanisms act on the local tumour mass: hyaluronidase through decompression and delivery, autophagy inhibition through tumour-cell metabolic failure.
Hyaluronidase added substantial systemic toxicity (musculoskeletal events 75.4% versus 46.2% any grade; grade >=3 fatigue 16.0% versus 9.6%).

glosses.reading-trial-results: This atlas's inference that response measures the index lesions while survival is set by disease elsewhere and by delivered dose intensity.
glosses.matrix-pressure: Atlas inference record proposing that tumor shrinkage and survival came apart in two randomized trials because survival in metastatic disease is governed by disease outside the measured lesions.
glosses.nutrient-scavenging: This atlas's reading of why two unrelated drugs each raised tumor shrinkage rates in randomized trials without improving survival.
glosses.stroma-lessons: An atlas inference on why two stroma- and metabolism-directed agents raised tumor response rates without improving survival.

INF-TME-03.phenomenon: Cytotoxic T cells can be present in human PDAC, can lie within 20 micrometres of cancer cells, and can be neoantigen-reactive, yet checkpoint blockade produces almost no responses.
INF-TME-03.missing: Nothing in the baseline explains why an adjacent, antigen-experienced T cell fails to kill. The baseline's only T-cell term is position (L-TME-08) and the clinical failure (L-TME-10), with no term for the functional state of a T cell that has reached its target.
INF-TME-03.mechanism: T cells that reach the cancer cells are functionally disarmed in situ by two convergent routes: antigen presentation without co-stimulation (by apCAFs, and by MHC class II on fibroblasts generally) which drives anergy or Treg differentiation rather than effector function; and the nutrient-poor, hypoxic interstitium plus direct fibroblast-derived suppression, which deprives the T cell of the glucose and glutamine that effector differentiation requires. Checkpoint blockade releases an inhibitory receptor but cannot restore co-stimulation or nutrients, so it has no substrate to act on.
assumptions: That the nutrient depletion measured in whole tumour tissue reflects the concentration a T cell experiences, which the authors of TME-028 explicitly say cannot be assigned to a compartment
That apCAFs, identified mainly in mice, perform the same function in human tumours
That the suppression is dominant over, rather than additive to, checkpoint-receptor inhibition
supporting: Direct CD8 suppression by a defined CAF subtype with improved checkpoint response on its depletion (TME-037)
Antigen presentation without co-stimulation demonstrated functionally, with the decoy hypothesis published by the discovering authors (TME-017)
Measured depletion of glucose and glutamine in human tumours (TME-028)
Checkpoint activity unmasked in mice only when a stromal or myeloid suppressor is removed first (TME-019, TME-020, TME-022)
Myofibroblast ablation expanding Tregs and lowering the effector/Treg ratio, with anti-CTLA-4 rescue (TME-012)
conflicting: TME-010 found higher collagen-I correlated with the presence of T-cell subpopulations rather than their absence, so the suppressive stroma and the T cells coexist without an obvious functional readout
TME-006 shows that in some patients this system fails and immunity apparently succeeds for years, so suppression cannot be uniform
No study in this domain measured exhaustion markers, metabolic state and spatial position in the same human tissue, so the mechanism is assembled across preparations
INF-TME-03.competing: Insufficient priming rather than local disarming: PDAC has a low mutational burden and few high-quality neoantigens (median 38 predicted per tumour), and cDC1 numbers are low, so the limiting step may be that too few tumour-specific T cells are ever generated. On this account the cells seen adjacent to cancer cells are largely bystanders of irrelevant specificity, and improving the local…
INF-TME-03.prediction: If local disarming dominates, then multiplexed analysis of the same human tumour regions should show that CD8 cells adjacent to cancer cells carry exhaustion and metabolic-stress signatures while retaining tumour-reactive TCR clonotypes, and that their proximity to MHC class II-positive fibroblasts predicts that state. If insufficient priming dominates, adjacent CD8 cells should be predominantly…
INF-TME-03.test: Paired single-cell TCR and transcriptome sequencing with spatial profiling on the same resected human PDAC specimens, linking each intratumoral CD8 clonotype to its position, its tumour reactivity (tested against autologous neoantigens), and its exhaustion and metabolic programme, with cDC1 density and fibroblast MHC class II as covariates. Pre- and post-treatment biopsies from any…
INF-TME-03.implication: For the atlas, this justifies telling visitors that in pancreatic cancer the problem is not simply that immune cells cannot get in - in many tumours they are already there and have been switched off, which is why releasing a single brake has not been enough and why research has moved to combinations. It is not a recommendation for or against any immunotherapy.

premises.statement: High cytotoxic T-cell infiltration within 20 micrometres of cancer cells correlates with longer survival, and collagen deposition does not reduce that infiltration; T-cell functional status was not measured.
Long-term survivors harbour intratumoral and circulating T-cell clones reactive to high-quality and MUC16 neoantigens.

A CAF state expresses MHC class II and CD74 without classical co-stimulatory molecules and ligates CD4 TCRs antigen-specifically; its authors hypothesise a decoy that anergises CD4 cells or induces Tregs.
Human PDAC tissue is depleted of glucose and glutamine relative to adjacent pancreas.
LRRC15+ myofibroblasts directly suppress tumour-infiltrating CD8 effector function, and depleting them augments anti-PD-L1 regression.

glosses.fibroblast-states: Atlas inference record carrying the published hypothesis that T cells reaching pancreatic cancer cells are disarmed in place by antigen presentation without co-stimulation and by a nutrient-poor environment.
glosses.t-cells: The published hypothesis that T cells reaching pancreatic cancer cells are disarmed in place by antigen without co-stimulation and by a nutrient-poor interstitium.

INF-DIAG-01.phenomenon: After neoadjuvant therapy, CT and MRI show persistent tumour-vessel contact that overwhelmingly turns out to be fibrosis, not viable tumour, so anatomic imaging over-calls unresectability.
INF-DIAG-01.missing: No routine imaging readout distinguishes treated acellular fibrosis from residual viable tumour at the vessel interface; the baseline links contact to invasion only in untreated disease.
INF-DIAG-01.mechanism: Viable tumour retains glucose metabolism (FDG uptake) and restricted diffusion, whereas chemoradiation-induced fibrosis is hypometabolic and less cellular; a functional signal (FDG-PET SUV/metabolic volume change, or MRI diffusion/ADC) at the residual contact should separate viable tumour from scar where anatomic contact cannot.
assumptions: FDG uptake is not dominated by post-treatment inflammation
Hyperglycaemia/diabetes, common in PDAC, does not void FDG quantitation
Diffusion restriction reflects cellularity rather than desmoplastic density
supporting: DIAG-008
DIAG-009
conflicting: DIAG-010
INF-DIAG-01.competing: Post-treatment inflammation and edema themselves cause FDG uptake and diffusion restriction, so a functional signal may over-call viable tumour just as anatomy over-calls contact.
INF-DIAG-01.prediction: In resected post-neoadjuvant specimens, voxel-level FDG avidity (or low ADC) at the vessel interface will correlate with histologic viable-tumour location, while matched fibrotic zones will be hypometabolic with high ADC.
INF-DIAG-01.test: Prospective radiologic-pathologic co-registration study mapping pre-surgical PET/MRI signal at the vessel interface to viable-tumour maps on the resected specimen, using a reliable (e.g., area-based) regression grade as reference.
INF-DIAG-01.implication: If confirmed, resectability after neoadjuvant therapy should be judged by functional viability at the interface rather than by degree of anatomic contact; this is an interpretation change, not a treatment recommendation.

premises.statement: Blinded post-treatment CT still called ~70% of resected tumours locally advanced/borderline yet 92% were resected R0 with fibrosis at the interface.
Anatomic size falls ~10% after therapy while FDG metabolic volume falls ~65%, and PERCIST matches pathologic response far better than RECIST.
FDG avidity at the tumour-vessel contact after therapy independently predicted recurrence (HR 4.37).

glosses.why-plans-change: This atlas's inference that functional imaging could separate treated scar from viable tumor at the vessel interface.

INF-DIAG-02.phenomenon: A negative post-operative ctDNA/MRD test is followed by recurrence in roughly half of patients, so negativity is weak reassurance.
INF-DIAG-02.missing: It is unresolved whether undetectable ctDNA in a recurring patient reflects genuinely low shedding by residual tumour or merely too few tumour genome-equivalents in the sampled plasma.
INF-DIAG-02.mechanism: At low tumour fraction the limiting factor is the Poisson-limited number of mutant genome copies in a standard blood draw; increasing the sampled genome-equivalents (larger plasma volume, serial draws, timing relative to cell release) should raise sensitivity if shedding exists, whereas truly non-shedding tumour would stay negative regardless.
assumptions: Residual micrometastatic clones shed at rates comparable to the primary
cfDNA half-life is short enough that timing matters
No-touch or sampling changes do not merely release non-viable DNA
supporting: DIAG-025
DIAG-011
conflicting: DIAG-024
INF-DIAG-02.competing: Residual PDAC is intrinsically low-shedding (desmoplastic, low-cellularity), so no practical increase in sampled volume will detect it and the ceiling is biological, not physical.
INF-DIAG-02.prediction: Increasing plasma input (e.g., multiple tubes or serial draws pooled) and optimising draw timing will raise MRD sensitivity in recurring patients proportionally to input genome-equivalents, up to a biological floor.
INF-DIAG-02.test: Prospective MRD study varying plasma volume/draw number per timepoint with tumour-informed assays, measuring detection rate among eventual recurrers as a function of genome-equivalents assayed.
INF-DIAG-02.implication: Defines how to read and how to improve a negative MRD result; it bounds the reassurance a clear liquid biopsy can give but does not itself prescribe treatment.

premises.statement: Even a one-in-10,000 assay with 100% plasma-tissue concordance detected only 30% of resectable tumours (0% in stage IB).
A tumour-informed 16-variant assay reached only 29% MRD-window positivity despite removing single-gene blind spots.
Surgical tumour mobilisation raised measured peripheral ctDNA ~2.5-fold and converted a negative to a positive, and portal sampling did not help.
Among ctDNA-negative resected patients, 2-year survival was still only ~53%.

glosses.microscopic-disease: This atlas's inference that the sensitivity floor of tumor-DNA tests is set by the number of mutant copies in a blood draw.
glosses.clear-scan: This atlas's inference that the sensitivity floor of tumor-DNA tests is set by the number of mutant copies in a blood draw.
glosses.molecular-testing: An atlas inference explaining why a negative early-stage blood test is weak reassurance, as a sampling limit.
glosses.ctdna: This atlas's inference that the sensitivity floor of tumor-DNA tests is set by the number of mutant copies in a blood draw.

INF-TX-01.phenomenon: Neoadjuvant (chemo)therapy improves survival in borderline resectable PDAC but not in anatomically resectable PDAC, despite improving R0 and nodal status in both.
INF-TX-01.missing: Why identical pathologic gains translate into survival only when the tumor abuts major vessels.
INF-TX-01.mechanism: The survival benefit of neoadjuvant therapy is the sum of two components: (a) margin/locoregional conversion, whose value scales with baseline R1 risk (high in borderline, low in resectable), and (b) early systemic therapy and progressor selection, whose value scales with the fraction of patients who would otherwise never receive effective adjuvant therapy. In resectable disease both components are small and are offset by attrition and delay before surgery, netting to zero or slight harm.
assumptions: Vessel contact on CT is a reasonable proxy for baseline R1 risk
Adjuvant completion rates in trials reflect practice
Effects are additive
supporting: PREOPANC-1 subgroup pattern
ESPAC-5 1-yr OS 39% vs 78-84% in borderline disease with low R0 in all arms
NORPACT-1 harm signal with implementation failure
conflicting: PREOPANC long-term report states effect consistent across resectable and borderline subgroups (abstract)
PREOPANC-1 interaction P=.14 (not significant)
Resectable trials are small phase 2 studies
INF-TX-01.competing: Statistical: the borderline/resectable split is chance within an underpowered trial, and neoadjuvant benefit is uniform but too small to detect in resectable cohorts (PREOPANC long-term abstract supports uniformity).
INF-TX-01.prediction: In A021806 and PREOPANC-3, the perioperative-arm HR will be near 1 overall, but will be <1 in strata with venous contact approaching 180 degrees or elevated CA19-9, and the control-arm HR advantage will shrink as adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX completion falls below ~60%.
INF-TX-01.test: Prespecified analysis of the pending phase 3 trials by degree of tumor-vessel interface (central radiology) and by adjuvant completion; alternatively an individual-patient meta-analysis of PREOPANC-1/-2, NORPACT-1, ESPAC-5, PANACHE01 with vessel-contact and adjuvant-delivery covariates.
INF-TX-01.implication: For the atlas: present neoadjuvant therapy as established for borderline disease and unresolved for resectable disease, and explain that the deciding factors are anatomy and the likelihood of receiving chemotherapy after surgery - not a treatment recommendation.

premises.statement: Neoadjuvant therapy raises R0 (72% vs 40%) and lowers N+ (33% vs 78%) across the whole PREOPANC-1 cohort, with OS benefit confined to the borderline subgroup.

In resectable disease, upfront surgery already achieves acceptable margins and the control arm receives highly effective adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX (median OS 53.5 mo; 79% complete gemcitabine, 67% complete mFOLFIRINOX).

Neoadjuvant delivery is imperfect: 21% of NORPACT-1 neoadjuvant patients never received FOLFIRINOX, 29% of S1505 'resectable' patients were misclassified at central review, and adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX use was lower after…
Resected-cohort survival after neoadjuvant therapy reflects selection of non-progressors.

glosses.why-chemo-first: This atlas's inference that neoadjuvant benefit scales with baseline margin risk and with the fraction of patients who would otherwise miss adjuvant therapy.
glosses.vessel-contact: This atlas's inference that preoperative chemotherapy helps most where vessel contact makes a positive margin likely.
glosses.treatment-sequencing: An atlas inference proposing that neoadjuvant benefit is the sum of margin conversion and early systemic treatment, which would explain why it helps borderline but not resectable disease.
glosses.vascular-resection: This atlas's inference that chemotherapy before surgery helps where margins are at risk, which is why its benefit appears in borderline but not clearly resectable disease.
glosses.radiation: An atlas inference proposing that the value of margin conversion scales with the baseline risk of a positive margin, which differs between borderline and clearly resectable disease.

INF-TX-02.phenomenon: Olaparib maintenance doubles PFS and delays subsequent chemotherapy in gBRCA metastatic PDAC, but OS is not significantly different (median 19.0 vs 19.2 mo) even though 3-year survival is 34% vs 18%.
INF-TX-02.missing: Why delaying progression by a median 3.6 months does not shift median survival.
INF-TX-02.mechanism: The authors' hypothesis: subsequent-therapy crossover and platinum re-sensitivity in the placebo arm, plus underpowering, mask an OS effect that manifests only as a long-tail (3-year) survival difference among durable responders.
assumptions: Post-progression PARP inhibitor use is as effective as maintenance use
Platinum re-challenge after a treatment break is as active in placebo patients as continuous therapy
supporting: TFST and TSST significantly longer
Durable responders exist (swimmer plot)
conflicting: PFS2 HR 0.76 not significant
Median OS identical
Early crossing of OS curves (possible early harm from stopping chemotherapy in some patients)
INF-TX-02.competing: Olaparib delays radiologic progression of indolent, platinum-sensitive disease without changing the kinetics of the lethal clone, so time to death is unaffected; the 3-year tail reflects prognostic heterogeneity within gBRCA carriers rather than drug effect.
INF-TX-02.prediction: If crossover masks a true effect, OS benefit should be larger in regions/sites where placebo patients did not access PARP inhibitors; if the lethal-clone explanation holds, OS will be identical regardless of crossover and PFS2 will remain unimproved.
INF-TX-02.test: Crossover-adjusted (RPSFT) OS analysis of POLO stratified by subsequent PARP inhibitor access, and a randomized comparison of olaparib maintenance vs continued fluoropyrimidine/platinum maintenance with PFS2 as co-primary endpoint.
INF-TX-02.implication: For the atlas: say olaparib maintenance buys time off chemotherapy with preserved quality of life and a possibly larger long-term survivor fraction, but has not been shown to lengthen average survival - kept distinct from advising its use.

premises.statement: PFS HR 0.53 by blinded review; investigator PFS HR 0.49; TFST HR 0.44.
Placebo patients received more subsequent therapy (87% vs 62%), including PARP inhibitors in 27% of discontinuers, and frequently platinum re-challenge.
OS curves cross at ~12 months and separate only after 24 months; trial was powered for PFS, not OS.

glosses.reading-trial-results: The POLO investigators' hypothesis that crossover and underpowering masked a survival benefit of olaparib.
glosses.olaparib: The published hypothesis that crossover and platinum re-sensitivity in the placebo arm masked an overall-survival effect of olaparib in POLO.

INF-TX-03.phenomenon: TTFields added to GnP in LAPC improved OS (HR 0.82) and pain-free survival but not PFS, local PFS, response or resectability.
INF-TX-03.missing: A local physical therapy producing a survival effect that bypasses every local-efficacy endpoint.
INF-TX-03.mechanism: Either (a) TTFields act within the field on peritoneal/retroperitoneal micrometastatic spread (consistent with the post hoc distant-PFS improvement), or (b) symptom control (pain) permits better chemotherapy delivery and supportive care (chemotherapy exposure by arm not extracted from accessed text), or (c) radiologic PFS/local PFS are too noisy in treated LAPC to register a real local effect that nonetheless changes survival.
assumptions: Open-label salvage therapy was balanced (reported 51% vs 47%)
Adherence (62% daily usage) is sufficient for a biological effect
supporting: Distant PFS improved post hoc
Pain-free survival improved
conflicting: No ORR or local PFS change
No resectability gain
mITT OS HR (0.73) better than ITT (0.82), suggesting early dropouts contribute
INF-TX-03.competing: Open-label performance/ascertainment effects (supportive care intensity, timing of progression calls) in a device trial without blinding.
INF-TX-03.prediction: If mechanism (a) holds, peritoneal/retroperitoneal recurrence will be specifically reduced in the TTFields arm; if (c) holds, CA19-9-defined progression will separate even though radiologic PFS did not.
INF-TX-03.test: Site-of-first-progression and CA19-9 kinetics analysis of PANOVA-3; a sham-device or blinded-assessment trial.
INF-TX-03.implication: For the atlas: report the OS and pain results as randomized evidence, state plainly that the mechanism of benefit is unexplained, and avoid implying local tumor control.

premises.statement: OS HR 0.82, PFS HR 0.85 (NS), local PFS not different; distant PFS improved post hoc.
Radiologic progression in LAPC is unreliable (inflammation/fibrosis vs tumor), as PANOVA-3 authors argue and as irradiated-tumor series imply.
Conventional radiation improves local control without OS (opposite dissociation).

glosses.ttfields: An atlas inference weighing possible explanations for a survival gain without a progression gain, from action on microscopic spread to open-label ascertainment effects.

INF-SURG-01.phenomenon: Recurrence years after a margin-negative resection.
INF-SURG-01.missing: Link between documented early dissemination (mouse) + single dormant liver DCCs and the clinical latency observed in patients.
INF-SURG-01.mechanism: Disseminated cells persist dormant in the liver under immune surveillance and unresolved ER stress; a later shift (XBP1s activation, waning immunity, niche remodeling) licenses outgrowth.
assumptions: Mouse DCC dormancy mechanism transfers to human liver
Human dormant DCCs are detectable
supporting: SURG-012
SURG-001
SURG-007
conflicting: SURG-009
INF-SURG-01.competing: Slow continuous subclinical growth (not true dormancy) below imaging threshold.
INF-SURG-01.prediction: If dormancy is real, serial ctDNA/DTC assays will show long negative intervals before relapse, and relapsing clones will show MHC-I re-expression/XBP1s activation.
INF-SURG-01.test: Longitudinal ctDNA/DTC sampling of resected patients with paired molecular profiling of dormant vs outgrowing liver lesions.
INF-SURG-01.implication: Supports surveillance strategies and dormancy-directed research, not a specific therapy yet.

premises.statement: Cells disseminate early and seed the liver.
Livers of PDAC patients/mice harbor single CK19-/MHC-I- dormant DCCs held in check by immunity and ER-stress state.
Late recurrence occurs in a substantial minority of resected patients.

glosses.microscopic-disease: A published hypothesis that late recurrence arises from dormant disseminated cells in the liver.
glosses.recurrence-meaning: A published hypothesis that late recurrence arises from dormant disseminated cells in the liver.

glosses.liver-niche: An atlas inference linking early dissemination and dormant liver cells to recurrence years after an apparently complete operation.
glosses.staging-laparoscopy: A published hypothesis that dormant disseminated cells in the liver explain late recurrence after margin-negative resection.
glosses.ctdna: A published hypothesis that dormant disseminated cells in the liver explain late recurrence after margin-negative resection.

INF-SURG-02.phenomenon: Isolated lung recurrence is far less lethal than liver recurrence.
INF-SURG-02.missing: Mechanistic reason the lung is a comparatively indolent site while the liver is lethal.
INF-SURG-02.mechanism: PDAC-specific hepatic niche programs (MIF/SAA/granulin fibrosis + immune exclusion) accelerate outgrowth and treatment resistance in the liver, whereas the lung lacks an equivalent PDAC-tropic niche, yielding slower, more indolent growth.
assumptions: Mouse niche biology is liver-specific and transfers to humans
Lung lacks comparable PDAC niche signals
supporting: SURG-015
SURG-022
SURG-023
SURG-024
conflicting: SURG-014
INF-SURG-02.competing: Lead-time/detection bias: lung nodules are found earlier and smaller on surveillance CT; indolent biology self-selects to lung.
INF-SURG-02.prediction: Matched lung vs liver metastases will show higher niche-fibrosis/immune-exclusion signatures and faster growth kinetics in liver, independent of size at detection.
INF-SURG-02.test: Lead-time-adjusted survival comparison + spatial profiling (fibrosis, CD8, SAA/granulin) of matched lung vs liver metastases.
INF-SURG-02.implication: Biological basis for selective pulmonary metastasectomy and for liver-niche-directed therapy research.

premises.statement: Lung recurrence median OS ~30 mo vs liver ~13 mo; liver confers 23x mortality vs 7x for lung.
The liver is actively conditioned into a pro-metastatic, fibrotic, immune-excluding niche.
Metastatic seeding is polyclonal and clonality differs by organ.

glosses.recurrence-meaning: This atlas's inference that organ-specific liver niche biology explains why lung recurrence is less lethal than liver recurrence.
glosses.liver: Atlas inference record proposing that the liver's PDAC-specific niche programs explain why liver recurrence is more lethal than lung recurrence.
glosses.liver-niche: An atlas inference proposing that liver-specific conditioning programs explain why liver recurrence behaves worse than lung recurrence.
glosses.liver-lesions: This atlas's inference that liver-specific niche biology explains why liver recurrence is far more lethal than lung recurrence.

INF-SURG-03.phenomenon: Pathologic complete response (pCR) of the primary followed by recurrence/death.
INF-SURG-03.missing: Whether pCR reflects true whole-body eradication or only local clearance with surviving extrapancreatic micrometastases.
INF-SURG-03.mechanism: Neoadjuvant therapy can clear the imaged/sampled primary while chemo-tolerant disseminated cells persist in liver/other sites, so pCR is a local phenomenon with residual systemic disease.
assumptions: Dissemination biology applies to the pCR subset
Occult disease is below current detection
supporting: SURG-018
SURG-005
SURG-009
INF-SURG-03.competing: Some pCR patients are genuinely cured; recurrences come from under-sampled residual primary (local), not systemic disease.
INF-SURG-03.prediction: ctDNA/DTC positivity at the time of pCR resection will predict recurrence better than pathology alone.
INF-SURG-03.test: Prospective ctDNA/DTC assessment in pCR patients correlated with site of first recurrence.
INF-SURG-03.implication: pCR should not be equated with cure; supports continued systemic therapy and molecular residual-disease testing (DIAG owns ctDNA).

premises.statement: pCR is rare (~3.3%) and strongly but not perfectly associated with survival (64.9 vs 21.6 mo).
Thorough sampling detects residual tumour that lesser sampling misses.
Disseminated/micrometastatic disease is typically present before resection.

glosses.microscopic-disease: This atlas's inference that pathologic complete response is a local finding that can coexist with residual systemic disease.
glosses.peritoneum: Atlas inference record proposing that a complete pathological response is a local event that can coexist with residual systemic disease.
glosses.ctdna: This atlas's inference that a pathologic complete response is local and that ctDNA should predict recurrence better than pathology alone.
glosses.pathology-report: This atlas's inference that a pathologic complete response is a local finding and that systemic disease can persist.
glosses.whipple: This atlas's inference that complete disappearance of tumor from the specimen is a local event that can coexist with surviving disease elsewhere.

INF-SUPP-01.phenomenon: Fat absorption stays subnormal after Whipple-type reconstruction in ~73% of patients despite 225,000-375,000 lipase units/day, whereas patients with motility-preserving operations respond better (M-SUPP-01).
INF-SUPP-01.missing: What, beyond lipase quantity, limits digestion after pancreatoduodenectomy.
INF-SUPP-01.mechanism: After pancreatoduodenectomy the enteric-coated microspheres and chyme leave the stomach asynchronously and enter a jejunal limb with altered pH and bicarbonate (no duodenum, reduced residual pancreatic bicarbonate), so enzyme release is mistimed and lipase is partly denatured; bacterial overgrowth and rapid transit add to the mismatch.
assumptions: Findings from mixed benign/malignant post-surgical patients transfer to resected PDAC patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy.
Jejunal pH after PD resembles that in other post-gastrectomy states.
supporting: SUPP-002 subgroup result
Guideline dosing concepts (SEC-SUPP-09, SEC-SUPP-18)
conflicting: No direct measurement of enzyme-chyme timing after PD located in this search.
INF-SUPP-01.competing: Incomplete response reflects residual-remnant insufficiency plus reduced intake and small-bowel mucosal changes (bile acid malabsorption), not timing; raising dose further or adding bile acids would then help.
INF-SUPP-01.prediction: If asynchrony/pH is the limit, uncoated or opened-capsule enzymes mixed with food plus a PPI will raise CFA more in Whipple patients than a further dose increase of coated microspheres; if remnant insufficiency is the limit, dose escalation will help equally.
INF-SUPP-01.test: Crossover trial after PD: (a) coated microspheres at 75,000 units/meal, (b) same dose plus PPI, (c) opened/uncoated enzymes mixed into food plus PPI; outcome 72-h CFA and breath-test fat digestion; stratify by reconstruction type.
INF-SUPP-01.implication: Explains to visitors why weight can fall despite 'taking enzymes' after a Whipple and why clinicians adjust timing and acid suppression, not just dose (distinct from a treatment recommendation).

premises.statement: High-dose enteric-coated enzymes raise CFA by ~25 points on average after pancreatic surgery.
Response is anatomy-dependent: 27% normalization after Whipple/duodenum-preserving resections vs higher after other operations.
Guidelines recommend adding acid suppression and taking enzymes with meals when response is inadequate.

glosses.digestion-enzymes: An inference record proposing that mistimed enzyme release, not enzyme quantity, limits digestion after a Whipple.
glosses.life-after-whipple: An inference record proposing that mistimed enzyme release, not enzyme quantity, limits digestion after a Whipple.
glosses.duodenum: Atlas inference record proposing that mistimed mixing of enzymes and food, not enzyme dose, limits digestion after a Whipple.
glosses.stomach: Atlas inference record proposing that mistimed mixing of enzymes and food, not enzyme dose, limits digestion after a Whipple.

glosses.total-pancreatectomy: This atlas's inference that mistimed enzyme delivery after reconstruction explains why fat absorption rarely normalizes on enzyme capsules.
glosses.enzyme-replacement: This atlas's proposed explanation for why fat absorption stays subnormal after a Whipple despite high enzyme doses: mistimed release and acid in the rebuilt intestine.

INF-SUPP-02.phenomenon: Within partial pancreatectomy cohorts, remnant volume is an inconsistent predictor of new diabetes while BMI, HbA1c and remnant steatosis predict it consistently (M-SUPP-03).
INF-SUPP-02.missing: How host insulin demand and remnant islet quality combine with the surgical loss of beta-cell mass to set the diabetes threshold.
INF-SUPP-02.mechanism: Diabetes appears when functional beta-cell capacity (remnant volume x islet density, reduced by steatosis/fibrosis and by post-operative atrophy) falls below insulin demand (set by adiposity/insulin resistance). Surgery removes a roughly fixed fraction of capacity, so inter-patient variation in demand and islet quality dominates; only very large capacity losses (total pancreatectomy, >=64% atrophy) make quantity decisive.
assumptions: CT attenuation ratio is a valid proxy for islet-functional tissue.
Cancer-associated paraneoplastic diabetes (ANAT domain) that regresses after resection is not misclassified as NODM.
supporting: Consistency of metabolic-load predictors across Swedish, Turkish and Japanese cohorts
Deterministic boundary at total pancreatectomy
conflicting: SUPP-034 found volume reduction the only multivariable predictor (BMI not modeled in accessed text)
SUPP-033 follow-up only 6 months
INF-SUPP-02.competing: Remnant atrophy is the true cause and the 6-month null (SUPP-033) is a timing artefact; metabolic-load associations arise because obese patients have fattier remnants that are harder to volumetrize.
INF-SUPP-02.prediction: In a cohort followed >=3 years with serial volumetry, HbA1c and BMI, the product (remnant volume x attenuation-based islet-quality index) divided by an insulin-resistance index will predict NODM better than either volume or BMI alone, and the volume term will gain weight with time since surgery.
INF-SUPP-02.test: Prospective multicentre cohort after PD/DP with preoperative OGTT/C-peptide, CT attenuation ratio, serial volumetry at 6, 12, 36 months; competing-risk models with time-varying volume.
INF-SUPP-02.implication: Visitors can be told that diabetes risk after surgery depends on both how much pancreas remains and their own metabolic state, which is why glucose monitoring and weight management are advised after surgery (an explanation, not a treatment recommendation).

premises.statement: Total pancreatectomy causes immediate universal insulin-dependent diabetes.
After distal pancreatectomy, obesity (SHR 2.23) and ASA class raise NODM risk; 28% develop NODM, median ~1 year.

After PD, BMI predicted NODM but volumetry did not (SUPP-033), whereas 6-month volume reduction >=64% predicted NODM in a smaller serial-CT cohort (SUPP-034); steatosis plus HbA1c >5.7% gave ~5x risk (SUPP-035).

glosses.glucose-diabetes: An inference record proposing a threshold model in which post-surgical diabetes depends on remnant capacity relative to insulin demand.
glosses.pancreas-body-tail: Atlas inference record proposing that diabetes after partial pancreatectomy depends on remaining islet capacity relative to the body's insulin demand.
glosses.spleen: Atlas inference record proposing that diabetes after partial pancreatectomy depends on remaining islet capacity relative to the body's insulin demand.
glosses.distal-pancreatectomy: This atlas's inference that diabetes after partial pancreatectomy depends on the body's insulin demand and remnant quality, not only on volume removed.
glosses.total-pancreatectomy: This atlas's inference that diabetes after pancreatic surgery depends on insulin demand and remnant quality except at the boundary of total removal.
glosses.diabetes-after-surgery: This atlas's two-component explanation of diabetes after partial pancreatectomy: remaining islet capacity set against the body's insulin demand.

INF-SUPP-03.phenomenon: Cachexia responders to a ghrelin agonist showed 2-fold higher chemotherapy disease control; GDF-15 blockade increases activity and weight; muscle loss predicts death independent of weight (M-SUPP-06, M-SUPP-02).
INF-SUPP-03.missing: Whether reversing cachexia improves chemotherapy delivery/tolerance (causal) or whether tumor control is the upstream driver of both appetite and survival.
INF-SUPP-03.mechanism: Cachexia reduces chemotherapy tolerance (dose reductions, delays, toxicity) and physical reserve; reversing the catabolic/anorexic drive restores dose intensity and activity, improving tumor control. The published alternative (authors of SUPP-023) notes reverse causation.
assumptions: Dose intensity mediates survival in pancreatic cancer regimens (TX domain evidence).
supporting: Activity increase with ponsegromab (SUPP-014)
Sarcopenia-FN/toxicity links in other cohorts (not re-extracted)
conflicting: No trial has shown survival or dose-intensity gains from any anti-cachexia drug in pancreatic cancer
Anamorelin response was lower in older patients and 38% stopped early (SUPP-023)
INF-SUPP-03.competing: Reverse causation: responding tumors reduce cytokine output (GDF-15, IL-6) so appetite and weight recover; the drug merely marks the responders.
INF-SUPP-03.prediction: In the randomized phase 3 ponsegromab trial in pancreatic cancer (NCT06989437), delivered chemotherapy dose intensity and time-to-dose-reduction will differ between arms if the causal path holds; if reverse causation dominates, weight gain will occur without dose-intensity change and will track radiographic response.
INF-SUPP-03.test: Pre-specified analysis of relative dose intensity and treatment discontinuation for toxicity in NCT06989437, with GDF-15 and CA19-9 trajectories as mediators.
INF-SUPP-03.implication: Frames anti-cachexia drugs as potentially changing what chemotherapy can be delivered, while warning that current evidence cannot separate marker from cause (not a treatment recommendation).

premises.statement: Muscle loss during chemotherapy predicts death independently of BMI.
GDF-15 blockade raises weight, appetite and physical activity within 12 weeks.
Anamorelin responders had disease control 75% vs 37.5%.

glosses.weight-loss-cachexia: An inference record weighing whether reversing cachexia improves chemotherapy tolerance or whether tumor response drives both.
glosses.growth-factor-support: A published hypothesis, recorded in this atlas, that reversing cachexia could improve chemotherapy tolerance and delivered dose, with reverse causation as the competing explanation.
glosses.cachexia-treatments: A published hypothesis, recorded in this atlas, that reversing cachexia could improve chemotherapy tolerance and delivered dose, with reverse causation as the competing explanation.
glosses.cachexia-research: A published hypothesis that reversing cachexia improves chemotherapy delivery and tumor control, set against the reverse-causation alternative that responding tumors relieve cachexia.

INF-RAS-01.phenomenon: Responses to RAS-directed drugs in pancreatic cancer are deep but short: tumour shrinkage of some degree in 79% of patients on sotorasib, a 30% objective response rate and HR 0.40 for survival with daraxonrasib, yet median progression-free survival of only 7.2 months and median duration of response of about 8 months - and in most patients no genetic cause of progression can be found.
INF-RAS-01.missing: There is no established human link between the immediate, non-genetic drug-tolerant state demonstrated in cells and the clinical timing of progression. The baseline jumps from drug occupancy (L-RAS-02) to detectable genomic escape lesions (L-RAS-08) with nothing in between, even though the lesions explain only a quarter to a half of progressions.
INF-RAS-01.mechanism: A drug-tolerant persister state, established within days of starting treatment and maintained by RTK-ligand-driven PI3K/GAB1 assembly of wild-type RAS signalling complexes, sets the floor of residual tumour that imaging reports as a partial rather than complete response. Progression is then the outgrowth of that persister pool, which acquires copy-number amplification of mutant KRAS or of RTK/RAF genes only as a late, consolidating step. On this account the genomic lesions are markers of an escape that was functionally established much earlier, which is why they are absent in most patients at the moment imaging first shows growth.
assumptions: That mechanisms shown in cell lines and in lung/biliary models transfer to pancreatic tumours in patients
That wild-type RAS engagement by multi-selective inhibitors does not already fully neutralise this route - plausible, since daraxonrasib inhibits wild-type RAS but patients still progress
That the stroma, which in PDAC is dense and a known source of growth-factor ligands, supplies at least as much EGFR ligand as tumour-cell autocrine production
supporting: The absence of drug-binding-site mutations in pancreatic cohorts, which argues that escape is not about the drug losing its grip on the target
The dominance of RAF and RTK lesions plus KRAS amplification, all of which raise pathway output rather than block the drug
The fact that cells prevented from making the adaptive changes are durably inhibited in vitro
Adaptive pEGFR rise observed under the clinical RAS(ON) agent in biliary epithelium
conflicting: WFS1-dependent resistance is explicitly independent of KRAS activation status, so at least one route does not require pathway reactivation
CDK8-driven microenvironmental immune evasion is a host-side mechanism this inference does not involve
Mesenchymal/basal states were more, not less, drug-responsive in vivo, which an RTK-persister model does not predict
INF-RAS-01.competing: Progression is driven primarily by the host-side reversal of the early immune response (CDK8-CXCL2-FAS axis) rather than by tumour-cell-intrinsic signalling reactivation; on that view the persister pool is immunologically rather than pharmacologically determined, and the right intervention is timing immunotherapy to the first weeks rather than adding an RTK inhibitor.
INF-RAS-01.prediction: If the persister mechanism is correct, serial on-treatment tumour biopsies or sensitive plasma assays taken at 2-4 weeks - well before radiographic progression - should show restored phospho-ERK and phospho-S6 in residual tumour together with rising EGFR-ligand (amphiregulin, HBEGF) levels, in patients who go on to progress early, and these changes should precede any detectable genomic lesion by…
INF-RAS-01.test: A prospective window-of-opportunity study in previously treated metastatic PDAC starting daraxonrasib, with paired tumour biopsies at baseline, day 14-28 and at progression, plus matched plasma for ctDNA and EGFR-ligand measurement. Primary readout: whether phospho-ERK/phospho-S6 restoration and ligand rise at day 14-28 predict time to progression independently of, and earlier than, ctDNA lesion…
INF-RAS-01.implication: If supported, the informative measurement in RAS-directed therapy is an early on-treatment pharmacodynamic and ligand readout rather than a resistance-mutation panel at progression, and the rational combination is upfront rather than at relapse. This is an inference about what to measure and when, not a recommendation to use any combination outside a trial - no RAS-inhibitor-plus-RTK-inhibitor…

premises.statement: Within hours of inactive-state KRAS G12C inhibition an isogenic population splits, with roughly 20% of cells resuming proliferation by synthesising new KRAS kept active by EGFR and aurora kinase signalling.
PI3K, acting upstream through membrane recruitment of GAB1, assembles EGFR/SHP2/SOS1-dependent complexes that activate wild-type RAS and reactivate MAPK while mutant KRAS is blocked.

Acquired lesions under daraxonrasib are RAF-gene variants and RTK events (HER2 amplification, MET fusion) usually accompanied by mutant KRAS amplification, in 25% of patients, with no drug-binding-site mutations.
In pancreatic cohorts 54% (G12C inhibitors) to 75% (daraxonrasib) of progressions have no identifiable genetic mechanism.
Adaptive EGFR activation under the same RAS(ON) inhibitor occurs in a second, non-pancreatic epithelial tumour type, and the responsible ligand in lung models is autocrine amphiregulin.

INF-RAS-02.phenomenon: KRAS inhibition reliably produces an immune response in pancreatic tumours - T-cell influx with granzyme B and Ki-67 induction in mice, necessary for durable control; mutant-KRAS-specific T cells in 84% of vaccinated patients - yet no immune-based intervention has ever improved outcomes in pancreatic cancer, and the mouse T-cell influx disappears by day 7.
INF-RAS-02.missing: No link exists between the open immune window and any clinical schedule. The baseline records the influx (L-RAS-03), its necessity (L-RAS-04) and its CDK8-mediated reversal (L-RAS-09), all in mice, and separately records human immunogenicity without clinical benefit - but nothing states when, in human treatment, immunity could be exploited.
INF-RAS-02.mechanism: RAS inhibition opens a short immunological window by releasing tumour antigen and relieving KRAS-driven suppression of antigen presentation and T-cell recruitment. The window closes because the same sustained pathway inhibition induces two counter-programmes: CDK8-dependent CXCL2 secretion and FAS downregulation in the microenvironment, and an interferon-driven NF-kB/basal-like cell-state shift in the tumour cells. Checkpoint blockade therefore has a target only during the first weeks of RAS-directed therapy, which is precisely the period in which it has never been tested clinically - prior pancreatic immunotherapy trials gave checkpoint inhibitors without, or long after, effective pathway…
assumptions: That mouse kinetics (days) scale to human kinetics (plausibly weeks) in a manner that can be bracketed by serial biopsy
That the human tumour has a comparable pool of recruitable KRAS-reactive T cells - supported by the 84% vaccine immunogenicity and by the TCR case, but not by tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte…
That CDK8 and TRIM22 programmes operate in human tumours under daraxonrasib, which has not been measured
supporting: Explicit demonstration that priming with a KRAS inhibitor then adding checkpoint blockade delays or prevents resistance in mice
T-cell dependence of durable control
Human proof that the KRAS G12D neoepitope can be presented and killed through
A pan-RAS inhibitor independently increasing CD8+ T cells and M1-like macrophages in immunocompetent pancreatic tumours
conflicting: Every randomised immunotherapy attempt in pancreatic cancer to date has failed, which is a strong prior against any immune strategy here
The AMPLIFY-201 relapse-free-survival signal is a post hoc split of 25 patients and its randomised successor has not reported
Patient-derived xenografts resistant to daraxonrasib also upregulate CDK8 despite lacking an adaptive immune system, so CDK8 is not exclusively an immune mechanism
INF-RAS-02.competing: The immune activation is epiphenomenal - a by-product of rapid tumour-cell death rather than a contributor - and the T-cell depletion result reflects loss of a general tissue-repair/homeostatic function rather than tumour-specific immunity; on that view no schedule of checkpoint blockade would help, and durability depends only on how completely the tumour-cell pathway is shut down.
INF-RAS-02.prediction: If the window hypothesis is correct, adding a checkpoint inhibitor during the first 4-8 weeks of daraxonrasib (concurrent or immediately sequential) should produce measurably deeper tumour regression and longer progression-free survival than adding the same agent at or after progression, and on-treatment biopsies at 2-4 weeks should show rising CD8+ density that is preserved by the checkpoint…
INF-RAS-02.test: A randomised phase 2 trial in metastatic PDAC of daraxonrasib plus early concurrent anti-PD-1 (or anti-CTLA-4, following the mouse data) versus daraxonrasib alone with the immune agent added only at progression, with mandatory paired biopsies at baseline and week 3-4 and co-primary endpoints of progression-free survival and change in intratumoral CD8+ T-cell density. CDK8 and CXCL2 expression in…
INF-RAS-02.implication: If supported, the atlas should describe immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer as schedule-dependent rather than simply ineffective, and should present the first weeks of RAS-directed therapy as the biologically meaningful moment to assess immune combinations. This is a statement about study design and about how to interpret past immunotherapy failures, not a recommendation for any treatment; no…

T-cell depletion abolishes durable control after an initial response to KRAS G12D inhibition.

Long-term KRAS G12D inhibition reverses the early immune activation through CDK8-induced CXCL2 secretion and FAS suppression, and CDK8 targeting with or without anti-CTLA-4 overcomes resistance; priming with a KRAS…
Sustained KRAS-MAPK inhibition drives an interferon-to-TRIM22-to-NF-kB programme producing a basal-like/EMT state, a cell state associated in pancreatic cancer with immune exclusion.
A mutant-KRAS vaccine in the minimal-residual-disease setting produced specific T cells in 84% of patients and biomarker clearance in 24%, with no randomised survival evidence.
A single patient treated with KRAS G12D-directed TCR gene therapy had a 72% partial response with engineered T cells persisting above 2% of circulating T cells at 6 months.

glosses.kras-g12d-inhibitors: An atlas inference proposing that RAS inhibition opens a brief immune window that closes within days, which would make the timing of any added immunotherapy decisive.
glosses.ras-resistance: This atlas's inference that RAS blockade opens a brief immune window which the same sustained blockade then closes.

INF-RAS-03.phenomenon: Three inhibitors of the identical target (KRAS G12C) in the identical disease and broadly the identical treatment line report pancreatic response rates of 21%, 33% and 46.9%; and one inhibitor at a fixed dose produces a 53.4% response rate with 13.1-month progression-free survival in lung cancer versus 29.1% and 5.6 months in colorectal cancer.
INF-RAS-03.missing: The baseline attributes effect to allele occupancy (L-RAS-01, L-RAS-02) and has no term for achieved target occupancy at tolerated human exposure, for the shape of the exposure-response curve, or for response-assessment method - yet these three studies differ more than two-fold.
INF-RAS-03.mechanism: The determinant of response depth in KRAS-driven pancreatic cancer is the fraction of time that mutant RAS-GTP is held below the threshold at which downstream effector output (not merely ERK phosphorylation, but S6 and the proliferative programme) collapses. First-generation inactive-state inhibitors reach that threshold only intermittently because they depend on nucleotide cycling and achieve submaximal trough occupancy; later agents designed for high trough occupancy, and agents that bind the active state directly, hold output below threshold for a larger fraction of the dosing interval. Tissue context modifies the threshold - which is why the same drug behaves differently in lung and…
assumptions: That the three pancreatic cohorts are comparable in prior lines and performance status, which is only approximately true
That investigator-assessed response rates are inflated relative to blinded central review by a magnitude smaller than the 26-point spread observed
That trough occupancy, not peak, is the governing exposure metric - supported by the stated design rationale of olomorasib but not directly measured in tumour
supporting: Olomorasib's 42% response rate in patients who had already failed a first-generation G12C inhibitor, including 48% among those for whom it was the immediate prior therapy, which is hard to explain by anything other…
The preclinical demonstration that active-state binding defeats a mutation that blocks inactive-state binding
The dissociation between MAPK suppression and growth inhibition when S6 phosphorylation is preserved, which supports a threshold rather than a linear model
conflicting: Divarasib's lung-versus-colorectal gap at a fixed dose shows tissue context alone can produce a two-fold difference in response and more than a two-fold difference in PFS, so potency need not be the dominant term
ctDNA clearance in 67% of patients including non-responders shows that near-complete target engagement does not guarantee a radiographic response
The glecirasib cohorts were predominantly from a different region and were investigator-assessed, so population and assessment confounding cannot be separated from potency
INF-RAS-03.competing: The differences are mostly measurement and population artefacts - investigator versus blinded central review, differing prior-therapy burden, small denominators of 21-38 patients with overlapping confidence intervals - and there is no real potency gradient. On this view the correct conclusion is that all G12C inhibitors perform similarly in pancreatic cancer and the apparent spread is noise.
INF-RAS-03.prediction: If the occupancy-threshold mechanism is correct, a trial that administers two G12C inhibitors of different trough occupancy in the same pancreatic population with a single blinded central review will show a response-rate difference in the predicted direction, and within each arm the depth of ctDNA KRAS variant-allele-frequency reduction at day 15 will correlate with response depth, while…
INF-RAS-03.test: The practical version does not require a head-to-head trial: pooled individual-patient reanalysis of the existing pancreatic G12C cohorts under a single blinded central review, with trough plasma concentration and day-15 ctDNA variant-allele-frequency change as covariates, would test whether exposure predicts response once assessment method is harmonised. A prospective paired-biopsy substudy…
INF-RAS-03.implication: If supported, the atlas should present 'a KRAS G12C inhibitor' not as a single intervention but as a class whose benefit depends on how completely and continuously it holds the target down, and should treat cross-trial response-rate comparisons with explicit caution about assessment method. This bears on how results are explained to readers, not on drug choice - neither sotorasib nor adagrasib…

glosses.kras-g12c-inhibitors: An atlas inference proposing that differences in target occupancy, not the target itself, explain why three G12C inhibitors gave response rates from 21 to 47 percent in pancreatic cancer.

INF-IMMUNE-01.phenomenon: Vaccine-induced and adoptively transferred tumour-antigen-specific T cells reach human pancreatic tumours and produce no measurable tumour shrinkage, even when antigen, HLA, antigen-processing machinery, interferon-gamma signalling and local lymphoid architecture are all intact.
INF-IMMUNE-01.missing: There is no term in the causal baseline linking the QUANTITY and local licensing of correctly specified T cells at the tumour to the probability of killing enough cancer cells to register as a response.
INF-IMMUNE-01.mechanism: The binding constraint is a combination of insufficient effector dose and active local de-licensing, acting after trafficking. Peripheral clone frequencies of roughly 0.07-3% of blood T cells, of which only a fraction traffics and of which the highest-avidity members decay fastest, deliver an effector-to-target ratio orders of magnitude below what is needed against a bulky, stroma-rich tumour; the T cells that do arrive are then held at low function by restraints the current drugs do not address (T-cell-intrinsic TLR2 signalling, and regulatory T cells that expand in step with CD8 cells under combination therapy) without acquiring canonical exhaustion markers.
assumptions: That mouse TLR2 biology transfers to human PDAC (supported only by a transcriptional correlation in humans).
That peripheral clone frequency is a usable proxy for intratumoural effector density, which has not been calibrated in PDAC.
That the regulatory T-cell expansion observed under CSF1R-containing combination therapy generalises to vaccine-only regimens.
supporting: IMM-012 and IMM-018: the two trials that measured the intratumoural endpoint both met it and both failed clinically.
IMM-002: the inverse relationship between relative neoepitope avidity and clone half-life after priming, which predicts preferential loss of exactly the most useful clones.

IMM-026: sufficient endogenous T-cell pressure DOES edit PDAC clones over a decade in long-term survivors, with no HLA class-I pathway alteration - so the killing step works when the dose is high enough and sustained…
IMM-023: entry capacity is a tumour property, not a product property.
conflicting: IMM-006 patient 1 achieved a 72% response with only 2.4% of circulating T cells transduced at 6 months, which argues that a modest peripheral frequency CAN suffice - though that product consisted of billions of…

This is an interpretive statement about evidence, NOT a recommendation for or against any treatment, and it does not bear on whether an individual…

INF-IMMUNE-02.phenomenon: Across four different vaccine platforms spanning 14 years, patients who mount an immune response survive markedly longer than those who do not, with remarkably consistent and very large hazard ratios, and no randomized trial has ever reproduced the effect at the arm level.
INF-IMMUNE-02.missing: Nothing in the causal baseline explains why an on-treatment immune-response biomarker would be so strongly associated with outcome while the treatment that produces it has no demonstrated effect.
INF-IMMUNE-02.mechanism: Reverse causation through a shared upstream variable. Occult residual tumour burden at the time of vaccination simultaneously (a) suppresses T-cell priming through systemic inflammation, myeloid expansion and the immune-competency deficit that the baseline signature measures, and (b) causes early recurrence. Immune-response status is therefore a DOWNSTREAM MARKER of how much disease the patient still had, which makes it an excellent prognostic indicator and a poor measure of treatment effect. A dichotomised, data-derived threshold then maximises the apparent separation.
assumptions: That post-surgical ctDNA or CA19-9 at the time of first vaccine dose is an adequate proxy for occult burden.
That the immune-suppressive effect of occult micrometastatic burden is large enough to flip a patient between responder and non-responder status.

If true mediation…
INF-IMMUNE-02.test: Prespecify, in the randomized trials, ctDNA at the time of first vaccine dose as a covariate in the responder-outcome model; and run the identical responder-style stratification in the control arm using the pretreatment immune-competency signature from IMM-022. Both analyses use data these trials already collect and neither requires a new study.
INF-IMMUNE-02.implication: When reading a report that 'patients who responded to the vaccine lived longer', the quantity that matters is whether that comparison was made between randomized groups or within one treated group. Within one group, the comparison cannot separate the vaccine's effect from how much cancer the patient still had. This is a statement about how to read evidence and carries no treatment recommendation.

INF-IMMUNE-03.phenomenon: Pancreatic cancer cells actively degrade their own surface MHC class I through NBR1-dependent autophagy, and this is pharmacologically reversible with a clinically available drug, yet no trial has combined an autophagy inhibitor with checkpoint blockade in pancreatic cancer.
INF-IMMUNE-03.missing: Whether restoring surface MHC class I in human PDAC at tolerated chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine exposures is achievable, and whether it converts a checkpoint-refractory tumour into a checkpoint-responsive one as it does in mice.
INF-IMMUNE-03.mechanism: Lysosomal inhibition raises the steady-state surface pool of MHC class I on PDAC cells by blocking its degradation, increasing the density of neoantigen-MHC complexes available to CD8 T cells; because the resulting T-cell response is cDC1-dependent and because PDAC is cDC1-poor, the restored presentation requires both CTLA-4 blockade (to broaden priming) and PD-1 blockade (to sustain effectors), which is why single-agent blockade is insufficient in the mouse data.
assumptions: That hydroxychloroquine at tolerated human doses achieves intratumoural lysosomal inhibition comparable to the mouse chloroquine exposures - unverified, and a known weakness of autophagy-inhibitor…
That OVA-based presentation gains predict gains for real, low-avidity PDAC neoantigens.
That the cDC1 deficit in human PDAC is not so severe that restored presentation cannot be converted into priming.
supporting: The rescue is specified to macroautophagy rather than to LC3-associated phagocytosis (Rubicon knockdown does not reproduce it) and is abolished by beta-2-microglobulin knockdown, so the mechanism is tightly constrained.
Hydroxychloroquine has established activity signals in PDAC trials, so the combination is clinically reachable.
Independent observations cited by the authors link the lysosomal pathway to reduced CD8 infiltration in human PDAC and enrich autophagy genes in MHC-class-I-negative PDAC cells in liver metastases.
conflicting: Chloroquine has autophagy-independent effects on LC3-associated phagocytosis, on macrophage polarisation and directly on CD8 T cells, so the mouse benefit may not be attributable to MHC class I restoration at all.

This would predict that beta-2-microglobulin knockdown should NOT abolish the effect - and the reported epistasis experiment argues against it, which is why this competing explanation is the weaker of the two.

INF-IMMUNE-03.test: A window-of-opportunity neoadjuvant study with surface versus intracellular HLA class I quantification as the primary pharmacodynamic endpoint and the baseline intracellular/surface ratio as a prespecified stratification factor, with PD-L1 as a negative control marker. No such trial was identified in this review.
INF-IMMUNE-03.implication: The mechanism by which pancreatic cancer hides from T cells has been identified precisely enough to name the protein that does it, and it is reversible in mice with an old, cheap, orally available drug. That is a reason to watch this specific combination, and it is not evidence that taking hydroxychloroquine helps anyone with pancreatic cancer - no human trial of this combination has been done.
